title: docs(cloudron): document moving a source-built install to a catalog-linked install
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `cloudron migrate source build install to community app catalog versions-url` → 0 hits
- [x] Discovery pass: issue search for catalog switch/`versions-url` → 0 results; no aidevops guide covers it
- [x] File refs verified: `.agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-app-publishing-skill.md:117-128` ("Catalog Updates Versus Source Rebuilds"); `.agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-server-ops-skill.md:58` (lists `--versions-url` for install/update)
- [x] Tier: `tier:simple` — docs only; facts below are verified
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-18
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** After publishing a new Cloudron community package, the operator asked for "the process for changing apps from our build to community app linked". It had been done once (a package's notes record a fresh `cloudron install --versions-url` on 2026-10-16, then uninstalling the source-built test app) but never captured in aidevops guidance, so the session couldn't find it.

## What

Add a short subsection after "Catalog Updates Versus Source Rebuilds" in `cloudron-app-publishing-skill.md`: **Moving a source-built install to the catalog**.

Verified facts to state (Cloudron CLI 8.2.6, `src/actions.js`):

- Only `cloudron install --versions-url <url>[@version]` links an app to a catalog. It calls `/api/v1/community/app` and sends `versionsUrl` with the install (`actions.js:540-548, 667-668`).
- `cloudron update` has no `--versions-url` option. It can switch an app to the catalog's digest-pinned image (the scratch-manifest method already documented at lines 124-128) but doesn't make the app catalog-linked, so it never receives catalog updates.
- So the switch is: back up → install a new copy from the catalog → move data or users → verify → uninstall the source-built app.

Procedure to document:

1. `cloudron backup create --app <old>`.
2. If data matters: `cloudron export --app <old>` and later `cloudron import --app <new> ...` (verify flags with `cloudron export --help` / `cloudron import --help` at implementation time), or restore through the dashboard's Import. If it was only a test instance, start fresh.
3. `cloudron install --versions-url <catalog-url> --location <temp-or-final-location>`. A location can hold only one app, so either install at a temporary location and use `cloudron set-location` after uninstalling the old app, or uninstall first (destructive, so confirm).
4. Verify health, sign-in and stored credentials, then `cloudron uninstall --app <old>`.
5. Confirm the new app reports catalog updates (dashboard shows the community source; `cloudron status --app <new>` shows the catalog image digest).

Also correct `cloudron-server-ops-skill.md:58`, which lists `--versions-url` as an `update` flag. In CLI 8.2.6 it's install-only.

## Why

Without this, every new package's production test install stays on a source build and silently misses updates, or an agent has to rediscover the CLI behaviour.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:simple`

**Tier rationale:** Docs-only change of about 20 lines with verified facts supplied.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-app-publishing-skill.md` — new subsection after line ~128.
- `EDIT: .agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-server-ops-skill.md:58` — `--versions-url` is install-only.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** agents loading the Cloudron publishing and server-ops skills.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** none.
- **Existing verification/tests:** markdown lint via `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`.
- **Schemas/config:** none.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** deployed via `setup.sh`.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert.

### Implementation Steps

1. Run `cloudron export --help` and `cloudron import --help` (CLI 8.2.6) and use the exact flags.
2. Write the subsection; keep it under about 25 lines.
3. Fix the server-ops flag line; run the linters.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** N/A.
- **Migration/rollback:** N/A.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** state the CLI version the facts were checked against.
- **Idempotency/retry:** N/A.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** the doc must say to keep the old app until the new one is verified.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
rg -n 'Moving a source-built install' .agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-app-publishing-skill.md
```

- **Surface mapping:** docs only.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-app-publishing-skill.md`
- `.agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-server-ops-skill.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The publishing skill documents the backup → catalog install → data move → verify → uninstall procedure, and says `update` cannot link an app to a catalog.

  ```yaml

    method: bash
    run: "rg -q 'Moving a source-built install' .agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-app-publishing-skill.md"
  ```

- [ ] The server-ops skill no longer lists `--versions-url` as an `update` flag.
- [ ] Linters pass.

body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-18
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** Installing the linked-issue-check caller in a managed package repo made Qlty report "1 blocking issue, including 1 vulnerability": `zizmor/dangerous-triggers` (high) on the `pull_request_target` trigger. The canonical template has the same trigger, so every repo that installs it gets this finding.

## What

Add a reviewed inline exception to the caller template's trigger. This was verified locally in the package repo: `qlty check` went from 1 high to "No issues":

```yaml
on:
  # pull_request_target is needed to post a status on fork PRs. Reviewed safe:
  # the reusable workflow reads PR metadata only and never checks out or runs
  # PR-head code, and this caller grants no contents permission.
  pull_request_target: # zizmor: ignore[dangerous-triggers]
    types: [opened, edited, synchronize, reopened]
```

## Why

The trigger is necessary and reviewed safe: `linked-issue-check-reusable.yml` uses only `actions/github-script` on `pr.body`/`pr.head.sha` metadata and `createCommitStatus`. But an unannotated high-severity finding on every managed repo trains maintainers to ignore Qlty security results.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:simple`

**Tier rationale:** Comment-only change to one template; exact text supplied and verified.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/templates/workflows/linked-issue-check-caller.yml:20-22`
- Check `.github/workflows/linked-issue-check.yml` (the framework's own caller) and other `pull_request_target` caller templates (`rg -l pull_request_target .agents/templates/workflows`); apply the same pattern only where the reusable workflow is likewise metadata-only.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Writers/mutation paths:** template only.

title: docs(cloudron): use update --versions-url to switch a source-built app to its catalog
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `cloudron update versions-url catalog switch` → 0 hits
- [x] Discovery pass: corrects guidance merged for #35003 (`e216d12840`)
- [x] File refs verified: `.agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-app-publishing-skill.md:135-151`, `.agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-server-ops-skill.md:58`
- [x] Tier: `tier:simple`; implemented interactively
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-18
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** #35003's brief was written against Cloudron CLI 8.2.6 and said `cloudron update` cannot link an app to a catalog. When the documented install-and-import route was used on a real Cloudron 10.1.5 server, `cloudron import` failed. The in-place switch below then worked.

## What

Verified on Cloudron 10.1.5 (`GET /api/v1/cloudron/status`) with CLI 9.0.3:

- CLI 9.0.0+ has `cloudron update --app <app> --versions-url <url>[@version] --force`. Its changelog says it updates or switches a community app's `CloudronVersions.json` URL; `--force` is required for a source-type change. It POSTs `{versionsUrl, skipBackup, force}` to `/api/v1/apps/<id>/update`, keeps the app ID, data, Postgres database, location and mailbox, and backs up first unless `--no-backup` is passed.
- Result: `cloudron status` shows `Source: <catalog URL>` and the catalog's digest-pinned image. The old `local/...` image is deleted, and `/app/data` secrets are untouched.
- `cloudron import --remote-path ... --backup-format tgz` fails against Cloudron 10 with `400 format must be string`: CLI 8.2.6 and 9.0.3 both send `backupFormat`. So the install-new-copy-and-import route in the current text doesn't work from the CLI.
- CLI 8.x has no `update --versions-url`. Check `cloudron --version` first; `npx -y cloudron@9 ...` runs the newer CLI without changing the global install and uses the same `~/.cloudron.json`.

## How

- `EDIT: .agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-app-publishing-skill.md:135-151`: make the in-place `update --versions-url --force` the primary procedure (check CLI version, optional manual backup, run, verify `Source:`/digest/health/secrets). Keep the reinstall route only as a fallback, noting that CLI import is broken on Cloudron 10.
- `EDIT: .agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-server-ops-skill.md:58`: `--versions-url` works with `install` and, on CLI 9.0+, with `update` (with `--force` to switch source).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The publishing skill documents `cloudron update --versions-url <url> --force` (CLI 9.0+) as the switch route and states the Cloudron 10 import failure.
- [ ] The server-ops skill no longer says `--versions-url` is install-only.
- [ ] `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed` passes.

## What

Two README badge defects found while re-rendering stale badge blocks across
managed repos (follow-up to GH#35012):

1. `badges-check-helper.sh` misclassifies drift. `_classify_badges_repo` runs

title: t18721: feat(badges): worktree-safe badges sync --apply and scheduled drift remediation
body:
**Task ID:** `t18721` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `auto-dispatch` `feat`

## Outcome

feat(badges): worktree-safe badges sync --apply and scheduled drift remediation

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Keep managed README badge blocks current automatically. Today a template fix
(e.g. GH#34145, GH#35012) only reaches a repo when someone runs
`aidevops init` or `aidevops badges sync --apply` by hand, so ~50 managed repos
kept an outdated badge block (language chart inline with badges) for weeks.

Two gaps:

1. `badges-sync-helper.sh --apply` mutates canonical checkouts:
   `git pull --ff-only` then `git checkout -q -B <branch>` in the canonical
   repo path, commit, push, then checkout back. This violates the
   linked-worktree invariant (interactive and automated sessions never switch
   or create branches in a canonical checkout) and skips any repo whose
   canonical checkout is dirty or off its default branch.
2. No routine runs drift detection + remediation. `badges-check-helper.sh`
   is only run manually.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/badges-sync-helper.sh`: create a linked worktree per repo
  from `origin/<default-branch>` (via `worktree-helper.sh add`), run
  `readme-badges-helper.sh inject` + `repo-metrics-helper.sh generate` +
  `check` inside it, commit, push, open the PR with `gh_create_pr`, then
  release the worktree. Never touch the canonical checkout.
- Add a weekly routine (pulse/maintenance path that already iterates
  maintained repos, see `test-maintenance-repo-selection.sh` for the repo
  selector) that runs `badges-check-helper.sh --json` and opens one sync PR per
  DRIFTED owned-org repo, deduplicating against an open sync PR.
- Respect owned-org scope (`badge-orgs.conf`), STARTER-OWNED, local-only and
  contributed repos exactly as today.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/badges-sync-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/badges-check-helper.sh`
- `.agents/aidevops/badges.md`

title: Star History workflow: skip with a warning when SYNC_PAT is not set
body:
## What

Make the reusable Star History workflow skip with a visible warning, not fail, when the caller has not set `SYNC_PAT`.

## Why

`aidevops init` adds `.github/workflows/star-history.yml` to managed repos, and the reusable workflow fails until the owner sets the `SYNC_PAT` repository secret. On 2026-10-18 five managed package repos had the caller but no secret, so each would have failed every Sunday. One already had: its run on 2026-10-18 failed at `Require owner-authorised repository token` with `SYNC_PAT is required because GitHub restricts timestamped stargazer history to repository collaborators.` The owner chose a warning that skips the run: a missing optional token is a setup gap, not a broken build, and a weekly red run hides real failures.

The token is still required to *generate* the chart (GitHub only returns timestamped stargazers to collaborators), so the job cannot fall back to `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Without the token it should do nothing and say why.

## How

Files to modify:

- `EDIT: .github/workflows/star-history-reusable.yml:21-43`
  - Keep the `SYNC_PAT` secret declaration, but change `required: true` to `required: false`. The caller always maps it, and an empty value is the case being handled.
  - Give the `Require owner-authorised repository token` step an `id` and an output, for example `present=true|false`. When it is absent, emit `::warning::` with a short fix (fine-grained PAT limited to the repo, Contents read/write, set as the `SYNC_PAT` repository secret; see `aidevops --help sync-pat`), write a line to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, and `exit 0`.
  - Gate every later step with `if: steps.<id>.outputs.present == 'true'`. Steps that use the token must never run with an empty value.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-star-history-helper.sh:108-124`. This file has a static contract test. Line 117 asserts `required: true`; replace it with assertions for the skip contract: a `::warning::` line mentioning `SYNC_PAT`, and the token-using steps being gated.
- `.agents/templates/workflows/star-history-caller.yml` needs no change; it already maps `SYNC_PAT: ${{ secrets.SYNC_PAT }}`.

Reference pattern: `.github/workflows/loc-badge-reusable.yml:111-120` already treats `SYNC_PAT` as optional and reports its presence with `::notice::`.

## Acceptance criteria

- A caller without `SYNC_PAT` finishes the run as success, with a warning annotation and a step-summary line naming the fix. No checkout with the token, chart fetch, commit or push runs.
- A caller with `SYNC_PAT` behaves exactly as now: it generates `docs/assets/star-history.svg` and commits it only when the file changed.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-star-history-helper.sh` passes with the updated contract assertions.
- `actionlint .github/workflows/star-history-reusable.yml` is clean.

## Verification

## Context

Found while setting up a managed Cloudron package repo: the repo owner added one fine-grained `SYNC_PAT` to all their package repos. A manually dispatched Star History run in a package repo then showed the with-token path; this issue changes only the without-token path.

   - `scratch_worktree_remove <path> <caller>` verifies that the lock reason is still this process's token, and that the worktree is clean, before unlocking and running a native non-force `git worktree remove`. It logs through `log_worktree_removal_event`. A mismatch or dirty state preserves the worktree.
   - `scratch_worktree_reap_stale <repo> <base_dir> <label>` reclaims only scratch worktrees that carry this helper's token, whose owner PID is gone, that are idle 30+ minutes, and that are clean.

3. Add `tests/test-worktree-add-register-interruption.sh`, modelled on `tests/test-worktree-fresh-base.sh`. Fault-inject a registration failure after `git worktree add`, then assert `REGISTRATION_FAILED`, the worktree is preserved, and no ownership row is recorded.

title: Cloudron publishing: document a repository protection baseline for package repos
body:
## What

Add a recommended repository protection baseline for Cloudron package repos to the publishing guidance, and show how to apply it.

## Why

`.agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-app-publishing-skill.md:199` says "Review protection, Actions permissions, package checks and credentials before enabling the variable" but gives no baseline. A package repo was published with no protection at all. The guide says published versions are append-only, yet nothing stopped a `v*` tag from being moved or deleted, or `main` from being force-pushed. On 2026-10-18 the owner applied two rulesets to seven package repos. Neither conflicts with the catalog workflow, which only fast-forwards `main` and creates new tags (`git push --atomic origin HEAD:main "v${VERSION}"`), nor with the metrics and Star History callers, which only fast-forward `main` (the metrics helper force-pushes only its own PR branch).

Applied baseline, both `enforcement: active` with no bypass actors:

1. Branch ruleset, `~DEFAULT_BRANCH`: `non_fast_forward`, `deletion`.
2. Tag ruleset, `refs/tags/v*`: `update`, `deletion`. Creation stays allowed because the publish job creates the tag with the job token.

Full PR gating (require pull request plus required checks) is a separate, optional step. It blocks the workflows' direct pushes to `main` unless the owner is a bypass actor and the pushes use owner PATs (`CLOUDRON_RELEASE_PAT`, `SYNC_PAT`). That bypass path is not yet verified with fine-grained PATs, so do not recommend it without testing.

## How

- `EDIT: .agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-app-publishing-skill.md:191-200`. After the publication-enable paragraph, add a short "Repository protection" paragraph with the two rulesets above, why each is compatible with the catalog workflow, and that PR gating needs bypass and PATs.
- Optional, if it fits the existing pattern: add a `protect` (or similarly named) subcommand to `.agents/scripts/cloudron-package-helper.sh` that prints or applies the two rulesets with `gh api -X POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/rulesets --input <file>`. It must refuse to create a duplicate when a ruleset with the same name exists, and must require an explicit flag to apply, because `.agents/scripts/commands/setup-git.md:158` says protection changes are a deliberate maintainer action. If adding the subcommand is not clean, keep this to documentation.

Reference: `marcusquinn/aidevops` itself has the tag ruleset "Protect aidevops release tags" (`refs/tags/v*`; creation, update, deletion; owner bypass). Package repos must not block tag creation, because the workflow, not the owner, creates their tags.

## Acceptance criteria

- The publishing skill names the two rulesets, the exact rule types and ref patterns, and why they are safe with the catalog, metrics and Star History workflows.
- PR gating is described as optional, with its bypass and PAT prerequisite stated as untested.
- If a helper subcommand is added: ShellCheck is clean, it is a dry run by default, and it is idempotent by ruleset name.

## Verification

- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh` (markdown, plus ShellCheck if the helper changes).
- If a helper is added: run it in dry-run mode against a package repo and confirm it prints both rulesets; with the apply flag on a repo that already has them, confirm it reports them as present instead of creating duplicates.
### Files Scope

- `.agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-app-publishing-skill.md`

body:
**Task ID:** `t18723` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `auto-dispatch` `bug`

## Outcome

fix(badges): derive owned repos from repos.json instead of hard-coded org allowlist

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`badges-check-helper.sh` and `badges-sync-helper.sh` classify registered repos as `EXTERNAL` (skipped by check and sync) whenever the slug's org is not in a hard-coded allowlist (`_DEFAULT_OWNED_ORGS`: three orgs) or `~/.config/aidevops/badge-orgs.conf`. Repos the user maintains in any other org are silently excluded from drift detection and sync, even when `repos.json` registers them with `maintainer` = the user and they carry an aidevops-managed badge block.

Observed: 28 registered repos in an org where the user is an active org admin (`gh api user/memberships/orgs/<org>` → `role: admin`) reported `EXTERNAL  badge block present` while their blocks were stale (inline languages chart, dead badges). They were only found by checking each README directly with `readme-badges-helper.sh check`.

## Why

Ownership should come from facts the framework already records, not a framework-shipped org list that every other user would also need to override. Hard-coded org names also don't belong in shared defaults.

## How

Locations: in `badges-check-helper.sh`, `_load_owned_orgs`, `_is_owned_org` and the `_is_external` classification (~line 188); in `badges-sync-helper.sh`, `_load_owned_orgs`/`_is_owned_org` (~lines 100–125) and the caller near line 533.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/badges-check-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/badges-sync-helper.sh`
- `.agents/aidevops/badges.md`

### Approach

Approach (reuse one shared function in both helpers):

1. A repo is owned when it is not `contributed: true`/`role: contributor` AND either (a) its `repos.json` `maintainer` equals the slug owner or the authenticated user, or (b) its org is listed in `badge-orgs.conf`.
2. Keep `badge-orgs.conf` as an additive override (append to derived ownership, do not replace it).
3. Replace the hard-coded default org list with the derived rule; keep no personal org names in shared code.
4. Update the header comments in both helpers and `aidevops/badges.md` if it documents the allowlist.

## Verification

- `shellcheck` both helpers.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-readme-badges-resilience.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-maintenance-repo-selection.sh` pass.
- With `badge-orgs.conf` absent, `badges-check-helper.sh --repo <org-repo maintained by the user>` reports CURRENT/DRIFTED, not EXTERNAL; a `contributed: true` entry still reports EXTERNAL.

## Context

Found during the fleet re-render for GH#35019 (PR #35021). Related: GH#35020 (worktree-safe sync and scheduled remediation) depends on correct ownership classification.

title: Cloudron package monitor: create the type:maintenance label before filing findings
body:
## What

Make `cloudron-package-monitor-helper.sh` ensure the `type:maintenance` label exists in the target package repository before it files a finding.

## Why

On 2026-10-18 `cloudron-package-monitor-helper.sh upstream --apply`, the command routine r916 runs, found a new upstream commit for a newly initialized package repo but did not file the issue:

```
could not add label: 'type:maintenance' not found
```

`_cloudron_monitor_create_issue` passes `--label "type:maintenance" --label "tier:standard" --label "auto-dispatch"` (`.agents/scripts/cloudron-package-monitor-helper.sh:436-437`). The `gh_create_issue` wrapper creates its own managed labels on demand (`status:*`, `origin:*`, `tier:*`, `auto-dispatch`), but nothing creates `type:maintenance`, and this helper is the only place in `.agents/scripts` that uses it. Older package repos happened to have the label; three of the owner's seven package repos did not. In those repos every upstream finding fails until someone creates the label by hand. After the label was created manually, the same command filed the finding at once.

## How

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/cloudron-package-monitor-helper.sh:394-444` (`_cloudron_monitor_create_issue`). Before calling the issue wrapper, ensure `type:maintenance` exists in `$slug`. Follow the read-first pattern in `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh:680-698` (`_gh_managed_label_names_snapshot` / `_gh_managed_label_snapshot_has`): read the label list once, and create the label only if it is missing (`gh label create "type:maintenance" --repo "$slug" --color ededed --description "Upstream or platform maintenance"`), using the wrapper's timeout helper if that is the established pattern there. Converged repos must stay read-only.
- If label creation fails, report it as an error naming the repo and label and return non-zero. Do not file the issue without the label silently.
- Check whether the helper's exit code reaches routine state when one package's issue creation fails while others succeed, and make sure a failed package write is not reported as overall success. Change this only if it currently reports success.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-package-monitor.sh`. That file already stubs the issue wrapper (`CLOUDRON_PACKAGE_ISSUE_WRAPPER`). Add a case where the label is missing and confirm the helper creates it before filing. The existing stubs make this the cheapest proof.

## Acceptance criteria

- In a repo without `type:maintenance`, `upstream --apply` creates the label and files the finding in the same run.
- In a repo that already has the label, no label write happens.
- A failed label creation fails that package's finding with a clear error and does not create an unlabelled issue.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-package-monitor.sh` passes; ShellCheck is clean.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-package-monitor.sh`
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/cloudron-package-monitor-helper.sh`
- `cloudron-package-monitor-helper.sh upstream` (dry run) still lists findings without writes.

title: t18724: fix(pulse): stop reassign_self/stampless-release churn on stale origin:interactive in-progress issues
body:
## Task


Stop the assign/unassign loop between two normalization passes. It holds an
`origin:interactive` issue left at `status:in-progress` with no live worker and
no interactive stamp. The issue is never dispatched again, and its draft-PR
checkpoint is never resumed.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Stop the assign/unassign loop between two normalization passes. It holds an
`origin:interactive` issue left at `status:in-progress` with no live worker and
no interactive stamp. The issue is never dispatched again, and its draft-PR
checkpoint is never resumed.

## Why (observed 2026-10-18, v3.39.43, three runners on one managed private repo)

- One issue (`origin:interactive`, `auto-dispatch`, `status:in-progress`) has
  had 28 assign/unassign events across three runners since 2026-10-11, about
  one per hour. There has been no DISPATCH_CLAIM or worker activity since the
  original worker's launch, and its draft PR has been idle for 7 days.
- Pass 1, `_normalize_reassign_self`
  (`.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`, about lines 675-726), assigns
  every `status:queued`/`status:in-progress` issue that has zero assignees to
  whichever runner is normalizing. It writes no claim stamp.
- Pass 2, `_normalize_unassign_stampless_interactive` (same file, about lines
  807-894), lists that runner's `origin:interactive` assignments older than the
  threshold with no stamp. For any status other than `status:in-review` it
  removes only the assignee (`gh issue edit --remove-assignee`) and leaves
  `status:in-progress` in place.
- On the next cycle, Pass 1 on any runner matches again. Log evidence:
  `Stampless interactive auto-release: unassigned <runner> from #N ... (>3600s old, no stamp)`.
  Between releases, dedup logs
  `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_SKIPPED: issue #N ... is assigned` and
  `DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=dedup_active_claim_unverified signal=ASSIGNED`.
- Knock-on effect: the wedged issue is also the footprint-overlap blocker for
  another available issue. That issue roots a 6-issue dependency chain.

## How (recommended; the worker may refine with evidence)

1. In `_normalize_reassign_self`, do not fabricate ownership. Skip issues where
   the stampless pass would immediately release this runner:
   `origin:interactive` issues with no interactive stamp for `runner_user`.
   More generally, skip issues with no live dispatch claim/lease for this
   runner.
2. In `_normalize_unassign_stampless_interactive`, when releasing a stampless
   `status:in-progress`/`status:queued` claim, also reset the lifecycle state
   with `set_issue_status ... "available" --remove-assignee`, as the
   `status:in-review` branch already does. Then dispatch dedup / the
   draft-checkpoint continuation path owns the next step instead of the
   reassign pass.
3. Keep the t1996 multi-runner guard and every existing trust and stamp check.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-reconcile.sh`

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-reconcile.sh`: three failures
  pre-exist on `main` (tracked separately in GH#34937); do not add new ones.
- Add one focused case. Input: an `origin:interactive` + `status:in-progress`
  issue with no assignee and no stamp. Expected: `reassign_self` does not
  assign it. Expected: a stampless aged release resets it to
  `status:available`.
- Live check after deploy: in `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`, no repeated
  `Stampless interactive auto-release: unassigned` lines for the same issue
  across cycles.

</details>

title: t18725: fix(pulse): worker-reported runner_capability_unmet must feed the runner-local capability cooldown
body:
## Task


When a launched worker reports `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=runner_capability_unmet`,
that runner should stop reclaiming the same unchanged task. A capable runner
should still be able to claim it. Today the same incapable runner relaunches
the task repeatedly. After that, a non-canonical reason string strands the
issue at `status:blocked`.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

When a launched worker reports `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=runner_capability_unmet`,
that runner should stop reclaiming the same unchanged task. A capable runner
should still be able to claim it. Today the same incapable runner relaunches
the task repeatedly. After that, a non-canonical reason string strands the
issue at `status:blocked`.

## Why (observed 2026-10-18, v3.39.41-v3.39.43, managed private repo)

- One code-fix issue received 8 `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked` comments from
  the same runner in 62 minutes (03:17-04:19Z). Each one carried
  `Terminal blocker: reason=runner_capability_unmet ... Projected state: status:available`
  with the same `terminal-blocker-observation revision=... blocker=...`
  fingerprint. Each was a full worker launch.
- The runner-local cooldown in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`
  (GH#33743, about lines 1018-1221) is recorded only from the pre-dispatch
  signal
  `DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=runner_capability_unmet signal=... cooldown=eligible`
  (`runner-capability-helper.sh`). A capability gap discovered by the worker
  after launch never feeds that cooldown.
- `terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` deliberately excludes `runner_capability_unmet`
  from circuit/backoff evidence (about lines 593 and 625), so nothing throttles
  this runner.
- A second runner then ended with the non-canonical line
  `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=verification_environment_missing_prerequisites`.
  The blocker was missing native host binaries needed by a repository test.
  The worker contract in `headless-runtime-lib.sh` (about lines 1066-1079)
  classes this as `runner_capability_unmet`. It was recorded as `unknown`
  with projected `status:blocked`, so no runner retries it.
- Impact: this one issue is the root of an 89-issue dependency chain. A
  different runner platform skips the failing host-specific test and could
  complete the task.

## How (recommended)

1. Record the existing runner-local capability cooldown from a trusted
   terminal-blocker observation. Conditions: the latest observation is
   `runner_capability_unmet`, it was posted by this runner's own login, and
   its task revision is unchanged. Keying and TTL match the pre-dispatch
   cooldown. Other runners stay eligible, and no global label is applied.
2. Normalize unrecognized `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON` values that describe a
   missing local tool or environment prerequisite to
   `runner_capability_unmet`. Do this only if the existing classifier has an
   allowlist hook for aliases; otherwise record the gap in the PR and keep
   scope to step 1.
3. Preserve all trust-boundary checks (`#aidevops:trust-boundary`).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`

## Verification

- `shellcheck` on the changed scripts.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- Focused case: comments contain this runner's own
  `runner_capability_unmet` observation for the current revision. Expected:
  enumeration skips the issue for this runner and still offers it to a runner
  with a different login.
- Live check: in `pulse.log`, a `runner_capability_unmet cooldown recorded`
  line appears after a worker-reported capability release, and that runner
  makes no repeated launches of the same issue within the TTL.

</details>

Stop `Dispatch_max` from spending a full `dispatch_with_dedup` attempt every
cycle on `consolidated` issues the management-label gate will always reject.

<details>

## Task Brief

## What

Stop `Dispatch_max` from spending a full `dispatch_with_dedup` attempt every
cycle on `consolidated` issues the management-label gate will always reject.
Surface draft-checkpoint consolidated issues stranded in that state.

## Why (observed 2026-10-18, v3.39.43, managed private repo)

- Four `status:available` issues labelled `consolidated` are rejected every
  cycle with `Dispatch_max: #N (...) blocked:consolidated benign dispatch block`
  (40 times each in the current log window). Each attempt took 12-21s
  (`dispatch_with_dedup returned rc=1 ... elapsed_ms=12393..21439`), so about
  60-70s of the dispatch budget is lost per cycle. Worker utilization is often
  0-1 of 20 slots, and other candidates are deferred with
  `cycle budget ... below per-candidate floor`.
- The gate is `_has_consolidated_label`
  (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-commit-gates.sh`, about lines 479-497),
  called at `pulse-dispatch-core.sh` about line 384 after earlier stages have
  already run. It allows `consolidated` only with `auto-dispatch` and the body
  line `_Supersedes #N — this issue is the consolidated spec._`.
- Three of the four have the spec line but lost `auto-dispatch`. The runtime
  removed it about 15s before posting

  resumes or surfaces these, and closed-NOT_PLANNED successor logic (GH#34341)
  keeps dependents blocked behind them.

  canonical line.

title: Qualify provider-only inference containment using the existing worker egress contract
body:
# Qualify provider-only inference containment using the existing worker egress contract

**Status:** Held capability/design brief, prepared on 2026-10-18. The operator
approved preparing this brief only. Implementation, worker dispatch, backend
configuration, infrastructure provisioning and model/comparison execution are not
authorized. Keep this work separate from application enrichment policy.

## Goal and observed gap

Provide a reviewed, verifiable route for source-extraction inference that can
contact its selected model provider while remaining unable to retrieve external
source pages, reach private services, read evaluator material or escape its
per-invocation filesystem boundary.

An offline construction component has passed a real Linux deny-all-network jail
check. That proves construction isolation, not online inference containment. The
current session has `AIDEVOPS_WORKER_EGRESS_BACKEND` unset or empty. A tool-denied
runtime profile is not evidence of kernel/process-tree isolation, and fake-backend
fixtures are not deployable enforcing backends.

This is an observed qualification/configuration gap in this environment, not a
claim that the framework has no implementation anywhere.

## Deduplication and evidence

- Memory recall for provider-only inference containment returned no relevant
  lessons.
- A bounded GitHub search for egress issue titles found the prior closed task:
  https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/27056

title: UI guidance: forms default to field names as placeholders (unless specified), lighter than typed text
body:
## What

Add a default form rule to the framework's UI guidance: **typed form fields show the field's name as their placeholder, unless the project's DESIGN.md or the task specifies otherwise.** Pair it with the colour rule that makes this safe: a placeholder is visibly lighter than typed text and still meets 4.5:1 against the field.

Rule text to add (adapt wording to each file's style):

- Text, email, phone, message (textarea) and each part of a name field use the field's name as placeholder text by default. Keep the visible label above the field: the placeholder never replaces it. Leave "(optional)" and required markers out of the placeholder ("Approximate budget", not "Approximate budget (optional)").
- Use a format hint instead of the name where it helps more ("https://" for a URL, "Search services" for a searchable multi-select, an example date format). Selects keep their own empty-choice text.
- Placeholder colour: lighter than typed text so an empty field never looks filled in, and at least 4.5:1 against the field background in light and dark modes. A palette-relative pattern that works for both: the input's text colour mixed about 75% towards the field background (`color-mix(in srgb, <text> 75%, <field>)`), with the plain text colour as the fallback for browsers without `color-mix()`. Never give placeholders the typed text's own colour, and do not start from a decorative/muted token that already fails 4.5:1.
- Record the project's choice (default, or an exception) in DESIGN.md's components/forms section.

## Why

Owner preference across projects, stated during a site design pass (2026-10-18): forms should show field names as placeholder text where relevant unless specified. Without a framework default, each project's agents leave placeholders empty or invent per-form text, and the preference has to be restated per project.

Observed pitfall when applying it: a theme-integration rule gave placeholders the input's own text colour, so every empty field looked filled in. Measured on Kadence palettes: typed text 11.99:1 (light) / 15.62:1 (dark) and placeholder identical; after mixing the text 75% towards the field, the placeholder was 5.52:1 light and 9.31:1 dark (Chromium and WebKit agree). Public fix and evidence: wpallstars/seoprostack#844 (PR #846). Kadence's default palette 6 placeholder alone is 4.02:1 on white, below WCAG AA.

## How / Files

- `.agents/product/ui-design.md` — add a short "Forms" subsection under "Design System Foundation" (after "Typography" or "Spacing and Layout") with the rule above; add one Accessibility Checklist item: "Placeholders are lighter than typed text and at least 4.5:1; labels stay visible."
- `.agents/tools/design/design-md.md` — in "Creating a DESIGN.md" (the `buttons_and_forms` → §7 Components mapping, around line 258) note that §7 records the form placeholder policy (field names by default, exceptions) and the placeholder colour token/derivation; in "Evolving an existing DESIGN.md during UI work" (around line 82) nothing new is needed unless wording conflicts.
- Optional, only if it shows inputs without placeholders: `.agents/tools/design/library/_template/preview.html.template` (Components section near line 599) so the preview input example shows a placeholder beside a typed value.
- Do not edit `AGENTS.md` or `prompts/build.txt` (size ratchet); this is progressive-disclosure guidance.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/product/ui-design.md`
- `.agents/tools/design/design-md.md`

## Acceptance

- `product/ui-design.md` states the default (field names as placeholders unless specified), the visible-label rule, format-hint exceptions and the placeholder colour rule with the 4.5:1 floor.
- `tools/design/design-md.md` tells agents to record the placeholder policy and colour in DESIGN.md §7.
- No contradiction with existing accessibility guidance (labels remain required; placeholder is never the only label).

## Verification

- `markdownlint-cli2` on the changed Markdown files.
- The repository's agent-doc checks (progressive-disclosure / size ratchet) pass unchanged.
- `rg -n -i "placeholder" .agents/product/ui-design.md .agents/tools/design/design-md.md` shows the new rule in both files.

title: t18729: feat(dispatch): per-repository cost budget override for the cost circuit breaker
body:
**Task ID:** `t18729` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `feat` `priority:high`

## Outcome

feat(dispatch): per-repository cost budget override for the cost circuit breaker

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## Origin

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

- Created 2026-10-18 by an interactive OpenCode session at a maintainer's request. A managed project repository needs a larger per-issue worker budget than the install default.

## What

Let a managed repository override the per-issue cost circuit breaker budgets (t2007) with a committed `.aidevops/dispatch-cost-budgets.conf` in its own checkout. Repositories without the file keep the install-wide budgets from `.agents/configs/dispatch-cost-budgets.conf`.

## Why

- `_get_cost_budget_for_tier` reads only the deployed framework config, so the 800K budget applies to every repository on a runner. A repository whose phases need several roughly 300K-token sessions trips the breaker after two sessions, and its continuation splits then multiply fixed per-part costs.
- Editing the deployed `~/.aidevops/agents/configs/` copy is lost on `aidevops update` and does not reach other maintainers' runners. A committed repository file is versioned, reviewed through that repository's PRs and identical on every runner.

## How

1. `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-cost.sh`:
   - `_get_cost_budget_for_tier <tier> [repo_slug]`. After loading the framework config, resolve the slug's checkout from `repos.json` (`initialized_repos[].path`, honour `AIDEVOPS_REPOS_FILE`, follow `_dsi_repo_path_for_slug` in `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`) and read `<path>/.aidevops/dispatch-cost-budgets.conf` when present.
   - Never `source` the repository file. Parse only `^COST_BUDGET_(SIMPLE|STANDARD|THINKING|DEFAULT)=[0-9]+$` lines; ignore everything else.
   - Clamp accepted values to 100000–20000000 so a typo cannot disable or zero the breaker.
   - `_check_cost_budget` passes its `repo_slug`.
2. `.agents/configs/dispatch-cost-budgets.conf`: document the override, its parsing rules and the clamp. Also correct the stale header comment, which still says the breaker applies `needs-maintainer-review`; it applies `status:blocked`.
3. `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cost-circuit-breaker.sh`: add assertions with a fixture `repos.json` and repository file. A repository budget of 2000000 allows 900K spend; a repository without the file still blocks at 800K; a line containing a command (`COST_BUDGET_STANDARD=1; touch <marker>`) is ignored and never executed.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-cost-circuit-breaker.sh` passes, including the new override assertions.
- [ ] ShellCheck reports no findings for the changed scripts.
- [ ] Repositories without the file see unchanged budgets.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-cost.sh
- .agents/configs/dispatch-cost-budgets.conf
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-cost-circuit-breaker.sh

title: planning-publisher: publication reverted TODO.md lines already on its base (t18504 regression)
body:
## What

A planning publication silently reverted TODO.md lines that were already on its base commit. t18504 (GH#32714, PR #33047) added a 3-way merge to stop this, but it happened again on 2026-10-18.

## Evidence

- `44e2863135` (planning publication, 15:04Z) marked `t18720` done (`pr:#35021 completed:2026-10-18`) and added `t18723` (GH#35032).
- PR #35048 (`planning/a06775cbc835-plan-add-t18727-t18728-pre-existing-test-failure`, author marcusquinn, labels `origin:interactive`, `allow-auto-merge`) has a single commit `b92c85d528`, whose parent is `a855452528` (15:23Z).
- `git merge-base --is-ancestor 44e2863135 a855452528` → ancestor. So the base already contained both lines.
- `git show b92c85d528 -- TODO.md` nevertheless shows:
  - `t18720` reverted from `[x] ... pr:#35021 completed:2026-10-18` to `[ ]`
  - `t18723` line deleted
  - `t18727`, `t18728` added (the intended change)
- PR file stats: `TODO.md +5 -2`. The `-2` are the clobbered lines.

So the publisher produced TODO.md from a stale copy (likely the canonical checkout's TODO.md, which predated `44e2863135`) and committed it as a whole-file replacement on a fresher base, rather than 3-way merging the intended delta.

Repaired by hand in PR #35061 (restores both lines).

## How

1. Find the code path that built #35048's commit: `planning-commit-helper.sh` and the planning publisher used by `claim-task-id.sh` / TODO add flows (branch prefix `planning/<hash>-plan-...`, trailer `Planning-Publication-ID`).
2. Confirm where the TODO.md content comes from (canonical working copy vs. `origin/main` blob) and whether the t18504 3-way merge (`base` = blob the edit was made against, `ours` = edited file, `theirs` = current `origin/main`) runs on this path. The likely gap: the merge base is taken as the publication base instead of the version the edit was made from, which turns a stale snapshot into a revert.
3. Fix so that only the intended delta lands; refuse to publish if the result removes or un-completes task lines not named in the publication.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/planning-publisher.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-todo-commit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-planning-publisher.sh` (extend the t18504 regression case)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Reproduction: edit TODO.md from a snapshot older than `origin/main`, where `origin/main` has since completed one task and added another; publish a new task line. Resulting commit adds only the new line; it does not revert either upstream change.
- A publication whose diff would delete or un-complete task lines it did not name fails closed with a clear message.

## Context

Found while restoring planning state for t18723/t18730 (aidevops PR #35061).

title: release-lane-helper: report GitHub rate-limit 403 as quota exhaustion, not 'Cannot verify repository release lane'
body:
## Observed

`aidevops release reconcile <source-PR>` failed with:

```
RELEASE_LANE_WRITE step=lane-head status=403 retryable=false
Cannot verify repository release lane
```

At the same moment `gh api rate_limit` reported `core.remaining: 0`, the gh-cooldown guard printed `primary-core active=true retry_at=<epoch>`, and `gh auth status` misreported the keyring token as invalid. After the reset, the same command succeeded unchanged: it queued publication and then published v3.39.45. Nothing was wrong with auth or the lane. The diagnostic pointed the operator at repository access instead of quota.

## Cause

`_release_lane_remote_head` in `.agents/scripts/release-lane-helper.sh` (around lines 108-137) maps every non-404, non-5xx status to `retryable=false` and a fatal "Cannot verify" message. GitHub returns 403 (or 429) for primary and secondary rate limits, so quota exhaustion looks identical to a permission failure. `_release_lane_api` (around lines 89-106) has the same classification.

## Proposed fix

- Before emitting the fatal message for 403/429, check whether the failure is a rate limit: the gh-cooldown state is active, the response says "rate limit", or `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`. If it is, print a distinct line such as `RELEASE_LANE_WRITE step=lane-head status=403 rate_limited=true retry_after=<epoch>`, followed by "GitHub API quota exhausted; rerun after <time>". Exit with a distinct code so callers and agents do not treat it as an auth or lane fault.
- Do not add automatic retry loops. Fail closed, but with the correct cause, consistent with the comment-storm and rate-limit invariants.
- Keep never forwarding response bodies, as today.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/release-lane-helper.sh`: `_release_lane_remote_head` and `_release_lane_api`.
- Possibly `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-helper.sh` around line 631, where "Cannot verify repository release lane" is printed for the reconcile path.
- Reference pattern: the existing gh-cooldown detection used by the shared gh wrappers (`shared-gh-wrappers*.sh`).

## Verification

- With a stubbed `gh` that returns a 403 rate-limit response (or an active cooldown marker), reconcile prints the rate-limited diagnostic and the new exit code, not "Cannot verify repository release lane".
- A genuine 403 permission failure still prints the existing fatal message with `retryable=false`.
- Run ShellCheck on the changed scripts.

title: Converge legacy recovery and new producers on verified compact archives
body:
## Objective

Converge legacy full recovery copies and all new recovery producers on the existing compact archive mechanism. Rootless operation must use saved managed-lifetime evidence, not privileged CWD inspection. This is a parent implementation objective, not an executable worker brief; it remains open until every acceptance criterion has verified evidence.

## Confirmed context

- The current compact helper preserves Git bundles, staged/unstaged changes and untracked files; its default contract excludes ignored files and does not preserve all legacy Git administration.
- `archive_worktree_path_recoverably` still creates full recovery buckets. `_clean_archive_worktree_recoverably` in `worktree-clean-lib.sh` uses it, as do other producers.
- Saved generation/source-inode/cgroup completion proof is already accepted by both `worktree_removal_guard` and `_worktree_recovery_plan_process_state` under degraded CWD visibility. Kernel-level EACCES alone is not the missing feature.
- The guidance/documentation correction is tracked separately in #35076 and PR #35077. It does not deliver this objective.
- An additive tar preservation prototype was rejected before publication: it would introduce a third representation and retain all originals, increasing storage rather than completing convergence.

## Implementation boundaries

Investigate and modify the narrow owning components:

- `.agents/scripts/worktree-archive-helper.sh`, `worktree_archive_snapshot.py`, `worktree_archive_filesystem.py` and `worktree_lifetime_archive.py`: extend or reuse the existing compact contract for supported legacy data, independent restoration and exact verification. Do not silently discard ignored files, unfinished admin state or reflog/index-only objects.
- `.agents/scripts/audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh` and `worktree-clean-lib.sh`: central producer and removal integration; preserve lease, identity, late-write, Git-lock and managed-lifetime checks. Native removal must remain the final mutation path for registered worktrees.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-recovery-lifecycle-helper.sh`, `worktree-recovery-apply-helper.sh`, `worktree-recovery-maintenance-helper.sh` and `worktree_recovery_archive_copy.py`: migrate existing buckets through an explicit recoverable transition without orphaning reservations, lifecycle evidence or retention journals.
- Search exact calls to `archive_worktree_path_recoverably` for remaining producers, including profile and scratch-worktree paths. Do not assume one cleanup caller covers all producers.
- Update `reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md`, `reference/worktree-cwd-visibility.md` and `scripts/worktree-archive-helper.md` in the implementation PRs.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A single supported archival mechanism handles newly produced recovery evidence; ordinary operation no longer accumulates parallel full recovery copies. Unsupported input stays protected with a precise reason, not an unverified lossy conversion.
2. Legacy migration preserves unique ignored/untracked contents, staged state, relevant Git administrative/history dependencies and supported filesystem metadata. Incomplete buckets remain explicitly incomplete.
3. Every replacement binds an exact source identity to a durable independently restored and compared archive. Interruption and retry cannot duplicate captures or remove an unverified source.
4. Rootless cleanup uses validated existing lifetime receipts where available. Positive CWD matches, active ownership, source drift and missing/invalid receipts still block their unsafe paths. No sudo, service shutdown or fabricated enrollment is a remediation.
5. Retention/expiry is distinct from migration. Do not treat age, size, path naming or success exit codes as authority to discard unique data.
6. Existing archive/lifecycle/removal regression suites cover the changed paths, with focused additions only where needed for migration safety. Verify the actual CLI path and independent restoration, not just mocks.
7. Report measured source/archive bytes and separately state whether any source was retired. Merging code is not evidence that deployment or local disk reclamation occurred.

## Execution and safety

The originating interactive session owns implementation. Keep this parent non-dispatchable; decompose into bounded implementation units only after the preservation/removal contract is established. Initial local work authorized inventory without deleting data. Do not infer blanket permission for destructive legacy cleanup from a request to merge code. Public discussion must use generic paths and omit installation-specific repository names or contents.

## Children

Proposed decomposition filed from GH#35099. All four children are held (`no-auto-dispatch`, `status:blocked`) because the originating interactive session owns implementation (see Execution and safety). That owner can accept them by restoring `auto-dispatch` on #35109, or revise or close them. Each child maps to the acceptance criteria above. Children 2 and 3 are blocked by child 1, and child 4 is blocked by child 3 (native GitHub blocked-by relationships).

- #35109 — t18737: preserve Git administrative state and reflog-only history in compact archives (preservation contract; criteria 2, 6)
- #35110 — t18738: converge every `archive_worktree_path_recoverably` producer on verified compact archives (criteria 1, 3, 4, 6)
- #35111 — t18739: migrate legacy full recovery buckets into verified compact archives with durable receipts, no retirement (criteria 2, 3, 5, 7)
- #35112 — t18740: retire migrated buckets only through a re-verified, interruption-safe, operator-confirmed transition (criteria 3, 4, 5, 7)

Prerequisite already merged: PR #35082 (`--include-ignored` capture). The parent-task label and the needs-decomposition close contract stay, so the parent cannot auto-close before its criteria have verified evidence. Running migration or retirement on an installed store is still an operator decision. These children do not authorize it.
