title: feat: session-attachments-helper.sh exports pasted OpenCode images on demand; document session DB locations
body:
## What

Add an on-demand helper that exports images pasted into an OpenCode session to files, so they can be handed to another session, a worker or a tool. Exports are pruned after 60 days. Also document every place OpenCode session data lives.

## Why

Pasted screenshots are stored only inline in the session database (`part.data` JSON: `{"type":"file","mime":"image/png","filename":"clipboard","url":"data:image/png;base64,..."}`), so neither the model nor the user has a path to them. Finding them took several wrong turns, because aidevops-launched sessions do not use the shared database:

- Current session: `$XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/opencode.db`. aidevops launches set `XDG_DATA_HOME` to a per-project folder, `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/work/opencode-interactive/<project-…>/` (`opencode-launcher-helper.sh`).
- Shared/legacy: `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`.
- Archived sessions: `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode-archive.db` (`opencode-db-archive.sh`).
- `AGENTS.md` and `reference/memory-lookup.md` name only the shared path.

Writing every pasted image to disk was rejected: sessions stay open or are reopened for weeks, so automatic copies would need a long retention for an occasional need. On-demand export keeps disk use proportional to actual use.

## How

- New `.agents/scripts/session-attachments-helper.sh`:
  - `locations`: the databases searched, in order, and whether each exists.
  - `sessions [--days N] [--title TEXT]`: recent sessions with title, database and image count.
  - `list <session-id|latest>`: images per message (time, message, position, type, size); `latest` = most recently updated session in the current database.
  - `export <session-id|latest> [--message ID | --last] [--out DIR]`: decode to files (dir 0700, files 0600), named `<UTC time>-<message>-<n>.<ext>` so `n` matches "Image N" in that message; prints the paths; skips files already exported; then prunes old exports.
  - `cleanup [--days N] [--dry-run]`: removes export folders untouched for 60 days (`AIDEVOPS_SESSION_ATTACHMENTS_RETENTION_DAYS`).
  - Read-only database access (`file:…?mode=ro` URI; plain `-readonly` fails on WAL databases), ID validation before SQL, indexed lookups by session ID only (the shared database can be tens of GB).
- Reference pattern: `opencode-db-inventory-lib.sh` (fixed-depth isolated-DB inventory), `session-introspect-helper.sh` (sqlite3 helper style).
- Docs: `AGENTS.md` Runtime References session-DB line; `reference/memory-lookup.md` item 5 gets the locations and the helper.

## Verification

- `shellcheck` clean; Bash 3.2 compatible.
- `export latest --last` from a live session with pasted images writes byte-identical PNGs (compare with Python base64 decode of the same part); re-running skips them.
- `cleanup --dry-run --days 0` lists the export folder; `cleanup --days 0` removes it.

title: fix(auto-update): squash-merged worktree hotfix deploys and plugin-only fixes never redeploy at same VERSION
body:
## Problem

`_cmd_check_stale_agent_redeploy` in `.agents/scripts/auto-update-helper.sh` (around lines 607-692) has two gaps that keep a runtime stale while VERSION is unchanged:

1. **A worktree deploy that is later squash-merged stays pinned until the next release.** A hotfix deployed from an interactive linked worktree with `setup.sh --non-interactive` writes the worktree commit to `~/.aidevops/.deployed-sha`. After a squash merge, that commit is not an ancestor of canonical `main`. The "diverged history" guard then skips the redeploy on every poll. The runtime gets no same-version fixes until VERSION changes.
2. **Plugin-only fixes are not detected.** The drift path filter lists `.agents/scripts/ .agents/agents/ .agents/workflows/ .agents/prompts/ .agents/hooks/ setup.sh .agents/scripts/setup/modules/ aidevops.sh`. It leaves out `.agents/plugins/`. A fix that touches only an OpenCode plugin file, such as `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-recovery-data.mjs` from GH#35462, never triggers a same-version redeploy.

## Reproducer

Observed after GH#35462 / PR #35464. The fix was deployed from the worktree commit `f308dd1`, then amended and squash-merged as `f3f5b8b`.

**Symptom command:** `tail -n 15 ~/.aidevops/logs/auto-update.log`

**Actual output** (repeats on every 10-minute poll):

```text
[INFO] Version matches upstream (v3.39.57); verifying commit freshness
Fast-forwarded canonical main to origin/main
[WARN] Skipping script-drift redeploy: deployed runtime f308dd1 diverges from canonical HEAD f3f5b8b
```

**Expected:** the hotfix content is already in `f3f5b8b`, so the runtime should redeploy from canonical `main`.

## Proposed fix

- **Diverged case:** before skipping, check whether the deployed hotfix has landed. Let `base=$(git merge-base deployed head)`. For each deploy-affecting path in `git diff --name-only base deployed`, compare `git rev-parse deployed:<path>` with `head:<path>`. If they all match, the hotfix is contained in `head`, so treat this as normal stale drift and redeploy (debounce still applies). Otherwise keep the current skip.
- **Path filter:** add `.agents/plugins/` to the list. Check whether other deployed runtime trees (for example `.agents/configs/`) are also missing, and add any that are.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/auto-update-helper.sh`

The change is in `_cmd_check_stale_agent_redeploy`. Reference pattern: the existing `merge-base --is-ancestor` branches in the same function.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/auto-update-helper.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-auto-update-health-check.sh`
- Manual check: deploy from a worktree commit, squash-merge an identical change to `main`, then run the auto-update check once. The log should show a redeploy, not `diverges`.

title: fix(tabby): failed-restore resume hint should work for renamed project folders
body:
## Problem

GH#35462 added `keep_tabby_tab_open` in `.agents/scripts/opencode-launcher-helper.sh`. When Tabby session recovery fails, it keeps the tab open and prints this hint:

```text
Saved session: ses_... (resume in its project with: aidevops opencode --session ses_...)
```

That command can't find the session in two cases:

- **Renamed project folder.** The isolated data directory is named from the original path (`build_project_session_id`). After a rename, the old data directory `project-<old-name>-<cksum>` still holds the session, but running `aidevops opencode --session` from the renamed folder opens a different, empty data directory.
- **Recovery not run.** The plain command in a project folder doesn't go through Tabby recovery, so it never reads the marker's `data_dir`.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** rename a project folder, then run `aidevops opencode --session <session-id>` from the new folder.

**Actual output:** OpenCode opens with a new data directory, `project-<new-name>-<cksum>`, which does not contain the session. The session is in `opencode-interactive/project-<old-name>-<cksum>`, as recorded in its marker `opencode-tabby-recovery/<session-id>/recovery.json`.

**Working command (verified in GH#35462):** `cd ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/work/opencode-tabby-recovery/<session-id> && aidevops opencode --tabby-shell`

## Proposed fix

In `keep_tabby_tab_open`, when `invocation_dir` is a recovery marker directory:

- Print the working command above, using the real marker path.
- Also print why recovery failed. Capture the resolver's stderr instead of discarding it, so the user knows whether retrying can help.
- Optionally, when `recovery.json` parses, also print its `directory` and `data_dir` so a manual resume is possible: `cd <directory> && XDG_DATA_HOME=<data_dir> AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_ISOLATED_DB=1 opencode --session <id>`.

Keep the output short and send it to stderr. Never `exec` anything other than the resolved login shell.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-launcher-helper.sh`

Reference pattern: `keep_tabby_tab_open` and `resolve_tabby_recovery` in the same file. The marker schema is in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-recovery-marker.mjs` (`writeSessionRecoveryMarker`).

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/opencode-launcher-helper.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-launcher-helper.sh` (all pass)
- Manual check: temporarily make a marker fail to resolve, for example by pointing `data_dir` at a missing directory in a copied marker. Open a tab with `--tabby-shell` from that marker directory. The tab should stay open and print a working resume command.

title: t18761: cert-watch: Certificate Transparency + CAA routine filing issues in each site...
body:
**Task ID:** `t18761` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `auto-dispatch` `security`

## Outcome

cert-watch: Certificate Transparency + CAA routine filing issues in each site's private repo

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `certificate transparency CAA monitoring` → 0 hits
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 open/merged PRs for CT or CAA monitoring. `crt.sh` is already in `.agents/configs/allowed-urls.txt:247`. CAA appears only as a record type in `services/hosting/dns-providers.md`.
- [x] File refs verified: 6 refs checked, all present at HEAD (`85938e7209`)
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — new helper plus core routine registration; data sources, routing and safety rules are decided below
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — new helper; the contract is in the brief

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-23
- **Session:** opencode:unknown-2026-10-23
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Parent context:** follow-up to the eMudhra CA compromise response (t18748, GH#35277). The maintainer asked for an aidevops routine that watches certificate issuance and CAA for the domains they operate, and that files issues in the relevant private repos when it finds problems.
- **Why:** trust-store checks (`tls-trust`) only protect clients after a distrust is announced. The direct risk from a compromised or misbehaving CA is a certificate issued for *our* domains. Certificate Transparency logs show those issuances within hours, often before an incident is public. CAA limits which honest CAs may issue at all.

## What

### 1. New helper `.agents/scripts/cert-watch-helper.sh`

It sources `shared-constants.sh`, uses explicit `return 0/1` and `local var="$1"`, and is Bash 3.2 compatible. It defaults to a read-only dry run.

- **`domains [--format text|json]`:** build the monitored set of registrable domains (apexes). Each apex records the hostnames that came from it. Sources, in order:
  1. `~/.config/aidevops/site-inventory.json`: each site's `canonical_hostname` and `aliases`.
  2. The Hostinger fleet inventory under `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/work/hostinger-fleet/` (`hostinger-helper.sh fleet`), when present.
  3. `~/.config/aidevops/repos.json`: slugs whose repo name is a domain (`<owner>/<domain>`, the fleet naming in `services/hosting/hostinger.md` "Plan and drift").
  4. `extra_domains` and `ignore` from the optional config `~/.config/aidevops/cert-watch.json`, which must be a regular 0600 file. Ship the template as `.agents/configs/cert-watch.json.txt`.

  Skip missing sources with an INFO line.

- **`ct [--domain D]`:** for each apex, query `https://crt.sh/?q=%25.<apex>&output=json&exclude=expired`. Space requests at least 2 s apart and allow 30 s per request. Keep per-apex state (seen certificate ids, issuer org, `not_before`, SANs) in a 0600 JSON state file under `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/work/cert-watch/`.
  - **First run:** record a baseline and report no findings.
  - **Fetch errors:** crt.sh is often slow or returns 502. A failed fetch is `UNKNOWN` for that apex. It must never be read as "no certificates" and never erases state.
  - Findings for certificates not seen before:
    - **`ct-unexpected-issuer` (high):** the issuer org is not in the apex's expected set. The expected set is the CAA-permitted issuers if CAA exists, otherwise issuers seen for that apex in the last 180 days of state, plus config `expected_issuers`.
    - **`ct-distrusted-issuer` (critical):** the issuer matches `.agents/configs/cert-watch-distrusted-issuers.conf` (one issuer CN/org substring per line). Seed it with the eMudhra intermediates named in `.agents/advisories/emudhra-ca-compromise-2026-10.advisory`.
    - **`ct-unknown-hostname` (medium):** a SAN under the apex that matches no known hostname or alias and no wildcard we already hold.

- **`caa [--domain D]`:** resolve CAA with `dig +short CAA`, walking up to the apex (RFC 8659 tree climbing). Findings:
  - **`caa-missing` (low):** no CAA anywhere up the tree. Include a recommended record set built from issuers observed over the last 180 days of CT state, plus an `iodef` suggestion.
  - **`caa-blocks-active-issuer` (high):** CAA exists but does not permit an issuer that issued a currently valid certificate for that apex. The next renewal will fail. This is common with Cloudflare Universal SSL and host auto-SSL, which may rotate between CAs.

  The helper **never writes DNS**. It only recommends; applying records is a human or DNS-agent decision through `dns-helper.sh`.

- **`run [--apply] [--format text|json]`:** runs `domains`, then `ct`, then `caa`. Without `--apply`, print the findings only. With `--apply`, file issues as described in section 2.

### 2. Issue routing (`run --apply`)

**Target repo per apex.** Use the first match:

1. `site_repos` in `~/.config/aidevops/hosting-fleet.json`.
2. The site's `knowledge_repo` in site-inventory.
3. The repos.json slug whose name equals the apex or one of its hostnames.
4. `fallback_repo` from `cert-watch.json`.

If nothing resolves, print the finding and do not file it.

**Privacy gate (`#aidevops:trust-boundary`).** Before filing, run `gh repo view <slug> --json visibility`.

- If the visibility is not `PRIVATE`, or the check fails, file in `fallback_repo` instead, and only if that repo is itself verified `PRIVATE`.
- Domain names, client names and certificate details never go into a public repo. In particular they never go into `marcusquinn/aidevops`.

**Filing.** Create issues only through `gh_create_issue` (see the existing pattern in `.agents/scripts/cloudron-package-monitor-helper.sh:393-500`).

- **Body marker:** `<!-- aidevops:generator=cert-watch apex=<apex> finding=<kind> key=<crt.sh id or CAA hash> -->`.
- **Labels:** `security` and `source:cert-watch`; `priority:high` for high findings, `priority:critical` for critical ones. No `auto-dispatch`: these are operator triage, because confirming a certificate is ours or changing DNS needs owner authority.
- **Body content:** apex, hostnames, cert id with a crt.sh link built from the id, issuer, `not_before`/`not_after`, SANs, why it was flagged, and the next steps. For a certificate that isn't ours: revoke it through the issuing CA, review DNS/registrar access, add or tighten CAA. For CAA findings: the exact recommended records plus `dns-helper.sh` usage.

**Dedup.** Skip a finding if an open issue in the target repo already carries the same marker. A `caa-missing` finding that is still present stays on its single open issue; never file it twice.

### 3. Core routine and CLI

- **Routine.** Add the next free core routine id (r923 at time of writing) to `get_core_routine_entries` in `.agents/scripts/routines/core-routines.sh`:
  `r923|x|Cert watch — CT issuance and CAA audit for operated domains|repeat:daily(@06:40)|~3m|scripts/cert-watch-helper.sh run --apply|script`
- **Description.** Add `describe_r923` following `describe_r921` (overview, schedule table, safety rails, pulse diagnostics).
- **CLI.** Add `aidevops security cert-watch [args]` dispatch in `aidevops.sh` `_cmd_security`, defaulting to `run` (dry run).
- **Doc.** Add `.agents/tools/security/cert-watch.md`: sources, config keys, finding kinds and severities, routing order, privacy gate, and how to triage an unexpected certificate.

## Integration scope evidence

The certificate monitor introduces a private-repository trust boundary and persistent baseline state. Add a standalone standard-library Python regression check at `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cert-watch-helper.py` to verify actual helper execution with isolated HOME and local command fixtures: no public writes, repeat filing dedup, baseline and UNKNOWN state preservation, CAA inheritance and wildcard handling. No new runner, dependency or CI gate. This adjacent verification file was absent at implementation start; collision discovery found no existing implementation. Verify with `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-cert-watch-helper.py`.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** Data sources, finding kinds, routing order, privacy gate and routine registration are all specified, and each has a verified in-repo pattern → tier:standard.

## How

- Issue filing, dedup and label-ensure pattern: `.agents/scripts/cloudron-package-monitor-helper.sh:370-500`.
- Core routine entry and description pattern: `.agents/scripts/routines/core-routines.sh:17-43` and `describe_r921` (around line 1040).
- Security subcommand dispatch: `aidevops.sh` `_cmd_security`. See how `tls-trust` was wired in PR #35282.
- Inventory readers: `.agents/scripts/site-context-helper.sh` (site-inventory) and `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md` "Plan and drift" (fleet inventory, `hosting-fleet.json`).
- CAA background and record syntax: `.agents/services/hosting/dns-providers.md`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cert-watch-helper.py`
- `.agents/scripts/cert-watch-helper.sh`
- `.agents/configs/cert-watch.json.txt`
- `.agents/configs/cert-watch-distrusted-issuers.conf`
- `.agents/tools/security/cert-watch.md`
- `.agents/scripts/routines/core-routines.sh`
- `.agents/reference/routines.md`
- `aidevops.sh`

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/cert-watch-helper.sh
.agents/scripts/cert-watch-helper.sh domains --format json | jq -e 'length >= 0'
.agents/scripts/cert-watch-helper.sh caa --domain example.com        # dry run, no network writes
.agents/scripts/cert-watch-helper.sh run --format json | jq -e 'type == "array"'
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-routines-selector.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `run` (dry run) lists monitored apexes and findings and makes no GitHub writes. The first `ct` run per apex produces a baseline only.
- [ ] A crt.sh fetch failure yields `UNKNOWN` for that apex and leaves its stored state unchanged.
- [ ] `run --apply` files each finding once, in the resolved private repo, with the `generator=cert-watch` marker. A second run with the same findings creates no new issues.
- [ ] Negative: findings are never filed in a repo whose visibility is not verified `PRIVATE`.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "visibility"
    path: ".agents/scripts/cert-watch-helper.sh"
    expect: present
  ```

- [ ] Negative: the helper never changes DNS.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "dns-helper\\.sh (add|update|delete|set)"
    path: ".agents/scripts/cert-watch-helper.sh"
    expect: absent
  ```

- [ ] r923, or the next free id, appears in `get_core_routine_entries`, and `describe_r923` renders. Existing routine tests pass.
- [ ] `shellcheck` is clean, and `linters-local.sh --changed` passes.

## Non-goals

- Automatic DNS changes and automatic certificate revocation.
- Monitoring third-party domains we do not operate.
- Re-running `tls-trust` fleet probes. Those are covered by t18750; a follow-up may route their TRUSTED rows through the same issue router.

</details>

<summary>Brief workflow contract</summary>

## Brief Workflow

This issue body is composed under `.agents/workflows/brief.md`. Newly queued auto-dispatch work must pass its `Dispatch Readiness Contract (brief schema v2)`: complete write surface, hazards and compatibility, executable verification mapped to affected surfaces, and positive plus negative/regression acceptance criteria.

title: new-task-helper.sh batch writes TODO.md/briefs into canonical checkout and ignores --labels no-auto-dispatch
body:
## Observed

`new-task-helper.sh batch --labels "<label>,no-auto-dispatch" --title A --title B --title C --repo-path <canonical-checkout>` run from an interactive session (aidevops v3.39.57, OpenCode):

1. **Wrote into the canonical checkout.** It appended three `- [ ] tNNN ... ref:none` lines to the canonical `TODO.md` and created three untracked `todo/tasks/tNNN-brief.md` stubs in the canonical working tree. Interactive sessions must never edit canonical, and the shared command policy then blocks `git restore TODO.md` there, so the session cannot undo the helper's own writes without the audited `sync-mirror` route.
2. **Ignored `--labels` for the TODO tags.** Each line was tagged `#auto-dispatch` even though `no-auto-dispatch` was passed.
3. **No issue was created.** For every title, issue creation failed: "No --description provided and no brief file found", then "Files Scope requires owned author-side repair". The summary table was empty. Task IDs were claimed on the counter, so a retry would allocate fresh IDs.

## Expected

- Batch planning writes go through a linked worktree or a planning-only publication path (as `planning-commit-helper.sh` does), never the canonical working tree.
- `--labels no-auto-dispatch` maps to the `#no-auto-dispatch` TODO tag and suppresses the `#auto-dispatch` default.
- When the stub brief cannot compose an issue body, the summary still lists the allocated IDs and prints the exact recovery commands per ID.

## Workaround used

Allocated IDs were kept. TODO lines and full briefs were rewritten in a linked worktree; `issue-sync-helper.sh push tNNN` from that worktree then created each issue. The canonical leftovers remain until an authorized `canonical-recovery-helper.sh sync-mirror`.

## Files to inspect

- `.agents/scripts/new-task-helper.sh` (batch path: TODO append, brief stub, labels → tags)
- `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh` (bare-creation fallback when no brief)
- `.agents/scripts/commands/new-task.md` "Batch Mode" (docs promise one planning publication)

## Verification

Run batch with `--labels x,no-auto-dispatch --repo-path <canonical>` against a scratch repo: canonical `git status --short` stays empty; TODO lines carry `#no-auto-dispatch`; summary table lists IDs.

title: fix(worktree-cleanup): local-branch-cleanup transport worktrees leak and exhaust the dispatch worktree cap
body:
## What

`local-branch-cleanup-helper.sh` leaks its isolated deletion transport worktree (`<repo>-local-branch-cleanup-<pid>`) on every run that deletes a branch. The leaked transports count toward the dispatch worktree cap (`_dispatch_worktree_capacity_gate`, cap 200), so a busy managed repo hits the cap and **all** issue dispatch for that repo is fail-closed.

## Evidence (observed 2026-10-23 by supervisor pulse)

- Pulse log: `Live worktree count 210 >= cap 200 for #<N> in <managed-repo>; attempting guarded cleanup (timeout 60s)` followed by `Guarded capacity cleanup could not recover dispatch capacity ... 210 -> 210 worktrees (cap 200, cleanup_rc=124)` → `pre-launch failure stage=dispatch_with_dedup rc=1 reason=local_capacity_gate`. Every candidate in that repo is deferred.
- Worktree base dir for that repo: ~150 of 210 entries are `<repo>-local-branch-cleanup-<pid>` directories; ~60 were created in the last 24h. A second managed repo (aidevops) has 19 such transports.
- `cleanup_worktrees.log` never mentions any `local-branch-cleanup-*` path (not even as skipped) — the guarded cleanup does not consider detached transport worktrees at all.
- `worktree-managed-lifetime.py status <transport>` for a 2-day-old transport returns `"state": "running"`, `"manager": "owner-cgroup"`, launch `reason: "owner-descendant-evidence-unavailable"`, owner cgroup = the transient `aidevops-cleanup-worktrees-*.service` that has long since exited.

## Root cause (hypothesis, verify first)

`.agents/scripts/local-branch-cleanup-helper.sh` `prepare_transport()` (~line 252) creates the transport with `worktree_create_registered ... HEAD --detach --no-checkout`, registering it in the managed-lifetime registry with the *current* cleanup process/cgroup as owner. `cleanup_transport()` (~line 235) calls `worktree_managed_require_removal_proof` (`audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh` ~line 1547) while that owner is still alive, so proof fails, it prints `Transport retained pending managed completion proof` and returns 0. Nothing later reclaims the retained transport once the owner exits.

## How (worker-ready)

Files to modify:
- `.agents/scripts/local-branch-cleanup-helper.sh` — `prepare_transport` / `cleanup_transport`: make the transport removable by its own creator (e.g. create it unregistered/ephemeral, or seal/complete its managed-lifetime record before removal so self-owned proof passes), and add an EXIT trap so the transport is removed on every exit path.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-clean-lib.sh` and/or `.agents/scripts/cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh` — add a reclaim pass for retained `*-local-branch-cleanup-<pid>` detached, no-checkout transports whose owner PID/cgroup is gone (they hold no work: detached HEAD, no checkout), so the existing backlog is drained without manual intervention.
- Reference pattern: the GH#32913 prunable-metadata pass in `cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh` (`_missing_metadata_repo_paths` and friends) for a local, API-free per-repo reclaim loop.

Verification:
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-local-branch-cleanup-helper.sh` passes and asserts no `local-branch-cleanup-*` worktree remains registered after a run that deletes a branch.

title: bug(pulse-triage): oversized consolidation child body fails silently and loops across runners
body:
## What

`_create_consolidation_child_issue` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-triage-dispatch.sh:468-494` fails silently when the consolidation child body is larger than GitHub's 65,536-character issue body limit. Because `gh_create_issue` stderr goes to `/dev/null`, the only log line is `ERROR: consolidation child creation FAILED for #N`. Every pulse runner then re-acquires and releases the `consolidation-in-progress` lock on the same issue indefinitely. The parent keeps `needs-consolidation`, so it is never dispatched.

## Evidence (private managed repo, issue number withheld)

- The parent had a body of about 8k characters and 22 substantive comments totalling about 81k characters. `_compose_consolidation_child_body` (`pulse-triage-dispatch.sh:162-205`) inlines the body and every substantive comment verbatim, so the child body exceeded 65,536.
- Between 2026-10-20 and 2026-10-21, three runners added and removed `consolidation-in-progress` over 100 times on that issue.
- Local `pulse.log` shows `Consolidation lock: acquired by <runner> on #N`, followed straight away by `ERROR: consolidation child creation FAILED for #N`, repeated in multiple cycles.
- An interactive maintainer stopped the loop by hand: removed `needs-consolidation` and added `consolidated`, because the issue body already held an authoritative rewritten brief.

## Fix

1. In `_compose_consolidation_child_body`, bound the output below 65,536 characters. Keep the instructions and parent body. Truncate the oldest or longest substantive comments, and add a line listing the omitted comment IDs and URLs, so the worker can fetch only those.
2. In `_create_consolidation_child_issue`, capture stderr from `gh_create_issue` and log a sanitized first line, so `body is too long` shows up in `pulse.log`.
3. After a deterministic creation failure (body too long, validation error), post one idempotent comment on the parent. Then stop retrying until the parent body or comments change, so runners don't loop.

Reference pattern: the existing idempotent marker comments in `_post_consolidation_dispatch_comment` (`pulse-triage-dispatch.sh:503`).

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-triage-dispatch.sh`
- Extend the existing `.agents/scripts/tests/test-consolidation-dispatch.sh` with a case whose comments total more than 70k characters. Assert that the composed body is 65,536 characters or fewer and lists the omitted comment references.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-consolidation-dispatch.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-consolidation-multi-runner.sh` pass.

title: bug(worker-permissions): Task(playwright) denial under seo agent posts an unsignable permission request
body:
## What

A headless award-enrichment worker in a private managed repo needed `Task(playwright)` for a read-only visual transcription of public images. Two framework gaps make this a permanent block that a maintainer cannot clear:

1. **Agent allowlist:** the worker ran under the `seo` agent. Its `subagents:` list in `.agents/seo.md` (lines 5-45 and onward) does not include `playwright`, so the generated config denies `task:*` except the listed subagents. The worker reported: "Denied by the static seo-agent task allowlist (task:* deny; playwright not listed), not by a runtime prompt."
2. **Unsignable request:** the worker permission flow still posted an `aidevops-permission-request` for `permission: task, tool: task, pattern: playwright` with `sudo aidevops approve permissions issue ...` instructions. But `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/config-worker-permissions.mjs:11` limits grants to `PATTERN_CAPABLE_PERMISSIONS = {bash, external_directory}`, and line 127 rejects any other permission. A signed grant for `task` can never take effect, yet the request comment invites the maintainer to sign it.

## Fix

- Decide the routing: either add `playwright` to the `seo` agent's `subagents:` (it already lists site crawling and `pagespeed`), or route `dispatch-class:award-enrichment` work to an agent that already permits `Task(playwright)`. Record the choice in `reference/agent-routing.md`.
- In `.agents/scripts/worker-permission-helper.sh` (request path near lines 418-503), classify any request whose permission is not in the plugin's pattern-capable set as `permission_non_grantable`. Post the non-grantable blocker with the agent-allowlist cause instead of a sudo approval command. Keep the two sets in sync from a single source.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/worker-permission-helper.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-permission-helper.sh`, with a case added: a `task` permission request produces `permission_non_grantable` and no `sudo aidevops approve permissions` text.
- Regenerate the runtime config and confirm the chosen award-enrichment agent permits `task` → `playwright`.

title: t18763: worker write fence: name the accepted roots instead of redirecting every bloc...
body:
**Task ID:** `t18763` | **Status:** open
**Assignee:** @marcusquinn | **Started:** 2026-10-23
**Tags:** `bug` `priority:high` `interactive`

## Outcome

worker write fence: name the accepted roots instead of redirecting every block to the worktree

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief


## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-23
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Issue:** GH#35495
- **Parent context:** follow-up to GH#35139 (read-wide, write-narrow worker boundary), observed in a managed private repository's imports lane.

## What

Make the headless worker write fence name the roots it actually accepts. When a
worker Write/Edit/patch or mutating Git target falls outside both
`WORKER_WORKTREE_PATH` and the managed temp root, the block message must state
both allowed roots (resolved paths) and say that private or scratch artifacts
belong in an owner-only subdirectory of `AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR`. Keep the existing
"Sibling worktrees are read-only for workers" prefix so current callers and
tests keep matching.

## Why

The fence (GH#35139) accepts the worker worktree and `AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR`, but
its only message is "Sibling worktrees are read-only for workers. Copy what you
need into your own worktree." Any rejected target, including a private scratch
directory that is not a sibling worktree (for example the sensitive-temp root
`~/.aidevops-private/tmp`), is therefore redirected to the worktree.

Observed on 2026-10-23 in a managed private repository: an imports-batch worker
chose a private scratch directory outside `AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR`, the fence
rejected it and pointed to the worktree, and the repository CLI then correctly
refused the Git-ignored worktree cache because batch directories must be
outside Git repositories and inside `AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR`. The worker reported
"conflicting artifact-location guards" and exited `BLOCKED`; the terminal
blocker circuit classified it as `permission_required` and held the issue at
`status:blocked`. Both guards already accept the same root, so the blocker was
caused by the fence guidance, not by missing authority. About 20 other batches
of the same brief completed on the same and other runners.

## How

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/worker-write-fence.mjs`: build the block
  message from `allowedRoots(env)` so it lists the worker worktree and the
  resolved managed temp root, and directs scratch/private artifacts to a 0700
  subdirectory of `AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR`. Apply it to both
  `assertWorkerWritePaths` and `assertWorkerGitTargets`. Keep
  `SIBLING_WORKTREE_MESSAGE` exported as the stable prefix.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-git-safety-gate.mjs`: extend the
  existing "headless workers cannot write or run mutating git in sibling
  worktrees" test (around line 1011) to assert the message names
  `AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR` and its resolved path.

## Acceptance

- A blocked worker write outside both roots reports the worktree path and the
  resolved `AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR` path, plus the scratch-directory guidance.
- Allowed writes (worktree, managed temp) are unchanged.
- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-git-safety-gate.mjs`
  passes.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/worker-write-fence.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-git-safety-gate.mjs`

## Verification

```bash
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-git-safety-gate.mjs
```

title: t18764: full-loop plugin validator fails on bounded-operation timing tests under worker host load
body:
## Task


Make the full-loop project validator for `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops`
(`npm run test` = `node --test tests/*.mjs`) reliable on a host that is busy
running pulse workers, so interactive and worker `commit-and-pr` runs stop
failing on unrelated timing assertions in
`tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs`.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Make the full-loop project validator for `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops`
(`npm run test` = `node --test tests/*.mjs`) reliable on a host that is busy
running pulse workers, so interactive and worker `commit-and-pr` runs stop
failing on unrelated timing assertions in
`tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs`.

## Why

On 2026-10-23 three consecutive `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` runs for an
unrelated plugin change (GH#35495, PR #35497) failed the validator, each on a
different timing assertion in `test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs`:

- `start returns control and explicit progress reaches a private terminal receipt`: `timed_out` instead of `succeeded` (line 110)
- `helper-created process groups are contained on timeout and cancellation (GH#33514)`: containment `incomplete` instead of `owned_process_tree` (line 506)
- `restoration ...`: state `running` instead of `restoring` (line 658), and `expired generations and private command data stay isolated`: `did not reach a terminal state: timing_out` (line 671)

The host load average was about 250-300 on 16 cores. The same file passed in
isolation (18/18), and the full plugin suite exited 0 with
`node --test --test-concurrency=2`. The session had to skip the validator with
`AIDEVOPS_SKIP_PROJECT_VALIDATORS=1`, which removes the local gate entirely.
Earlier one-test fixes (GH#34012, GH#34330, GH#34573) raised individual budgets;
the failures keep moving to the next timing-sensitive test because the
validator runs the whole suite at default concurrency on a saturated host.

## How

Pick the smallest change that keeps the gate and removes load sensitivity, for
example:

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit-validators.sh` (project validator runner, see
  `_validators_should_run` near line 745 and the npm validator invocation): when
  the 1-minute load average per CPU is high, run the plugin suite with bounded
  test concurrency (for example via an env var that the plugin `test` script
  honours), or retry only the failed test files once serially before reporting
  failure.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/package.json` `test` script: accept an
  optional concurrency setting without changing CI behaviour.
- Keep `plugin-import-check.yml` CI semantics unchanged.

## Acceptance

- On a host with load average per CPU above 4, the validator either passes for
  a change that does not touch bounded operations, or reports a failure that
  also reproduces serially.
- An unloaded host keeps the current runtime within about 20%.
- No test budget is raised without evidence that the assertion itself is
  load-sensitive.

A test-side change to `test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs` is in scope
only if the chosen fix needs it.

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit-validators.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/package.json`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs`

title: fix(opencode-db): archive refuses new session_context_epoch schema; per-DB budget overrun and silent run termination
body:
## What

The daily OpenCode DB archive (`opencode-db-archive-async-helper.sh` → `opencode-db-archive.sh archive-all`) has not recorded a successful run since 2026-10-20. Two independent causes:

1. **Schema whitelist drift (deterministic).** Newer OpenCode builds added three columns to `session_context_epoch`. Every DB created/migrated by those builds is refused, `archive-all` returns rc=3, and the helper logs `Unsupported OpenCode schema — active data left untouched and last-run NOT updated` (2026-10-21 and 2026-10-22 runs).
2. **Per-DB budget not enforced / run ends without a terminal line.** The 2026-10-23 run started 04:00Z with `budget=60s`, spent ~70 minutes on the shared `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` (30.6 GB; 52 sessions moved, `0 B freed`), then the log stops mid-DB at ~06:55 local with no `Completed`/`Protected skip`/`rc=` line, and no archive process remains. The 2026-10-14/15/16 runs ended the same way (next run logs `Reclaiming stale lock (PID … no longer alive)`).

## Evidence

Observed schema in an affected per-project DB:

```sql
CREATE TABLE `session_context_epoch` (
  `session_id` text PRIMARY KEY,
  `baseline` text NOT NULL,
  `snapshot` text NOT NULL,
  `baseline_seq` integer NOT NULL,
  `replacement_seq` integer,
  `revision` integer DEFAULT 0 NOT NULL, `agent` text DEFAULT 'build' NOT NULL,
  CONSTRAINT `fk_session_context_epoch_session_id_session_id_fk` FOREIGN KEY (`session_id`) REFERENCES `session`(`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE
)
```

Log line: `table=session_context_epoch actual_columns=[session_id,baseline,snapshot,baseline_seq,replacement_seq,revision,agent] supported_columns=[session_id,baseline,snapshot,baseline_seq] reason=column-mismatch`.

The shared DB still has the old 4-column shape, so both shapes must be supported.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-safety-lib.sh:210` — `session_context_epoch) supported="session_id,baseline,snapshot,baseline_seq"`; accept the 3 added columns (old and new shapes).
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh:481` — archive-DB `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS session_context_epoch`; add the new nullable/defaulted columns, and add them to existing archive DBs (`ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN`) so name-based copy (GH#35418 pattern, `_archive_copy_sql`) works old→new and new→new. Restore path (`cmd_restore` / `session_context_epoch` handling near line 1831) must copy them back.
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh` `--max-duration-seconds` handling — confirm where the per-DB budget is checked; the shared-DB step exceeded 60s by ~70 minutes. Budget must bound candidate selection + copy/delete batches, not only the loop between DBs.
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-async-helper.sh:188-198` — make termination observable: trap/log signal exit with rc, and consider per-DB rc so one unsupported/deferred DB does not block `last-run` for the whole fleet (record per-DB outcomes instead).
- Tests: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh:221` fixture uses the old shape; add a new-shape fixture round-trip (archive + restore).

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-safety-lib.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-async-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-restore.sh`

Brief repaired: GH#35511 extracted restore into this sibling module after the original brief. Independent review found that restoring new epoch values into an old-shape active DB would discard archive-only fields before deleting the archive row. Add a fail-closed compatibility guard for non-default archive-only epoch values. Existing shared-column restore is the reference; verify with the archive regression suite and ShellCheck. Scope recovery is limited to this directly necessary integration; assignment and authorized outcome are unchanged.

## Reproducer

1. Create a fixture DB whose `session_context_epoch` has the 7-column shape above (otherwise copy the existing fixture at `tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh:221`).
2. Run `OPENCODE_DB_PATH=<fixture> OPENCODE_ARCHIVE_DB=<fixture-archive> opencode-db-archive.sh archive --dry-run`.
3. Observe `Unsupported or unavailable OpenCode session schema … reason=column-mismatch` and rc=3.
4. For the budget issue: `rg -n "opencode-db-archive-async\]" ~/.aidevops/logs/opencode-db-archive.log` shows starts on 2026-10-14/15/16/23 with no terminal line, followed by `Reclaiming stale lock`.

## Acceptance

- `archive-all` archives DBs with both `session_context_epoch` shapes; restore round-trips the new columns.

title: Playwriter status reports managed MCP as not installed and approved pin as latest
body:
## Description

The aidevops tool checker reports Playwriter MCP as not installed when the supported, on-demand package-runner integration is configured and usable. It also labels the approved 0.8.0 pin as the latest version even though the registry reports 0.9.0. The associated diagnostic suggests a global installation despite successful managed-MCP execution.

Please fix status reporting and remediation through the existing aidevops-managed integration. An independent global installation or manual persistent relay is not the desired workaround.

## Expected Behavior

Distinguish global CLI availability, configured package-runner version, actual MCP/relay health, approved package version, and latest upstream version. An intentionally disabled on-demand entry is not absent. Configuration or cached files alone must not be presented as proof of live usability, but a missing PATH binary must not imply that the supported MCP is missing.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command** (read-only, no `--update`):

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/tool-version-check.sh --category npm --json
```

**Actual output**: exit 0; the complete Playwriter row was:

```json
{"name":"Playwriter MCP","category":"npm","installed":"not installed","latest":"0.8.0","status":"not_installed","update_cmd":"npm install -g playwriter@0.8.0"}
```

Other tools' rows are omitted as unrelated. The operator's preceding update output likewise said `Playwriter MCP: not installed` and `Latest: 0.8.0`.

Separately, `npm view playwriter version` returned `0.9.0`.

**Positive supported-path control**: an explicitly scoped Playwriter agent invoked the existing registry-approved `aidevops_mcp` connector, received `Connected MCP playwriter for the playwriter agent. Its tools remain scoped to that agent.`, actually called `playwriter_execute`, and obtained:

```text
Console output:
[log] {"controlledPageCount":0}
```

The only browser code was:

```javascript
console.log(JSON.stringify({controlledPageCount: context.pages().length}))
```

The live diagnostic during connection reported relay version `0.8.0`, `extension-connected`, one extension connection, and zero rejected sockets, port conflicts or token rejections. It nevertheless also printed `Command not found: playwriter` and `Try: npm install -g playwriter`. The MCP disconnected successfully afterward. Zero controlled pages does not establish successful tab handoff; that is a separate investigation.

**Expected output**: report the managed package-runner installation/configuration and absence of a standalone global CLI separately, retain truthful live-health states, and label 0.8.0 as approved/pinned rather than latest upstream. Do not recommend a global install to repair an already working MCP.

**Causal status**: confirmed

Confirmed only for installation/version reporting and the misleading global-install suggestion. No claim is made here about the cause of the user's icon-click problem.

**Owning-path proof**:

- **Production entry point**: `aidevops.sh:518` calls `_update_check_tools`; `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-update-lib.sh:324-330` invokes `tool-version-check.sh --update`.
- **Call chain**: `check_tool` in `.agents/scripts/tool-version-check.sh` obtains `_tool_installed_version` / `_tool_latest_version`, classifies the result and emits console/JSON status. The npm path calls `get_installed_version`; the initial `command -v` test returns `not installed` without considering configured package-runner MCPs. `_tool_latest_version` hard-codes the Playwriter approved pin as its latest value.
- **Integrated verification**: the read-only production checker above reproduced the exact Playwriter JSON row on current installed code, while the real managed MCP connection and execute control succeeded in the same investigation. The full mutating updater was not replayed.

**Causal code / attribution** at public source `db7e83fee3a42d191eaef40f3d68984c4032602a`:

```text
tool-version-check.sh:318  if command -v "$cmd" &>/dev/null; then
tool-version-check.sh:374  echo "not installed"
tool-version-check.sh:571  if [[ "$pkg" == playwriter ]]; then printf '%s\n' 0.8.0; else get_npm_latest "$pkg"; fi ;;
```

`git blame` attributes the PATH-only gate to `3bcbbe38b8` and the current 0.8.0 latest branch to `95ec9b7b44`. These identify relevant code history, not proof that the original generic PATH behavior was a defect for every tool.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use aidevops's generated, scoped on-demand Playwriter entry with no global Playwriter CLI. Preserve the guarded launcher and configured telemetry opt-outs.
2. Connect through the actual Playwriter agent and perform the count-only execute control; disconnect when done.
3. Run the read-only tool checker above and compare the Playwriter row with the supported-path control.
4. Run `mcp-diagnose.sh playwriter` while connected to observe the standalone-CLI error/suggestion alongside a healthy managed relay.

## Workarounds Applied

Used the existing scoped managed connector and count-only execute canary to disprove the missing-MCP inference; used the installed relay diagnostic to separate relay and extension states. No global installation, alternate relay, browser/profile replacement, package update or configuration edit was performed. This manual cross-check should not be required of future operators.

## Implementation Scope / Reference Pattern

- `.agents/scripts/tool-version-check.sh:151,313-375,537-571,618-622,687-690`: package specification, PATH-only detection, version policy and rendered classification.
- `.agents/scripts/mcp-diagnose.sh:453-549,803-874`: supported configured-command detection and missing-global fallback. Disabled generated on-demand Playwriter entries currently fall out of configured-runner probing; respect their intended lifecycle without launching a relay just to display status.
- Reuse generated-command recognition in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-registry.mjs` / `.agents/scripts/lib/mcp_config.py` and the existing configured-command diagnostic pattern. Do not expose environments, tokens, process arguments or browser metadata.
- Existing tests: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-version-check-classify.sh`, `test-aidevops-update-tool-reporting.sh`, `test-mcp-diagnose-configured-command.sh`, and `test-playwriter-pin.sh`.
- Call-site sweep: production `check_tool` calls installed/latest detection; installed detection is also used for post-update verification. Keep JSON, console output and update planning consistent. The updater and standalone `aidevops tools` route share `tool-version-check.sh`.

## Acceptance / Verification

- [ ] Correctly distinguish absent integration, configured on-demand integration, failed runtime, and working package-runner MCP without requiring a global install.
- [ ] Report approved/pinned versus registry latest honestly; keep reviewed-version update policy intact.
- [ ] Remove misleading global-install remediation for an existing supported managed entry; do not create another worker/relay or edit operator configuration automatically.
- [ ] Preserve global-CLI users, custom-command boundaries, disabled unrelated servers, explicit activation and safe diagnostic output.
- [ ] Verify JSON/console output and update planning using the existing focused checks below, plus the real managed-MCP control. Do not count configuration/cache existence alone as a health pass.

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-version-check-classify.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-aidevops-update-tool-reporting.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-mcp-diagnose-configured-command.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-playwriter-pin.sh
```

Suggested implementation tier: standard; the product boundary is decided, with no permission widening or independent deployment. Those proposed repair checks were not run as part of issue filing.

## Environment / Discovery

aidevops 3.39.59, OpenCode 1.19.4, macOS 26.6.2, gh 2.103.0; managed Playwriter 0.8.0; official Chrome extension manifest 0.0.170. Public source HEAD matched remote main at discovery time. No private repository, profile identity, tab data or credentials are included.

All-state Playwriter/installation searches and open/merged PR searches found no matching open repair. #31097 previously addressed diagnostic version visibility; #34648/#34663 added relay-state classification. This report includes a current reproduced false installation classification after those changes, not an assumption that their earlier fixes never shipped. Recent source history does not supersede the reproduced checker result.

title: Investigate reliable selected-tab extension handoff through aidevops-managed Playwriter
body:
## Description

Investigate and repair the explicit selected-tab handoff experience through aidevops's existing Playwriter integration. The operator reports that clicking the installed extension no longer hands over a browser tab as it did in their 0.5-era workflow.

The desired outcome is one coherent aidevops-managed toolchain: the operator chooses the tab by clicking its extension button, the scoped agent acknowledges that attachment, and work continues on that explicitly authorized tab. This is not a request for desktop control, a parallel Playwriter deployment, a manually persistent relay, broad tab inspection, or an isolated-browser fallback.

## Expected Behavior

Provide a clear, bounded ready-to-receive handoff state while the existing guarded MCP is active. A user click on an eligible normal web tab must either result in a verified attachment or a classified actionable failure. Do not require the user to race a brief subagent's start/disconnect window, pre-enable an extension against a stopped relay, or keep clicking blindly.

An extension connection and a tab attachment are different states. If no page is attached, keep that fact explicit. If multiple previously authorized tabs exist, do not guess the target, silently select the first page or create a replacement tab. Aidevops should coordinate the existing owner, not start another controller.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**: this is a reported GUI action, not a terminal command: the operator clicks the Playwriter extension icon to hand over their intended tab and cannot obtain the expected usable session. Exact live click-time icon color/tooltip, target-page eligibility and service-worker error have not been captured. Do not invent them. The actual terminal/tool diagnostics are recorded below.

**Diagnostic commands / actions already performed**:

1. Installed `mcp-diagnose.sh playwriter` before activation: `Live local relay version: unavailable`, verdict `relay-down`.
2. Actual Playwriter agent called the registry-approved `aidevops_mcp` connector and received:

```text
Connected MCP playwriter for the playwriter agent. Its tools remain scoped to that agent.
```

3. While connected, the diagnostic reported live relay version `0.8.0`, `extension-connected`, one extension connection and zero rejected sockets, port conflicts or token rejections.
4. The actual `playwriter_execute` tool executed only:

```javascript
console.log(JSON.stringify({controlledPageCount: context.pages().length}))
```

**Actual output**:

```text
Console output:
[log] {"controlledPageCount":0}
```

5. The agent disconnected successfully. After the earlier startup-only diagnostic, a separate diagnostic confirmed that the guarded relay had stopped as designed.

**Expected output**: when the operator performs the intended click during a live, ready handoff, acknowledge the explicitly selected tab without enumerating unrelated browser tabs. A failed click must return a precise classified outcome rather than a generic request to enable the extension again.

**Causal status**: unconfirmed investigation

The MCP startup, extension socket and real execute path worked. Zero controlled pages was observed without a contemporaneous user-click canary; it is not by itself a defect or proof that the icon is broken. No current stale-relay conflict, missing execute-tool defect, extension rejection, or 0.8/0.9 compatibility regression was demonstrated. A successful connection alone is also not evidence that the reported handoff works.

**Owning-path proof / candidate causes**:

- Framework owning interface: scoped on-demand Playwriter agent -> `aidevops_mcp` lifecycle -> guarded relay -> extension -> explicitly controlled tab.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-activation-tool.mjs:252-286` enforces agent identity and connects/disconnects the managed MCP; this path was exercised successfully.
- `.agents/tools/browser/playwriter.md:100-167` documents guarded ownership, tab preflight, zero-page states and disconnect cleanup. Preserve these safeguards while making the waiting/handoff lifecycle usable.
- Upstream `extension/src/background.ts` at tag `extension@0.0.170`, corresponding to the installed manifest version, explicitly states that the icon attaches a tab but does not start the daemon. Its `onActionClicked` handler ignores repeated clicks for an already-connecting tab and rejects restricted targets. Those are relevant hypotheses, not evidence of the user's precise click-time cause.
- Relay lifecycle versus click timing, stale service-worker state, page eligibility and debugger attachment need capture during the real failing handoff. No blocked command/trace establishing a transport root cause was captured.

## Steps to Reproduce / Next Bounded Investigation

1. Use the existing aidevops-managed Playwriter entry, not a global install or a direct CLI relay. Preserve exact reviewed-version/authenticated loopback policy.
2. Establish a clearly signalled bounded handoff window with the scoped MCP still connected. Do not navigate, open tabs, inspect desktop state or read page content to prepare the test.
3. Have the operator click the extension once on their intended eligible web tab. Record only necessary icon status/tooltip and attachment counts; classify relevant browser/relay errors without leaking identities, URLs, credentials or unrelated tab data.
4. Verify the transition from no attached page to the intended user-selected attachment. Where destination validation is needed, use only approved target metadata; multiple enabled tabs are not permission to guess.
5. End with success, classified failure, timeout or cancellation and verify normal managed cleanup without closing user tabs.
6. If the fault is upstream extension code, provide the bounded repro to its owner; do not implement another framework browser engine.

## Workarounds Applied

Used the existing scoped managed connector, installed diagnostic and count-only execute canary to separate installation, relay, extension socket and controlled-page states. No desktop control was used, no private tab metadata/content was read, no tab was selected by guesswork and no replacement browser or parallel relay was installed. A real user-click test is still required.

## Implementation Scope / Reference Pattern

Verified candidate framework targets:

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/config-agent-profiles.mjs:113-151`: on-demand agent activation guidance/profile.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-activation-tool.mjs:252-286`: lifecycle and connection messaging.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-registry.mjs`: generated managed entry and guarded launcher integration.
- `.agents/scripts/playwriter-authenticated-relay.mjs` and its existing lifecycle/guardian/reconciliation modules: inspect only if the live trace implicates lifecycle; do not weaken cleanup or add a daemon as a speculative fix.
- `.agents/scripts/mcp-diagnose.sh:579-770`: existing privacy-bounded relay/extension classification.
- `.agents/tools/browser/playwriter.md`: tab preflight, user consent and failure guidance.
- Existing `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-mcp-activation.mjs` and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-playwriter-authenticated-relay.mjs` are the reference patterns for a scoped repair. Exact upstream extension repair paths beyond the observed handler remain unknown until reproduction.

## Acceptance / Verification

- [ ] Reproduce or explicitly classify the operator's live icon-to-tab outcome using the managed path; preserve the evidence and its limitations.
- [ ] Implement the smallest owner-appropriate repair if a fault is established. Otherwise document a verified supported handoff and explain which state caused the reported failure.
- [ ] Confirm that an operator click on the intended tab, not broad computer access or agent guesswork, is the handoff mechanism.
- [ ] Preserve reviewed package policy, token challenge, loopback-only access, telemetry opt-out, single-owner conflict handling, per-agent permissions, bounded waiting/cancellation, owned-relay cleanup and all user-owned tabs.
- [ ] Do not count healthy relay startup, unit tests or `controlledPageCount:0` as successful selected-tab handoff.


These are proposed existing repair checks, not tests already run during filing. Final acceptance additionally requires the live user-approved click canary. Suggested scope is standard-tier bounded investigation within existing privacy/ownership boundaries; escalate any consequential change to those boundaries rather than silently implementing it.

Those issues are closed, and actual execute availability was verified here. This report does not reopen them by assuming their fixes failed. title: feat(opencode-db): idle-gated archive of DBs held open by idle OpenCode sessions
body:
## What

The OpenCode DB archive defers any database held open by a process (`_archive_mutation_preflight` in `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh`). Interactive OpenCode processes stay open 24/7 on many installs, so their per-project DBs are never archived and grow without bound. On 2026-10-23 four per-project DBs were deferred (1–4 holders each); every holder was an interactive `opencode` process, one per session.

Add an idle gate: archive a held DB in small batches only when every holder is an OpenCode process that reports no busy session for a quiet period, and stop between batches as soon as one becomes busy.

## How

1. **Plugin activity heartbeat** (new `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/db-activity-heartbeat.mjs`, wired in `index.mjs` `event` hook): track `session.status` busy/retry/idle per session and write `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/state/opencode-activity/<pid>.json` atomically with `{pid, busy_sessions, last_activity_epoch, updated_epoch, sessions:[recent IDs]}`. Write on busy/idle transitions and throttled activity (≤1 write/30 s). Remove the file on process exit where possible.
2. **Archive idle gate** (`.agents/scripts/opencode-db-safety-lib.sh` + `opencode-db-archive.sh`): when holders > 0, list holder PIDs (`lsof -t`). Proceed only if each holder has a heartbeat file for that PID, its command is `opencode`, `busy_sessions == 0`, and `now - last_activity_epoch >= OPENCODE_DB_ARCHIVE_IDLE_SECONDS` (default 900). Also require user input idle `>= OPENCODE_DB_ARCHIVE_USER_IDLE_SECONDS` (default 1800; 0 disables; unavailable on headless hosts = not required). Held mode: batch size `OPENCODE_DB_ARCHIVE_HELD_BATCH_SIZE` (default 10), re-check gate before each batch (stop with rc=2), exclude every session ID listed by holder heartbeats, never VACUUM (existing VACUUM holder veto stays).
3. **Scheduler** (`.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-platform.sh` `setup_opencode_db_archive`): run hourly 00:00–07:00 local instead of once at 05:00 (launchd `StartCalendarInterval` array; cron `0 0-7 * * *`; systemd `*-*-* 00..07:00:00`). The async helper skips when `last-run` already records a complete run today.

## Files Scope

- NEW: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/db-activity-heartbeat.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-safety-lib.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-async-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-platform.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh`

## Acceptance

- Held DB whose holders all report idle heartbeats (past threshold) archives in batches of ≤10; heartbeat-listed sessions are never archived; no VACUUM while held.
- Any holder without a heartbeat, busy, recently active, or user recently active → deferred (rc=2), DB unchanged.
- Gate turning busy mid-run stops before the next batch with committed batches preserved.
- Scheduler installs hourly 00–07 on macOS/Linux; repeated runs after a complete daily run are no-ops.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh`, plugin `node --test` for the new module, ShellCheck pass.

Builds on #35509 / PR #35512 (per-DB deadline, schema support).

## Description

The local full-loop project validator (`full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` → `npm run test` in `.agents/scripts`) fails for any PR that touches `.agents/scripts` when the `playwright` package cannot be resolved from `.agents/scripts`. The failure is in a test unrelated to the change being shipped, so the validator blocks unrelated PRs.

`.agents/scripts/tests/test-higgsfield-extracted-helpers.mjs:11` imports `../higgsfield/higgsfield-browser.mjs` purely to match the self-test bootstrap order; that module's top-level `import { chromium } from 'playwright'` (`.agents/scripts/higgsfield/higgsfield-browser.mjs:6`) throws `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. `playwright` is not declared in `.agents/scripts/package.json`. CI does not run this `npm run test` suite (no workflow invokes it), so the break is only visible locally. Introduced with the GH#35425 extraction (#35440).

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `cd .agents/scripts && node --test tests/test-higgsfield-extracted-helpers.mjs`

**Actual output** (2026-10-23, Node v26.12.0, macOS, no resolvable `playwright`):

```text
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'playwright' imported from .../.agents/scripts/higgsfield/higgsfield-browser.mjs
✖ tests/test-higgsfield-extracted-helpers.mjs
```

Observed while shipping GH#35514 (PR #35526): `[validators] CHECK FAILED (exit 1): npm run test (.agents/scripts)` with 85/87 passing and only this file failing; the PR changed no Higgsfield files and the file is identical on `origin/main`.

## Expected

The extracted-helper test exercises only pure helpers (`higgsfield-image-options.mjs`, `higgsfield-pipeline-assembly.mjs`, `higgsfield-image.mjs` re-exports) without requiring a browser runtime, or skips cleanly with a clear reason when `playwright` is unavailable. The local validator must not fail unrelated PRs.

## Implementation scope

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-higgsfield-extracted-helpers.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/higgsfield/higgsfield-browser.mjs`

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-higgsfield-extracted-helpers.mjs`: avoid the hard `higgsfield-browser.mjs` import, or guard it with a resolvability check and `test.skip` reason. Check whether `higgsfield-image.mjs` itself imports `playwright` transitively; if so, prefer a lazy/dynamic import in the browser module over adding a dependency.
- Do not add `playwright` to `.agents/scripts/package.json` just to satisfy the test, and do not weaken the validator.

## Verification

```bash
cd .agents/scripts && node --test tests/test-higgsfield-extracted-helpers.mjs
cd .agents/scripts && npm run test
```

Both should pass (or skip this file with an explicit reason) on a machine where `playwright` is not resolvable from `.agents/scripts`.

title: Native desktop automation repeatedly steals focus without a bounded progress handoff
body:
## Description

An interactive OpenCode operational task repeatedly raised the operator's everyday Brave window while the operator was working in other sessions. A delegated native macOS automation attempt continued through repeated screenshots/window interactions after a successful target receipt was visible. The operator interrupted the session because of the desktop disruption.

This reports an observed human-interruption failure and requests a bounded native-desktop execution contract. It does not assert an MCP implementation defect, model-service outage, or permission to remove authentication/security checks.

## Expected Behavior

Native desktop automation must have an explicit, task-scoped foreground-interaction budget and a usable stop/handoff path. Routine observation must not repeatedly seize the working desktop. Repeated unchanged observations must result in a bounded return of evidence and remaining actions, not indefinite foreground retries. Preserve a deliberate, bounded exception for genuinely necessary user-visible interaction.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**: The recorded `macos-automator_execute_script` calls repeatedly included this AppleScript, followed by clicks or screenshot collection:

```applescript
tell application "System Events" to tell process "Brave Browser"
  set frontmost to true
  perform action "AXRaise" of window 1
end tell
```

Equivalent recorded JXA included `p.frontmost=true; p.windows[0].actions.byName('AXRaise').perform();`.

**Actual output**: Read-only retrospective counts from the final delegated attempt, 2026-10-23 18:53:58 through 19:25:31 UTC:

```text
macos-automator_execute_script|97
read|48
```

The 48 read calls inspected saved screenshots. Later screenshots repeatedly showed the terminal launcher/verification receipts. The operator reported repeated focus theft while trying to use other sessions. These counts describe the attempt; they do not establish that every call was redundant or measure MCP execution latency.

**Expected output**: A bounded terminal result or progress handoff, with verified facts, remaining work, and desktop-control release. No further focus-raising observation loop once a terminal result has been captured.

**Causal status**: unconfirmed investigation

The focus-raising script is directly recorded and explains the immediate desktop effect. The missing/ineffective framework control and its owning implementation need investigation; no integrated reproducer of a specific plugin defect or blame commit is available. This is not a claim that a child continued running after cancellation.

## Suggested Safe Reproduction

1. Use an isolated test desktop/browser and a synthetic page displaying a terminal task receipt; do not use the operator's real authenticated session.
2. Delegate a native UI task with explicit target, allowed actions, time/action budget, and stopping conditions.
3. Exercise repeated unchanged observations and attempted focus changes through the real scoped MCP/tool-hook route.
4. Verify that the bounded contract returns control and evidence without indefinite focus changes. Verify a short authorized foreground interaction still works.

## Owning Interfaces and Implementation Scope

Verified tracked files on inspected source HEAD `2b306a2550b3ae0bb400d74a70186105d627ed17`:

- `.agents/tools/automation/macos-automator.md:24-29,84-111`: delegated native MCP entry/tool interfaces.
- `.agents/tools/browser/browser-automation.md:154-163`: existing terminal-outcome and bounded-handoff contract. Reuse it instead of adding repetitive global prompt rules.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs:736-755`: existing before/after tool hooks; a candidate integration surface, not a confirmed causal location.
- `.agents/reference/agent-routing.md:77-84`: bounded summaries and completed-unit evidence reuse.

The exact control module and cross-runtime equivalent are not yet identified. First locate existing session-stall/progress and scoped-MCP controls; extend the narrowest existing owner rather than inventing a second controller. Do not assume arbitrary-script text matching alone can securely enforce all desktop effects.

## Acceptance and Verification

- Demonstrate bounded handling of repeated no-progress native UI actions through the production route.
- Distinguish tool activity from meaningful target-state progress.
- Bind budget and foreground authority to the correct parent/child task; unrelated sessions must not gain control.
- Return captured evidence and remaining actions when stopping. Do not silently discard successful partial work.
- No new broad OS/browser permissions, credentials, or access to everyday profiles by default.
- Use existing relevant checks plus a focused isolated regression for the chosen mechanism. Do not reproduce by disturbing a real working desktop.

## Workarounds Applied

- The operator terminated the disruptive session.
- Follow-up investigation used read-only session records and already-saved images; no browser interaction or launcher replay occurred.
- Recovered completed-operation evidence manually and separated it from unverified remaining scheduling work. This evidence-handoff gap is a sibling report, not proof of a cancellation bug.
- A worker runtime-policy conflict is being reported separately; no runtime installation or guard bypass was used during this investigation.

## Discovery and Scope Limits

Searched upstream issues for foreground/focus automation and browser loops, and reviewed relevant PR search results and recent source history. No matching fix was identified. Current upstream content SHAs match the inspected native-automation/browser/routing documents. Existing browser isolation guidance does not by itself prevent this native desktop fallback failure. Raw session IDs, images, host identities, credentials and private operational configuration are intentionally excluded.

## Environment

- aidevops at investigation: 3.39.60
- OpenCode: 1.19.4; the interrupted long-running session also spanned older installed generations
- macOS: 26.6.2
- Shell diagnostics: Bash 5.3.20
- GitHub CLI: 2.103.0
- Recorded native automation route used the configured macos-automator MCP; its actual package version was not independently verified, so no package-specific regression is asserted

Suggested priority: high. Implementation boundaries require maintainer triage before selecting a mechanism.

title: Preserve verified operational substeps when a delegated task is interrupted
body:
## Description

A delegated operational workflow obtained a successful target verification receipt but continued native UI inspection instead of completing the remaining authorized action and returning a bounded result. After the operator interrupted it, the parent Task result only exposed `Tool execution aborted`; follow-up investigation had to reconstruct the successful work from child tool history and saved screenshots.

This sibling of #35528 focuses on completed-unit evidence and parent recovery, not foreground-control enforcement. It is not a claim that cancellation failed to terminate a child, that every aborted Task loses evidence, or that a receipt flag alone proves the entire operational objective.

## Expected Behavior

Persist/reuse verified completed-unit facts with their evidence references, freshness and scope separately from the child's eventual terminal status. A target operation's success must neither be lost because the child was interrupted nor be expanded into success for unperformed remaining actions. A parent should recover a concise state such as `transfer verified; schedule activation not verified` without replaying the operation or reconstructing dozens of images.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**: An OpenCode `task` delegation to the `macos-automator` subagent performed an authorized operational transfer and subsequent verification. Private target identifiers and deployment contents are excluded; this is a historical trace, not a newly executed generic reproducer.

**Actual output**:

The target receipt visible in the child's saved screenshots reported:

```text
status=complete-copy-verified
complete=true
backup_ready=true
elapsed_seconds=337
last_healthy_copy_deleted=false
```

The saved receipt also contained matching source/destination checksums; private identifiers and hash values are omitted here. A screenshot read at 19:18:55 UTC on 2026-10-23 already exposed the terminal receipt. Later screenshot reads at 19:23:55, 19:24:26 and 19:25:10 continued revisiting terminal receipt views. The parent task ultimately ended at 19:25:31 with:

```text
Tool execution aborted
```

The last captured scheduler evidence remained disabled. No later activation/read-back was recorded. Thus the verified transfer was successful while the recurring-workflow objective remained incomplete. Counts and timestamps come from indexed, read-only session/part queries; raw records and screenshots remain private.

**Expected output**: A bounded evidence handoff distinguishing the successful completed unit, unfinished schedule state, evidence timestamps, and next safe action. Do not retry/replay the transfer merely to reconstruct state.

**Causal status**: unconfirmed investigation

Observed: evidence existed in child tool history and did not become a final parent summary before interruption. Unknown: whether existing cancellation-ledger/event handling was active for that installed generation and whether a runtime error path skipped a hook. No specific cancellation implementation regression is asserted.

## Owning Interfaces and Reference Pattern

Verified tracked paths on source HEAD `2b306a2550b3ae0bb400d74a70186105d627ed17`:

- `.agents/reference/agent-routing.md:77-84`: final-only summaries and persistence/reuse of completed-unit evidence already required.
- `.agents/tools/browser/browser-automation.md:154-163`: terminal result and bounded evidence handoff contract.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs:736-755`: existing tool lifecycle hooks.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/subagent-cancellation-receipt.mjs:94-118,153-170`: existing bounded cancellation/side-effect receipt. Preserve its termination and unknown-outcome safeguards; it is a reference integration, not a proven defective owner.

Exact completed-unit checkpoint/parent recovery owner is not yet established. Investigate the existing lifecycle/evidence mechanism before adding any new store or controller. Do not attach private target receipts or full tool output to public telemetry.

## Acceptance and Verification

1. Use a synthetic operational target through the real Task/child route; capture one verified completed unit while a second unit remains pending.
2. Interrupt before the final child response. Parent recovery should retain the completed fact with an inspectable safe evidence reference, pending second unit, and unknowns.
3. Verify that a stale, contradictory, malformed or merely launcher-success receipt does not become target/objective acceptance.
4. Verify that stopping/cancellation remains effective and that recovery does not repeat side effects.
5. Bound both receipt size and checkpoint work. Reuse existing relevant tests; add only focused coverage in the existing owner once identified.

## Workarounds Applied

The operator terminated the disruptive attempt. A follow-up session used read-only child history and saved screenshot inspection to recover the verified transfer, compare it with source evidence, and explicitly retain schedule activation as unfinished. No desktop interaction, operation replay, credential/permission expansion or automatic schedule change occurred during recovery.

## Discovery and Scope Limits

Checked upstream issue/PR searches for evidence handoff, completed evidence and terminal browser behavior. No matching report/fix was identified; the similarly named merged handoff-warning issue concerns a separate Git merge path. Existing guidance already calls for completed-evidence reuse, so another global prompt reminder alone is not the requested solution. Investigation and current upstream versions of the cited browser/routing documents match by content SHA.

## Environment

aidevops 3.39.60 and OpenCode 1.19.4 at investigation; the interrupted multi-day session spanned earlier installed generations. macOS 26.6.2. The exact installed-generation ownership of this particular interrupted Task hook requires investigation.

See-also: #35528
