title: Worker completion: own merged closing PR with finalized cleanup is falsely classified premature_exit
body:
## Summary
A worker completed implementation, merged its own closing PR, synchronized canonical and finalized the guarded cleanup receipt, then exited naturally with raw runtime exit 0. Classification nevertheless recorded premature_exit, classifier exit 77, model_stopped_before_completion and resume_session_with_completion_contract. This is a false completion classification, not unfinished implementation.

## Sanitized evidence (2026-10-25)
Protected excerpt line 28: merge succeeded, required checks terminal-success, review gate PASS, linked closure converged. Line 31: canonical fast-forward succeeded (exit 0). Line 35: worker readback confirmed MERGED PR, CLOSED issue and one MERGE_SUMMARY. Line 47: cleanup receipt finalized, release:not-requested (exit 0). Line 53: final answer reports delivered implementation, merge, sync and finalized cleanup. Lines 106-109: raw and structured exit_code=0, kill_reason=natural, then cause=premature_exit with no provider error. Correlated headless-runtime-metrics row records exit_code=77, activity=true, natural exit and resume recommendation. Replaying the installed output_has_completion_signal Python parser against the excerpt returned 1.
Fresh independent gh pr view confirmed MERGED, merge commit and exact same-repository closing linkage; gh issue view confirmed CLOSED one second after merge. All private repo names, issue/PR numbers, session/attempt IDs, local paths, domain content and raw logs are omitted from this public brief. Protected evidence remains local and is not a worker dependency.

## Deduplication
Searched all-state framework issues for premature_exit, model_stopped_before_completion, premature titles and merged-completion classification. Related closed repairs: #32529 (argv parser crash), #33331 (continuation visibility), #33672 via #33674 (PR-less terminal outcomes), #27907 (attempt reconciliation). No exact own-merged-PR repair found. Current deployed code already includes #33672, but its verifier requires no PR on the worker branch and no commits ahead of the default tip. That cannot prove this own-PR/squash-merge completion. Do not weaken PR-less guards globally.

## Files Scope
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-result.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-provider-tests.sh`

## Source references and implementation pattern
Verified deployed source counterparts; edit repository .agents/scripts, never deployed files:
- .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-result.sh:158-254, particularly 240-249: success gate only falls back to PR-less completion before returning 77.
- .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh:668: output_has_completion_signal parses model markers and direct PR commands; wrapper/bounded-tool lifecycle completion need not contain those.
- .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh:1375-1466: terminal backstop delegates to PR-less cleanliness even for already-delivered merged linkage. Also inspect final reconciled-outcome handling. Reuse existing exact-head, exact closing-linkage and guarded cleanup-receipt proof patterns, bound to current attempt.
- .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:492-516: maps premature_exit to model_stopped_before_completion and resume recommendation.
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-provider-tests.sh through existing test-headless-runtime-helper.sh harness. Confirm additional no-work/outcome-routing suite paths before editing.

## Reproducer
1. In the existing local runtime harness, use synthetic manual-cli-<ISSUE>-<TIMESTAMP> identity with matching WORKER_ISSUE_NUMBER and repository. Model implements and uses wrappers/bounded argv tools to merge its own exact head with a same-repository closing reference. Issue closes, canonical sync succeeds and cleanup receipt is finalized.
2. Model ends with an ordinary completion summary, without bare FULL_LOOP_COMPLETE/TASK_COMPLETE or POST_PR_HANDOFF and without a literal gh pr create/merge command; raw runtime exits naturally with code 0.
3. Invoke existing success-output classification and finalization. Parser rejects the output; PR-less backstop rejects the own PR and/or squash head; result becomes premature_exit/code 77 and recommends continuation despite delivered objective.
Use synthetic fixtures rather than the original completed issue or protected logs; verification uses the existing local harness.

## Acceptance and compatibility
Reconcile verified own merged-PR completion before premature-exit/continuation decisions. Bind evidence to current issue, repository, session/attempt, worker branch/head, fresh merged PR, exact closing linkage and guarded receipt where applicable; preserve proven state through finalization. Extend existing fixtures for own squash-merged closing PR plus finalized receipt and natural exit, including the negative controls. Run existing no-work and worker-outcome-routing suites after confirming paths. Assert raw exit 0 remains observable, terminal objective is success and no continuation is scheduled. No new test infrastructure or live API spend required.

This is a worker-ready implementation bug eligible for normal automatic dispatch. The reporting session does not personally launch workers. Preserve the existing completed worker session and never resume or reopen the original closed issue. Retain all genuine permission, security, trust, publication and guarded-cleanup gates; use sanitized local fixtures for verification.

title: t18769: Playwright-first browser preference: headed-hidden mode and explicit Playwrig...
body:
**Task ID:** `t18769` | **Status:** open
**Assignee:** @marcusquinn | **Logged:** 2026-10-25 | **Started:** 2026-10-25
**Tags:** `feat` `interactive`

## Outcome

Playwright-first browser preference: headed-hidden mode and explicit Playwright/Playwriter disambiguation

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Make the browser-automation preference explicit and enforceable:

1. Playwright is the default for all browser work, in one of three modes: headless (default), headed, or **headed-hidden** (new).
2. Playwriter is used only when the user names "Playwriter" explicitly.
3. Every routing surface states that Playwright and Playwriter are different tools, so a model must not auto-correct one name into the other.

## Why

The operator finds Playwriter slow to start and use (selected-tab relay handoff, GH#35516) and prefers Playwright. The two names differ by a few letters, which risks a model substituting one for the other when routing or delegating. "Headed but hidden" is not available today: `AIDEVOPS_PLAYWRIGHT_HEADED=1` opens a visible window.

Probe evidence (2026-10-25, macOS, Brave, playwright-core 1.64.1):

- `--window-position=-32000,-32000` does not hide the window on macOS; it was clamped onto a secondary display (`left: -1728`), and Brave took focus.
- CDP `Browser.setWindowBounds {windowState: "minimized"}` per page keeps the browser headed and fully working: rAF ran at 60 fps, `visibilityState` stayed `visible`, the UA was not headless, and screenshots (41 ms), clicks, and a second page all worked.
- Launch can take focus depending on the user's activity. `lsappinfo setfront` returns `permErr`; LaunchServices `open -b <bundle-id>` needs no extra permission. Restoring focus must be guarded so it runs only when the frontmost app is the MCP's own browser child process (one run showed the user's app still in front).

## How

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-registry.mjs`: in `playwrightMcpCommand()`, accept `AIDEVOPS_PLAYWRIGHT_HEADED=hidden`. It drops `--headless` and adds `--init-page <scripts/playwright-headed-hidden-init.cjs>`. Headless-runtime markers still force headless. Update the `playwright` and `playwriter` descriptions/guidance to name the tools explicitly.
- NEW `.agents/scripts/playwright-headed-hidden-init.cjs`: a Playwright MCP init-page hook that minimises each page window through CDP, then restores focus on macOS only if the browser is the frontmost app. It never throws.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-mcp-activation.mjs`: extend the headed test with the hidden mode.
- Docs: `tools/browser/browser-automation.md`, `tools/browser/playwright.md`, `tools/browser/playwriter.md`, `build-plus.md` (Domain Expertise row), `reference/agent-routing.md`, `configs/prompt-hook-candidates.conf` (Task guard candidate).

## Acceptance

- `AIDEVOPS_PLAYWRIGHT_HEADED=hidden` generates an MCP command without `--headless` and with `--init-page`; worker/CI markers still produce `--headless`.
- A live `@playwright/mcp@0.0.79` run in hidden mode navigates and snapshots a page, and its window ends minimised.
- Playwright vs Playwriter disambiguation appears in browser-automation, playwright, playwriter, build-plus, agent-routing and both MCP registry descriptions.
- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-mcp-activation.mjs` and markdownlint pass.

## Files Scope

- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-registry.mjs
- .agents/scripts/playwright-headed-hidden-init.cjs
- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-mcp-activation.mjs

- .agents/tools/browser/playwright.md

title: Bug: blocked-checkpoint approval rejects private-org-member runners (author_association=CONTRIBUTOR) in pr_checkpoint_events trust
body:
## Observed

On a private org-owned managed repo, a runner whose account has **admin** repository permission (`gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/collaborators/LOGIN/permission` → `admin`) posts its coordination comments with `author_association: CONTRIBUTOR` (private org membership is not exposed to the comment payload).

The blocked-checkpoint approval path then rejects that runner's own, unedited evidence:

```text
$ pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh approval-template OWNER/REPO <pr> <issue> <release_comment_id> attempt:<id>
approval-template: release <release_comment_id> is not a trusted CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked by <runner> closing attempt:<id>; dispatch-approved would reject this approval, so none was generated
```

Verified for one case on 2026-10-25:

- Release comment: `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked runner=<runner>`, `created_at == updated_at`, `author_association=CONTRIBUTOR`.
- Prior ready lease by the same login: `DISPATCH_LEASE phase=ready ... attempt_id=attempt:<id>` (attempt matches exactly), also `CONTRIBUTOR`.
- The runner's repo permission is `admin`.

Pulse emits `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION` for these drafts and tells the brief owner to publish an `approval-template` line, but no approval can be generated. In that repo, more than ten green draft checkpoint PRs (lane-batch data PRs whose Finder verification failed on a transient sign-in network error) remain stuck. Their issues are skipped every cycle with `cross-cycle block:worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked`, which leaves slots idle.

## Root cause

Trust is decided only from `author_association`:

- `.agents/scripts/pr_checkpoint_events.py` — `TRUSTED = {"OWNER", "MEMBER", "COLLABORATOR"}` and `trusted()`, used by `release_for`, `ready_leases`, `events` and `successors_valid`.
- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` — `_PCC_JQ_RELEASE_DEFS` `def trusted` (about line 51), and the inline association filter (about line 549).
- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-revision.py` consumes the predicates above.

This is the same family as GH#34644, GH#34703, GH#34875, GH#35268, GH#35355 and GH#35569, which were fixed for dispatch claims, linked-issue checks and terminal-blocker recovery. They were not fixed for the checkpoint continuation/approval path.

## Fix direction

Reuse the existing permission-backed elevation pattern. Do not invent a new one:

- Reference: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-trust.sh` `_claim_permission_trusted_authors` (it resolves `CONTRIBUTOR`/`NONE` authors once per snapshot through `_gh_actor_has_repo_write_authority` from `shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh`, marked `#aidevops:trust-boundary`).
- In `pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`, compute the permission-trusted login list for the fetched comment snapshot and pass it into the jq defs (for example `--argjson trusted_logins`) and into the Python payload (for example a `trusted_logins` field). Then extend `trusted()` in both places so that a comment is also trusted when its login is in that list. The unedited-comment requirement stays unchanged.
- Never derive trust from body fields. Edited comments must remain untrusted. External/read-only authors must remain untrusted.

## Files to modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pr_checkpoint_events.py`
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-revision.py` (only if the payload plumbing needs it)
- Existing tests for these helpers under `.agents/scripts/tests/` (extend the closest existing checkpoint test with one private-member case, modelled on `tests/test-dispatch-lease-claims-private-member.sh`)

## Verification

1. A `CONTRIBUTOR` author with write/maintain/admin permission: `approval-template` prints a `CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_APPROVED` line, and `validate` accepts the matching approval.
2. A `CONTRIBUTOR` author with read/none permission: still rejected.
3. Edited release/lease comments: still rejected.
4. ShellCheck is clean on the edited shell. The existing checkpoint tests pass.

## Acceptance

`approval-template` succeeds for blocked releases posted by private-org-member runners that have write authority. Pulse can then continue approved blocked checkpoints in private org repos.

title: Bug: large-file gate holds consolidation-task issues, deadlocking file-size-debt consolidation (#35614 <-> #28476)
body:
## Observed (2026-10-25)

The large-file simplification gate holds consolidation tasks that only rewrite an issue body. When the consolidation parent is itself the file-size-debt issue, the two issues deadlock:

- #28476 `file-size-debt: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh exceeds 2000 lines` has the labels `needs-consolidation` and `consolidation-in-progress`, so it waits for its consolidation task.
- #35614 `consolidation-task: merge thread on #28476 into single spec` has the labels `consolidation-task` and `needs-simplification`. The pulse defers it every cycle:

```text
Large-file gate: #35614 in marcusquinn/aidevops targets .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh (2691 lines)
Dispatch deferred for #35614 in marcusquinn/aidevops: targets large file(s), simplification gate
Dispatch_max: #35614 (marcusquinn/aidevops) blocked:policy_gate benign dispatch block
```

Its gate comment names `Simplification issues: #28476 (existing)`. That is the parent the consolidation task is meant to unblock.

- Downstream, #35612 (bug: worker completion misclassified as premature_exit) is also held behind #28476.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh` `_large_file_gate_precheck_labels` exempts `simplification`, `file-size-debt`, `function-complexity-debt`, `simplification-debt`, `parent-task` and `meta`, but not `consolidation-task`. A consolidation task's write surface is the parent issue body (via the consolidation workflow). It never edits the referenced source file, so the context-budget rationale for the gate does not apply. The gate matches the parent's quoted file path inside the inlined parent body.

## Fix

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh`: in `_large_file_gate_precheck_labels`, treat `consolidation-task` the same way as the existing `parent-task`/`meta` exemption. Return early, and auto-clear a stale `needs-simplification` label with the same remove-and-log pattern used at the `parent-task` branch (about lines 99-111).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-core-consolidated-label.sh` or the closest existing large-file-gate test: add one case where a `consolidation-task` issue that references a >2000-line file is not held.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-core-consolidated-label.sh`

## Verification

1. The existing large-file gate tests pass. ShellCheck is clean on the edited script.
2. A `consolidation-task` issue whose inlined parent body references a >2000-line file returns the exemption code without applying `needs-simplification`.
3. Ordinary implementation issues that target the same file are still held.
4. After deploy, #35614 dispatches and the `needs-simplification` label is cleared on the next cycle.

title: consolidated: simplify headless worker while preserving merged preparation split
body:
_Supersedes #28476 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Simplify `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh` to fewer than 2000 lines by extracting cohesive function groups into focused, guarded modules, retaining a thin orchestrator and unchanged worker entry point and behavior. Build on the already-merged preparation extraction rather than repeating or reverting it.

## Why

The large-file simplification gate originally reported that #28473 was blocked by this file exceeding 2000 lines. Workers spend excessive context reading the orchestrator instead of implementing changes. PR #28479 temporarily reduced the file from 2115 to 1866 lines, but current default-branch content checked during consolidation on 2026-10-25 is 2691 lines. The historical split is delivered; the current size objective is not. Recheck the current branch before implementation and avoid duplicating concurrent work.

## How

1. Read `.agents/reference/large-file-split.md`, especially identity-key preservation, CI false positives (section 4), and the PR body template. Use `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh` plus `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-lib.sh` as the simple include-guard and SCRIPT_DIR-fallback reference; `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh` and its sub-libraries are the complex precedent.
2. Preserve PR #28479 (merged 2026-07-22, merge commit `dfd165f96eee498e92b76eb783ae029ab2569b14`). Per @alex-solovyev, that change extracted worker launch preparation, retry selection, detach, and stall-cap helpers into `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker-prepare.sh`, with `_cmd_run_prepare` then at line 95. That line reference is historical, not an instruction to overwrite the current module. Both worker files exist on the current default branch and must retain EDIT markers.
3. Inspect current function boundaries in `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh`; extract further cohesive groups into guarded modules and source them from the original file. Preserve entry points, function identity, source ordering, SCRIPT_DIR fallback, and worker semantics. Additional module names must be chosen from current cohesive boundaries; before writing any additional path, persist the minimal corrected canonical Files Scope using the integration-scope recovery policy. Do not restart the completed extraction.
4. Run `wc -l .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh` and require fewer than 2000 lines. Run `bash -n` and ShellCheck on the orchestrator and every changed/extracted shell module. Run `bash tests/test-headless-runtime-helper.sh` through the existing runtime loading and preparation path, including prelaunch lease validation. Run `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh` with the applicable scoped checks and compare complexity against the PR base.
5. The original spec anticipates a file-split identity-key complexity regression: apply `complexity-bump-ok` and include a `## Complexity Bump Justification` section citing actual scanner evidence, following playbook section 4. Do not use a mechanical-relocation justification to conceal genuinely added complexity.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker-prepare.sh
- ADD: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker-invocation.sh
- ADD: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker-ownership.sh

Integration evidence (GH#35626): baseline b6301d54f has 2691 worker lines. Extract the invocation and early-output diagnostics block (lines 117–506) and worktree ownership/prelaunch-lease block (lines 1630–2015) verbatim into guarded modules, sourced at their original positions. Existing preparation stays intact. Current assigned worker owns this issue; exact-issue PR/branch discovery and prework collision checks found no salvageable or concurrent implementation. Verification: bash -n and ShellCheck on the orchestrator and both modules; bash tests/test-headless-runtime-helper.sh; scoped linters-local.sh --base-ref origin/main; complexity checks against the PR base.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The current worker orchestrator is fewer than 2000 lines, with cohesive extracted modules and a thin sourcing entry point.
- [ ] The already-merged launch preparation, retry selection, detach, and stall-cap extraction remains preserved and is not duplicated.
- [ ] Include guards and SCRIPT_DIR fallback follow the existing simple split precedent; source order, worker entry points, and runtime behavior are unchanged.
- [ ] `bash -n` and ShellCheck pass for changed modules; the existing runtime helper test exercises module loading and prelaunch lease validation.
- [ ] Applicable local lint and complexity checks pass; any identity-key false positive has scanner-backed justification and the prescribed label and PR body section.
- [ ] Any pre-existing or environment-dependent test failures are reported with baseline evidence rather than repaired out of scope.

## Context & Decisions

- Per @marcusquinn's self-hosting tier override on 2026-07-22: retain `tier:thinking`. The detector matched `pulse-dispatch-` in the parent body; dispatch-path changes are self-referential because workers execute through the code under modification. Applying the terminal workload tier upfront avoids wasted lower-tier attempts; runtime routing retains exact model/reasoning control. The source records `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_SELF_HOSTING_DETECTOR=1` as the detector bypass and the once-only `<!-- self-hosting-tier-override -->` marker in `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh` (t2819); this history does not authorize bypassing guards.
- Per @alex-solovyev's completion summary on 2026-07-22: PR #28479 extracted `_cmd_run_prepare` to the guarded preparation module; source size fell from 2115 to 1866 lines. Scanner evidence was base=0, head=0, new=0 function-complexity violations, supporting relocation rather than added complexity. The existing runtime helper test loaded the orchestrator, sourced the module, and executed preparation through prelaunch lease validation. `bash -n`, ShellCheck, and `linters-local.sh` passed for that revision. No additional key decisions were recorded.
- The same completion summary reports broad-test failures from stale `openai/gpt-5.3-codex` expectations versus then-configured `openai/gpt-5.4`, plus the live worker lease environment, neither caused by relocation. These are historical baseline observations, not proof of present failures: verify current runtime/configuration and baseline before attributing any new failure.
- The deterministic merge pass (`pulse-wrapper.sh`) confirmed PR #28479 merged to main. Current default-branch API checks confirm the worker and preparation modules both exist; the worker again exceeds the threshold. Consolidation preserves the delivered extraction while continuing the original size goal.
- Original provenance: generated by `large-file-simplification-gate` in `pulse-dispatch-core.sh` with threshold 2000; parent #28476, dependent context #28473. Consolidation task #35614 is operational and requires no implementation PR.

body:
## Consolidation target: #35612

**Parent issue:** #35612 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** Worker completion: own merged closing PR with finalized cleanup is falsely classified premature_exit
**Parent labels:** `bug,status:available,auto-dispatch,tier:thinking,origin:worker,consolidation-in-progress`

> Sources are inlined below unless explicitly listed as omitted. Fetch omitted references before consolidating.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below, fetching any explicitly omitted sources first.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
     Preserve every wildcard scope entry verbatim from every superseded issue, including tool-generated paths such as `- NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Never invent a concrete machine, date, timestamp or filename in place of a pattern. Never change an existing `EDIT:` entry to `NEW:`.
     Check each path against the current default branch before copying its scope marker: use `git ls-files` in an up-to-date default-branch checkout or `gh api` for that branch's contents. Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.
   - **Runner prerequisites** — copy verbatim every line matching `^requires-secrets:` and its runner-prerequisite paragraph from every superseded issue. Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #35612 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`

3. **Validate before filing the new consolidated issue.** Save the parent body (inlined or explicitly fetched) verbatim to a local file, plus a separate body file for each additional superseded issue. Validate the merged body against ALL sources; a failed check stops publication and parent closure until the merged body is repaired:

```bash
python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/consolidation-contract-validator.py \
  --source "<file containing the verbatim parent body>" \
  --successor "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
# Repeat --source for each additional superseded issue body.
```

The validator must pass before running the signed creation command below. It checks verbatim secret lines and prerequisite paragraphs, wildcard scope preservation, and EDIT-to-NEW regressions. Also run `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check` on the merged body for ordinary scope syntax validation.

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,status:available,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding all status:* labels, needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body-file "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Use the signed wrapper above rather than the raw GitHub CLI so the successor retains the managed signature and origin metadata.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` and `status:available` are also mandatory. Keep exactly one `status:*` label on the successor: `status:available`, never the parent's lifecycle status. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch; the fill-floor enumerator also needs the available status.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close the parent #35612:**

```bash
gh issue comment 35612 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 35612 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 35612 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
# Repoint open dependants' blockedBy edges and Blocked-by lines at the successor (GH#35130):
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dependency-supersession-repoint-helper.sh repoint "marcusquinn/aidevops" 35612 $NEW_NUM
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #35612 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @vladimirdulov."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- Read only explicitly omitted source references when the packet size limit prevents inlining them; otherwise do NOT re-read #35612.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @alex-solovyev @vladimirdulov

title: consolidated: reconcile verified own merged-PR worker completion before premature_exit
body:
_Supersedes #35612 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Fix worker completion reconciliation so a worker that merges its own exact-head closing PR, verifies delivery, synchronizes canonical, finalizes guarded cleanup and naturally exits 0 is classified as objective success even without prose completion markers or literal direct PR commands. Preserve verified completion through finalization without weakening PR-less guards or genuine security gates.

## Why

Per @alex-solovyev, completed implementation was falsely classified as `premature_exit`, classifier exit 77, `model_stopped_before_completion`, and `resume_session_with_completion_contract`. This is false completion classification, not unfinished implementation, and can trigger retries, model penalties and failure mining against delivered work.

### Sanitized evidence (2026-10-25)

Protected excerpt line 28: merge succeeded, required checks terminal-success, review gate PASS, linked closure converged. Line 31: canonical fast-forward succeeded (exit 0). Line 35: worker readback confirmed MERGED PR, CLOSED issue and one MERGE_SUMMARY. Line 47: cleanup receipt finalized, release:not-requested (exit 0). Line 53: final answer reports delivered implementation, merge, sync and finalized cleanup. Lines 106-109: raw and structured exit_code=0, kill_reason=natural, then cause=premature_exit with no provider error. Correlated headless-runtime-metrics row records exit_code=77, activity=true, natural exit and resume recommendation. Replaying the installed output_has_completion_signal Python parser against the excerpt returned 1.
Fresh independent gh pr view confirmed MERGED, merge commit and exact same-repository closing linkage; gh issue view confirmed CLOSED one second after merge. All private repo names, issue/PR numbers, session/attempt IDs, local paths, domain content and raw logs are omitted from this public brief. Protected evidence remains local and is not a worker dependency.

### Deduplication and compatibility

The parent searched all-state framework issues for premature_exit, model_stopped_before_completion, premature titles and merged-completion classification. Related repairs are #32529 (argv parser crash), #33331 (continuation visibility), #33672 via #33674 (PR-less terminal outcomes), and #27907 (attempt reconciliation). No exact own-merged-PR repair was found. Deployed code already includes #33672, but its verifier requires no PR on the worker branch and no commits ahead of the default tip; that cannot prove own-PR/squash-merge completion. Do not weaken PR-less guards globally. Consolidation discovery found no linked PR for #35612 or #35628, no pushed issue branch, and no prior successor.

## How

Edit repository `.agents/scripts/`, never deployed files. The parent supplied these bounded source references; revalidate offsets and runtime/dependency versions before implementation:

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-result.sh:158-254`, especially 240-249: success gate only falls back to PR-less completion before returning 77. Reconcile verified own merged-PR completion before premature-exit decisions.
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh:668`: `output_has_completion_signal` parses model markers and direct PR commands; wrapper/bounded-tool lifecycle completion need not contain either.
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh:1375-1466`: terminal backstop delegates to PR-less cleanliness even for delivered merged linkage. Inspect final reconciled-outcome handling too; preserve proven completion through finalization.
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:492-516`: maps premature exit to stopped-before-completion and a resume recommendation. Verified objective success must not take this route.
- Extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-provider-tests.sh` through the existing read-only harness `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-helper.sh`. Confirm existing no-work and worker-outcome-routing suite paths before running them; no new test infrastructure.

Reuse existing exact-head, exact same-repository closing-linkage and guarded cleanup-receipt proof patterns bound to the current attempt. Evidence must identify the current issue, repository, session/attempt, worker branch/head, fresh merged PR and guarded receipt where applicable. Keep raw process events queryable separately from reconciled objective success.

### Reproducer

1. In the existing local harness, use synthetic `manual-cli-<ISSUE>-<TIMESTAMP>` identity with matching `WORKER_ISSUE_NUMBER` and repository. Model implements and uses wrappers/bounded argv tools to merge its own exact head with a same-repository closing reference; issue closes, canonical sync succeeds and cleanup receipt finalizes.
2. End with an ordinary completion summary, without bare `FULL_LOOP_COMPLETE`/`TASK_COMPLETE` or `POST_PR_HANDOFF`, and without literal `gh pr create`/`gh pr merge`; raw runtime exits naturally with code 0.
3. Invoke existing success-output classification and finalization. Before repair, parser rejects output and PR-less backstop rejects own PR and/or squash head, producing premature exit/code 77 and continuation despite delivery.

Use synthetic fixtures rather than the original completed issue or protected logs; verification uses the existing local harness without live API spend.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Verified own merged-PR completion is reconciled before premature-exit/continuation decisions and survives finalization, including own squash-merged closing PR, finalized receipt, ordinary summary, wrappers/bounded tools and natural exit 0.
- [ ] Proof binds current issue, repository, session/attempt, worker branch/head, fresh merged PR, exact closing linkage and guarded receipt where applicable; unreadable or unverified evidence fails closed.
- [ ] Raw exit 0 and natural process events remain separately observable; reconciled objective is success, with no retry, model penalty, failure mining or resume recommendation solely for missing prose markers.
- [ ] Negative fixtures reject open issues, unmerged/unrelated/mismatched PRs, non-closing partial merges, unpublished local edits, stale/foreign receipts, unreadable/unverified evidence, synthetic/tool-result marker mentions and genuine silent stops.
- [ ] Existing PR-less guards remain intact; no permission, security, publication, trust or guarded-cleanup waiver is introduced.
- [ ] ShellCheck passes on changed scripts and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-helper.sh` passes with the extended existing fixtures. Existing no-work and worker-outcome-routing suites pass after confirming their paths. No new test infrastructure or live API spend is required.
- [ ] Preserve the existing completed worker session; never resume or reopen the original closed issue. Use sanitized local fixtures only.

### Files Scope
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-result.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh

## Runner prerequisites

The supplied parent and substantive comments contain no secret requirements or runner-prerequisite paragraphs to carry over. Protected logs and the original completed session are not worker dependencies; use the existing local harness and synthetic fixtures.

## Context & Decisions

- Per @alex-solovyev: this is a worker-ready implementation bug eligible for normal automatic dispatch; the reporting session does not personally launch workers. Retain genuine permission, security, trust, publication and guarded-cleanup gates. Broadening marker matching or weakening PR-less guards is not a substitute for verified own-PR reconciliation.
- Per @alex-solovyev's 2026-10-25T11:45:12Z self-hosting override: retain `tier:thinking`. The detector matched `headless-runtime-helper.sh`; workers execute through the dispatch path being repaired, so the terminal workload tier avoids wasted lower-tier attempts while runtime routing controls the exact model and reasoning level. The documented detector bypass is `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_SELF_HOSTING_DETECTOR=1`; this brief does not request or apply it.
- Per @vladimirdulov's 2026-10-25T16:01:55Z simplification-gate-cleared comment: the previous held-from-dispatch note no longer applies. Re-evaluation found cited references within the scoped-range bypass (≤ 300 lines per range) or the target simplified below 2000 lines. `needs-simplification` was removed and the issue is open for dispatch. Preserve bounded reference ranges rather than reinstating the superseded hold.
- Consolidation #35628 preserves the five inherited EDIT paths, each confirmed present on current default branch `main`. Harness and additional suite references are read-only, not extra write scope. The implementation successor, unlike this operational consolidation task, follows the normal worktree/PR lifecycle.

title: t18770: Guard Playwriter Task/MCP connect behind an explicit user mention (Playwright is the default)
body:
## Task


Add an OpenCode plugin guard so Playwriter can be selected only when the user's own latest message names it. In interactive sessions, block a `task` call with `subagent_type: "playwriter"` and an `aidevops_mcp` call with `{action: "connect", name: "playwriter"}` unless the most recent user message in the root session contains `playwriter` (case-insensitive). The block message must say: "Playwriter (extension relay) is not Playwright. Use subagent_type playwright / @playwright unless the user writes 'Playwriter'."

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Add an OpenCode plugin guard so Playwriter can be selected only when the user's own latest message names it. In interactive sessions, block a `task` call with `subagent_type: "playwriter"` and an `aidevops_mcp` call with `{action: "connect", name: "playwriter"}` unless the most recent user message in the root session contains `playwriter` (case-insensitive). The block message must say: "Playwriter (extension relay) is not Playwright. Use subagent_type playwright / @playwright unless the user writes 'Playwriter'."

## Why

GH#35617 (PR #35618) made Playwright the default browser tool and Playwriter explicit-name-only, but only through prompt guidance. The two names differ by a few letters, and a model can auto-correct "Playwright" into "Playwriter" when routing or delegating. That launches the slow relay handoff the operator wants to avoid. `.agents/configs/prompt-hook-candidates.conf` records this as the `Playwright versus Playwriter selection` candidate (status `candidate`).

## How

- Reference pattern: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/browser-task-transport.mjs` (`assertBrowserTaskTransport`), a `tool.execute.before` Task guard keyed on `args.subagent_type`, wired from `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs` (`"tool.execute.before"` near line 741). Tests: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-browser-task-transport.mjs`.
- NEW `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/playwriter-selection-guard.mjs`: export a pure `assertPlaywriterExplicitlyRequested({ tool, args, latestUserText })` and a small resolver for the latest user message text. Inspect how existing plugin code reads session messages before choosing an API. If the latest user text cannot be resolved, fail open (allow) and log once, so a lookup failure does not break explicit Playwriter use.
- Wire it into `index.mjs` `tool.execute.before` beside the browser-task-transport guard. Scope it to `task` and `aidevops_mcp` only. Headless sessions are unaffected: Playwriter is already interactive-only.
- Update `.agents/configs/prompt-hook-candidates.conf`: change the row's STATUS to `partial` (prompt guidance stays for non-OpenCode runtimes) and set ENFORCEMENT to the new module.
- Add focused cases to a new `tests/test-playwriter-selection-guard.mjs` following the `test-browser-task-transport.mjs` style:
  - "use playwright headed" → playwriter Task blocked
  - "connect Playwriter" → allowed
  - playwright Task → untouched
  - non-browser tool → untouched

- A playwriter Task or MCP connect is blocked, with the disambiguation message, when the latest user message lacks "playwriter"; it is allowed when the message contains it.
- `playwright` and all other tools are unaffected.
- `node --test` passes for the new test and the existing `test-browser-task-transport.mjs` and `test-mcp-activation.mjs`.
- The prompt-hook-candidates row is updated, and `.agents/scripts/progressive-load-check.sh` passes.

title: fix(cloudron): catalog publish drops releases when main moves mid-run; add automatic reconcile
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->
## What

The reusable Cloudron catalog workflow loses releases when `main` moves while a publish job runs. A merged version bump then stays unpublished until some later non-skip-CI push to `main` happens to trigger reconciliation.

Evidence from package repos on 2026-10-23..25: the `publish` job's atomic push failed with `! [rejected] HEAD -> main (non-fast-forward)` and `vX.Y.Z -> vX.Y.Z (atomic push failed)`:

- `cloudron-opendesk-app` 0.2.3 (run 39915281814): never published. 0.2.5 (run 40154168205): still unpublished. `main` is a metrics commit with the skip-CI marker, pushed one minute after the merge.
- `cloudron-headscale-app` 0.1.2 (run 40157688790): published five hours later, only because a star-history push re-ran the workflow.

The racing commits come from the repos' own metrics and star-history workflows. They touch only README, metrics and SVG files.

## Files Scope

- `.github/workflows/cloudron-catalog-publish-reusable.yml`
- `.agents/scripts/cloudron-package-monitor-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-package-monitor.sh`
- `.agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-app-publishing-skill.md`

## File notes

- Reusable workflow: the `publish` job runs `git push --atomic origin HEAD:refs/heads/main "refs/tags/v$VERSION"` (`rg -n "git push --atomic" .github/workflows/cloudron-catalog-publish-reusable.yml`). On a non-fast-forward rejection, fetch `main`. If every commit between the validated SHA and `origin/main` touches only paths outside the package build inputs (allowlist: `README.md`, metrics or star-history assets, `docs/`), rebase the catalog-only commit onto `origin/main`. Then re-verify that the validated SHA is an ancestor and retry once. Otherwise fail closed, as the workflow does now.
- Monitor: add a reconcile check. If the manifest `version` on the remote default branch is absent from `CloudronVersions.json`, publication is enabled and no catalog run is in progress, report it. With `--apply`, run `gh workflow run cloudron-catalog-publish.yml --ref main` once per version, deduplicated. The merge already authorized publication, so this adds no new release authority.
- Skill doc: replace "rerun against the new revision after review" with the automatic path and its fail-closed limits.

## Acceptance criteria

- A docs-only commit that lands on `main` during a publish no longer drops the release.
- A drifted `main` version (manifest version not in the catalog) gets published by the next daily monitor run without human action.
- Package-source drift between the validated SHA and `main` still fails closed.

## Verification

`bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-package-monitor.sh`; `shellcheck .agents/scripts/cloudron-package-monitor-helper.sh`; `actionlint .github/workflows/cloudron-catalog-publish-reusable.yml`. Live check: after the caller pin update, `cloudron-opendesk-app` 0.2.5 is published.

title: fix(cloudron): PR preflight never builds the package image, so build breaks surface only after merge

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->
## What

PR preflight in the reusable Cloudron catalog workflow never builds the package image. On pull requests the `build` job is skipped (`needs.preflight.outputs.publish == 'true'` only on `main`). Worker update PRs therefore pass every check and merge, and the image build only fails after the merge, on `main`.

Evidence: `aidevops-cloudron-app` has five consecutive failed `main` catalog runs: 39387876739, 39540551017, 39722582957, 39826217335 and 40186373867. All fail at `npm install -g aidevops@X` with `npm error Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')`. Every matching PR preflight was green. The catalog has been stuck at 0.1.35 since 2026-10-10, while `main` is at 0.1.39.

## Files Scope

- `.github/workflows/cloudron-catalog-publish-reusable.yml`
- `.agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-app-publishing-skill.md`

## File notes

- Reusable workflow: add a no-push `linux/amd64` `docker buildx build` to PR preflight (or a PR-only build job), with no registry credentials and read-only permissions. Reuse the build arguments of the `main` build job so both paths stay identical. Give the job a bounded timeout.
- Skill doc, "Managed Catalog Workflow": state that PR preflight proves the image builds, and that publication still happens only on `main`.

## Acceptance criteria

- A PR whose Dockerfile fails to build gets a failing required check before merge.
- No publication credentials or GHCR write tokens are available to PR jobs.

## Verification

`actionlint .github/workflows/cloudron-catalog-publish-reusable.yml`. Then, in a package repo, temporarily point the caller at the branch SHA and confirm that a PR with a broken `RUN` step fails preflight.

body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->
## What

`npm install -g aidevops@3.39.x` fails on npm 10.x, the npm bundled with Node 20 LTS. Root `package.json` declares `"engines": {"node": ">=20.0.0"}`, so Node 20 is a supported platform.

The published root package lists GUI build tooling (`vite`, `@vitejs/plugin-react`) as runtime `dependencies`. These pull in the peer graph that crashes Arborist, although the `aidevops` CLI does not need them.

### Files Scope

- `package.json`
- `bun.lock`

## File notes

- `package.json`: move GUI-only build tooling (`vite`, `@vitejs/plugin-react`) out of root runtime `dependencies`. Keep it in the GUI workspace packages or in `devDependencies`. Root `setup:bun` requires a frozen Bun lockfile, so updating it is directly necessary. title: t18771: Strict no-redirect-link policy: auto-close spam, block authors, never open re...
body:
**Task ID:** `t18771` | **Status:** open
**Assignee:** @marcusquinn | **Logged:** 2026-10-25 | **Started:** 2026-10-25
**Tags:** `feat` `priority:high` `security` `interactive`

## Outcome

Strict no-redirect-link policy: auto-close spam, block authors, never open redirect links

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Enforce a strict, deterministic **no-redirect-links** policy for public contributions and for every aidevops session:

1. Any issue, PR, comment, review comment, discussion, or discussion comment from a non-collaborator that contains a URL-shortener or redirector link is spam. It is closed or hidden, labelled `spam`, and locked **without any comment**. The author is blocked from every repository the maintainer controls.
2. aidevops never resolves, fetches, or opens a redirect link, in interactive sessions, workers, or the pulse. That covers Bash network clients (`curl`, `wget`, `open`, ...), OpenCode tools with URL arguments (WebFetch, browser MCP navigation), and Claude Code `WebFetch`/MCP tools.

## Why

Issue #35640 was templated star-exchange spam: a security-themed title, engagement bait, and an anchor-masked URL-shortener link. The same title template was filed against several public repositories about an hour apart from a 9-day-old account with no footprint. Evidence gathered during review:

- `external-content-spam-detector.sh score issue 35640` → `score 2, verdict clean`. `bounty-spam-detector.sh` → `clean`. Neither has a redirect-link signal, and `prompt-injection-patterns.yaml` has no shortener pattern.
- `external-content-spam-detector.sh` is not wired into any workflow or the pulse.
- `.github/workflows/issue-triage-gate.yml` publicly thanked and @-mentioned the spammer (welcome comment) before any spam check.
- `maintainer-gate-reusable.yml` "Protect Triage Labels" posted a label-protection notice on the spam issue after maintainer cleanup.
- Nothing scans `issue_comment`, `pull_request_review_comment`, or discussion content for spam.
- No framework capability blocks users. Actions `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot call `PUT /user/blocks`, so bans need the maintainer token (pulse).
- The "never fetch untrusted URLs" rule in `reference/gh-command-discipline.md` is prompt-only. `network-tiers.conf` denies only 5 shorteners, and only for sandboxed workers ("Interactive sessions are unrestricted").
- Resolving a link, even in a remote sandbox, credits the campaign through per-account UTM attribution. Detection must therefore be host-based and never resolve.

## How

- Single source of truth: `.agents/configs/redirect-hosts.conf`. One host, `*.host` wildcard, or `host/path-prefix` per line.
- Pure scanner `.agents/scripts/redirect_link_policy.py` (`scan`, `check-url`, `check-argv`). It normalises obfuscation (zero-width characters, fullwidth/ideographic dots, `[.]`/`(.)`, `hxxp`, percent-encoded hosts), matches scheme URLs, markdown/HTML links, and bare `host/path` tokens with boundaries, and never performs network I/O.
- `.agents/scripts/redirect-link-guard-helper.sh`: `enforce` (close/hide + `spam` label + lock, no comment) and `block` (user-level plus admin orgs; never OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR or bots). It also provides `sweep` and is sourceable by the pulse (`redirect_spam_sweep_all_repos`, interval-gated).
- `.github/workflows/redirect-link-spam-guard.yml`: base checkout only and trusted-author skip (`#aidevops:trust-boundary`), covering issues, `pull_request_target`, issue/PR-review comments, and discussions.
- Triage gates suppress the welcome comment for redirect-link spam. The label-protection notice is skipped for closed or `spam` issues; NMR re-application is unchanged.
- Command policy: new `command_policy_redirect.py` decision evaluated for **all** sessions (not only workers) in `command_policy_evaluation.py`.
- OpenCode: `quality-hooks-redirect-link.mjs` checks URL-bearing tool args before execution.
- Claude Code: `git_safety_guard.py` handles `WebFetch|mcp__.*` URL args. `install-hooks-helper.sh` registers that matcher.
- Docs: `CONTRIBUTING.md` link policy, `reference/gh-command-discipline.md`, `workflows/review-issue-pr.md` (spam closures: no comment, keep NMR), plus the spam signal in `external-content-spam-detector.sh`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/configs/redirect-hosts.conf`
- `.agents/scripts/redirect_link_policy.py`
- `.agents/scripts/redirect_link_rules.py`
- `.agents/scripts/redirect_link_tool_check.py`
- `.agents/scripts/redirect-link-guard-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/command_policy_redirect.py`
- `.agents/scripts/command_policy_evaluation.py`
- `.agents/scripts/external-content-spam-detector.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/install-hooks-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-redirect-link-policy.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-maintenance-selector-contract.sh`
- `TODO.md`
- `todo/tasks/t18771-brief.md`
- `.agents/hooks/git_safety_guard.py`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-redirect-link.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks.mjs`
- `.github/workflows/redirect-link-spam-guard.yml`
- `.github/workflows/issue-triage-gate.yml`
- `.github/workflows/pr-triage-gate.yml`
- `.github/workflows/maintainer-gate-reusable.yml`
- `.agents/reference/gh-command-discipline.md`
- `.agents/workflows/review-issue-pr.md`
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `redirect_link_policy.py scan` flags shortener links in scheme, markdown, HTML, bare, and obfuscated forms, and does not flag ordinary GitHub/docs links or lookalike hosts (`this.gd`, `notbit.ly`).

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-redirect-link-policy.sh"
  ```

- [ ] The shared command policy forbids `curl`/`wget`/`open` of a redirect host in an interactive (non-worker) evaluation and still allows ordinary hosts.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "python3 .agents/scripts/command-policy-helper.py check-command --cwd . --command 'curl https://bit.ly/x'; test $? -eq 20"
  ```

- [ ] Enforcement never posts a comment, never resolves the link, and never acts on OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR or bot authors.
- [ ] `external-content-spam-detector.sh` scores a redirect-link body from a non-collaborator as `spam-likely`.
- [ ] ShellCheck clean on changed shell files; workflow YAML parses.

## Context & Decisions

- Maintainer decision: ban **every** redirect link; there is no legitimate need for one. The maintainer's own sites are not on the list, so no exception mechanism is published.
- Spam closures carry no comment (no attention, no notification payload). NMR stays applied by design on closed spam.
- Detection is host-based only. Destinations are never resolved, even in sandboxes.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Brief workflow contract</summary>

## Brief Workflow

This issue body is composed under `.agents/workflows/brief.md`. Newly queued auto-dispatch work must pass its `Dispatch Readiness Contract (brief schema v2)`: complete write surface, hazards and compatibility, executable verification mapped to affected surfaces, and positive plus negative/regression acceptance criteria.

</details>

title: feat(cloudron): signed release-approval issues so approved upstream updates publish automatically
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->
## What

Add a signed release-approval gate for Cloudron package updates. A maintainer-approved release then completes without further human steps.

Today, monitor briefs forbid publication (`cloudron-package-monitor-helper.sh` brief: "Do not publish a release… without separate operator authorization"). Merging a version bump to `main` publishes through `cloudron-catalog-publish.yml`. Workers therefore finish a tested PR, label it `hold-for-review` and stop. Nothing tells the maintainer a release is waiting, so update PRs sit for days or weeks. Examples: cloudron-netbird-app PR #202 and cloudron-buzz-app PR #89.

Maintainer decision (2026-10-25): when an upstream update needs a package release, log a release issue. The maintainer runs `sudo aidevops approve issue <N> <repo>` on it, and automation then cuts the release.

**Design constraint:** do not use `needs-maintainer-review` for this gate. Workers post as the maintainer's account, so the issue author is write-authorized. `auto_approve_maintainer_issues` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh`, `issue_has_required_approval` and `_nmr_translate_trusted_author_hold`) normalizes trusted-author NMR to `hold-for-review` or clears it, without any signature. Use a dedicated label that only a verified signed approval can satisfy, e.g. `release-approval-required`.

## Flow

1. The worker completes the update PR: version bump, both changelogs, package tests, `preflight-release`, and a green PR preflight (plus the image build once GH#35650 lands). It leaves the PR open, unmerged.
2. The worker (or the helper below) files `Release <package> v<version>` in the package repo, labelled `release-approval-required` and not `auto-dispatch`. The body contains the PR number, exact head SHA, package and upstream versions, the changelog entry and the evidence. Deduplicate by a `<!-- aidevops:cloudron-release-approval <version> -->` marker. A newer release issue for the same package supersedes older unapproved ones (close them and link the new one).
3. The maintainer runs `sudo aidevops approve issue <N> <repo>`. The snapshot-v2 payload binds the issue content, including the head SHA.
4. A frequent routine processes approved release issues. For each one it must:
   - Verify `approval-helper.sh verify issue <N> <repo> --require-authority` returns `VERIFIED`.
   - Check that the PR is open, its head equals the SHA recorded in the approved issue body and its checks are green.
   - Merge through `full-loop-helper.sh merge <PR> <repo> --squash`.
   - Wait, bounded, for the `main` catalog run. On a non-fast-forward failure, `gh workflow run cloudron-catalog-publish.yml --ref main` once (until GH#35649 lands).
   - Verify that `CloudronVersions.json` contains the version, tag `v<version>` exists and the GitHub release exists.
   - Close the issue with that evidence.
   If the head SHA changed, comment and request re-approval instead of merging. Fail closed on any verification error.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge-authority.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/cloudron-package-monitor-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/routines/core-routines.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-release-approval.sh`
- `.agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-app-packaging.md`
- `.agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-app-publishing-skill.md`

## File notes

- `cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh` (new): subcommands `request <repo> <pr>` (files the release issue) and `process [--apply]` (handles approved issues across `app_type == "cloudron-package"` repos in `repos.json`). Source `shared-constants.sh`. Use `gh_create_issue` / `gh_issue_comment` wrappers. Mark trust checks with `#aidevops:trust-boundary`. Bash 3.2 compatible, with explicit returns.
- `cloudron-package-monitor-helper.sh` (`_cloudron_monitor_create_issue` acceptance criteria): replace the "do not publish" line with: "Prepare and verify the release PR, then run `cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh request <repo> <pr>`; do not merge. Merge and publication happen only after signed maintainer approval of the release issue."
- `core-routines.sh`: add a routine (next free `r9xx` ID) running `scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh process --apply` every 30 minutes, following the `r916` line format and its `describe_*` function.
- Docs: in "Managed Package Lifecycle" / "Publication boundary", document the states (upstream detected → release PR ready → release approval requested → approved → published) and the single maintainer command.

## Acceptance criteria

- An unapproved release issue never results in a merge.
- An approved issue whose PR head changed after approval does not merge, and posts a re-approval request.
- A verified approval with a matching head results in merge, catalog entry, tag and GitHub release, and the issue is closed with evidence, with no further human action.
- `needs-maintainer-review` semantics are unchanged.

## Verification

`bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-release-approval.sh` (stub `gh` and `approval-helper.sh verify`; cover unapproved, approved+matching head, approved+changed head, and verify API error). Also `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-package-monitor.sh`, `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-package-routines.sh`, and `shellcheck` on the changed scripts. Live: the next upstream update in cloudron-netbird-app reaches a published catalog entry after one `sudo aidevops approve issue`.

title: Guard clean tracked project config during canonical untracking sync
body:
## What
Prevent canonical synchronization from silently deleting a clean tracked machine-local `.aidevops.json` when an incoming index-only migration stops tracking it. Preserve the existing canonical/read-only and restore authorization boundaries. This is a narrow follow-up to #32525 and #32277, not a request to repeat either fix.

## Evidence / why
Source inspection on deployed 3.39.70:
- `canonical-recovery-helper.sh:1506-1512` selects dirty-state preservation only for nonempty porcelain status. A clean tracked project config is not represented as dirty or untracked.
- Incoming tree materialization at `:1952-1957` uses `read-tree -u -m`; an incoming tracked-file deletion can therefore remove the clean local config.
- Reinstatement at `:674-691,2037-2042` consumes `untracked-files.nul`, which does not establish reinstatement of the clean tracked config.
- The existing `project-config-restore-helper.sh:109-113` requires a genuine attached terminal and typed destination; do not simulate or bypass this confirmation. Its backup apply uses `jq .` at `:130-136`, which preserves JSON values but does not guarantee byte-identical formatting.
- A real index-only migration was reviewed: implementation-worktree bytes remained unchanged, but the canonical merge/sync was intentionally held. A private mode-0600 backup was verified against the untouched canonical file. No data loss was executed, and no private repository identity or config content is needed for a fixture reproducer.

## Files Scope
- `.agents/scripts/canonical-recovery-helper.sh`
- `.agents/reference/dirty-worktree-preservation.md`

## Candidate verification surface
Locate the existing canonical-recovery/dirty-preservation fixture tests under `.agents/scripts/tests/` and extend them; exact test filenames are not established here. Read `.agents/scripts/project-config-restore-helper.sh` and the project-config migration library as reference only unless an independently reviewed scope extension is necessary. Never edit deployed copies.

## Implementation / safety contract
1. Recheck active issues/PRs and integrated fixes before implementing; use one linked worktree and the source `.agents` files.
2. Exercise the existing canonical synchronization CLI in disposable registered fixture repositories with a clean tracked customized `.aidevops.json` and an incoming commit that adds the exact ignore rule and removes only the config index entry.
3. Detect that migration before destructive tree materialization. If existing approved preservation/reinstatement machinery can preserve exact bytes, ownership, permissions and audit provenance without a new canonical-write exception, use and verify it. Otherwise fail closed **before removing the file**, with actionable supported recovery guidance. Do not silently convert an interactive restore boundary into unattended write permission.
4. Preserve target ownership/ref freshness, foreign/symlink refusal, non-overwrite rules, dirty/untracked recovery, and unknown-outcome reconciliation. Never use reset/clean/index flags, raw canonical writes, pseudo-terminal confirmation, full init, history rewrite or overwrite of another actor's file as a workaround.
5. Document whether the result is safely preserved/restored or refused; do not claim autonomous exact-byte migration if only JSON-value restoration or a human-terminal path exists.

## Acceptance / verification
- Regression demonstrates the existing clean-tracked deletion boundary and proves the repaired CLI either preserves/reinstates the exact bytes as ignored local config or refuses before removal.
- Existing dirty/untracked fixtures continue passing; cover config already absent, modified local config, target appearing concurrently, unsafe symlink and changed expected source/ref.
- Run existing focused canonical-recovery/project-config tests and ShellCheck on changed shell files. No live repository, remote state, user config or service is required.
- No source-project names, private paths, PII or config values in public diagnostics, fixtures or issue text.

## Routing
Standard bounded safety fix; automatic dispatch intended. Independent review before merging any canonical mutation/preservation logic. Do not delegate again. Use owned compute only; no hosted fallback. No production operation, framework deployment, automatic update, or permission expansion is authorized by this brief.

title: Hostinger helper: read-only ssl-status command and SSL status endpoint docs
body:
## What

Document Hostinger's per-website SSL status endpoint in
`.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md`, and add a read-only `ssl-status`
command to `.agents/scripts/hostinger-helper.sh`.

## Why

Agents diagnosing a Cloudflare `525` on a Hostinger addon domain had no
documented way to read the origin certificate state. They had to guess routes
or search old sessions. Observed on 2026-10-25:

- `GET /api/hosting/v1/accounts/{username}/websites/{domain}/ssl/status`
  returns `status` (`active`, `waiting_for_retry`), `provider` (`hssl`),
  `is_lifetime`, `is_https_redirect_enabled`, `expires_at` and `last_error`
  (for example "Domain challenge failed").
- `/ssl` on the same website supports DELETE only; GET is rejected with
  "Supported methods: DELETE".
- `{username}` comes from `GET /api/hosting/v1/websites?domain=<domain>`
  (`.data[0].username`). OpenCode's Bash policy blocks `$(...)`, so the helper
  should resolve it internally.
- A new addon domain behind a proxied Cloudflare wildcard can land in
  `waiting_for_retry` / "Domain challenge failed", while its siblings behind the
  same proxied IPs hold active Let's Encrypt (`hssl`) certificates. The plain
  HTTP `/.well-known/acme-challenge/<missing>` path returned 404 with no
  redirect (healthy) at the time of the check.
- Verify the origin certificate without exposing the server IP: from the
  server, use `curl -skv --resolve <host>:443:<own public IP> https://<host>/`
  and read `subject`, `issuer` and `expire date`.

## How

- `EDIT: .agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md`: add an "SSL status over the
  API" bullet beside "Per-site PHP version over the API", with the endpoint,
  fields, the DELETE-only `/ssl` route and the origin-certificate check.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/hostinger-helper.sh`: add `ssl-status DOMAIN`, a GET
  only call that resolves the username and prints the JSON. Mention it in
  `help`.

### Files Scope

title: Hostinger: lifetime SSL behind a proxied Cloudflare record, and WordPress detection for copied sites (helper + docs)
body:
## What

Two Hostinger behaviours cost an interactive session hours on 2026-10-25/26, and neither is in the Hostinger docs or helper:

1. **Lifetime SSL cannot issue while the name resolves to Cloudflare's proxy.** A new Hostinger website on a subdomain covered by a proxied Cloudflare wildcard (`*.example.com`, proxied) stayed at `waiting_for_retry` / `last_error: "Domain challenge failed"` for three hours, although the HTTP challenge path was reachable through the proxy (a test token placed in `public_html/.well-known/acme-challenge/` answered 200 via Cloudflare). With Cloudflare SSL mode Full (strict) the site answered 525. Adding temporary **DNS-only** A records for the site's host and `www.` name (pointing at the wildcard's origin IP, TTL 60) let Hostinger's next automatic retry issue the certificate within 2 minutes (second site: within 15 minutes). Deleting the temporary records afterwards restored the proxy; HTTPS then answered 200 through Cloudflare. `POST .../ssl/setup` returns 422 while the status is `installing` or `waiting_for_retry`, so the API cannot force a retry; only the retry timer or hPanel Cancel → Install SSL.
2. **hPanel shows a restored/copied site as `website_type: other` (no WordPress tools, no WP Admin button)** until a detection scan runs. `POST /api/hosting/v1/accounts/{username}/wordpress/installations/detect` (non-destructive, asynchronous) queues it; within a minute `GET /api/hosting/v1/wordpress/installations` listed the site and `GET /api/hosting/v1/websites?domain=...` reported `website_type: wordpress`.

Both routes are in Hostinger's published API definitions: `hostinger/api-mcp-server`, `src/core/tools/hosting.ts` (`hosting_ssl_install`, `hosting_ssl_status`) and `src/core/tools/wordpress.ts` (`wordpress_installations_detect`, `wordpress_installations_list`).

## Proposed change

- `.agents/scripts/hostinger-helper.sh`: add `wordpress-detect <domain>` (POST detect, then poll the installations list for the domain, bounded, print `id`/`domain`/`is_valid` only) and, if not already present in the deployed helper, `ssl-status <domain>` (GET only). Keep `api` as the raw escape hatch. Every function: `local var="$1"`, explicit returns, ShellCheck clean.
- `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md`: a short "Lifetime SSL behind Cloudflare" section: symptom (`Domain challenge failed`, 525 under Full strict), cause (the challenge is checked against the host's own IP, so a proxied record fails), fix (temporary DNS-only A/`www` records with a comment, wait for the retry, verify the origin certificate with `openssl s_client -servername`, then delete only the temporary records), and the 422 rule for `ssl/setup`. Plus one line on `wordpress/installations/detect` for copied/restored sites.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/hostinger-helper.sh` (subcommand dispatch near the existing `api`/`cron` cases)
- `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md`

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/hostinger-helper.sh` → 0 findings.
- `hostinger-helper.sh wordpress-detect <a site already detected>` → returns its installation without changing anything else (the scan is idempotent).
- `hostinger-helper.sh ssl-status <domain>` → prints `status`, `provider`, `expires_at`, `last_error`.
- Docs: markdown lint passes; no private domains, usernames or IPs in examples (use `example.com`).

title: feat: add opt-in lossless historical Markdown archive helper
body:
# Add opt-in lossless historical Markdown archive helper

## Goal and observed need
An archival task encountered the existing non-root Markdown size gate. The safe resolution was seven bounded verbatim fragments plus a separate historical-status index, rather than bypassing hooks or modifying historical prose. Ordered concatenation reproduced both source documents byte-for-byte. Automate that narrow operation with synthetic fixtures; do not import project-specific documents, paths, names or evidence.

## Pre-flight
- Memory recall `lossless archive preservation split Markdown`: no relevant hits.
- Bounded worker discovery found no existing Markdown partition/reconstruction helper. Parent verified the three reference paths below are tracked and inspected the hashing/validation patterns.
- Prework discovery found recent commit `fdecc6bb7` touching worktree recovery; no related merged/open PRs or claimed issues were reported. Do not modify that recovery path. Recheck collisions before implementation.
- Selected tier: standard. New standalone utility with decided non-destructive boundaries; implementation and fixture details remain, so this is not an exact-transform simple task.
- Draft PR not seeded: this is a worker-ready implementation handoff, not an implementation in the originating project.

## Deliverables and files
Proposed new files (not existing implementations):
- `.agents/scripts/historical-markdown-archive.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-historical-markdown-archive.py`
Select a small existing script-documentation location after inspecting local conventions; exact documentation path is unknown. Do not add this detailed workflow to always-loaded AGENTS.md.

Reference patterns, not modification targets:
- `.agents/scripts/document-forensics-lib.sh:243-258`: SHA256 validation; `:1090-1150`: source/output hashes and manifest precedent.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_untracked.py:30-68`: streaming byte hashing and duplicate-path rejection. Do not couple to tar restore, cleanup, or worktree lifecycle machinery.
- `.agents/scripts/file-size-regression-helper.sh`: inspect current thresholds, keep unchanged. Never relax gates to accommodate the archive.

## Decided contract
1. Python standard library only. Provide explicit archive and verify operations with help, useful errors and nonzero exit on failure. Require explicit source and new destination; no recursive source discovery or automatic scanning outside these paths.
2. Archive one regular Markdown source per invocation. Default chunks to at most 400 LF-delimited lines; allow a positive explicit limit. Preserve exact bytes including UTF-8 BOM, CRLF and missing final newline. Do not decode/re-encode, normalize, inject headings or rebalance code fences in payloads. A short or empty source is valid and must have an unambiguous reconstruction representation.
3. Source remains read-only and unchanged. Reject source symlinks, source/output overlap and unsafe symlink destination components. Refuse an existing final destination. Use exclusive/staged output creation so failures cannot overwrite user files or leave a completed-looking partial archive; remove only temporary files created and owned by this invocation. Do not claim a hostile concurrent-writer boundary not implemented by the filesystem operations.
4. Write ordered numbered chunks, a versioned JSON manifest, and a separate README. Record neutral source label `source.md` by default (never automatically publish a potentially private basename), byte/line counts and SHA256, plus each chunk ordinal, relative path, contiguous line range, counts and SHA256. Use deterministic serialization/order and document the precise line-count definition. No timestamps required.
5. README clearly declares historical/noncanonical data: embedded commands, tasks, approvals and architectural claims are not active instructions. Give exact manifest-order verification/reconstruction usage. Do not invent canonical links, owner approval, Git provenance or approval status.
6. Verify manifest schema/types, unique paths/ordinals, contiguous order/ranges/counts and chunk hashes. Reject symlinks in manifest and all chunk-path components, absolute paths, traversal, missing/duplicate/reordered/tampered parts and unsupported schemas before consuming unsafe paths. Concatenated payload hash/size/count must equal the source record. With explicit original supplied, also require byte-for-byte equality and unchanged-source checking; without original, describe integrity-only scope rather than asserting original equality.
7. Before successful archive publication, independently verify the staged archive against the original and check the original has not changed since capture. No rendering, execution, Git mutation, network calls, source deletion, backup acknowledgement, restore or automatic dispatch of embedded historical tasks.

## Verification and acceptance
Use existing unittest/test conventions, no new test framework or infrastructure. Fixtures must be generated synthetic data. Cover ordinary multiline input; empty, single line and exact-boundary cases; BOM, CRLF, invalid UTF-8 bytes and no final LF; repeatable outputs; hashes/reconstruction; unchanged source; existing-output refusal; source/destination symlinks and overlap; traversal/absolute/duplicate/reordered/missing/tampered manifest/parts; unsupported schema; controlled source-change and interrupted-write failures. Run CLI archive then independent verify on synthetic fixtures. Inspect help and failure exit statuses. Run scoped existing Python lint/format checks and whitespace checks. Do not change global gate thresholds or add production/browser requirements unrelated to this utility.

Rollback is reverting the new utility/tests/docs; no existing source or runtime state should change. No publication, production deployment, dependency upgrade, billing or secret access authorized.

Document that line bounds do not guarantee byte-size gate compliance; cover an oversized single-line fixture without weakening any gate. Document source-change detection limits under concurrent writers; do not promise adversarial race protection without implementing it. A separate read-only worker accepted this brief with these clarifications; parent incorporated them before filing.

## Worker and compute policy
Implement through normal linked-worktree and reviewed PR workflow, use a closing reference to this leaf issue. User requested low-level workers for bounded work with orchestrator review and verification. No nested delegation. Qualification must use owned compute with approved disposable isolation under protected controllers, without host credentials or production sockets; no hosted fallback or skipped-as-pass. Bind qualification evidence to immutable source/controller SHAs, runner identity and terminal results. Honor owner-bound leases, reconcile unknown outcomes before ownership-checked release, never force-unlock. Missing capacity queues/blocks qualification; it does not waive gates.

## Problem

`cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh request <repo> <pr>` exits 1 with no message when the PR is a draft. `release_pr` (`.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh`) requires `.draft == false` and returns 1 silently. `release_authority` fails silently in the same way (unregistered repo, wrong `app_type`, missing admin/maintain permission).
