title: Blocked checkpoint becomes unapprovable after a never-ready claim is released as blocked
body:
## What

A blocked worker draft checkpoint can become permanently unapprovable when a later claim is released as `blocked` before it ever reaches a ready lease (a prelaunch terminal blocker such as `permission_required`). `blocked-attention` then posts an approval command that `approval-template` always refuses, and no other documented route closes the state except discarding the draft.

Observed on a managed private repo (issue/PR numbers withheld), aidevops 3.39.72, all events by the same trusted MEMBER runner, none edited:

1. Attempt A: `DISPATCH_CLAIM` → prelaunch leases → `Dispatching worker` → `DISPATCH_LEASE phase=ready attempt_id=attempt:A` → `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked` (legacy line: no `lease_token`/`attempt_id`) → terminal lease for A. The draft PR head is from this attempt.
2. Claim B: `DISPATCH_CLAIM` (prelaunch) → `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked` with a terminal-blocker observation `reason=permission_required owner=permission-maintainer`. No prelaunch lease renewal, no ready lease, no launch, no terminal lease.

Then:

- `pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh blocked-attention` treats release B as the checkpoint release and pairs it with attempt A (the last ready lease before it, `_pcc_blocked_release_evidence`), posting `approval-template … <release B> attempt:A`.
- `approval-template … <release B> attempt:A` fails: `release … is not a trusted CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked by <runner> closing attempt:A` (`release_for` → `original_lease` → `intervening_events_valid` rejects the intervening `DISPATCH_CLAIM` of B).
- `approval-template … <release A> attempt:A` fails: `intervening coordination is not fully released` (`released_successor_history` only closes a never-ready claim with an exact `reason=claim_only_no_worker` release bound by nonce and `claim_id`; B's release is `reason=blocked`).
- `dispatch-claim-helper.sh abort-pr-checkpoint-claim` cannot repair it: it refuses a claim that already has a release.

Result: ordinary redispatch stays held by the draft, a revision-bound approval cannot be generated, and the only exit is closing the draft (discarding the checkpoint) even after the brief owner has corrected the brief.

## How

1. `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` (`_pcc_blocked_release_evidence`): only pair a blocked release with a ready lease from the same claim episode. When the newest blocked release closes a never-ready claim, report the checkpoint's own release (A) and attempt, or post no template and say why, instead of an approval line that cannot validate.
2. `.agents/scripts/pr_checkpoint_history.py`: let `released_successor_history` close a never-ready claim whose release is a trusted, unedited `reason=blocked` from the same runner after the claim, with no ready lease, no `Dispatching worker`, no other release, and every claim/renewal expiry known and elapsed before the release. Emit it as an explicit `released_successors` entry (for example `outcome: "blocked_before_ready"`) so the approval must acknowledge it; keep `#aidevops:trust-boundary` and fail closed on any unknown expiry, ordering gap, other actor or edit. A legacy release line without `nonce`/`claim_id` binds only by runner, ordering and the absence of any other open claim in between.
3. `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-revision.py` and `.agents/scripts/pr_checkpoint_events.py`: accept the new history entry in `history_approved` exactly as generated; no other relaxation.
4. `.agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md`: document the "blocked before ready" successor and the `blocked-attention` pairing rule.

### Files Scope
- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pr_checkpoint_history.py`
- `.agents/scripts/pr_checkpoint_events.py`
- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-revision.py`
- `.agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/` (existing checkpoint revision/history test files only)

## Verification

- Extend the existing checkpoint history/approval tests with the two-episode sequence above: `approval-template` for release A produces one line whose `released_successors` lists claim B as `blocked_before_ready`, and `dispatch-approved` validates it; a variant where B has a ready lease, a launch, an unknown expiry, an edit or a different actor is still refused.
- `blocked-attention` on the same fixture names release A (or posts no template), never release B paired with attempt A.
- ShellCheck clean on the changed shell file.

title: Playwriter 0.9.0 activation loops on cold npx cache: 5s relay proof kills the package download
body:
## Observed

After the Playwriter pin moved to `playwriter@0.9.0` (GH#35514), `@playwriter` activation failed on every attempt on a host that had previously used older Playwriter builds (npx cache held `^0.4.0`, `^0.5.0` x2, `^0.8.0`, but no `0.9.0`).

- The `@playwriter` subagent reported activation failure on the initial attempt and on its automatic bounded reset; `mcp-diagnose.sh playwriter` → `relay-down`.
- `~/.playwriter/relay-server.log` was last written 3 days earlier, so no 0.9.0 relay ever started.
- The operator's extension click then showed the extension's "Daemon not running yet" page, which suggests `npx -y skills add https://playwriter.dev -g -y` and `npx playwriter session new` (the unguarded path the docs warn against).
- Operator report: "ever since we updated from our modified 0.5 playwriter this extension hand-off has just not worked."

## Root cause

`scripts/playwriter-authenticated-relay.mjs` gives the relay `START_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000` to prove version + token. On a cold npx cache, `npx playwriter@0.9.0` spends longer than that downloading, the launcher stops the child, and the download never completes, so the cache never warms and every subsequent activation fails identically. This is a persistent failure loop, not a one-off first-activation delay.

`tools/browser/playwriter.md` documents a manual workaround ("First activation after a pin change fails the relay proof": warm with `npx -y playwriter@0.9.0 --version`), but nothing does it automatically, the subagent's failure output does not mention it, and `mcp-diagnose.sh` reports only `relay-down`.

## Verification of the cause

Running `PLAYWRITER_TELEMETRY=0 DO_NOT_TRACK=1 npx -y playwriter@0.9.0 --version` once (no global install) printed `playwriter/0.9.0`; activation is then retried. (Result recorded in a follow-up comment.)

## Proposed fix (worker-ready)

Files: `.agents/scripts/playwriter-authenticated-relay.mjs`, `.agents/scripts/mcp-diagnose.sh`, `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/migrations.sh` (or the pin-change path in `setup.sh`), `.agents/tools/browser/playwriter.md`.

1. Pre-warm: when `setup.sh`/`aidevops update` changes or installs the Playwriter pin, run the exact pinned `npx -y playwriter@<pin> --version` with telemetry opted out (bounded, non-fatal, no global install).
2. Launcher: distinguish "child still running / package not yet resolved" from "relay unreachable". Either allow a separate, bounded package-resolution phase before the 5 s relay proof, or on proof timeout with a cold cache emit a closed diagnostic such as `relay-package-not-cached` with the exact warm command instead of a generic activation failure.
3. `mcp-diagnose.sh playwriter`: when nothing listens, check whether the pinned version is present in the npx cache and report `relay-down (pinned package not cached)`.
4. Docs: in "Selected-tab handoff order", note that the extension page's suggested commands remain prohibited and point to the warm step for this specific symptom.

Verification: on a host whose npx cache lacks the pin, `@playwriter` activation succeeds after setup (1), or fails with the new closed diagnostic (2/3); `test-playwriter-authenticated-relay.mjs` and `test-playwriter-pin.sh` pass.

title: bug(opencode-v2): investigate accumulated observability sqlite3 subprocesses
body:
## Description

Investigate accumulated observability sqlite3 children in a long-running OpenCode V2 server. On 2026-10-26, one server owned 581 children accessing the same llm-requests.db; a second server owned one. Children accumulated across October 21–26. This is an observed process/resource accumulation; the exact mechanism is not yet confirmed.

## Expected Behavior

Observability transports have bounded ownership and lifetime. Plugin reload/disposal must not leave unused subprocesses behind or disrupt connections still used by other plugin instances.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command** (sanitized, read-only; inspect a running affected server):

```bash
ps -C sqlite3 -o pid,ppid,stat,etime,comm
ps -p <server-pid> -o pid,nlwp,rss,etime,comm
```

**Actual output** (complete aggregate output from read-only /proc enumeration):

```text
sqlite_children_by_parent {'<primary-server>': 581, '<secondary-server>': 1}
spawn_dates {'2026-10-21': 76, '2026-10-22': 105, '2026-10-23': 157, '2026-10-24': 80, '2026-10-25': 121, '2026-10-26': 43}
waits {'unix_stream_data_wait': 554, 'hrtimer_nanosleep': 27, 'folio_wait_bit_common': 1}
total_RSS_MiB 2248.0
parent_open_fds 2454
```

RSS sums include shared pages and are not unique physical memory usage. Sampled children had stdin/stdout/stderr socket descriptors and open database, WAL and SHM descriptors. Sampled idle children were waiting on their input sockets, not executing builds. The visible command was `sqlite3 -cmd .timeout 15000 <observability-dir>/llm-requests.db`. The timeout is a database busy timeout, not a process lifetime limit.

Current plugin-log aggregates:

```text
Observability: SQLite DB ready: 402
SQLite async queue full: 10796
SQLite sync exec failed: 1
SQLite async exec failed: 1
```

These logs aggregate plugin activity and do not independently attribute every initialization or dropped write to one server. Do not infer that every initialization produced one leaked child.

**Expected output**: bounded persistent subprocess count; disposal/reload does not grow retained children indefinitely; ordinary observability writes do not remain dropped behind a saturated queue.

**Causal status**: unconfirmed investigation.

**Owning-path proof / candidate cause**:

- Production entry point: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2-plugin/index.mjs` re-exports `../v2.mjs`.
- `setupAidevopsV2()` in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs:308` calls `initObservability()` at line 319 in installed 3.39.49.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/observability.mjs:255-263` initializes observability and registers `process.on("exit", _shutdownSqlite)`.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/observability-sqlite.mjs` re-exports `.agents/scripts/sqlite-process.mjs`.
- `.agents/scripts/sqlite-process.mjs:77-138` owns a module-local persistent child; `shutdownSqlite()` is at lines 201-215. Its synchronous exec path at lines 183-195 should also be investigated rather than assuming every retained child is the async transport.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs:297-306` disposes events, bounded operations, MCP runtime and registrations but does not explicitly release observability ownership.
- Static omission is verified; no controlled integrated reload/disposal reproducer has yet proved it caused all observed children. Investigate module isolation/reloads, shared ownership, synchronous timeout paths, and stale child close/error callbacks before selecting the repair.

**Causal code history**: local blame attributes the V2 disposal routine to `f402f502d3` (2026-09-15); this is provenance, not proof of the introducing regression. On 2026-10-26 the default-branch Contents API still showed the same missing observability release and module-local child transport. The local last-week file-history check found only an unrelated OAuth account wiring change in V2.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run OpenCode V2 with the aidevops V2 plugin over several days while opening/reloading project locations and sessions.
2. Record per-server sqlite3 child count, start times, wait channels and descriptor ownership before/after location/plugin disposal.
3. Construct a bounded deterministic reproducer exercising the actual V2 setup/dispose path. The exact minimal trigger is not known yet.

## Implementation Scope and Verification

Tier: standard. Investigate and repair the verified owning path; do not merely add a process-count kill script. Candidate files: `.agents/scripts/sqlite-process.mjs`, `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/observability.mjs`, `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs`, and their existing lifecycle tests. Reference pattern: existing `disposeAidevopsV2()` and `shutdownSqlite()`; preserve concurrent consumer ownership.

Acceptance: repeated real plugin setup/disposal and transport error/restart paths keep children and descriptors bounded; final owner release terminates/reaps its child; one consumer disposing does not break another active consumer; telemetry still records successfully. Exercise existing relevant plugin checks and the production V2 lifecycle. Confirm/deny whether queue saturation is related rather than treating correlation as proof. No new test infrastructure is requested.

## Workarounds Applied

No child processes were killed and no plugin source was changed during diagnosis. The operator requested reboot preparation after preserving this evidence; a normal server exit/reboot may clear symptoms but is not a durable fix.

## Environment

- aidevops 3.39.49; diagnostics reported latest 3.39.73, but no update was applied.
- OpenCode V2 2.0.27; plugin log reports Bun 1.3.14.
- Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, Bash 5.2.21, gh 2.102.0.
- Primary server had been running about 4 days 19 hours.
- No credentials, prompts, private repository names or machine-specific absolute paths are included.

## Duplicate Search

Searched all-state platform issues for `sqlite subprocess`, `observability leak`, `sqlite in:title`, and `subprocess in:title`; searched all-state PRs for `sqlite process` and `observability in:title`. No matching accumulation/lifecycle report found. Historical concurrent SQLite startup-lock fixes address a different symptom.

title: Dependency graph JQ reducer reintroduces fixed hold-marker false positives and stalls resolved continuation chains
body:
## Observed regression

A managed product's sequential continuation is still `status:blocked` after its only predecessor closed with a merged delivery PR. The pulse log explicitly reports `dep-graph-cache: NOT unblocking ... non-dep block detected (body-defer)`. There are no comments or assignees on the waiting continuation.

On deployed commit `8f8bbfacc7ef240751c58e7055decca7c12057f9`, feeding the current issue JSON through the installed `.agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph-reduce.jq` reproduces `has_defer_marker: true` and a true entry in `defer_flags`. Identifiers and product details are intentionally omitted from this public report.

The offending explanatory lines include:

- `Other rows of this phase belong to other parts ...; neither is a hold for this part.`
- A sentence referring to historical `navigation holds`.

The first matches `hold for ` mid-sentence. The second matches `on hold` as a substring of `navigation holds`. Neither is a new operational hold on the continuation.

## Root cause and previous fix

GH#34885 was correctly fixed by merged PR #34886: `.agents/scripts/issue-hold-marker-lib.sh:86-140` now classifies explicit line-leading operational holds, normalizes Markdown prefixes, skips fences and HTML comments, and preserves the strong `HUMAN_UNBLOCK_REQUIRED` marker.

However, `.agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph-reduce.jq:97-98` still uses the old unanchored expression:

```text
defer until|do[-[:space:]]not[-[:space:]]dispatch|on[-[:space:]]hold|HUMAN_UNBLOCK_REQUIRED|hold for |paused[[:space:]:]
```

Its `parsed_issue` function applies that expression to the whole body at line 131. The reduced cache then reaches `.agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh:466-479` and `:768-778`, where either cached true flag correctly preserves a non-dependency hold. The defect is classification drift in the fast JQ producer, not the conservative release gate.

## Implementation scope

- Bring `.agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph-reduce.jq` hold detection into parity with `issue_hold_text_has_operational_hold` and `issue_body_has_defer_marker` in `.agents/scripts/issue-hold-marker-lib.sh`.
- Extend the existing `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-reduce.sh` and, if appropriate, existing hold-classification tests to compare both production paths. Do not add another runner or test-only interface.
- Cover negated mid-sentence `hold for`, the `navigation holds` substring, Markdown-normalized explicit directives, fences, HTML comments, table rows, and the strong marker. Preserve actual operational holds and independent native/body dependency checks.
- Verify that a resolved predecessor plus ordinary explanatory prose does not manufacture a body hold, while an explicit human/worker hold still prevents release.
- Do not manually relabel the observed product issue, bypass capability/ownership gates, edit product data, or remove source-backed historical holds. Recovery should occur through normal dependency reconciliation after deployment.

## Verification

Use the existing commands from a session-owned framework worktree:

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-reduce.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-non-dep-block.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh
```

Also run the appropriate existing lint for changed files. After reviewed deployment, inspect the normal dependency refresh: the affected dependency-only continuation should become eligible without losing genuine non-dependency holds. A cached heartbeat alone is not delivery evidence.

title: full-loop commit-and-pr risk check counts untracked .full-loop-cleanup-deferred marker and blocks data-only PRs
body:
## Observed

`full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` stopped before staging with:

```text
[ERROR] Critical runtime risk requires runtime-verified evidence; PR body generation blocked.
```

The pending change was data-only (Markdown, JSON and JSONL under a `todo/` path that the risk policy classifies as Low). A previous `full-loop-helper.sh merge` in the same linked worktree had left the untracked runtime marker `.agents/.full-loop-cleanup-deferred` (`LIFECYCLE_STATE=CLEANUP_DEFERRED`).

## Cause

- `full-loop-helper-risk.sh` `_pending_runtime_files_changed` builds the prospective PR file list from `git diff --name-only <base>` plus `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`, so it includes the untracked `.agents/.full-loop-cleanup-deferred`.
- That path is not Low, so `_derive_runtime_risk` falls through to keyword matching on the `--summary` text. An ordinary phrase such as "in this session" matches `_runtime_context_has_session_pattern` and raises the risk to Critical.
- `full-loop-helper-commit.sh` `_stage_product_changes` already excludes `.agents/loop-state` and `.agents/.full-loop-cleanup-deferred` from staging, so the risk check evaluates a file that can never enter the PR.

## Expected

The pending risk check should exclude the same runtime paths that `_stage_product_changes` excludes (`.agents/loop-state`, `.agents/.full-loop-cleanup-deferred`), so a data-only PR stays Low however its summary is worded.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-risk.sh`: `_pending_runtime_files_changed` (or `_runtime_path_is_low`) — share the runtime-path exclusion list with `full-loop-helper-commit.sh` `_stage_product_changes` instead of duplicating it.
- Reference pattern: the `runtime_paths` array in `_stage_product_changes`.

## Verification

- Extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-runtime-risk.sh`: an untracked `.agents/.full-loop-cleanup-deferred` plus a Low-only diff and a summary containing "session" must derive `Low` and must not block PR body generation.
- Run ShellCheck on the changed scripts.

## Workaround used

Rewording the summary to avoid the `session` keyword let the PR proceed. The marker was left in place because the merge helper owns it.

title: Supervisor heartbeat callback is rejected after the production instance-lock release
body:
## Finding: production integration gap after GH#35704

PR #35705 merged and was deployed at `8f8bbfacc7ef240751c58e7055decca7c12057f9`. Its watchdog callback is present in the installed file. Deployment is verified, but supervisor-path liveness acceptance remains open.

Source inspection shows the new callback cannot refresh the normal unlocked supervisor path:

1. `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh:1858-1863` publishes `supervising`, then calls `release_instance_lock` before the optional LLM supervisor. This release deliberately allows subsequent deterministic cycles to run concurrently.
2. `.agents/scripts/pulse-instance-lock.sh:319-346` sets `_LOCK_OWNED=false` when releasing that lock.
3. `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh:385-463` obtains a separate LLM lock and invokes `run_pulse`; it does not reacquire the instance lock. `run_pulse` at lines 230-304 starts the child and calls `_run_pulse_watchdog`.
4. `.agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog.sh:667-668` now invokes `_pulse_cycle_state_stage_heartbeat || true`.
5. `.agents/scripts/pulse-logging.sh:357-362` immediately returns 1 unless `_LOCK_OWNED=true`. The watchdog intentionally ignores that failure, so no structured heartbeat is written on this legitimate path.

This is a source-level integration finding, not a claim of a newly observed live stale-supervisor incident. Current sampled live cycles were in `preflight` with fresh heartbeats. Do not manufacture a production supervisor run, force a scheduler restart, or disturb live children merely to reproduce it.

## Why existing positive coverage misses the lifecycle

`.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-cycle-state-contract.sh:470-471` sets `_LOCK_OWNED=true` before publishing `supervising` and later invokes the real watchdog. This proves the callback works for a locked owner, but does not exercise the real release-before-supervisor sequence. Existing unlocked-owner rejection is valuable and must remain covered.

## Requested bounded repair

- Reconcile supervisor liveness with the intended lock lifecycle. Relevant code is in the five production files named above; use the existing cycle ownership/current-health and terminal-publication patterns in `pulse-logging.sh` as references.
- Keep deterministic cycles concurrent with the LLM supervisor. Do not retain the global instance lock across the whole LLM run.
- Do not simply delete `_LOCK_OWNED` checks or weaken the generic stage heartbeat. Preserve executor identity, current-cycle ownership, terminal-state protection, and serialization against a newer cycle publishing between a health read and replacement.
- An obsolete supervisor must never overwrite or revive a newer/completed cycle. A missing/replaced lock or a failed best-effort liveness write must not change the child's exit status or bypass stop/watchdog checks.
- Heartbeats may update only structured liveness; do not change delivery-progress timestamps, progress kinds, counters, log bytes, issue claims, scheduling, or publication state.
- Extend the existing contract/watchdog tests to exercise the actual release-before-supervisor lifecycle with the separate LLM owner evidence and concurrent newer-cycle publication. No new test runner or production-only test interface is needed.

## Verification

Run existing focused checks from a session-owned framework worktree:

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-cycle-state-contract.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-watchdog-tick.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-cycle-gates.sh
```

Run ShellCheck on changed shell files. Positive coverage must start from the released instance-lock state, not assume `_LOCK_OWNED=true` throughout supervision. Assert heartbeat-only changes for a legitimately current supervisor, no writes by children/obsolete/completed cycles, no stale-snapshot overwrite of a newer cycle, unchanged log bytes and preserved child failure/stop outcomes. After normal reviewed deployment, observe a naturally occurring eligible supervisor if available; otherwise report runtime observation as pending rather than claiming it passed.

title: Bug: worker draft checkpoints released as worker_ownership_lost are never continued
body:
## What

Worker draft checkpoints whose last release reason is `worker_ownership_lost` are held forever. Ordinary redispatch, stall continuation and blocked-checkpoint attention all decline them, so a draft PR with green checks sits with no owner and no next action.

## Why (observed 2026-10-26, runner v3.39.74)

In a managed plugin repo (name withheld), an issue's worker pushed draft PR at exact head `d5e81383`, then posted `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=worker_ownership_lost` on 2026-10-25T03:48Z. Some 41 hours later, every path still declines it:

- Ordinary dispatch: `Dedup: WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT: draft PR #N is a durable checkpoint for issue #M; ordinary redispatch is blocked`
- Blocked attention: `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION_SKIPPED: ... has no current blocked release`
- Merge pass: `draft PR not eligible for auto-merge (GH#23525)`
- Manual `pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh dispatch <slug> <path> <pr> <issue> <assignee> <login>` → `PR_CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_BLOCKED: ... is not an open, unheld worker draft linked to issue #M with an exact head`

The draft PR is open, has the `origin:worker` label, links its issue through closing references and passes all checks. Its issue is `status:available`, assigned to the runner login.

Root cause: `_PCC_STALL_RELEASE_PATTERN` in `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh:45` allows `no_activity|wall_clock_stale|stale_assignment_reset|watchdog_kill:*|*_stall|*timeout*`. It does not allow `worker_ownership_lost`. The blocked-attention path only accepts blocked releases. #35363 fixed the same deadlock class for `stale_assignment_reset`, and #35342 covered legacy ownership-loss releases only on the explicit claim-only recovery path.

## How

1. In `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`, classify a current `worker_ownership_lost` release on a worker draft as stall-continuable. Do this only when no live lease or human claim exists and the exact head still matches. Follow the `stale_assignment_reset` handling added for #35363.
2. Check `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh` so the candidate pass routes such drafts to `dispatch-stalled` rather than leaving them on `WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT`.
3. Make `_pcc_target_row` (used by `_pcc_dispatch`, about line 499) report which condition failed. The generic message hides the reason.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh` (only if candidate routing needs the new class)
- Existing checkpoint tests under `.agents/scripts/tests/` that already cover `stale_assignment_reset`. Extend these only if they exist; do not add new harnesses.

## Verification

- `shellcheck` on the changed scripts.
- Run the existing checkpoint-continuation tests that cover the stall release pattern.
- Recheck the observed case: after deploy, the next pulse logs a stall continuation, not `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_SKIPPED`, for a `worker_ownership_lost` draft.

title: Local-only policy: operator-owned local-ai-providers override that survives aidevops update
body:
## Problem

The local-only provider list is only read from the deployed bundle file `configs/local-ai-providers.conf` (`plugins/opencode-aidevops/local-only-policy.mjs` `LOCAL_PROVIDERS_FILE`, and `scripts/vault-data-policy-helper.sh` `VAULT_POLICY_LOCAL_PROVIDERS_FILE`). `~/.aidevops/agents` is a symlink to a versioned runtime bundle, so an operator who runs a local model under their own provider ID (for example an OpenAI-compatible server reached over a loopback tunnel) must edit the bundle copy, and `aidevops update` silently reverts it. Bound `local-only` sessions then fail closed for that operator's only local model.

## Proposed fix

Support an operator-owned override that replaces the shared list when present:

- Path: `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/aidevops/local-ai-providers.conf`, same format.
- Same trust checks as `local-only-roots.json`: regular file, current-user owned, not group/world writable, not a symlink; otherwise fail closed (nothing is local) rather than fall back to the shared list.
- Read once at plugin init (frozen) and by `vault-data-policy-helper.sh`, so both enforcement points stay identical.
- Loopback endpoint check is unchanged.

## Files

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/local-only-policy.mjs` (`LOCAL_PROVIDERS_FILE`, `readLocalProviders`)
- `.agents/scripts/vault-data-policy-helper.sh` (`VAULT_POLICY_LOCAL_PROVIDERS_FILE`)
- `.agents/reference/vault-local-only-binding.md` (document the override)
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-local-only-policy.mjs` (override present / insecure / absent)

## Verification

`node .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-local-only-policy.mjs`; with an override listing only `custom-local`, a bound session allows `custom-local/*` on a loopback URL and denies `ollama/*`; after `aidevops update` the override still applies.

title: object-storage-helper: guarded resumable bucket migration (copy, verify, retire source) between S3-compatible providers
body:
## What

Add a guarded, resumable provider-to-provider bucket migration capability to `object-storage-helper.sh` (Wasabi / IDrive e2 / Backblaze B2 and other S3-compatible accounts already in `configs/object-storage-config.json`).

## Why (observed evidence)

An interactive session migrated 40 Wasabi buckets (~1.27 TB, ~10M objects) to IDrive e2 and then retired the source. The current helper could not be used: `copy`/`download` are dry-run previews even after the `preview:<account>:<bucket>` confirmation token (`.agents/scripts/object-storage-helper.sh` `run_transfer`, ~line 227), and `.agents/services/hosting/wasabi.md` / `idrive-e2.md` forbid deletes. The session had to hand-write one-off scripts for:

1. Injecting credentials from `aidevops secret` into an rclone config streamed over SSH stdin to a transfer host (root-only 0600 file, removed afterwards). Secrets never in argv or output.
2. Read-only preflight per bucket: region (GetBucketLocation), versioning, Object Lock, public ACL, bucket policy, object count and bytes, newest upload time (detects live writers).
3. Lanes for parallel copies (large-object vs small-object tuning) in detached `screen` sessions on a remote host.
4. Verification after copy (`rclone check --one-way`) with per-bucket status files (`VERIFIED`, `COPY_FAIL`, `CHECK_FAIL`, ...).
5. A gated source delete that refuses non-VERIFIED buckets and re-checks immediately before `rclone purge`.

## Lessons to encode

- Old distro rclone (v1.60) holds whole directory listings in memory. A flat prefix with 8.8M objects would exhaust a 4 GB host. Require rclone >= 1.70 and pass `--list-cutoff` (we used 200000). Avoid `--fast-list` for very large buckets.
- Memory budget for large objects ≈ `transfers × s3-upload-concurrency × s3-chunk-size`. For small objects, use a high `--transfers` count with a small `--buffer-size`.
- Killing a run mid-copy loses in-flight multipart uploads. Prefer finishing the current bucket, and afterwards run `rclone backend cleanup` on the destination.
- Bucket policies and ACLs are not copied. Report them in the preflight so the operator decides about public access.
- `pkill -f <pattern>` over `ssh` can match the remote shell's own command line.

## How (files)

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/object-storage-helper.sh`: add `migrate-plan <src-account> <dst-account>` (read-only preflight report), `migrate-run` (copy plus verify, resumable, status per bucket, optional `--remote-host` alias) and `migrate-retire-source` (gated delete requiring an exact token per bucket plus re-check). Follow the existing account/allowlist/endpoint validation and `emit_result` JSON patterns.
- EDIT `.agents/services/hosting/wasabi.md`, `idrive-e2.md`, `backblaze-b2.md`: document the migration path and the narrow delete exception (source retirement after verification only).
- Tests: extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-object-storage-helper.sh` only where an existing pattern covers argument and gate validation (no live network).

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/object-storage-helper.sh` is clean.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-object-storage-helper.sh` passes.
- `migrate-retire-source` refuses buckets without VERIFIED status and refuses a wrong confirmation token (gate test).
- `migrate-plan` against a configured test account prints region, versioning, lock, policy, count, bytes and newest upload, without mutation.

title: t18773: fix: linters-local Python complexity check reports no issues when lizard/pyfl...
body:
**Task ID:** `t18773` | **Status:** open
**Assignee:** @marcusquinn | **Logged:** 2026-10-26 | **Started:** 2026-10-26
**Tags:** `auto-dispatch` `bug`

## Outcome

fix: linters-local Python complexity check reports no issues when lizard/pyflakes cannot run

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`check_python_complexity` in `.agents/scripts/linters-local-analysis.sh` reports a false pass when `lizard` or `pyflakes` is on `PATH` but cannot run.

Both checks use `command -v <tool>` and then `out=$(<tool> ... 2>/dev/null || true)`. A tool whose shebang points at a removed interpreter (observed: pip entry points left in `/opt/homebrew/bin` with `#!/opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.11/bin/python3.11` after Homebrew dropped python@3.11) exits 126 with only stderr ("bad interpreter"). Stdout is empty, so the check prints `Python complexity: N files checked, no issues` instead of saying the tool is unavailable.

## Fix

Distinguish "ran and found nothing" from "could not run":

- Capture each tool's exit status instead of `|| true`. pyflakes exits 0 (clean) or 1 (findings); lizard with `--warnings_only` exits 0 or 1 when warnings exist. Any other status, or a status that is non-zero with empty stdout, means the tool did not run.
- When a tool did not run, print a warning naming the resolved path and the reinstall hint (`pipx install <tool>`) and do not claim "no issues" in the summary line; name the skipped tool instead.
- Keep the check advisory (`return 0`), as today.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/linters-local-analysis.sh`

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/linters-local-analysis.sh:868-938` (`check_python_complexity`). Shared helper or inline status capture; follow the existing `print_warning`/`print_info` style.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/linters-local-analysis.sh` clean.
- Reproduce with a temporary `PATH` directory containing `pyflakes` and `lizard` scripts whose shebang is a missing interpreter: before the fix the summary says "no issues"; after, it warns that each tool is not runnable and the summary names the skipped tools.
- With working tools (`pipx install pyflakes lizard`), output is unchanged for clean files and still counts findings for a file with an unused import.
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed --base-ref origin/main` passes.

</details>

## Brief Workflow

This issue body is composed under `.agents/workflows/brief.md`. Newly queued auto-dispatch work must pass its `Dispatch Readiness Contract (brief schema v2)`: complete write surface, hazards and compatibility, executable verification mapped to affected surfaces, and positive plus negative/regression acceptance criteria.

body:
## Task


`.agents/scripts/tests/test-linters-local-bash32-gate.sh` fails locally on unmodified `main` with `FAIL create feature repo`. The test passes in CI.

Root cause, confirmed locally:

1. `test_feature_branch_uses_regression_helper` runs `cd "$repo_dir"` (inside `TEST_ROOT`), then `teardown` runs `rm -rf "$TEST_ROOT"`. The shell is left in a deleted directory.
2. `test_timeout_is_warning_only` then calls `git -C "$repo_dir" ...`. title: cloudron-release-approval-helper process fails every approved release: gh run watch capped at 120s
body:
## Problem

`cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh process --apply` reports failure for every successful approved merge, because it watches the catalog run with `AIDEVOPS_GH_READ_TIMEOUT=120 _gh_with_timeout read gh run watch ...` (`release_process_issue`). A managed catalog run (preflight with package checks and image build, build, publish, release) takes well over 120 seconds, so the watch is killed, the function returns 1, and the approval issue stays open until the next routine pass.

## Evidence (2026-10-27)

`process --apply` for marcusquinn/cloudron-nostr-relay-app#21 confirmed PR #20 merged at the signed head (`bf8e2583b4`), started `gh run watch 40440804288`, and exited 1 after about 2 minutes while the run's `catalog / preflight` was still on "Static and package-specific checks".

## Fix

Don't block on the run. If the catalog run for the merge SHA is still `queued`/`in_progress`, print `Catalog run <id> still running for <repo>; verification resumes next routine` and return 0, the same as the existing "run not yet visible" branch. Treat only a completed non-success conclusion as failure. `release_published` already makes the next pass resume verification without re-merging.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-release-approval.sh`

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-release-approval.sh`: an in-progress run returns 0 with the issue still open, a completed success closes the issue with evidence, and a completed failure returns 1.

title: cloudron-catalog-publish-reusable: release repair step rejects releases signed by an earlier signer ref
body:
## What

The `release` job's "Verify existing tag, public image and catalog; repair release only" step in `.github/workflows/cloudron-catalog-publish-reusable.yml` (lines 342-379 at `e774543b16b778c3e95a431d0a2b6d91a89e8803`) verifies the **latest already-published** version's catalog and image attestations with `--signer-workflow .../cloudron-catalog-publish-reusable.yml --signer-digest "$AIDEVOPS_REF"`, where `AIDEVOPS_REF` is the caller's *current* `aidevops_ref` input.

A release signed by an earlier signer cannot satisfy that. Either:

1. the release predates a repo's migration to the managed caller (it was signed by the repo's own workflow), or
2. the caller's pinned `aidevops_ref` has since been bumped.

In both cases every non-release push to `main` fails with `Error: verifying with issuer "sigstore.dev"` until a new package version is published. Nothing is published or damaged, but `main` shows a red catalog run for unrelated (docs/source-only) merges.

## Observed evidence

- Repo: a Cloudron package repo migrated to the managed caller in its GH#203 (caller pins `e774543b...`). Its v2.6.3 release was published *before* the migration.
- The next non-release push (a source/docs-only fix, manifest still 2.6.3) ran the repair step with `VERSION: 2.6.3`. `docker buildx imagetools inspect` passed; the first `gh attestation verify` failed: `Error: verifying with issuer "sigstore.dev"`.
- The following release (2.6.4, signed by the reusable workflow at `e774543`) succeeded, including its release step. So the defect is the signer identity used for *previously* published versions, not publication itself.

## Expected

The repair step verifies the version against the signer that actually produced it. Options, for the worker to evaluate:

- (a) Read the signer workflow/digest recorded in the existing attestation and accept it when it's the same repo's own workflow or a prior `marcusquinn/aidevops` reusable-workflow ref, i.e. a bounded trusted-signer set.
- (b) Record the signer ref in the catalog entry or tag trailer (like `Cloudron-Source`) at publish time and verify against that value.
- (c) Skip repair when the GitHub release for the tag already exists and is non-draft, verifying only when a repair (release creation) is actually needed.

Keep fail-closed behaviour for genuinely missing or forged attestations. Do not widen the trusted signer to arbitrary workflows.

## Files

- `.github/workflows/cloudron-catalog-publish-reusable.yml` (release job, repair step ~L342-379; the same `--signer-digest "$AIDEVOPS_REF"` pattern is at ~L190, L216, L283 for the current-build paths, which are correct as-is)
- Possibly `.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh` `release_published()` if signer metadata is added to the catalog.
- Docs for the managed caller migration, if a note is needed: path unknown, worker to locate.

## Verification

- Reproduce: a caller repo whose latest release was signed by a different signer ref; push a non-release commit; the repair step must pass for a legitimately signed older release and fail for an unsigned/forged one.
- Existing workflow lint/tests in the aidevops repo for the reusable workflow.

title: cloudron release approval: preflight CLOUDRON_RELEASE_PAT before merge; accept managed signer in release receipts
body:
## What

`cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh` merges an approved Cloudron release PR even when the target repository lacks the `CLOUDRON_RELEASE_PAT` Actions secret. The managed reusable workflow (`.github/workflows/cloudron-catalog-publish-reusable.yml`) requires that secret for the protected-branch catalog/tag push. So the release merges, builds and attests the image, then fails at publish ("Commit catalog and push tag atomically": `CLOUDRON_RELEASE_PAT is required for the protected-branch push`). `main` is left with a merged version bump and no catalog entry, tag or GitHub release, and `process --apply` exits non-zero.

Separately, `full-loop-helper.sh record-published-release ... --generated-cloudron-catalog` rejects managed-caller releases because its attestation check does not accept reusable-workflow signers ("Generated catalog verification failed: GitHub API or attestation verification failed"). Repos migrated to the managed caller therefore cannot record `release:published` / `release:superseded` receipts.

## Observed evidence

- A Cloudron package repo on the managed caller (`@80f3166c...`) had only `SYNC_PAT` configured. Its approved 0.1.2 release PR was merged by `cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh process --apply`; the catalog run's preflight, build and image attestation passed; publish failed on the empty secret; the release job was skipped.
- A second repo on the managed caller (`@e774543b...`) published 2.6.4 successfully, but `record-published-release <PR> v2.6.4 <repo> --workflow cloudron-catalog-publish.yml --event push --generated-cloudron-catalog` returned "Generated catalog evidence for tag v2.6.4 was rejected", while `release_published()` in the approval helper verified the same release.

## Expected

1. `release_request` (and ideally `release_process_issue` before merge) fails closed with an actionable message when `gh secret list --repo <repo>` lacks `CLOUDRON_RELEASE_PAT` (or the caller does not pass it), before requesting approval or merging. Never read secret values; check names only.
2. `record-published-release` / `record-included-release` with `--generated-cloudron-catalog` accept the bounded managed signer `marcusquinn/aidevops/.github/workflows/cloudron-catalog-publish-reusable.yml` at the caller's pinned `aidevops_ref`, the same identity the reusable workflow itself verifies. Keep rejecting arbitrary reusable-workflow signers.

### Files Scope
- `.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-evidence.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-release-approval.sh`

## Files

## Verification

- A repo without the secret: `release request` refuses with the missing-secret message, and no merge occurs.
- A managed-caller repo with a verified published release: `record-published-release ... --generated-cloudron-catalog` records `release:published`; a forged or other-workflow signer is still rejected.

title: cloudron: detect missing CLOUDRON_RELEASE_PAT before a managed catalog release fails
body:
## Problem

The managed catalog workflow (`.github/workflows/cloudron-catalog-publish-reusable.yml`) requires the repository secret `CLOUDRON_RELEASE_PAT` for the catalog commit and tag push. The GH#35667 migrations moved three packages that lack the secret onto it, and nothing flagged the gap until a real release failed. Their old inline workflows pushed with the job token.

## Evidence (2026-10-27)

- marcusquinn/cloudron-nostr-relay-app run 40440804288 (signed release 0.1.2, merge `bf8e2583b4`): preflight, build and catalog attestation succeeded, then `publish` failed with `CLOUDRON_RELEASE_PAT is required for the protected-branch push`. The image is built and attested, but there is no catalog entry, tag or release.
- `gh secret list` (names only): the PAT is present in netbird, aidevops-cloudron-app, buzz and librecrawl, and **missing** in nostr-relay, headscale and opendesk. All three are migrated and have `CLOUDRON_PUBLICATION_ENABLED=true`.
- buzz 0.1.23 (PAT present) published end-to-end through the same reusable workflow (run 40441368327).

## Fix

1. `cloudron-package-helper.sh scaffold catalog --migrate` (and plain scaffold): after writing the caller, check `gh secret list --repo <slug> --json name` for `CLOUDRON_RELEASE_PAT`. If it's missing, print a blocking warning with the documented setup from `cloudron-app-publishing-skill.md` ("fine-grained PAT restricted to this package repository, Contents write"). Never read or echo values.
2. `cloudron-package-monitor-helper.sh`: for each maintained `cloudron-package` repo with `CLOUDRON_PUBLICATION_ENABLED=true`, report a missing `CLOUDRON_RELEASE_PAT` once per repo (deduplicated issue or monitor finding), so it is caught before a release fails.
3. `cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh request`: refuse with an explicit error when the secret name is absent. A signed approval should not lead to a guaranteed publish failure.

Do not add a `GITHUB_TOKEN` fallback here. The PAT boundary is a deliberate GH#34983 design decision and needs its own reviewed issue if it changes.

### Files Scope

title: Bug: terminal-blocker unknown exits hold status:blocked with no wake condition; trusted retry never releases them
body:
## What

A headless worker that stops with `Terminal blocker: reason=unknown` is labelled `status:blocked`, and nothing ever returns it to `status:available`. A trusted OWNER/MEMBER `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry` and a brief edit both have no effect, even though the recovery note posted on the issue says "No global dispatch hold is imposed."

## Why

Evidence from a managed private repo (award enrichment queue). Nine issues have stayed `status:blocked` for 20+ hours after a worker exit with `reason=unknown` (`Projected state: status:blocked`) followed by an OWNER-authored standalone `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry` comment. No runner claimed them again and no re-arm receipt was posted. The repo's queue retry policy relies on that directive, so these awards are effectively parked and each retry is spent without a dispatch.

Code path (deployed v3.39.76, unchanged on `main` at 3b6548f8e):

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh` `_hrff_blocked_exit_holds` (~line 549) projects `status:blocked` for every blocked exit except a runner-local capability gap, so `unknown` included (GH#34775/GH#34846).
- `_hrff_enqueue_observation_recovery` (~line 668) enqueues recovery only for `terminal_blocker_rearms_on_revision` classes. `unknown` is not in `_TBC_REVISION_REARM_REASONS` (`.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh:29`).
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh` `_tbr_seed_reason` (~line 304) backfills only the same classes. `_tbr_release_circuit_hold` returns 2 for `unknown` (`[[ "$reason" != "$_TBC_UNKNOWN" ]] || return 2`, ~line 473), so even a seeded entry could never release.
- `_terminal_blocker_recovery` (`terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` ~line 624) tells readers "No global dispatch hold is imposed" for `unknown`, which contradicts the projected label.

The result is a hold with no wake condition. GH#34775 intended blocked exits to hold until their wake condition, not forever.

## Reproducer

1. A headless worker on the full runtime exits `BLOCKED` without a recognised `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON`, so the release posts `Terminal blocker: reason=unknown … Projected state: status:blocked` and applies `status:blocked`.
2. An OWNER posts a comment whose standalone line is `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry`.
3. Run `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh seed --force` and `pending` on any runner. `_tbr_seed_reason` returns 1 for `unknown`, so nothing is queued. A hand-enqueued entry reaches `_tbr_release_circuit_hold`, which returns 2 at the `unknown` guard.
4. The issue stays `status:blocked` indefinitely. Observed on 9 open issues in a managed private repo, each with an OWNER retry posted 2026-10-26 ~11:45Z and no subsequent claim.

## How

1. `terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`: add `unknown` to `_TBC_REVISION_REARM_REASONS`. In `terminal_blocker_task_revision`, compute the `unknown` revision from brief plus linked dependencies, without default-branch HEAD, using the same branch as `external_trigger_pending`/`input_required`. Unrelated merges must not churn an unknown hold into a redispatch loop. Update the `unknown` recovery action text: record a known blocker class or repair the brief; a brief/dependency change or an OWNER/MEMBER `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry` re-arms dispatch.
2. `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh` `_tbr_release_circuit_hold`: drop the `unknown` refusal for observation evidence. Unknown never opens a circuit, and `_tbr_circuit_blocks_release` keeps its own guard for circuits.
3. Keep every trust boundary: only OWNER/MEMBER retries clear holds, and receipts still suppress replay. Unknown redispatch stays throttled by `terminal_blocker_backoff_active`.

Already-stranded `unknown` holds were observed under the old HEAD-based revision. They are seeded by the recovery helper and re-armed once. That matches the trusted retries already posted on them.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`

## Acceptance

- [ ] An `unknown` first observation held as `status:blocked`, followed by an OWNER/MEMBER `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry`, is seeded by `_tbr_seed_reason` and released to `status:available` by `_tbr_release_circuit_hold`, with one re-arm receipt.
- [ ] Without a retry or brief/dependency change, the `unknown` hold stays (`terminal_blocker_observation_hold_active` returns 0). A COLLABORATOR-only retry does not release it.
- [ ] `unknown` task revision does not change on default-branch HEAD movement.
- [ ] `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` passes. ShellCheck is clean on changed scripts.

## Verification

`bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`; `shellcheck .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`. After release, on a runner, `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh pending` re-arms a stranded `unknown` hold that has a later trusted retry.

title: release reconcile fails with gh exit 127 under bounded operations and hides the shim's cause
body:
## What

`aidevops release reconcile <PR>` fails with `GitHub read failed (exit 127 ...; not retryable)` when it runs under the interactive bounded-operation runner (`aidevops_bounded_operation start`). The same command run from a normal shell succeeds and records `release:published`. The failure message drops the shim's stderr, so the cause is hidden.

## Evidence (2026-10-27, macOS, session runtime bundle 3.39.57)

- Bounded operation `["aidevops","release","reconcile","35746"]`, cwd = aidevops linked worktree, output: `release-snapshot: source PR #35735 in marcusquinn/aidevops: GitHub read failed (exit 127, attempt 1; not retryable)`, then `release-tag-signature-verification ... result=failed`.
- The same command from the OpenCode Bash tool, a minute later, printed `RELEASE_REMOTE_STATE=published` and `release:published tag=v3.39.77`.
- Inside a bounded operation, `command -v gh` resolves to the runtime-bundle shim `~/.aidevops/runtime-bundles/3.39.57-<id>/agents/scripts/gh`. `/opt/homebrew/bin` is also on PATH, and `gh run watch` as argv[0] worked in another bounded operation.
- Exit 127 from the shim means `_find_real_gh` failed (`.agents/scripts/gh`: the `auth:*`, passthrough and `REAL_GH` branches all `exit 127`). Its `_shim_report_missing_native_gh` stderr goes to `error_file` in `.agents/scripts/release-snapshot-helper.sh:60` and is discarded at `:81`.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/release-snapshot-helper.sh:79-82`: include a sanitized, bounded first line of `error_text` in the not-retryable message (and in `.agents/scripts/release-provenance-helper.sh:107`, which has the same pattern).
- `.agents/scripts/gh` `_find_real_gh`: reproduce under the release flow's nested PATH (release worktree `agents/scripts` plus runtime bundle) inside a bounded operation, and fix native-gh resolution if a nested shim directory hides `/opt/homebrew/bin/gh`.

## Verification

- `aidevops_bounded_operation start ["aidevops","release","reconcile","<published PR>"]` completes with `release:published`, or the failure names the actual cause.
- Existing shim tests: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-shim-native-resolution.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-shim.sh`.

body:
## Consolidation target: #35744

**Parent issue:** #35744 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`

**Parent labels:** `bug,status:blocked,tier:thinking,origin:worker,consolidation-in-progress`

> Sources are inlined below unless explicitly listed as omitted. Fetch omitted references before consolidating.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below, fetching any explicitly omitted sources first.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
     Preserve every wildcard scope entry verbatim from every superseded issue, including tool-generated paths such as `- NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Never invent a concrete machine, date, timestamp or filename in place of a pattern. Never change an existing `EDIT:` entry to `NEW:`.
     Check each path against the current default branch before copying its scope marker: use `git ls-files` in an up-to-date default-branch checkout or `gh api` for that branch's contents. Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.
   - **Runner prerequisites** — copy verbatim every line matching `^requires-secrets:` and its runner-prerequisite paragraph from every superseded issue. Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #35744 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`

3. **Validate before filing the new consolidated issue.** Save the parent body (inlined or explicitly fetched) verbatim to a local file, plus a separate body file for each additional superseded issue. Validate the merged body against ALL sources; a failed check stops publication and parent closure until the merged body is repaired:

```bash
python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/consolidation-contract-validator.py \
  --source "<file containing the verbatim parent body>" \
  --successor "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
# Repeat --source for each additional superseded issue body.
```

The validator must pass before running the signed creation command below. It checks verbatim secret lines and prerequisite paragraphs, wildcard scope preservation, and EDIT-to-NEW regressions. Also run `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check` on the merged body for ordinary scope syntax validation.

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,status:available,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding all status:* labels, needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body-file "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Use the signed wrapper above rather than the raw GitHub CLI so the successor retains the managed signature and origin metadata.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` and `status:available` are also mandatory. Keep exactly one `status:*` label on the successor: `status:available`, never the parent's lifecycle status. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch; the fill-floor enumerator also needs the available status.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close the parent #35744:**

```bash
gh issue comment 35744 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 35744 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \

gh issue close 35744 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #35744 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @vladimirdulov."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"

- Read only explicitly omitted source references when the packet size limit prevents inlining them; otherwise do NOT re-read #35744.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.

title: consolidated: classify and suppress unchanged GraphQL commit permission denials
body:
_Supersedes #35744 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Implement the dispatch permission-denial fix. Keep PR deduplication fail-closed. Classify nested GraphQL commit-access denials as explicit permission/evidence-unavailable blockers, and keep sanitized diagnostics and recovery checkpoints. Suppress unchanged admission reads until the relevant capability context changes or a bounded supported recheck is due.

## Why

Configured capacity was 3 with 0 live workers. Two independent issue admission attempts deferred with `PR_LOOKUP_UNCERTAIN scope=open_commits reason=api_request_failed`. Reproducing the production query returned GraphQL `FORBIDDEN` at `repository.pullRequests.nodes[].commits.nodes[]` (`Resource not accessible by integration`) with null commit nodes. PR metadata and `rateLimit.cost=1` were still available. Remaining GraphQL quota exceeded 4000, and supervisor logs showed repeated generic failures across candidates. This is permission/evidence unavailability, not quota exhaustion and not evidence that no PR exists. Project identifiers and protected paths are intentionally omitted and must remain so.

## How

1. **Implement from this spec on the current default branch.** The earlier checkpoint commits `6cdde1f8f` and `0519aac6a` were never pushed. On 2026-10-29 GitHub returns HTTP 422 for both, and no branch or PR holds them. They are historical evidence of a working design (summarised in step 3 and Context), not a salvage requirement. Do not wait for or block on them (GH#35871). If a remote ref holding them appears, compare and reuse it.
2. Reference `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh` `_ddpr_graphql_open_commits` and its caller. The query reads the ten newest open PRs with `commits(first:100)`, `messageHeadline` and `pageInfo`. stderr is discarded, and callers map failures to generic `api_request_failed`. Classify nested commit `FORBIDDEN` explicitly without weakening evidence requirements. Use fixture responses, never live permission changes. Keep transient transport errors independently retryable. This defect is distinct from the oversized-file/pagination fixes, including #34385 (closed).
3. Reference `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`: the prelaunch uncertainty guard and `_dsi_write_recovery_checkpoint`. The earlier design, per @vladimirdulov, had four parts: sanitized human-owned recovery state; repository/capability-scoped suppression; guarded rechecks after a context change or 900 seconds; and a cached-denial admission guard extracted to satisfy function complexity. Preserve exact checkpoint identity and ownership, and avoid repeated candidate scans while the denial is unchanged.
4. Use the existing GraphQL stub and request counts in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-helper-has-open-pr.sh` and the existing checkpoint ownership harness in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-single-issue-prelaunch.sh`. Do not introduce new infrastructure or a new test harness.
5. Verification tooling: run `bun run typecheck` when the repository toolchain is present. Never bypass hooks or install dependencies to evade a missing prerequisite. Since GH#35871, a missing local `tsc` defers typecheck to the CI `Typecheck` workflow instead of blocking the push.
6. Run the scoped dedup/single-issue checks, fail-closed and call-budget checks, scoped complexity regression gate, ShellCheck, Bash syntax and `git diff --check`.

### Files Scope
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-helper-has-open-pr.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-single-issue-prelaunch.sh

## Constraints

- Preserve fail-closed deduplication and commit evidence. Nested `FORBIDDEN` and null commit nodes must never become a clear/no-PR result or cause replacement PR creation.
- Never grant permissions, rotate credentials to bypass a denial, weaken commit evidence, or change live permissions to reproduce the issue. Permission repair is human-owned.
- No new infrastructure, access grants, spending, publication or deployed-file edits. Do not bypass hooks.
- Retain sanitized diagnostic/checkpoint evidence without leaking protected project identifiers, paths, credentials or raw sensitive provider output.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The implementation starts from the current default branch after checking for an existing PR or remote branch for this issue. Unreachable historical checkpoints are not required.
- [ ] Nested commit `FORBIDDEN` is an explicit permission/evidence-unavailable outcome and never clears the fail-closed guard. This holds even when metadata and cost are available and commit nodes are null.
- [ ] An unchanged repository/capability denial suppresses repeated admission/candidate reads. A relevant context change or a bounded supported recheck (900 seconds) re-enables guarded reads.
- [ ] A transient transport failure stays independently retryable and does not inherit permanent permission suppression.
- [ ] Sanitized diagnostics and exact checkpoint ownership remain intact. Permission repair stays human-owned, with no replacement PRs and no permission bypass.
- [ ] The scoped dedup, single-issue, fail-closed, call-budget and complexity checks, ShellCheck, Bash syntax and whitespace checks pass. No verification hook is bypassed.
- [ ] A ready PR linked to this issue (`Resolves #35751`) is opened and follows the normal merge workflow. Publication is not authorized.

## Context & Decisions

- Original parent #35744 is the binding scope: the permission-denial reproduction, the fail-closed outcome, sanitization, human-owned permission repair, bounded suppression and the explicit exclusions.
- @vladimirdulov's 2026-10-27T08:21:03Z report: the work was committed locally in `6cdde1f8f` and `0519aac6a`, but upload was blocked because Bun and a worktree-local TypeScript were missing for the enforced pre-push typecheck. Those commits never reached GitHub. Reported checks were: 69 has-open-pr, 96 single-issue, 8 fail-closed, 10 call-budget, plus ShellCheck, Bash syntax and whitespace. These are reproducible targets, not proof.
- 2026-10-29 (GH#35871): this issue looped for 116 comments. The brief demanded salvaging commits that no runner other than the originating one could reach, so every capable runner exited BLOCKED. The salvage requirement is removed. Typecheck stranding is fixed separately by the CI `Typecheck` workflow plus the pre-push deferral.

cc @vladimirdulov

title: todo_mapping_keys counts HTML-comment-wrapped template examples as real tasks, blocking merges
body:
## Observed

`issue-sync-pr-task-resolver.sh` `todo_mapping_keys()` (awk near line 14) matches every `- [ ] tN` line. That includes the format examples in the TOON TODO template, which GH#17804 wrapped in an HTML comment so parsers would skip them (`t1`, `t2`, `t1.1`, `t3`).

In a project repo whose real tasks are `t1` to `t3`, upgrading with `aidevops upgrade-planning` makes `full-loop-helper.sh merge` fail with `Merge blocked: prospective merge introduces duplicate TODO mappings` / `Duplicate task ID: t1 (TODO.md lines: 18,107)`. This is common after `task-id-normalize-helper.sh --apply` turns `t001` into `t1`. The pre-commit duplicate check did not flag the same file, so the two validators disagree.

Related: normalization renames historical padded duplicates. Two `t034` lines on main become two `t34` lines, and both the pre-commit and merge duplicate gates then treat them as new collisions because the baseline compares literal IDs. The normalizer dry-run only reports a conflict when `t034` and `t34` coexist. It does not report a `t034` that was already duplicated, so the failure first shows up at commit or merge time.

## Expected

- `todo_mapping_keys` skips lines inside `<!-- ... -->` blocks, using the same rule as the upgrade-planning parser.
- Duplicate baselines compare normalized IDs (leading zeros stripped), so normalizing a historical duplicate is not a new collision. Alternatively, the normalizer dry-run reports pre-existing duplicates as conflicts.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-pr-task-resolver.sh` (`todo_mapping_keys`, `todo_duplicate_report`)
- `.agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh` (`validate_duplicate_task_ids`)
- `.agents/scripts/task-id-normalize-helper.sh` (dry-run conflict detection)

## Verification

- TODO.md with the v1.1 template plus a real `- [x] t1 ...` line: `todo_duplicate_report` returns 0 against a baseline that has the same real line.
- TODO.md with two `t034` lines normalized to `t34`: not reported as a new duplicate (or reported by the normalizer dry-run before apply).

Workaround used: replaced the commented examples with `tN`/`tM` placeholders and re-IDed the real duplicates with claimed IDs.

title: playwright-runtime install: optionally include pinned @axe-core/playwright in the owned prefix
body:
## Observed

Guarded landing-page QA adapters on a user install resolve `@axe-core/playwright` beside the Playwright selected from the framework-owned runtime (`~/.aidevops/runtimes/playwright`). `playwright-runtime.mjs install` installs only `playwright@<pin>` plus browsers. On a fresh prefix, axe-based accessibility checks therefore block (`axe_package_unavailable`) until someone separately runs:

```bash
npm install --prefix ~/.aidevops/runtimes/playwright --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund --save-exact @axe-core/playwright@<pin>
```

Once axe is present it survives Playwright reinstalls and version bumps, because the prefix `package.json` records it. Only the first install is affected.

## Proposed

- File: `.agents/scripts/playwright-runtime.mjs`, `installPlaywrightRuntime()`, around the `npm install --prefix` call.
- Add an optional, framework-pinned `@axe-core/playwright` to the same install, either by default or behind an `install --with-axe` flag.
- Report axe presence in `runtime-check` output.
- Document it in `tools/browser/playwright.md`.
- Keep npx disabled and keep the existing `--ignore-scripts` behaviour.

## Verification

- On an empty prefix, `install` (or `install --with-axe`) results in both packages under `node_modules`.
- `runtime-check` reports axe readiness.
- Importing `@axe-core/playwright` resolved beside the owned Playwright module succeeds.

title: t18775: fix: skip credential-less config-only providers in subagent model routing
body:
## Task


Subagent model routing must not select a provider that OpenCode lists as "connected" only because the aidevops config hook injected model metadata for it. Such a provider has no credentials, so the child session fails.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Subagent model routing must not select a provider that OpenCode lists as "connected" only because the aidevops config hook injected model metadata for it. Such a provider has no credentials, so the child session fails.

## Why

Observed on an OpenCode install whose only credential is Anthropic (OAuth plus `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; `opencode auth list` shows no OpenAI entry; the OpenAI OAuth pool is empty). A Build+ `Task` with `subagent_type: "playwright"` failed immediately inside the child session with:

```text
OpenAI API key is missing. Pass it using the 'apiKey' parameter or the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable.
```

Root cause, verified against a local `opencode serve` `/provider` response:

```json
{"connected":["anthropic","opencode","openai", "..."],
 "providers":[{"id":"openai","source":"config","env":["OPENAI_API_KEY"],"hasKey":false,"optionKeys":[]}]}
```

1. `config-hook.mjs` and `context-budget-gpt6.mjs` always populate `config.provider.openai.models` (context limits for GPT-5.6/6 models).
2. OpenCode merges every configured provider into its provider state, so `openai` appears in `connected` with `source: "config"`, no `key`, and no `options.apiKey`.
3. `selectConnectedRoutingCandidate()` in `model-routing.mjs` treats membership in `connected` plus a registered model as usable.
4. `routeBrowserDelegate()` in `browser-delegate-routing.mjs` therefore pins the `playwright` child to `openai/gpt-6-luna`; tier routing (`applyConnectedRoutingModel`) can pick OpenAI Sol candidates for the same reason.

The `[effort:low]` marker in the original prompt is not the cause: it does not match the marker regex and falls back to `standard`; the playwright route ignores the tier.

## How

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/model-routing.mjs`: in `selectConnectedRoutingCandidate()`, skip a provider when there is positive evidence it is credential-less — `source === "config"` with no `key`, no non-empty `options.apiKey`, and no `options.baseURL`. Providers without a `source` field (older servers, fixtures) keep the current behaviour. Env, auth.json API keys and OAuth loaders populate `key` or `options.apiKey`, so they stay eligible.
- The browser delegate then falls back to the parent model (existing `browser_parent_fallback` path), and tier routing falls through to the next connected candidate.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-model-routing.mjs`: add a regression case for a config-only provider.

### Files Scope

- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/model-routing.mjs
- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-model-routing.mjs

## Acceptance

- A config-only `openai` provider is never returned by `selectConnectedRoutingCandidate()`; a credentialed one (key, `options.apiKey`, or custom `options.baseURL`) still is.
- `node .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-model-routing.mjs` and `node .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-subagent-effort.mjs` pass.

## Verification

```bash
node .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-model-routing.mjs
node .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-subagent-effort.mjs
node .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-local-only-policy.mjs
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Brief workflow contract</summary>

## Brief Workflow

This issue body is composed under `.agents/workflows/brief.md`. Newly queued auto-dispatch work must pass its `Dispatch Readiness Contract (brief schema v2)`: complete write surface, hazards and compatibility, executable verification mapped to affected surfaces, and positive plus negative/regression acceptance criteria.

</details>

title: Pulse: freshly pre-created worktrees classified legacy (match rc=3), worktree_precreation_failed on every fresh dispatch
body:
## Problem
On aidevops v3.39.77, pulse dispatch aborts with `PRE_RUNTIME_FAILURE reason=worktree_precreation_failed` whenever it has to create a **fresh** worktree. The path is created (`exists=1`), but `worktree-managed-lifetime.py match <path> <issue> <repo>` returns rc=3 (`legacy`) instead of `managed`, so `_dlw_classify_reuse_candidate` in `pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh` (~line 1054, `[[ "$_class" == managed\ * ]] || return 1`) fails without logging why. Reusing an already-existing worktree works.

Likely cause: path canonicalization. Our worktrees live under `/data/Git/_worktrees/...`; the path recorded at create time (`worktree-helper-add.sh`) and the path compared in `match` appear to differ by symlink resolution, so the fresh worktree is never recognized as managed.

Cross-repo impact on one host (counts of `worktree_precreation_failed` in pulse.log): 72, 31, 11, 10, 9, 9, 4, 1, 1 across nine repos. Each failed attempt also leaves an orphan `feature/auto-*-ghN` worktree.

## Evidence
```

title: fix(postflight): --tag should resolve the tag commit instead of caller worktree HEAD
body:
## What

`postflight-check.sh --tag vX.Y.Z` still takes the release commit from the caller's worktree HEAD (`.agents/scripts/postflight-check.sh:252`: `POSTFLIGHT_COMMIT_SHA` or `git rev-parse HEAD`), not from the tag. Run from any linked worktree that is not exactly the tag commit (the normal full-loop case, because the release helper builds its own detached worktree), it polls 20 snapshots for `Publish GitHub, npm, and Homebrew` on the wrong SHA and reports `POSTFLIGHT VERIFICATION FAILED`, even though publication succeeded.

## Evidence

The v3.39.78 release on 2026-10-27, run from a session worktree whose HEAD was `185aac036d`:
- `postflight-check.sh --tag v3.39.78` printed `Release commit: 185aac036d…`, then `Publish GitHub, npm, and Homebrew: missing`, then FAILED after about 11 minutes.
- The same run with `--sha baabd4dce4…` (the tag commit) passed within 50 seconds.
- `aidevops release status` already reported `RELEASE_RECEIPT=published`.

## How

When `--tag` is set and `--sha`/`POSTFLIGHT_COMMIT_SHA` is not, resolve the tag's commit (`git rev-parse "${tag}^{commit}"` after a tag fetch, or `gh api repos/<repo>/commits/<tag>`) and use it as `release_sha`. If `--sha` is also given and disagrees with the tag commit, fail clearly instead of silently choosing one. Keep the existing HEAD fallback only when no tag is given.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/postflight-check.sh`

## Verification

- From a worktree whose HEAD is not the tag commit: `bash .agents/scripts/postflight-check.sh --tag v3.39.78` prints `Release commit: baabd4dce4…` and passes.
- `--tag v3.39.78 --sha <other-sha>` fails with a clear mismatch message.
- shellcheck is clean.
