title: Fleet-level circuit for runner_capability_unmet: stop cross-runner ping-pong, escalate once, survive lockfile bumps
body:
## What

When every runner in the fleet lacks the same capability, the dispatcher must stop cycling the issue between runners. It should post **one** maintainer-actionable escalation that names the exact remediation, and wake only when a runner reports that capability. Today the fleet ping-pongs indefinitely and posts about 6 ops comments per attempt.

Related, not duplicated: #35689 defers headless admission *before* launch on a single runner. This issue covers the **fleet-level** circuit, the escalation, and policy staleness that keeps re-creating the blocker.

## Why (observed 2026-10-25 → 2026-10-27)

All three runners (marcusquinn, alex-solovyev, vladimirdulov) report `Terminal blocker: reason=runner_capability_unmet` with the **same** blocker fingerprint `blocker=0738181c7fb715c10ad8e589`. The cause is that worktrees lack `node_modules/.bin/tsc`, so the mandatory pre-push `bun run typecheck` exits 127. Workers correctly refuse to install dependencies or bypass hooks.

| Issue | Comments | Delivery |
|---|---:|---|
| #35689 | 119 | none (fix commits stranded on one runner, unpushed) |
| #35751 | 52 | none (commits `00cbe0f03`/`20d91b0bd` stranded, unpushed) |
| #35592 | 21 | draft #35598 parked since 2026-10-25 |
| #35600 | 20 | draft #35603 parked since 2026-10-25 |

Mechanisms:

1. `_DISPATCH_CAPABILITY_COOLDOWN_TTL_SECONDS` (default 21600) in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh:1031` is **runner-local**. Each runner and device retries on its own schedule, so the same unchanged environment fails over and over.
2. `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` projects `status:available` after every `runner_capability_unmet` release, even when N distinct runners have reported the identical fingerprint.
3. `js_dependency_policy` (`.agents/scripts/worktree-js-readiness-helper.sh`, `_jsr_policy_evaluate`, around line 626) binds approval to `lockfile_sha256`. Every Dependabot or deps PR (5 `bun.lock` changes in the last week, latest #35773) silently revokes every runner's approval (`stale-lockfile`). This brings back the fleet-wide `tsc` outage without telling anyone. The frozen-lockfile, `--ignore-scripts` install already pins exact contents, so the SHA binding adds churn without adding integrity.
4. `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION` text (`.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh:790-800`) tells the *brief owner* to revise the brief. For a `runner_capability_unmet` release the brief is fine. GH#34758 already lets such checkpoints continue once a capable runner exists, so the message points the human to the wrong action.

## How

1. In the terminal-blocker circuit, count distinct runner logins per (issue, task revision, capability fingerprint). At ≥2 distinct runners with the same fingerprint and no capable runner, record a durable fleet hold with wake condition `capability:<fingerprint>`. Do not set a global issue hold for single-runner reports (existing behaviour stays).
2. Post **one** escalation comment per fingerprint per repo, not per issue, on the maintainer's supervisor or health issue (pattern: `[Supervisor:<login>]` health dashboard issue). Give the concrete remediation, for example `worktree-js-readiness-helper.sh approve <worktree>` for `node-modules-missing (tsc)`, and list the held issues. Edit it in place on later observations.
3. Release the hold automatically when any runner's readiness probe reports the capability (`JS_TOOL_READINESS=ready`), or when the policy is (re)approved.
4. Policy staleness: keep `package_manager`, `node_major` and `scope` binding, but accept a lockfile change that arrived through a commit on the default branch. Re-verify through the frozen install (which fails closed on drift). Record the new SHA. Never accept an uncommitted or worktree-local lockfile change. Mark this with `#aidevops:trust-boundary`.
5. Branch the `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION` text on release reason. For `runner_capability_unmet`, state that no brief change is needed and point at the capability remediation instead.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-js-readiness-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-js-dependency-bootstrap.sh`

## Acceptance

- Same capability fingerprint from 2 runners → no third dispatch until a runner reports the capability. Exactly one escalation comment exists and later observations edit it.
- A `bun.lock` change merged to the default branch leaves an approved policy `current` after a successful frozen install. A worktree-local lockfile edit still yields `stale-lockfile`.
- Attention text for capability releases contains no brief-revision instruction.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-js-dependency-bootstrap.sh`
- `shellcheck` on changed scripts. `.agents/scripts/complexity-regression-helper.sh check --base origin/main --head HEAD`

## Runner prerequisite note

Workers on runners without an approved `js_dependency_policy` will hit the same `tsc` blocker on this issue. Each runner owner should first run `worktree-js-readiness-helper.sh approve <any-linked-worktree>` interactively.

title: approval-helper: show local retry time when core rate limit is exhausted
body:
## Problem

When `sudo aidevops approve ...` hits GitHub core API rate-limit exhaustion, `approval-helper.sh` prints only the raw reset epoch:

```
[ERROR] GitHub core API rate limit is exhausted for the invoking user's credential (reset epoch: 1793144448)
[INFO] Wait until reset epoch 1793144448 before retrying. ...
```

The operator has to convert the epoch by hand to know when to retry.

## Fix

`.agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh` `_approval_report_core_rate_limit` should render the reset as local wall-clock time plus the remaining wait. Use GNU `date -d @N` first, then BSD `date -r N`. Keep the epoch and the existing "Re-authentication or forwarding GH_TOKEN will not help before reset" text, because `tests/test-approval-helper-sudo-gh-auth.sh` asserts on both.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-sudo-gh-auth.sh`
- Source the helper and call `_approval_report_core_rate_limit <future-epoch>`. Expected output: `Retry after YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS TZ local time, in about N min (reset epoch ...)`.

title: pulse: detect and halt cross-runner needs-maintainer-review label flapping
body: ## Problem Two pulse runners can disagree on whether an issue author is trusted. When that happens, one runner applies `needs-maintainer-review` (NMR) and the other removes it. Nothing detects this oscillation, so the loop runs silently until a human notices. ## Observed evidence (private managed repo, 2026-10-13 to 2026-10-14) - Issue A (author association `MEMBER` in a live REST check): **80 NMR labeled/unlabeled events in about 25 hours**, from 2026-10-13T19:34Z to 2026-10-14T20:14Z. Runner X (aidevops v3.39.31) applied the label every time. Runner X and runner Y both removed it. No comment explained any toggle. - Issue B (same author): 10 toggles in the same window. - Root cause was GH#34644 (fixed by PR #34645, merged 2026-10-14T18:49Z). Runner X saw the private org member as `author_association=CONTRIBUTOR`, treated the author as untrusted and applied NMR. Runner Y saw `MEMBER` and normalized the label away. The loop stopped about 1.5 hours after the fix merged. No NMR toggles have occurred in that repo since then (checked 2026-10-28). - No detector caught this. `gh-audit-log-helper.sh` flags each `protected_label_removed:needs-maintainer-review` op on its own, but nothing checks the add/remove cadence on a single issue. The only rate-control code is hysteresis in `peer-productivity-monitor.sh`, which covers peer votes, not labels. ## Why it matters The next trust-evaluation divergence will burn API writes and dispatch cycles in the same way. Examples: a token scope difference, a permission-cache disagreement, or a version skew between runners. It also makes the protected-label audit trail meaningless while the loop runs, and it hides real maintainer holds. ## Proposed fix (worker-ready) Add a protected-label flap guard. When the same protected label (start with `needs-maintainer-review`; make the list configurable) is added and removed N times (default 4) on one issue or PR within a window (default 6h): 1. Stop mutating that label on that target for a cooldown period. Leave the label applied, which is the fail-closed choice. 2. Post one deduplicated marker comment. Include the runners and versions involved, plus the trust decision each runner made (association, authority reason). 3. Log an anomaly line that `gh-audit-log-helper.sh` reports, e.g. `protected_label_flap:

title: fix(pulse-merge): auto-merge scoped OpenCode pin-canary worker briefs
body:
## What

Let worker PRs that implement the scheduled OpenCode pin-canary briefs auto-merge through the existing worker-briefed gate. Trust is bound to the canary workflow's exact titles and file scope. Do not add a broad `github-actions[bot]` exception.

## Why

`.github/workflows/opencode-pin-canary.yml` files `origin:worker` + `auto-dispatch` issues as `github-actions[bot]` (`author_association=CONTRIBUTOR`). `_attempt_worker_briefed_auto_merge` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh` therefore rejected the worker PRs. `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh` reported `pm-wb-not-owner`. Green worker PRs #35754 and #35757 (briefs #35752 and #35753) sat unmerged and unreleased until a maintainer merged them by hand.

## How

- New `_is_trusted_opencode_canary_issue_pr` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh`, checked after the trusted-author allowlist and before crypto approval. It is marked `#aidevops:trust-boundary`.
  - The issue author must be exactly `github-actions[bot]` with `user.type == Bot`. Fork tokens cannot create issues as this identity, so only this repository's workflows can.
  - The title must match the two canary titles exactly, and the issue must carry `origin:worker`.
  - Every changed PR file must be on the canary allowlist: the workflow's Files Scope plus its two named verification tests. The PR must change 1-20 files, and renames fail closed.
  - Changes to `shared-constants.sh` may only touch comments, `readonly OPENCODE_*="literal"` assignments, or `vN:key) printf 'literal\n' ;;` rows. Expansions, sourcing and new code fail closed.
  - Any API error or missing patch fails closed. All other merge gates (required checks, reviews, review-bot, NMR) still apply.
- Add a sync comment in the workflow that points at the gate.

## Verification

- Ran the live predicate (read-only API): #35754/#35752 → trusted, #35757/#35753 → trusted. An unrelated wide PR paired with a canary brief is rejected (out-of-scope file). A non-bot issue is rejected.
- Patch validator: `$(...)` expansion and `source` lines are rejected. Profile-table rows are accepted.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-worker-briefed.sh` (26/26) and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-issue-sync-authority.sh` (19/19) pass. ShellCheck is clean.

## Consolidation target: #28839

**Parent issue:** #28839 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`

**Parent labels:** `status:available,auto-dispatch,tier:thinking,origin:worker,consolidation-in-progress,file-size-debt`

> Sources are inlined below unless explicitly listed as omitted. Fetch omitted references before consolidating.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below, fetching any explicitly omitted sources first.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
     Preserve every wildcard scope entry verbatim from every superseded issue, including tool-generated paths such as `- NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Never invent a concrete machine, date, timestamp or filename in place of a pattern. Never change an existing `EDIT:` entry to `NEW:`.
     Check each path against the current default branch before copying its scope marker: use `git ls-files` in an up-to-date default-branch checkout or `gh api` for that branch's contents. Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.
   - **Runner prerequisites** — copy verbatim every line matching `^requires-secrets:` and its runner-prerequisite paragraph from every superseded issue. Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.

title: t18776: fix(release): stop recurring CodeRabbit CHANGELOG reference-definition blocks on release PRs
body:
## Task


Stop CodeRabbit from requesting changes on every protected release PR (`chore/release-v<semver>-provenance`) because of a missing Markdown reference definition for the new `## [X.Y.Z]` CHANGELOG heading.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Stop CodeRabbit from requesting changes on every protected release PR (`chore/release-v<semver>-provenance`) because of a missing Markdown reference definition for the new `## [X.Y.Z]` CHANGELOG heading.

## Why (observed evidence)

- Release PR #35792 (v3.39.79) and release PR #35805 (v3.39.80) both got a CodeRabbit `CHANGES_REQUESTED` review at the signed release commit. The finding was the same both times: `[X.Y.Z]` at `CHANGELOG.md:13` has no matching reference definition.
- `CHANGELOG.md` on `main` has **zero** `[x.y.z]: https://...` reference definitions in its history (checked with `rg -c '^\[[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\]: ' CHANGELOG.md`). The headings follow the Keep a Changelog bracket style but have never had link targets. So this is a convention gap across the whole repo, not a defect in any one release.
- A signed release PR cannot take a fix commit, because that breaks the merge topology (see #35798, which stranded v3.39.79). Each release currently needs a maintainer `coderabbit-nits-ok` label plus `review-bot-gate-helper.sh dismiss-coderabbit-nits <PR>` before native auto-merge can proceed. #35805 was unblocked this way.

## How

Pick the smaller option. Prefer option 1.

1. `.coderabbit.yaml`: add a `reviews.path_instructions` entry for `CHANGELOG.md` saying that version headings use bare `[X.Y.Z]` brackets by convention and must not be flagged for missing reference definitions. Alternatively, exclude `CHANGELOG.md` from review on release-provenance PRs if the config supports that.
2. Alternative: have the changelog writer emit a compare-link definition for each new version (for example `[X.Y.Z]: https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/compare/vPREV...vX.Y.Z`). Find the writer with `rg -n "## \[" .agents/scripts --glob 'version-manager*.sh'`. This must happen before the release commit is signed. It does not backfill history.

### Files Scope

- `.coderabbit.yaml`
- `.agents/scripts/version-manager-release.sh`

## Notes

Option 2's exact changelog-writer function has not been identified. `version-manager-release.sh` is the likely file. Confirm with the `rg` command above.

## Verification

- Option 1: the next release PR gets no CHANGELOG reference-definition finding from CodeRabbit, and auto-merge proceeds without `coderabbit-nits-ok`.
- Option 2: `rg -n '^\[X\.Y\.Z\]: ' CHANGELOG.md` matches on the next release commit. ShellCheck is clean on the edited script.

Related: #35798 (never push to release provenance PRs).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Brief workflow contract</summary>

## Brief Workflow

This issue body is composed under `.agents/workflows/brief.md`. Newly queued auto-dispatch work must pass its `Dispatch Readiness Contract (brief schema v2)`: complete write surface, hazards and compatibility, executable verification mapped to affected surfaces, and positive plus negative/regression acceptance criteria.

</details>

title: aidevops_bounded_operation: long runs end as failed/SIGKILL after about 2 hours with no cancel or budget expiry; 30 s kill grace cuts TERM handlers short
body:
## What happened Two interactive `aidevops_bounded_operation` runs in one OpenCode session ended with `state: failed`, `process_signal: SIGKILL` and `containment: incomplete` long before their budgets, with no cancel action and no budget expiry: | Run | Budget | Elapsed at kill | |---|---|---| | 1 | 21,600 s | 8,545 s (2h22m) | | 2 | 21,600 s | 7,452 s (2h04m) | Both ran a long Bash script (a resumable data import over SSH) that wrote ordinary progress lines to stdout but no `AIDEVOPS_PROGRESS:` lines, so status showed `progress_events: 0` and `progress_overdue: true` throughout. In run 2 the script's `trap ... INT TERM` handler logged that it had caught the signal at 2h00m, then started a remote clean-up over SSH; it never reached its next line (releasing its lock) before the SIGKILL. The supervisor's `killGraceMs` is at most 30 s (`bounded-operation-supervisor.mjs`, `createTerminator`), so a trap that needs to stop remote work cannot finish. ## Unknown What sent the first SIGTERM. Candidates from the code: `disposeOperations()` in `bounded-operation-runtime.mjs` (plugin dispose or reload), or an idle or no-progress policy. The OpenCode log under `~/.local/share/opencode/log/` had not been written since July, so it gave no evidence either way. ## Asks 1. Record the termination cause in the receipt (budget, cancel, dispose or reload, supervisor exit), so `failed` + `SIGKILL` can be told apart. 2. If dispose or reload is the cause, document that operations do not survive it, next to the existing "restarting OpenCode expires the operation" note in `reference/context-efficient-output.md`. 3. title: Worker blocker contract omits source_access_blocked, so external source denials classify as unknown
body:
## What
The headless worker blocker contract never mentions `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=source_access_blocked`. `terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` already supports it: it's in the allowed set, in the revision re-arm set, and in the `access-owner` routing added by GH#34223. Workers can't emit a class they've never been told about. When an external source refuses access, they either leave out the reason line or pick the wrong class.

## Evidence (one pulse recovery pass, managed project repo, award-enrichment issues)
In 9 queued terminal-blocker entries, every cause was an external source refusing access: HTTP 403 or a bot challenge, Cloudflare 525, DNS NXDOMAIN, or an "event not found" page. The reported classes were:
- `unknown`, with workers writing variations of "no defined class covers an external source-access gap, so I'm omitting the reason line" (4 entries)
- `external_trigger_pending`, used where no named trusted trigger exists (2 entries)
- `target_code_blocker`, later corrected by the worker itself as wrong because provider failures are excluded (1 entry)
- `input_required`, later corrected by the worker itself (1 entry)

Each misclassification sends the hold to `worker-triage`, or the wrong owner, instead of `access-owner`. That costs extra supervisor passes and repeat worker attempts on unchanged sources.

### Files Scope
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`

## Files to modify
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh`: in `_worker_headless_contract_blocker_text()`, add a `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=source_access_blocked` stanza. Model it on the `external_trigger_pending` and `permission_required` stanzas. Use it when a required external source keeps refusing access (403, bot challenge, DNS failure, TLS or origin failure, removed page) on every approved acquisition path. Never use it for missing local credentials (`runner_capability_unmet`) or for permission guards (`permission_required`). The dossier must name the URLs or hosts, the status per path, and the reopen condition.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`: the contract assertion near the existing `target_code_blocker` and `missing_files_scope` checks (around line 94) should also assert the new line is present.

## Reference pattern
- `terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` `_TBC_SOURCE_ACCESS` and its `source_access_blocked)` owner/action case
- `reference/worker-discipline.md` "Terminal-blocker recovery" (already lists the class as revision-re-armed)

## Verification
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh`
- The rendered worker contract contains exactly one standalone `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=source_access_blocked` line.

title: Add portable Worker Lifecycle Registry in observe-only mode
body:
## Goal

Add a portable Worker Lifecycle Registry in explicitly opt-in, observe-only mode. This is an interactive implementation already owned by the current session; do not dispatch a competing implementation.

## Scope and reference pattern

- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/`: standard-library Linux/macOS process adapters, readiness, `LifecycleRegistry`, SQLite schema 1, events and reconciliation.
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker-launch.py`, `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-invoke.sh`, `.agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh`: worker-only pre-exec observation using `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_STATE_DIR`, preserving admission, sandbox policy and native behavior.
- `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml`: scoped Ruff/mypy and existing unittest runner.
- Two validators: `worker-lifecycle-process-validate.pyz` and `worker-lifecycle-registry-validate.pyz`.
- Exactly four latest reports: process/Linux, process/macOS, registry/Linux, registry/macOS. Stable filenames and actual fingerprints, no accumulated dated copies.
- Contracts: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/DESIGN.md`, `PROTOCOL.md`, `REGISTRY.md`, `REGISTRY-VALIDATION.md`, `COMPATIBILITY.md` and `tests/`.

## Acceptance and verification

Current Linux evidence: 37 unit tests, 10 process-validator checks and 26 registry-validator checks pass. Ruff, mypy, scoped Pylint, Bandit and ShellCheck pass locally. Sandbox command-policy suite passed 55 checks. Retained macOS reports qualify only their recorded builds; final rebuilt-bundle revalidation and real macOS worker/sandbox integration are not claimed.

Unknown identity never implies ended; signal-zero lookup sends no signal. `cleanup_authorized` is always false. No existing worktree deletion, legacy mutation, protected-workload collection, global activation or root requirement. Runtime dependencies remain standard-library only.

Full Pulse coverage, durable producer delivery, physical generation identity, retention, scheduling and cleanup migration remain outside this prototype. Remote CI/review must pass before delivery is complete.

title: browser-qa-helper a11y reports found contrast failures as 'contrast check failed' and drops them
body:
## What

`browser-qa-helper.sh a11y` reports `{"error": "contrast check failed"}` for a page whenever `accessibility/playwright-contrast.mjs` **finds** contrast failures, and drops the findings.

- `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper-a11y.sh`, `_run_contrast_checks()` (around line 56): `contrast_result=$(run_playwright_node "$contrast_script" ... 2>/dev/null) || contrast_result='{"error": "contrast check failed"}'`.
- `.agents/scripts/accessibility/playwright-contrast.mjs` line 286: `process.exit(hasFailures ? 1 : 0)`; exit 2 is the real error path (line 290).

So exit 1 ("ran, found failures", with valid JSON on stdout) is treated like a crash. A page with failures looks like a tool error, and a page that only shows contrast results is a page with none, the opposite of what a reviewer needs.

## Observed (2026-10-28, a WordPress review site, `--level AA`, six pages)

- The helper printed "contrast check failed" for 4 pages and real results for 2 (114 and 59 elements, 0 failures).
- Running `node playwright-contrast.mjs <url> --format summary --level AA --fail-only` on the 4 pages gave valid results: 1 to 4 failures each (a decorative `aria-hidden` star glyph, and text over a CSS gradient measured against white).

## Fix

In `_run_contrast_checks()`, capture the exit status and accept stdout when it is 0 or 1; report an error only for other statuses or unparsable JSON. For example: run, keep `rc=$?`, then `if [[ $rc -le 1 ]] && jq -e . >/dev/null <<<"$contrast_result"; then ... else contrast_result='{"error":"contrast check failed","exit":'"$rc"'}'; fi`.

Related (optional): the summary flags text over gradients with `WARNING: gradient — manual review needed` but still counts it as a failure at 1:1 (white on its white fallback). Counting those under "Complex backgrounds (manual review)" instead of "Fail" would avoid false failures.

## Verification

1. On a page with a known contrast failure, `browser-qa-helper.sh a11y --url <site> --pages "/" --level AA` shows the failing elements in `contrast`, not `{"error": ...}`.
2. On a clean page, the output is unchanged.
3. `shellcheck .agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper-a11y.sh`: zero violations.
<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->
<!-- aidevops:sig -->
---
[aidevops.sh](https://aidevops.sh) v3.39.80 plugin for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) v1.19.5 with claude-opus-5-5 spent 3d 6h and 6,699,021 tokens on this with the user in an interactive session.

### Files Scope
- `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper-a11y.sh`

Scope: preserve valid JSON for contrast exit statuses 0 and 1; report execution/JSON errors. Optional gradient classification is excluded from this fix. Verify with ShellCheck and focused runtime checks for clean, failing, malformed and execution-error results.

title: consolidated: diagnose bounded-operation termination and preserve TERM grace
body:
_Supersedes #35817 — this issue is the consolidated spec._ ## What Recover and deliver the existing bounded-operation termination diagnostics and configurable TERM grace work. Record first termination cause across manager and supervisor paths; expose bounded per-operation `kill_grace_seconds` up to 300 seconds without changing the default; preserve containment, process-identity checks and session ownership. This is the implementation handoff from consolidation task #35822, not a claim that the existing implementation has shipped. ## Why Per @vladimirdulov, two interactive `aidevops_bounded_operation` runs in one OpenCode session ended with `state: failed`, `process_signal: SIGKILL` and `containment: incomplete`, long before their budgets, without a cancel action or budget expiry: | Run | Budget | Elapsed at kill | |---|---|---| | 1 | 21,600 s | 8,545 s (2h22m) | | 2 | 21,600 s | 7,452 s (2h04m) | Both ran a long Bash script performing a resumable data import over SSH. Ordinary stdout progress did not include `AIDEVOPS_PROGRESS:` lines, so status showed `progress_events: 0` and `progress_overdue: true` throughout. Progress overdue must remain diagnostic-only, not a termination policy. In run 2, the script's `trap ... INT TERM` handler logged receipt of a signal at 2h00m and started remote cleanup over SSH, but never reached its next line releasing the lock before SIGKILL. The original supervisor capped `killGraceMs` at 30 seconds. A longer configurable grace (90 seconds was suggested) should let a command's TERM handler stop remote work and release locks, without changing the existing default. The sender of the first SIGTERM is unknown. Candidate code paths were `disposeOperations()` during plugin dispose/reload or an idle/no-progress policy; these are hypotheses, not established causes. The OpenCode log had not been updated since July and supplied no evidence. Do not attribute the historical two-hour signal without evidence. The original workaround was to restart the resumable script using per-part receipts and `--break-lock`, only after checking that nothing remained running remotely and repairing the one record left incomplete by interruption. This is incident context, not authorization to run remote operations or break locks in this task. ## Reproducer **Observed incident, not a deterministic reproduction of the historical signal source:** Start a long-running SSH import through `aidevops_bounded_operation` with a 21,600-second budget, ordinary stdout progress and an INT/TERM trap performing remote cleanup before releasing its lock. The two reported runs stopped after 8,545 and 7,452 seconds without cancellation or budget expiry. The original import script and a reproducible first-SIGTERM trigger were not supplied; do not run remote imports to recreate this incident. **Actual output:** `state: failed`, `process_signal: SIGKILL`, `containment: incomplete`, `progress_events: 0`, `progress_overdue: true`; the second run's TERM handler began cleanup but did not reach lock release. For the three review defects, use the concrete manager-fallback, restoration exit-zero and same-group-survivor scenarios in How as focused local regressions within the existing lifecycle suite. **Expected output:** Receipts distinguish first termination cause from final escalation, effective grace matches the supervisor, live-command cleanup receives configured grace, restoration termination cannot become false success, and descendants drain promptly after main exit. Historical SIGTERM attribution remains unconfirmed. ## How ### Recover existing work before implementing 1. Recheck current default-branch and PR state. PR #35818 (https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/35818) is closed, not merged. Its pushed branch `feature/auto-20261028-062419-gh35817` remains at `94ca041d80185e8f84fb120840ad756f7f515e64`, verified during consolidation. Reuse salvageable commits, reconciling with the current default branch rather than rebuilding the feature. 2. Per @vladimirdulov's 2026-10-28 06:22 UTC checkpoint, original attempt commits `b3ca16bac` (implementation) and `058f54d44` (regressions) were preserved on `feature/auto-20261028-061433-gh35817`, with a clean worktree. Changes stayed in the six scoped files; first cause was retained, grace supported up to 300 seconds with defaults unchanged, and no historical signal source was attributed. 3. Per @vladimirdulov's 2026-10-28 09:36 UTC checkpoint, local merge commit `c9a477df6` on that original branch preserved both histories, including PR #35818 at `94ca041d8`, and addressed all three review findings below. It reported a clean worktree and no replacement PR. The consolidation worktree does not contain that object; its content here is unverified, not proof it was lost. Recover it when available; otherwise reuse the verified pushed PR branch and reapply only missing repairs. 4. The default branch still has the original manager grace wiring and 30-second supervisor cap; the outcome is not already satisfied. No replacement PR or existing consolidated successor was found during discovery. ### Implementation references Line references below identify the default-branch baseline inspected during consolidation; they shift in recovered commits. Verify recovered code before editing. - `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-interactive-operation.mjs:60,117,223,322`: manager default (500 ms), launch wiring, `runRestoration()` and disposal. Record first termination cause instead of overwriting it during cleanup or SIGKILL escalation. Distinguish budget, cancel, dispose/reload and supervisor exit in receipts so `failed` plus `SIGKILL` is diagnosable. - `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-runtime.mjs:118`: `disposeOperations()` and supervisor report handling. Keep main/restoration cause and termination evidence independent, preserving containment and session ownership. - `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-supervisor.mjs:73,111,133,190`: `createTerminator()`, `ownedTreeDrained()`, grace clamping and exit cleanup. Preserve TERM grace while the main command remains alive; retain PID/start-identity checks and containment reports. - `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-tool.mjs:27-42`: seconds-based schema and manager conversion. Add `kill_grace_seconds`, bounded to 300 seconds, without changing the omitted-option default. - `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs:33-49`: existing manager fixture/lifecycle suite. Add focused regressions here; do not add a runner or test-only interfaces. Read-only reference: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-operation-dispatch-launcher.mjs` for dispatch containment verification. - `.agents/reference/context-efficient-output.md:76-100`: existing progress receipts and OpenCode lifetime/restart note. Document disposal/reload lifetime next to it, grace configuration, first-cause diagnostics and diagnostic-only progress overdue. Operations do not survive dispose/reload; do not imply durable scheduling. ### Cumulative review requirements from PR #35818 Consolidation retrieved the omitted review source. @coderabbitai[bot] requested changes with exactly three actionable inline findings. The recovery checkpoint reports repairs, but verify recovered code/tests rather than assume they exist on the pushed PR head: 1. **Clamp the manager fallback as well as requests.** At PR baseline `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-interactive-operation.mjs:144`, `boundedInteger()` returned an out-of-range manager default unchanged when the request omitted `killGraceMs`. Clamp fallback to the same 10–300,000 ms range. Receipt `kill_grace_ms` must match the supervisor's actual deadline, including manager options above the maximum. 2. **Preserve restoration termination reports.** At PR baseline `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-runtime.mjs:84-86`, the non-main-stage branch discarded restoration supervisor budget/disposal reports. Retain restoration cause and termination state separately. Use them in `runRestoration()` classification: budget termination is `timed_out` even if the TERM handler exits zero before the manager timer fires; disposal classification uses its recorded cause, not exit-zero success. 3. **Escalate same-group survivors after main exit.** At PR baseline `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-supervisor.mjs:135`, a same-group child ignoring SIGTERM could delay `ownedTreeDrained()` for the new 300-second grace, allowing budget expiry to turn a completed command into a timeout during cleanup. Escalate survivors promptly after the main command exits while retaining identity checks and containment evidence. Preserve grace for children while the main command is still alive. Review sources: https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/35818#pullrequestreview-5679424900, https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/35818#discussion_r4398136483, https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/35818#discussion_r4398136490. The optional CodeRabbit CLI suggestion is not a prerequisite or permission to install it. ### Verification and delivery recovery Original verification target: Node v24.21.0 using existing `node --test`. Consolidation runner: Node v22.23.3. Current `package.json` declares Node >=20, Bun 1.3.11 and TypeScript 7.0.2; `typecheck` is `tsc --noEmit`. Within the existing lifecycle suite cover first-cause attribution, request/fallback grace bounds, live-command TERM-handler grace, restoration budget/dispose with exit-zero cleanup, and prompt post-main same-group descendant cleanup. Historical verification, per @vladimirdulov: the first attempt passed 24/24 lifecycle/dispatch tests under Node v24.21.0; review recovery passed 29/29. Both reported passing changed-module syntax checks, scoped Markdown lint and whitespace checks. Independent supplied-file reviews found no concrete in-scope defects. These are prior checkpoint reports, not verification newly run by consolidation. **Runner prerequisites / unresolved delivery dependency:** Both checkpoints were blocked by unchanged mandatory pre-push `bun run typecheck`: no TypeScript executable or worktree-local dependency environment, exit 127. The worker was forbidden to install dependencies and reported no typecheck equivalent in repository workflows. No hook or signing bypass was attempted. title: Review followup: PR #35805 — chore(release): preserve signed v3.39.80 publication
body:
## Unaddressed review bot suggestions PR #35805 was merged with unaddressed review bot feedback. Each comment below includes its file path, line number, a direct link to the inline review comment, and a `diff` fence with the code context the bot was flagging. Resolved and outdated threads are filtered out via GitHub's GraphQL review-thread state. Read the relevant lines, decide whether the suggestion is correct, and either apply the fix or close this issue with a wontfix rationale. **Source PR:** https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/35805 --- ### You are the triager (worker-is-triager rule) This issue is **auto-created from review bot output** and dispatched directly to you. Review bots can be wrong: hallucinated line refs, false premises about codebase structure, template-driven sweeps without measurements (see GH#17832-17835 for prior art and `AGENTS.md` "AI-Generated Issue Quality"). **Do not assume the bot is correct.** Verify before acting. You must end in exactly one of three outcomes — no fourth "hand it back to the human" path exists. Humans approve decisions; they do not re-do analysis. #### Outcome A — Premise falsified → close the issue 1. Read the cited `file:line` (listed under *Files to modify* below). 2. title: Tool-output redaction replaces the word aidevops with [redacted-credential], breaking Edit matches
body:
## What In an OpenCode session, the Read and Bash tool output replaced the plain word "aidevops" with `[redacted-credential]` in some contexts, though it is not a secret. Examples: the Markdown heading `## Built with aidevops`, the HTML comment marker ``, and prose like "the weekly Star History workflow is pinned to one aidevops version". Other occurrences in the same files, such as `aidevops-managed`, were shown unchanged. `od -c` on the file confirmed the bytes are `aidevops`. Because Read shows the redacted text, an Edit whose `oldString` copies such a line never matches ("oldString not found"). The agent then has to use line-number `sed` deletes and retype the line, which risks silent data loss. Observed while working on public repo wpallstars/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding (README.md, changelog.txt, readme.txt, scripts/preflight-release.sh), 2026-10-28. ## Expected The secret-redaction filter on tool output does not treat the framework's own name as a credential. Redaction should be keyed to credential shapes (token prefixes, high-entropy values, known secret names), not to the word "aidevops" after "with", ":" or "one". ## How (worker guidance) - Find the tool-output redaction layer in the OpenCode plugin (search `.agents/` and the opencode-aidevops plugin sources for `redacted-credential`). - Find the pattern matching `aidevops` (probably an allowlist or denylist entry for the `aidevops:` marker or the signature-comment prefix) and narrow it, so literal content in user files passes through. - Verify: Read a file containing `## Built with aidevops` and ``; the output shows them verbatim, and an Edit using that text as `oldString` succeeds. ### Files Scope - `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/registered-value-sources.mjs` - `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/registered-value-redaction.mjs` - `.agents/scripts/redaction-digest-registry.py` - `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-registered-value-redaction.mjs` - `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks.mjs` - `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-output-scrub.mjs` ### Implementation evidence and verification The pattern scrubber does not match the bare framework name. Exact-value registration accepts arbitrary credential-file/injected values of eight characters or more. A registered digest for the public name explains boundary-dependent redaction while leaving `aidevops-managed` unchanged. Exclude this single public value from exact-value registration/matching, including stale digest entries. Keep sensitive named assignment, URL userinfo, private-key and token-shape scrubbing intact; do not broadly exclude low-entropy secrets or arbitrary credential names. No local credential files need inspection. Verify with Node 24 using existing registered-value, credential-scrub and redacted-edit-guard tests. Add synthetic post-tool Read/Bash coverage with a stale digest, prove exact oldString replacement, and assert named password assignments and longer secrets containing the framework name remain scrubbed. Mirror registration exclusion in the Python helper and exercise it via existing fixtures. --- [aidevops.sh](https://aidevops.sh) v3.39.80 plugin for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) v1.19.5 with claude-opus-5-5 spent 30m and 30,754 tokens on this with the user in an interactive session. ## Review Feedback routed from PR #35831 (t2093) This section was auto-generated when the deterministic merge pass detected `reviewDecision=CHANGES_REQUESTED` on the linked worker PR. title: wait-checks treats a concurrency-cancelled required check as terminal failure after gh pr ready
body:
## What `full-loop-helper.sh wait-checks ` returned exit 1 ("FAIL: required checks reached a terminal failure") when the only "failure" was a required check with conclusion `cancelled`. The run was cancelled by the workflow's `concurrency: cancel-in-progress` group after `gh pr ready` started a new run for the same head. Sequence on public repo wpallstars/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding PR #566, 2026-10-28: 1. PR created as draft (interactive default); `wait-checks` started. 2. `gh pr ready 566` triggered a `ready_for_review` run; the draft run's "Release build, preflight and Plugin Check" job was cancelled. 3. `wait-checks` printed `added as cancel` and exited 1. 4. A second `wait-checks` call passed (pass=4) about 4 minutes later. ## Expected A `cancelled` check is not a terminal failure while a newer run of the same check name exists, or is queued, for the same head SHA. `wait-checks` should keep waiting (exit 8 or continue) until the superseding run finishes. Only a cancellation with no newer run for that head is terminal. ## How (worker guidance) - File: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh` (the `wait-checks` subcommand) and any sourced CI-state library it uses for terminal classification. - When a required check's conclusion is `cancelled`, query the check runs for the same head SHA and name. If a later run exists (larger id or later `started_at`) that is queued, in progress or completed, follow that one. - Verify: on a test PR with a cancel-in-progress workflow, start `wait-checks` on a draft, then `gh pr ready`; `wait-checks` stays pending and ends with PASS when the new run passes. --- [aidevops.sh](https://aidevops.sh) v3.39.80 plugin for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) v1.19.5 with claude-opus-5-5 spent 31m and 30,754 tokens on this with the user in an interactive session. ## Review Feedback routed from PR #35832 (t2093) This section was auto-generated when the deterministic merge pass detected `reviewDecision=CHANGES_REQUESTED` on the linked worker PR. title: Agents reuse stale remote GitHub state across turns (releases, deploys, PR status)
body:
## What happened

In a long interactive session that followed an outside public GitHub repository, the agent twice answered status questions with out-of-date state:

1. **Release and deploy status.** In one turn the agent queried releases (correct at about 11:30 UTC). About three hours later it answered "the latest release is still vX, nothing is deployed" without querying again. A new release tag had been created at 12:20, its production deploy ran from 12:20 to 12:32, and the release was published at 14:00. To support "not deployed", the agent looked at only the newest Deploy run, a manual run on `main` that skipped the server jobs, and generalised from it. That run's commit was newer than any `main` the agent had seen, which should have prompted a fresh fetch.
2. **PR merge status.** A "not merged" answer was correct when queried, but the PR merged through the merge queue a few minutes later. This was not an error, but nothing in the answer said it was a point-in-time result.

GitHub's API was accurate whenever it was queried. Each tool call returned live data, with no caching. The failure was in the agent: it reused results from earlier turns. One harness factor contributed: the model's context shows only today's date, with no time on each user message, so the agent cannot see how long it has been since a previous query unless it checks.

The risk: repairs, rebases or new code built on stale remote state (an already merged PR, an already shipped release, an already fixed bug).

## Proposed rule

For any answer about mutable remote state (PR or issue status, CI, releases, tags, deployments, branch heads), and before any repair or code based on it:

- Query in the current turn. Never repeat a previous turn's result as current. If citing it, give its time.
- Run `date -u` first, and state times in the answer.
- Fetch first: `git fetch --tags <remote>` or `git ls-remote --tags`. Release pages can be drafts after the tag exists, so `gh release list` alone misses the gap between tagging and publishing.
- For deploy questions, list several runs filtered by `event` (tag push vs. branch push vs. `workflow_dispatch`), not `--limit 1`.
- If an observation is newer than the state already known (an unseen SHA or a newer run), stop, re-fetch and re-check before concluding.

## Files to change

- `.agents/reference/diagnostics-discipline.md`: add a "Remote state is a current-state query" section next to the existing current-state rules (t3222, "Productivity questions are current-state queries").
- `.agents/reference/gh-command-discipline.md`: a short pointer to that section.
- Possibly one line in `.agents/AGENTS.md` "Automation safety invariants" or "Quality and diagnostics" (watch the size ratchet).
- Candidate for `.agents/configs/prompt-hook-candidates.conf`: if a turn answers status without any `gh`/`git fetch` call in that turn, a hook could flag it, or prepend the current time to each user turn.

## Verification

- `markdownlint` / the repo's docs checks pass, and the AGENTS.md size ratchet holds if AGENTS.md is touched.
- Manual check: in a session, ask "is there a new release of <repo>?" twice, some time apart. The second answer runs `date -u`, a fetch with tags and a release query in that turn.

title: Make worker lifecycle launch registration atomic
body:
## Summary

Make pre-exec worker lifecycle registration atomic in the existing observe-only registry. Follow-up to #35826 and #35821. This work is being implemented in the owning interactive session, not delegated to a background worker.

## Problem and contract

The pre-exec observer currently commits process registration and its initial worktree binding separately. A binding conflict or journal-capacity failure can leave a registered process without its binding. Commit both existing events and both projections in one SQLite transaction. Preserve schema 1, current event formats, observation-only behavior and native command execution when observation fails.

Use the run UUID as the namespace for stable UUIDv5 registration/binding event keys. Exact retries must be no-ops, including after termination; conflicting payloads must fail without changing prior evidence. Resolve paths and capture process identity before the write transaction. A committed attempt is not proof of successful exec, readiness or descendant quiescence.

## Files and reference pattern

- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/store.py`: reuse the existing connection transaction and event deduplication helpers; add the atomic attempt API without a second database or outbox.
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/launch.py`: use that API at the existing pre-exec boundary.
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_store.py` and `tests/test_launch.py`: extend existing rollback, owned-process crash, capacity and replay contracts; no new test framework.
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/{REGISTRY,COMPATIBILITY}.md`: document guarantees and non-guarantees.
- Replace the existing `worker-lifecycle-registry-validate.pyz` and two `reports/validation-registry-*.json` files with a matching Linux/macOS-validated artifact. Leave the process validator and its reports unchanged; retain exactly two archives and four reports.

## Acceptance and verification

- No partial run/binding/event pair after rollback or a crash before commit.
- Lost-acknowledgement replay and concurrent retries retain exactly one event pair; ended runs never revive.
- Existing native stdout/exit behavior and observe-only fail-open diagnostics remain intact.
- Ruff, mypy for Linux and Darwin, existing source unit tests and existing sandbox policy tests pass.
- The identical registry archive passes on native Linux x86-64 and macOS Intel; preserve operator-returned reports without rewriting fingerprints.
- `cleanup_authorized` remains false; no legacy state changes, strict admission, scheduler, schema migration or cleanup executor.

## Pre-flight

- Memory recall: atomic lifecycle registration — no relevant results.
- Scoped discovery found the merged registry PR #35826 and the local implementation; no open competing PR was returned.
- All target files and existing transaction/test patterns were inspected.
- Tier: standard; the transaction contract is specified and non-destructive, without unresolved authority or migration decisions.
- Draft PR skipped: implementation and native verification are complete; publish a review-ready PR.

## Rollback

Revert this change to the prior two-transaction observer. No schema or stored-event migration is needed. Do not reset or delete registry data.

title: aidevops secret: add guarded rm/remove subcommand (gopass + tenant plaintext, read-back, multi-name safe)
body:
## What

Add a guarded `aidevops secret rm <NAME>` (alias `remove`/`delete`) subcommand so operators can retire a credential without dropping to raw `gopass`.

## Why (observed evidence)

After closing a provider account, the operator ran `aidevops secret remove <NAME>` and got `Unknown command: remove`. The agent had suggested that command without checking `aidevops secret help`. Removal then required raw `gopass rm -f <prefix>/<NAME>`, which has two traps:

- Passing two names (`gopass rm -f a b`) is read as "remove field `b` inside secret `a`". gopass reports a key clash and deletes nothing.
- The operator must know the store prefix (`GOPASS_PREFIX` in `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh`) and whether a plaintext copy also exists in the tenant `credentials.sh` loader.

## How (files)

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh`: add `rm|remove|delete <NAME> [NAME...]`. It should:
  - resolve each name through the same lookup as `check`
  - remove it from gopass (one `gopass rm -f` per name) and from the active-tenant plaintext loader if present
  - require confirmation (interactive prompt or `--yes`)
  - print names only, never values, and end with a `check` read-back confirming the name is absent.
  - Warn when `dependents NAME` finds references, or when the credential registry still describes the name, and offer to remove that registry record.
- EDIT the `aidevops secret` help text and the secret-handling reference to document the command.
- Reuse existing argument parsing and the output/redaction patterns in `secret-helper.sh`.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh` is clean.
- With a throwaway name: `aidevops secret set TMP_X`, then `aidevops secret rm TMP_X --yes`, then `aidevops secret check TMP_X` exits non-zero.
- Removing two names in one call deletes both, with no gopass key clash.
- Unknown name: exits non-zero with a clear message and does nothing else.

title: cloudron: publish catalog with the job token; require CLOUDRON_RELEASE_PAT only when main rules block it
body:
## Problem

The managed catalog workflow (`.github/workflows/cloudron-catalog-publish-reusable.yml`) requires a per-repository `CLOUDRON_RELEASE_PAT` for its catalog commit and tag push. Creating and rotating a fine-grained PAT for every package repo is a large manual cost, and it bought no protection.

Evidence (2026-10-29):

- Every package repo (`gh api repos/<owner/repo>/rules/branches/main`) has only the documented baseline rules: `non_fast_forward` and `deletion`. Neither blocks a fast-forward push by the job token (`github-actions[bot]`).
- The pre-migration inline workflows in nostr-relay, headscale and opendesk already pushed with `secrets.CLOUDRON_RELEASE_PAT || github.token`. nostr-relay's 0.1.0 and 0.1.1 catalog commits were pushed by `github-actions[bot]` with no PAT.
- Callers already grant `contents: write` to the reusable job.
- nostr-relay 0.1.2 (run 40440804288) failed only at `CLOUDRON_RELEASE_PAT is required`, after a signed approval and merge.

The per-run job token is scoped to the one repository and expires with the job. That is narrower than any PAT and needs no rotation.

## Fix

- In the `publish` job, grant `contents: write` and push with `secrets.CLOUDRON_RELEASE_PAT || github.token`. Only the final push step receives the credential; npm/CLI steps get no token in their environment.
- Add `cloudron_publication_pat_required` (`cloudron-package-release-lib.sh`). It reads `rules/branches/main` and requires the PAT only for `pull_request`, `required_status_checks`, `required_deployments` or `update` rules. The approval, scaffold and monitor helpers use it, so the secret check runs only when the rules need one.
- Docs: the job token is the default. If an owner adopts required-PR rules, one multi-repo fine-grained PAT is enough.

### Files Scope

- `.github/workflows/cloudron-catalog-publish-reusable.yml`

A rollout command on the same line as ordinary prose with an apostrophe (for example "each repo's `main`") is never found. The gate then fails with "permission increase requires a named rollout in the PR body", even though the command is present. Evidence: PR #35856, Framework Validation run 40792710551. The body contained `` `aidevops sync-workflows --apply --workflow cloudron-catalog-publish` `` on a line that also had "repo's"; the check still reported a missing rollout. title: t18778: fix(coderabbit): post advisory COMMENTED reviews instead of blocking CHANGES_REQUESTED
body:
## Task


Stop CodeRabbit from submitting formal `CHANGES_REQUESTED` reviews. In `.coderabbit.yaml`, set `reviews.request_changes_workflow: false` so its findings arrive as `COMMENTED` reviews. They then stay advisory and get picked up by the post-merge review scanner, which is how the framework policy says they should be handled.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Stop CodeRabbit from submitting formal `CHANGES_REQUESTED` reviews. In `.coderabbit.yaml`, set `reviews.request_changes_workflow: false` so its findings arrive as `COMMENTED` reviews. They then stay advisory and get picked up by the post-merge review scanner, which is how the framework policy says they should be handled.

## Why

`.agents/reference/review-bot-gate.md` says CodeRabbit is advisory and that late feedback "is swept after merge and filed as worker-ready follow-up issues". Only human `CHANGES_REQUESTED` blocks. The config does something else. `request_changes_workflow: true` makes CodeRabbit post a formal `CHANGES_REQUESTED` review whenever it has an actionable comment. That sets `reviewDecision=CHANGES_REQUESTED`, and `_handle_changes_requested_review_gate` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh:357`) then sends the worker PR down the t2093 route: close the PR, append the feedback to the issue, redispatch. The next worker PR gets a new CodeRabbit change request, so the issue goes round the loop again.

What we saw after CodeRabbit reviews came back (#35791 merged 2026-10-28T00:17Z), point-in-time 2026-10-29:

- 15 worker PRs got the `review-routed-to-issue` label and were closed unmerged. In every one, CodeRabbit's `CHANGES_REQUESTED` was the only change request, with no human change requests. 7 of them already had a human `APPROVED` review.
- Issues went round the loop several times: GH#35830 had 4 PRs (#35832, #35834, #35838, #35840), GH#35793 had 4 (#35796, #35802, #35808, #35814), and GH#35798 had 2 (#35852, #35854).
- Over the same window, 23 PRs merged and 17 closed unmerged.

## How

1. `.coderabbit.yaml`: set `request_changes_workflow: false`. Replace the GH#3932 comment with the current rationale. The review-evidence check is state-agnostic: `bot_has_real_review` in `.agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh` accepts any settled bot review or comment on the exact head, and `commit_status: true` stays on. So the GH#17671 external-contributor gate keeps its evidence.
2. `.agents/reference/review-bot-gate.md`: add one short paragraph saying CodeRabbit posts non-blocking `COMMENTED` reviews, and that turning `request_changes_workflow` back on brings back the close/redispatch loop.

### Hazards

- CodeRabbit will stop posting `APPROVED` reviews too. No merge gate needs CodeRabbit approval: evidence is state-agnostic, and the stale-review dismissal path only acts on existing `CHANGES_REQUESTED` reviews.
- External-contributor PRs will no longer be blocked by CodeRabbit findings. They still need a completed review plus maintainer and cryptographic approval, so a human reads the findings before merge.
- Existing `CHANGES_REQUESTED` reviews on open PRs (for example #35835) stay in place until a new review replaces them or they are dismissed.

### Files Scope

- `.coderabbit.yaml`
- `.agents/reference/review-bot-gate.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.coderabbit.yaml` sets `request_changes_workflow: false`.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "rg -q '^  request_changes_workflow: false$' .coderabbit.yaml"
  ```

- [ ] Regression guard: CodeRabbit's state-agnostic review evidence path is unchanged, so external-contributor PRs still need settled review evidence.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "bot_has_real_review\\(\\)"
    path: ".agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh"
  ```

- [ ] After merge, the next CodeRabbit review on a worker PR has state `COMMENTED`, not `CHANGES_REQUESTED`, and that PR is not routed by t2093.

## Context

Root cause found during the maintainer stall diagnosis on 2026-10-29. Related: GH#35782 / #35791 (CodeRabbit eligibility restored), and t2093 review routing in `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback-review.sh`.

</details>

title: Email exposure audit: reference doc and scan helper for addresses readable by HTML scrapers
body:
## What

Agents have no guidance or tooling for auditing whether a site exposes email addresses to HTML scrapers. In a recent WordPress plugin rollout, the agent had to compose two one-off scripts to verify the result: an HTTP scan and a real-browser check of decoded links. The audit then found an address on every page of one site, coming from places no obfuscation should touch: an SEO plugin's JSON-LD and a chatbot plugin's settings printed for its script. Both were fixed at the source, after backing up the settings, once the owner approved.

## How

1. **New reference `.agents/seo/email-exposure-audit.md`** (with the generated `SKILL.md` sibling if the build expects one), modelled on `.agents/seo/schema-validator.md`:
   - Where addresses leak: text, `mailto:` hrefs, other attributes (the block editor's `data-id="mailto:…"`, `title`), JSON-LD, inline script data/JSON in attributes, theme templates, `cfemail` (Cloudflare obfuscation, decodable).
   - Rules: never encode JSON-LD (the schema email is optional; clear it at the source if the owner agrees); change third-party plugin text at its source, never by filtering its output; back up options before writing (serialized copy, mode 600) and verify after; purge page caches.
   - Verify twice: raw HTML (scraper's view) and a JS-enabled browser (visitor's view: links and attributes restored, no page errors). Wait for `domcontentloaded`, not `load`, on sites with slow third-party resources.
   - Expectation setting: obfuscation reduces harvesting by HTML-only scrapers; guessable addresses (`hello@domain`) and JS-running bots are not stopped.
   - Never put client hostnames in public issues (the privacy guard blocks them).
2. **New helper `.agents/scripts/email-exposure-helper.sh`** (ShellCheck clean, `local var="$1"`, explicit returns, sources `shared-constants.sh`):
   - `scan <url>...`: fetch with curl (cache-busting query), list each readable address once with its context (`text`, `href`, `attribute:<name>`, `json-ld`, `script`), plus counts of known placeholders (`data-cfemail`, `data-sps-e`/`data-sps-mailto`) and whether a decoder script is present. Exit 0 = none readable, 1 = some found, 2 = fetch error.
   - `browser <url>`: optional Playwright check printing restored `mailto:` links and their attributes, plus page errors; reuse the existing browser tooling (see `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper.sh`) rather than a hard-coded module path.
3. Register the reference in `.agents/subagent-index.toon` and link it from `.agents/seo/seo-audit-skill.md` (an exposure check in technical audits) and from the WordPress tools docs that discuss site operations, as relevant.

### Files Scope

- NEW: `.agents/seo/email-exposure-audit.md`
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/email-exposure-helper.sh`
- `.agents/subagent-index.toon`
- `.agents/seo/seo-audit-skill.md`
- `.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-dev.md`

Integration scope correction: the requested WordPress operations link belongs beside the existing private pre-change backup guidance in wp-dev.md. Add only an audit-reference pointer; verify with changed-file documentation lint. No site settings are changed.

## Acceptance

1. `email-exposure-helper.sh scan` on a local fixture page with a plain address, a `data-id="mailto:…"` attribute, a JSON-LD `email` and a `data-cfemail` span reports the first three with the correct contexts and counts the placeholder; exit 1. On a page with none, exit 0.
2. ShellCheck reports no violations; the repo's agent/doc linters and size ratchets pass.
3. The reference is discoverable through `subagent-index.toon`.

title: fix(pulse): retire daily CodeRabbit full-review requests on closed issue #2632
body:
## What

Stop the daily "@coderabbitai Please run a full codebase review" comment on closed issue #2632, or replace it with a trigger that actually produces findings. Today it posts about 4 times a day and gets nothing useful back.

## Why

Evidence, point-in-time 2026-10-29:

- `CODERABBIT_REVIEW_ISSUE="2632"` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-config.sh:456`) points at a quality dashboard that was closed as a duplicate on 2026-04-30 (`cleanup-quality-dashboard-dupes.sh` lists it in `DUPES`).
- #2632 now has about 1,200 comments. Since 2026-10-01 there have been 125 requests: alex-solovyev 50, vladimirdulov 48, marcusquinn 27. The interval gate in `_coderabbit_review_check_interval` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-review.sh:39`) uses a timestamp file local to each runner, so every maintainer runner posts once a day.
- Every CodeRabbit reply since 2026-10-14 is "Oops, something went wrong! Please try again later." (178 error replies in total, the first on 2026-03-16). The last non-error reply (2026-10-14T19:03Z) said it "cannot report a completed review … No new checks ran in this response." Issue-thread chat does not run a repository review.
- No code reads these replies. `run_daily_codebase_review` claims findings are "routed through quality-feedback-helper.sh", but the replies contain no findings to route.

## How

1. Check the premise first: confirm no non-error reply in the last 90 days contained actionable findings that got filed (search #2632 comments for `coderabbitai[bot]` replies without "something went wrong").
2. Recommended: retire the posting step in `run_daily_codebase_review` and its stage call in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:1490`. Per-PR CodeRabbit reviews plus `post-merge-review-scanner.sh` already cover the code-quality audit. Remove `CODERABBIT_REVIEW_ISSUE` and `CODERABBIT_REVIEW_LAST_RUN` if nothing else uses them.
3. If a periodic whole-repo review is still wanted, use a mechanism CodeRabbit supports, never a closed issue. Before posting, check that the target is open. Dedupe across runners using the last request timestamp on the target, not a local file.
4. Do not post any further comments on #2632.

Update those existing expectations and move generic resume/interruption coverage to retained stages. Collision discovery found no open related PRs. Verify with these three existing bash test scripts and bash syntax checks; ShellCheck is covered by code-quality CI if unavailable locally.

Premise correction: historical replies on 2026-10-06 through 2026-10-09 do contain actionable audit findings (for example https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/2632#issuecomment-6014070815). title: feat(quality): alert when CodeRabbit review coverage of merged PRs collapses
body:
## What

Alert when CodeRabbit review coverage collapses, so a silent outage cannot leave the post-merge review scanner with nothing to file for months.

## Why

Evidence, point-in-time 2026-10-29:

- Between 2026-07-29 and 2026-10-27, 3,542 PRs merged into `marcusquinn/aidevops`. A `reviewed-by:coderabbitai[bot]` search finds only 13 PRs reviewed by CodeRabbit in that window.
- In the same window, `post-merge-review-scanner.sh` (label `review-followup`) filed no follow-up issues for review feedback. It filed 3 on 2026-10-28, within a day of CodeRabbit reviews coming back (#35791, GH#35782). So the scanner works; it had no review input.
- Nothing surfaced the outage. It was found by hand three months later. The user's policy is that CodeRabbit reviews feed code-quality audit sweeps that log follow-up issues, and a coverage collapse silently turns that pipeline off.

## How

1. In the daily quality sweep (`_sweep_review_scanner` / `_sweep_coderabbit` in `.agents/scripts/stats-quality-sweep-tools.sh`), compute coverage: of the PRs merged in the last 7 days, the share with at least one CodeRabbit review or a `CodeRabbit` commit status on the merged head. Use one bounded search query, for example `search/issues` with `reviewed-by:coderabbitai[bot]` plus a merged-PR count, to keep API cost low.
2. When coverage falls below a configurable threshold (suggest 50%) and at least 20 PRs merged in the window, print a visible warning in the sweep output. Also create or update one deduplicated worker-ready issue that cites the counts and points to `.coderabbit.yaml`.
3. Do not add a new test runner. A focused case may go in the existing `.agents/scripts/tests/test-quality-sweep-serialization.sh` if it is cheap.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/stats-quality-sweep-tools.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/stats-functions.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The quality sweep reports CodeRabbit review coverage for the last 7 days of merged PRs and warns below the threshold.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "coverage"
    path: ".agents/scripts/stats-quality-sweep-tools.sh"
  ```

- [ ] Regression guard: no warning and no issue is created when fewer than the minimum number of PRs merged in the window, or when the coverage query fails (it fails open, with a logged reason).
- [ ] ShellCheck reports zero findings on the modified scripts.

## Context

title: fix(pulse): do not close/redispatch worker PRs on bot-only CHANGES_REQUESTED (t2093 route)
body:
## What

Make the pulse t2093 review route ignore bot-only `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. For trusted PRs where every active change request comes from a review bot, treat the review as advisory and do not close the PR or redispatch its issue. The post-merge scanner should handle the findings instead.

## Why

`.agents/reference/review-bot-gate.md` lists only human `CHANGES_REQUESTED` as a merge blocker. But `_handle_changes_requested_review_gate` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh:357`) acts on the aggregate `reviewDecision` alone. When it is `CHANGES_REQUESTED`, the function calls `_route_pr_to_fix_worker`, which closes the worker PR and redispatches the issue, no matter who requested the changes. The trust check that already exists, `_review_feedback_has_trusted_body_change_request` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback-review.sh:167`), runs only on the opt-in remediation-first path.

On 2026-10-28 this closed 15 worker PRs where CodeRabbit's review was the only change request. Seven of them had a human `APPROVED` review. GH#35830 and GH#35793 each went round the loop 4 times. GH#35860 removes the trigger at the source by setting `request_changes_workflow: false`. This issue adds defence in depth for any repository or bot that still submits formal change requests.

## How

1. In `_handle_changes_requested_review_gate`, before the default `_route_pr_to_fix_worker` call, reduce the reviews to each reviewer's latest state-changing review, as `_review_feedback_has_trusted_body_change_request` does. If no trusted human (OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR, `user.type == "User"`) has an active `CHANGES_REQUESTED`, do not route.
2. For trusted-author PRs that are blocked only by bot reviews, reuse the shared dismissal mechanics behind `_pulse_merge_dismiss_coderabbit_nits` / `review-bot-gate-helper.sh` (exact bot identity, head re-read before and after dismissal) so that branch protection stops blocking. Then return 0 so the normal merge gates run.
3. Keep `external-contributor` and unknown-author PRs fail-closed (GH#17671). Mark the new check with `#aidevops:trust-boundary`.

Integration scope recovery: the shared dismissal helper currently permits only maintainer-labeled nits or superseded clean re-reviews. Add a trusted-author advisory mode there to reuse exact CodeRabbit identity and pre/post-head checks without inventing a maintainer label. PR #35873 explicitly excludes this fix and does not touch these paths. Verification: the scoped dispatch regression suite and ShellCheck on changed scripts.

### Hazards

- This path closes PRs and rewrites issues. Fail closed: if review evidence is unavailable, defer (rc 75) rather than route or dismiss.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback-review.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-fix-worker-dispatch-cases.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A trusted worker PR whose only active `CHANGES_REQUESTED` is from `coderabbitai[bot]` is not closed and does not get the `review-routed-to-issue` label.
- [ ] Regression guard: a trusted human's active `CHANGES_REQUESTED` still takes the existing t2093 route, and external-contributor PRs stay blocked.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: ".agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-fix-worker-dispatch-cases.sh"
  ```

- [ ] ShellCheck reports zero findings on the modified scripts.

## Context

Found during the 2026-10-29 maintainer diagnosis of stalled aidevops issues. Root-cause config fix: GH#35860.

title: t18779: fix(cloudron): release evidence rejects catalog publication recovered by gh run rerun --failed (attempt mismatch)
body:
## Task


`full-loop-helper.sh record-published-release ... --generated-cloudron-catalog`
rejects a genuine release when the catalog publication workflow succeeded on a
re-run of failed jobs. `cloudron-release-evidence.py` builds the accepted
invocation set from each successful run's *current* `run_attempt` only
(`invocations()`, around lines 220-235). Then it requires the image and the
catalog to be attested by the same invocation URI (`verify()`, around line 290).
With `gh run rerun <id> --failed`, the successful `build` job is not re-run. Its
image attestation keeps `.../actions/runs/<id>/attempts/1`, while the catalog
attestation from the re-run `publish` job carries `.../attempts/2`.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`full-loop-helper.sh record-published-release ... --generated-cloudron-catalog`
rejects a genuine release when the catalog publication workflow succeeded on a
re-run of failed jobs. `cloudron-release-evidence.py` builds the accepted
invocation set from each successful run's *current* `run_attempt` only
(`invocations()`, around lines 220-235). Then it requires the image and the
catalog to be attested by the same invocation URI (`verify()`, around line 290).
With `gh run rerun <id> --failed`, the successful `build` job is not re-run. Its
image attestation keeps `.../actions/runs/<id>/attempts/1`, while the catalog
attestation from the re-run `publish` job carries `.../attempts/2`.

## Evidence

- marcusquinn/cloudron-nostr-relay-app run 40440804288: attempt 1 `build`
  success, `publish` failure (repo secret `CLOUDRON_RELEASE_PAT` was missing);
  after setting the secret, `gh run rerun --failed` gave attempt 2 success. v0.1.2
  tag, GitHub release and catalog entry were published.
- `gh attestation verify oci://ghcr.io/marcusquinn/cloudron-nostr-relay-app@sha256:88dbd313...
  --signer-workflow marcusquinn/aidevops/.github/workflows/cloudron-catalog-publish-reusable.yml`
  returns `runInvocationURI=.../runs/40440804288/attempts/1`.
- `record-published-release 20 v0.1.2 marcusquinn/cloudron-nostr-relay-app
  --workflow cloudron-catalog-publish.yml --event push --generated-cloudron-catalog`
  fails: "attestation does not bind the artifact to the expected source/workflow/run".

## How

1. EDIT `.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-evidence.py`: for each successful
   exact-source run, accept invocation URIs for attempts `1..run_attempt` of
   that run ID. Replace the same-invocation requirement with a same-run-ID
   requirement: image and catalog attestations must belong to the same
   successful run, not necessarily the same attempt. Keep every other binding
   (signer, source digest, ref, trigger, subject digest, SLSA predicate,
   `invocationId == runInvocationURI`) unchanged. Mark the changed check
   `#aidevops:trust-boundary`.
2. Add a regression case to the existing tests for this evidence module
   (locate with `rg -l cloudron-release-evidence .agents/scripts/tests`): image
   attested by attempt 1, catalog by attempt 2 of the same successful run
   → accepted; attestations from two different run IDs → still rejected.
3. Optional doc line in `.agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-app-publishing-skill.md`:
   after fixing a missing secret, `gh run rerun <id> --failed` is the supported
   recovery.

## Acceptance

- The nostr-relay command above records `release:published` for PR #20.
- Different-run and non-success-run attestations remain rejected.
- Existing release-evidence tests and shellcheck/python checks pass.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-evidence.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-release-evidence.py`
- `.agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-app-publishing-skill.md`
