title: t18780: Show per-turn UTC receive time to the model in interactive OpenCode sessions (follow-up GH#35839)
body:
## Task


An OpenCode plugin step that shows the model when each root-session user turn was received, as a short synthetic UTC timestamp, so it can see how much time has passed between turns.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- NEW: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/turn-time-annotation.mjs`: export `annotateTurnTimes(input, output)`.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs`: call it in `messagesTransformHook` (around line 607) after `compactionInputReplay.inject` and before `ttsrMessagesTransformHook`, inside try/catch (fail-open, log via `qualityLog`).
- NEW: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-turn-time-annotation.mjs`: focused node test following `tests/test-playwriter-selection-guard.mjs` fixture shape (`{ info: { role, time: { created } }, parts: [...] }`).
- EDIT: `.agents/configs/prompt-hook-candidates.conf`: change the GH#35839 row from `candidate` to `partial` and name the module.

### Implementation Steps

1. For each message in `output.messages` where `info.role === "user"` and `Number.isFinite(info.time?.created)`, prepend one text part `{ type: "text", text: "[turn received <ISO-8601 UTC to the minute>]", synthetic: true }`. Skip it if a part with that exact prefix is already there (idempotent).
2. **Prompt-cache safety:** take the time only from the message's own `info.time.created`, never from `Date.now()`. The text for older messages then stays the same on every request, so the cached prompt prefix is not invalidated (see `reference/context-efficiency.md`).
3. Headless sessions are excluded: reuse the `isHeadless` signal already used in `index.mjs` (as `greetingHandler` does). Skip subagent (non-root) sessions in the same way as `session-boundary-advisory.mjs`.
4. Opt-out: `AIDEVOPS_TURN_TIME_ANNOTATION=0`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/turn-time-annotation.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-turn-time-annotation.mjs`
- `.agents/configs/prompt-hook-candidates.conf`

### Complexity Impact

New module of about 40-60 lines; `messagesTransformHook` grows by about 5 lines (currently about 12).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-29, interactive session (ai-interactive)
- **Follow-up from:** GH#35839 (docs rule merged in PR #35869). This is the deterministic half registered in `.agents/configs/prompt-hook-candidates.conf` row "Remote-state answers are current-turn queries".

## What

An OpenCode plugin step that shows the model when each root-session user turn was received, as a short synthetic UTC timestamp, so it can see how much time has passed between turns.

## Why

The model's context gives today's date but no time for each message. In GH#35839 an agent answered "nothing is deployed" about three hours after its last query because it could not see that time had passed. The docs rule asks agents to run `date -u`; adding the timestamp in the plugin fixes the cause in every interactive session.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every root interactive user message seen by the model starts with a `[turn received …Z]` synthetic part derived from `info.time.created`. Verify with the new node test, which uses fixed timestamps.
2. Repeated transforms of the same message list give byte-identical output (cache-safe, idempotent). Covered by the test.
3. Headless, subagent and `AIDEVOPS_TURN_TIME_ANNOTATION=0` sessions are unchanged. Covered by the test.

5. `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-turn-time-annotation.mjs` passes, the existing plugin tests still pass, and `progressive-load-check.sh` passes.

## Context & Decisions

- Messages-transform injection was chosen over `chat.message` mutation so the stored transcript is unchanged and the step is fully reversible.
- Minute precision is enough for elapsed-time judgment and keeps the token cost to about 8 tokens per turn.

title: Systemic: stranded worker commits, unsatisfiable salvage briefs and close-and-recreate review routing loop issues
body:
## What

Remove the root causes that left pulse/worker issues looping, accumulating lifecycle comments and producing PRs that never merge (reported set includes #35689, #35751, #35798, #35824, #35828, #35194, #35592, #35600).

## Why (evidence)

1. **Stranded unpushed commits.** `bun run typecheck` in `.agents/hooks/repo-verify-pre-push.sh` was a local-only gate: no workflow in `.github/workflows/` ran it. Worker worktrees without `node_modules/.bin/tsc` failed with exit 127, the push was blocked, and committed work stayed on one runner's disk (#35686 → #35689: `0454795df`, `748b04f50`; #35744 → #35751: `6cdde1f8f`, `0519aac6a`).
2. **Unsatisfiable consolidated briefs.** The consolidation prompt (`.agents/scripts/pulse-triage-dispatch.sh`, "Preserve all substantive content") promoted "salvage these exact commits; do not recreate" into binding acceptance. Every other runner exited BLOCKED (classified `runner_capability_unmet` or `source_access_blocked`), and the fleet capability circuit's readiness probe (tsc present) kept re-waking them: 139 and 116 comments, five "Ready checkpoints" on the #23126 fleet dashboard.
3. **Close-and-recreate review routing.** CodeRabbit `CHANGES_REQUESTED` closed worker PRs within minutes (#35854, #35836) and redispatched the issue for a fresh PR, restarting review every generation. GH#35860 has since made CodeRabbit advisory at the source. Remediation-first stays opt-in here, because its converged branch cannot dismiss a legacy bot change request and would stall instead of churn (follow-up issue).
4. **Not-reproduced investigations wait forever.** #35194's recovery supervisor ruled a "not reproduced" closeout outside delegated authority, so it stayed `status:blocked`.
5. **Silent test gap.** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-review-thread-remediation.sh` pointed at a moved sub-library and ran 0 cases while exiting 0.

## How

title: AWS support on a par with gcloud and Cloudflare: aws.md guide, secret-backed credentials, ses-helper fixes, secret verify aws
body:
## What

First-class AWS support, on a par with Google Cloud (`services/hosting/google-cloud.md`) and Cloudflare (`services/hosting/cloudflare.md`, `aidevops secret verify cloudflare`): one guide that tells agents and users how to grant access safely, credentials held in `aidevops secret` (never plaintext config), and helpers that inject them per command.

## Why (observed 2026-10-23)

An interactive session had to diagnose SES delivery for a client site with no AWS access: no AWS secret, no `aws` CLI, no guide. The only route was the website's own SES key, signing SESv2 requests by hand from the server. That worked, but it meant borrowing an application credential for account-level management. Findings while looking for the framework path:

- `.agents/scripts/ses-helper.sh` reads `aws_access_key_id`/`aws_secret_access_key` in plaintext from `configs/ses-config.json` (`set_aws_credentials`, around line 77). That contradicts `reference/secret-handling.md`.
- `.agents/services/email/ses.md` "IAM Policy" uses the prefix `sesv2:` (`sesv2:GetSuppressedDestination` etc.). IAM has no `sesv2` prefix; SESv2 actions use `ses:`. As written, the policy grants no suppression-list access.
- There is no `services/hosting/aws.md`, and `aidevops secret verify` supports only `cloudflare` (`secret-helper.sh` around line 1443; pattern `credential_inventory_cloudflare.py`).
- SES's account-level suppression list silently drops mail to any address that bounced once. The sender still gets a MessageId, so app logs say "sent". Nothing in `ses.md` warns about this or mentions configuration-set suppression options.
- Hand-signed SigV4 gotcha: for `GET /v2/email/suppression/addresses/{email}`, the canonical URI must encode `@` twice (`%2540`) while the request path encodes it once. Worth one line if any helper signs requests without the CLI.

## How

1. New `.agents/services/hosting/aws.md`, modelled on `google-cloud.md`:
   - Access in order of preference: (a) IAM Identity Center with a named profile (`aws configure sso --profile aidevops-<account>`), so there is no long-lived key; (b) an IAM user access key with least privilege, for unattended work only.
   - Naming per `tools/credentials/credential-inventory.md`: `AWS_<ACCOUNT>_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_<ACCOUNT>_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, plus `aidevops secret account add aws-<account> --provider aws`. The IAM user/key label is `aidevops-<account>-<purpose>`.
   - Console-only steps to give the user, a default region, rotation, and what to do if a key is compromised. Never request values in chat.
2. Credential injection: `aidevops secret AWS_<ACCOUNT>_ACCESS_KEY_ID AWS_<ACCOUNT>_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY -- aws ...` mapped to `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`/`AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` (check whether `secret-helper.sh` aliases/defaults already cover the mapping; if not, add an explicit `aidevops secret default aws` path rather than storing bare names).
3. `ses-helper.sh`: take credentials from `aidevops secret` or `--profile`, keeping `ses-config.json` for non-secret metadata only, and warn if plaintext keys remain. Add commands for `account-suppression` (get/put `SuppressedReasons`), `config-set create|suppression <name> <reasons...>|list` and `suppressed --filter <domain>` (paged).
4. Fix the `ses.md` IAM policy (`ses:` prefix for v2 actions). Document the silent-drop behaviour, and that a configuration set with `SuppressedReasons: []` can exempt internal recipients (sent with `X-SES-CONFIGURATION-SET` or `ConfigurationSetName`).
5. `aidevops secret verify aws`: new `credential_inventory_aws.py` calling `sts get-caller-identity`. It prints the account ID and ARN only; neither value is a secret.
6. Routing: add AWS to `reference/domain-index.md` and to the Build+ domain table if it fits the size ratchet.

## Files

- NEW `.agents/services/hosting/aws.md`
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/ses-helper.sh`, `.agents/services/email/ses.md`
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh` (verify dispatch), NEW `.agents/scripts/credential_inventory_aws.py`
- EDIT `.agents/reference/domain-index.md`; `.agents/configs/ses-config.json.txt` (drop the key fields)

## Verification

- ShellCheck is clean on the changed shell scripts; the Python linter is clean on the new file.
- With a real least-privilege key stored through `aidevops secret set`: `aidevops secret verify aws` prints the caller ARN; `ses-helper.sh quota <account>` and `ses-helper.sh suppressed <account>` work with no `ses-config.json` secrets present.
- `rg -n "sesv2:" .agents` returns nothing.

title: GH audit anomaly scanner: skip same-actor protected-label self-reversals instead of filing stale alerts
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## What

Stop the GH audit anomaly scanner from filing `GH Audit Anomaly Alert` issues for protected-label removals that only reverse the same identity's own recent add. Check the GitHub issue timeline before filing. Every other signal stays fail-closed.

## Why

#35694 flagged two `protected_label_removed:no-auto-dispatch` edits, on #35610 and #35612. The GitHub timeline showed that the account doing the removal had added `no-auto-dispatch` 1–5 minutes earlier, while creating each issue, and then swapped it for `auto-dispatch`. No hold placed by anyone else was bypassed.

The alert is labelled `no-auto-dispatch`, and only the filing runner can review its local `gh-audit.log`. It stayed open for 3 days until a maintainer session closed it by hand. This false positive therefore creates stale issues that no worker can resolve.

The local log cannot detect the pattern. It records `issue_edit`, `issue_close`, `pr_edit` and `pr_close`, but not `issue_create` (`.agents/scripts/gh-audit-log-helper.sh:84-88`), so a label added at creation is invisible to it. The issue timeline does show it.

## Reproducer

1. A runner creates an issue labelled `no-auto-dispatch`, then swaps the label for `auto-dispatch` through the wrapped issue edit. Its `gh-audit.log` records an `issue_edit` with `"suspicious":["protected_label_removed:no-auto-dispatch"]`.
2. `gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh scan` then files a `GH Audit Anomaly Alert`. Observed case: #35694, for #35610 and #35612.
3. The timeline shows the same actor on both events, 5 minutes apart:

```bash
gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/35610/timeline --paginate \
  --jq '.[] | select(.event=="labeled" or .event=="unlabeled") | select(.label.name=="no-auto-dispatch") | "\(.event) \(.actor.login) \(.created_at)"'
# labeled alex-solovyev 2026-10-25T11:31:15Z
# unlabeled alex-solovyev 2026-10-25T11:36:28Z
```

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh` — add a new `_ga_filter_self_reversals` function and call it once from `_cmd_scan_collect_anomalies` (lines 219-270), after the `gh-audit-anomaly-filter.jq` pass at line 243.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-audit-anomaly-expected-transitions.sh` — add cases using the `gh()` stubs the file already defines (lines 175-471).
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/gh-audit-log.md` — document the exemption.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `cmd_scan` → `_cmd_scan_collect_anomalies` → `_cmd_scan_build_issue_body` / `_cmd_scan_file_issue` in `.agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh`. `rg -l gh-audit-anomaly-scanner .agents/scripts` finds no other filer.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** the only write is `gh_create_issue` in `_cmd_scan_file_issue` (line 325). The new filter only removes entries before that call. The scan state file (`_ga_write_state`) must still advance past excluded lines.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-audit-anomaly-expected-transitions.sh` already runs the helper with stubbed `gh`.
- **Schemas/config:** the audit log line schema (`gh-audit-log-helper.sh:601-638`) is read-only here. No config change.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/` to `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/`. Edit only the repo copy.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because the filter applies only to future scans. Open historical alerts are not rewritten.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** reverting the `.agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh` change restores the current always-file behaviour. No persistent state is added.

### Implementation Steps

1. In `_ga_filter_self_reversals`, select entries whose `suspicious` array contains only `protected_label_removed:<label>` signals. For each one, read `gh api repos/{repo}/issues/{number}/timeline --paginate` (cap at 5 pages). Find the latest `labeled` event for `<label>` before the entry's `ts`, and the `unlabeled` event matching that removal.
2. Exclude the entry as `self_reversal` only when all of these hold, and log one `_ga_info` line per exclusion:
   - Both events' `actor.login` equal the scanner's login. Read it once per scan with `gh api user --jq .login`.
   - The add happened no more than 24h before the removal.
   - No other actor labelled or unlabelled that label in between.
3. Keep the entry on any API error, a missing event or an actor mismatch. Also keep it when it carries any extra signal, such as `body_delta_pct=*` or `state_capture_unavailable:*`.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** scans are single-runner and read-only until the existing `gh_create_issue` call. Timeline reads add no shared state.
- **Migration/rollback:** none. Old and new scanner versions produce the same alert format.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** runners without the change keep filing these alerts, which is today's behaviour. Log lines are unchanged.
- **Idempotency/retry:** the classification is deterministic for a given timeline, so a rescan gives the same result. The state cursor advances as it does today.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** a timeline or `gh api user` failure keeps the alert. That is fail-closed and matches current behaviour.

### Complexity Impact

- **Target function:** `_cmd_scan_collect_anomalies` in `.agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh`
- **Current line count:** about 52 lines (219-270)
- **Estimated growth:** +3 lines, because the logic lives in the new function
- **Projected post-change:** about 55 lines (55% of the threshold)
- **Action required:** None

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-audit-anomaly-expected-transitions.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** the test file covers all acceptance criteria through the stubbed `gh` timeline and user responses. ShellCheck and the changed-file linters cover the helper edit and the complexity gates.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required, because the change is confined to one helper.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-audit-anomaly-expected-transitions.sh`
- `.agents/reference/gh-audit-log.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] When the same login adds `no-auto-dispatch` and removes it within 24h, no alert issue is filed and the scan logs `self_reversal`.
- [ ] Negative: when the label was added by a different login and removed by the scanner's login, the alert is still filed.
- [ ] Negative: when the timeline API fails, the alert is still filed.
- [ ] Negative: when the removal entry also carries `body_delta_pct=-100`, the alert is still filed.
- [ ] Existing expected-transition cases still pass, and ShellCheck reports zero findings on the helper.

## Context & Decisions

- Found while closing #35694 during the systemic stale-issue review (#35871). Timeline evidence: https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/35694#issuecomment-6484908184
- The timeline check was chosen over a local-log lookup, because the log never records `issue_create`.

title: Capability releases exhaust the draft-checkpoint continuation budget for every runner (#35598, #35603 stuck)
body:
## What

Stop runners that lack a capability from exhausting the exact-head continuation budget of a worker draft checkpoint. A `runner_capability_unmet` release should exclude only the runner that posted it, not every capable runner in the fleet.

## Why

#35592 (draft PR #35598) and #35600 (draft PR #35603) have been `status:available` with open drafts since 2026-10-25. Nothing has continued them since, and neither PR can merge.

- Every release on both issues is `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked` with `Terminal blocker: reason=runner_capability_unmet owner=runner-recovery`. The work needs an isolated WordPress fixture that the releasing runners do not have.
- `_pcc_stall_release_evidence` (`.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`) counts capability releases as stalls (GH#34758). After two of them, `_pcc_dispatch_stalled` posts `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION` ("Pulse will not continue the same head again"). From then on, every runner's pulse logs `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION_EXISTS` and `dedup_active_claim`.
- The budget was spent by two runner logins that lack the fixture. Runners that never tried were locked out with them, and the attention asks the brief owner to act, although no brief edit can supply a runner capability. The GH#35788 attention text says the opposite: "Pulse can continue this exact head on a capable runner".

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:**

```bash
gh issue view 35592 --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --json comments \
  --jq '.comments[] | select(.body | test("CLAIM_RELEASED|STALLED_CHECKPOINT")) | "\(.createdAt) \(.author.login) \(.body | capture("(?<k>CLAIM_RELEASED reason=[a-z_]+|STALLED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION[^\n]*stalls=[0-9]+)").k)"'
rg -c 'STALLED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION_EXISTS: PR #35598' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log
```

**Actual output:**

```text
2026-10-25T01:41:26Z vladimirdulov CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked
2026-10-25T02:45:18Z vladimirdulov CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked
2026-10-25T02:59:03Z alex-solovyev STALLED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION pr=35598 head=7d006ead… reason=blocked stalls=2
2026-10-25T09:59:13Z vladimirdulov CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked
31
```

All three releases carry `Terminal blocker: reason=runner_capability_unmet`. The maintainer runner has never attempted the head, yet its pulse logged `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION_EXISTS` 31 times.

**Expected:** a runner with no capability release for this head continues it.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`:
  - All capability releases since the head count as one original stall, so genuine stalls keep the one-continuation budget.
  - A runner whose own login posted a capability release for the head skips it quietly, and other runners stay eligible.
  - A trusted standalone `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry` re-arms a runner after its prerequisite is installed.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`: add the capability cases.
- `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md`: describe the per-runner bound.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] When capability releases come from other logins, a runner with no capability release for the head continues it.
- [ ] Negative: a runner that already posted a capability release for the head is skipped, with no comment or dispatch.
- [ ] Negative: two genuine stall releases still post one `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION`, as before.
- [ ] A trusted retry directive newer than the runner's own capability release makes the runner eligible again.
- [ ] `test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` and `test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh` pass, and ShellCheck is clean.

title: t18781: OpenCode sidebar Prompts shows command templates and timeline dialog closes o...
body:
**Task ID:** `t18781` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-10-29
**Tags:** `bug`

## Outcome

OpenCode sidebar Prompts shows command templates and timeline dialog closes on click

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Fix two defects in the OpenCode sidebar "Prompts" section added by the aidevops TUI plugin.

1. Rows for slash-command turns show the expanded command template (for example `<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT…` from `/full-loop`) instead of what the user typed.
2. Clicking a row briefly shows the native Timeline dialog, which closes immediately.

## Why (root causes, verified)

1. OpenCode `SessionPrompt.command()` (v1.19.5 `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts`) stores the expanded template as an ordinary non-synthetic user text part, and no durable message field records the command name or arguments. `extractPromptRows()` in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tui-prompts.mjs` therefore treats the 45 KB template (beginning with the command file's SPDX comment) as the prompt. Local session DB evidence: `/full-loop` user messages have one text part starting `<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->`.
2. `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v1-tui/tui.tsx` opens the timeline on `onMouseDown`. OpenCode's `Dialog` backdrop (`packages/tui/src/ui/dialog.tsx`) closes on `onMouseUp`, so the release of the same click lands on the new full-screen backdrop and dismisses the dialog. Native header controls trigger commands on `onMouseUp`.

## How

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs`: add a `command.execute.before` hook that stamps the template text part with `metadata.aidevops.command = { name, arguments }` (in-place mutation; model input and native transcript unchanged).
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tui-prompts.mjs`: render stamped parts as `/name arguments`; for legacy/unstamped text strip leading HTML comments and YAML frontmatter before truncation.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v1-tui/tui.tsx`: dispatch the timeline on `onMouseUp` (V2 renderer already uses `onMouseUp`).

### Files Scope

- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs
- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tui-prompts.mjs
- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v1-tui/tui.tsx
- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-tui-prompts.mjs

## Acceptance

- New `/full-loop foo` turn shows `/full-loop foo` in the sidebar.
- Legacy command turns no longer show SPDX comment headers.
- Clicking a row opens the Timeline dialog and it stays open.
- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-tui-prompts.mjs` passes.

## Verification

`node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-tui-prompts.mjs`; deploy with `setup.sh --non-interactive`; restart the OpenCode TUI and click a Prompts row.

</details>

title: Compaction routing sends local-provider sessions' context to a cloud simple-tier model
body:
## Problem

`applyCompactionRouting` (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-routing.mjs`, called from `config-hook.mjs` in the config hook) sets one **global** `config.agent.compaction.model`. It uses the first simple-tier candidate whose input limit fits `DEFAULT_COMPACTION_TARGET`; with the shipped routing table that is `openai/gpt-6-luna`. OpenCode uses that model for every compaction, **whatever the parent session's provider**.

So a session running on a local provider listed in `configs/local-ai-providers.conf` (for example an LM Studio provider) has its compaction summaries generated by a cloud provider. The whole conversation is sent for summarization, including tool results. Operators who chose a local model reasonably expect its context to stay local.

- **Unbound sessions** (no `AIDEVOPS_RUNTIME_POLICY`): the context goes to the cloud model, with no warning.
- **Bound sessions** (`AIDEVOPS_RUNTIME_POLICY=local-only`): the routed compaction model is non-local, so the egress gate should refuse it, and compaction fails instead of staying local. Expected from reading the code, not yet observed.

## Evidence

OpenCode 1.19.5, aidevops agents 3.39.80. Two sessions ran wholly on a local provider listed in `local-ai-providers.conf` and auto-compacted twice each. The OpenCode session store shows all four `agent=compaction` assistant messages with `providerID=openai`, `modelID=gpt-6-luna`. No `agent.compaction` model was configured by the operator, and there is no custom routing-table override.

## Expected

Compaction for a session whose parent model is a local provider stays local: on the parent model, or on a local simple-tier candidate. At minimum, when the local-only policy is bound, compaction must never be routed to a non-local model.

## Suggested approach (verify before implementing)

1. When `activeLocalOnlyPolicy().bound` is true, `applyCompactionRouting` should consider only candidates for which `isLocalProvider(policy, providerID)` holds. With no fitting local candidate, it should leave `agent.compaction` unset so compaction stays on the parent model.
2. Unbound sessions with a local parent: the config-time route is global, so check whether OpenCode 1.19.x lets a plugin override the compaction model per session or per request. One place to look is a `chat.params`-time hook when `input.agent === "compaction"`, as `capCompactionEffort` does for effort. If no per-session override exists, document the behaviour in the local-model docs and log a one-time warning when a local provider is configured and compaction is routed to a non-local model.

Files: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-routing.mjs`, `config-hook.mjs`, `local-only-policy.mjs` (`isLocalProvider`), tests in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-model-routing.mjs` (existing `applyCompactionRouting` cases).

Verification: unit cases for a bound policy with a local candidate, a bound policy with no local candidate (no route), and unbound behaviour unchanged. Then a manual check that a local-provider session's `agent=compaction` message records a local `providerID`.

Related: GH#32934 (introduced simple-tier compaction routing), GH#34125 (local-only egress policy).

title: cloudron-release-evidence.py rejects valid catalog tags rebased over docs-only commits
body:
## What

`full-loop-helper.sh record-published-release ... --generated-cloudron-catalog` (via `.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-evidence.py`, `CatalogEvidence.generated_commit`) requires the generated catalog tag commit's sole parent to equal the merged source commit. The managed publisher (`cloudron-catalog-publish-reusable.yml`) deliberately allows the catalog commit to land on top of later docs-only commits. It records the build source in a `Cloudron-Source:` trailer, and its release job verifies that only `README.md|docs/*|metrics/*|.github/metrics/*|.github/star-history/*|star-history.svg|star-history-dark.svg` (reusable workflow lines ~312 and ~359 at pin `802af93`) changed between source and tag parent ("New tags retain the attested source across a docs-only rebase").

So any repository whose metrics or star-history bot pushes to `main` while the catalog build runs gets a valid, attested, published release that the receipt verifier rejects. `release:published` can then never be recorded, and `full-loop-helper.sh complete` stays at `FINALIZATION_PENDING`.

## Evidence

The observed case is a managed Cloudron package release v0.2.6 (repository name omitted):

- Merge commit (source) `ded52f2`.
- The metrics bot then pushed commit `6ba592e`, touching only `docs/metrics/*`.
- Catalog tag commit `276ea80`, whose parent is `6ba592e`, carries the trailer `Cloudron-Source: ded52f2…`.
- The publish run succeeded (preflight/build/publish/release). Image and catalog attestations verify against `--source-digest ded52f2` and the managed signer. `cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh` `release_published` (ancestor comparison) accepted it and closed the approval issue.
- `cloudron-release-evidence.py` `generated_commit()` fails with "tag must be a direct child of the merged source".

## How

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-evidence.py` `CatalogEvidence.generated_commit` to mirror the publisher's release-job contract. Accept parent == source, or (a) a single `Cloudron-Source` trailer equal to `self.source` in the tag commit message, (b) the source being an ancestor of the tag parent (`compare/<source>...<parent>` status `ahead`), and (c) every file changed in `source..parent` matching the publisher's docs-only allowlist. Keep the single-file `CloudronVersions.json` modification check. Compare `before` catalog content at the tag parent (equal to source by the allowlist), or keep it at source and also assert the catalog is unchanged in `source..parent`.
- Mark the new branch `#aidevops:trust-boundary`; the allowlist must stay identical to the reusable workflow's.
- `full-loop-helper.sh` help text (lines ~452-457) and the full-loop doc "Generated Cloudron catalogs" paragraph say "direct catalog-only child". Update both to describe the docs-only tolerance.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-evidence.py`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-release-evidence.py`
- `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md`

Integration scope recovery: the How section explicitly requests the Generated Cloudron catalogs documentation update; its actual path is `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md` (lines 333–356). No matching open PR or claimed work on this path was found. Verification: scoped documentation diff and existing catalog evidence tests.

## Verification

- Existing tests for `cloudron-release-evidence.py` pass. Add a case where an intervening docs-only commit is accepted, and cases where an intervening non-docs commit, a missing trailer, and a mismatched trailer are each rejected.
- Re-run `full-loop-helper.sh record-published-release <PR> <tag> <repo> --workflow cloudron-catalog-publish.yml --event push --generated-cloudron-catalog` on the observed release: it records `release:published`.

title: aidevops secret -- wrapper loses large concurrent MCP stdio responses when parent does not read stderr
body:
## Problem

When a stdio MCP server is launched through `aidevops secret NAME -- <cmd>`, as OpenCode `mcp.<name>.command` entries do to inject an API key, **large responses to concurrent requests are lost**. The client never receives them and times out (`MCP error -32001: Request timed out` after 60 s in OpenCode 1.19.5).

The trigger needs all three conditions:

1. the server is launched via the `aidevops secret … --` wrapper;
2. two or more requests with large responses (~160–180 KB each) are in flight concurrently;
3. the parent does not read the wrapper's stderr. OpenCode spawns local MCP servers with `stderr: "pipe"` and never consumes it (upstream anomalyco/opencode#46367, closed not planned), so this always holds under OpenCode.

## Evidence (deterministic, no model involved)

A script drives the same `npx -y mcp-remote <streamable-http-url>` stdio bridge with six `tools/call` requests: two large responses (~178 KB and ~162 KB) and four small ones.

| Launch | Requests | stderr | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| direct `npx mcp-remote` | concurrent | read / unread | all 6 OK in ~1 s |
| `aidevops secret NAME -- bash -c 'exec npx mcp-remote …'` | concurrent | read | all 6 OK in ~1 s (2/2 runs) |
| same wrapper | concurrent | **unread** | **1–2 large responses never arrive** (2/2 runs, 90 s wait) |
| same wrapper | sequential | unread | all 6 OK |

The same pattern holds in OpenCode itself. A minimal config using the wrapped command fails, and the identical config launching `npx mcp-remote` directly passes. Plugins and agents were bisected and ruled out.

## Likely location

`.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh`: the run paths execute `( … ) 2>&1 | redact_stream "$env_file"`, around the `Execute command with secrets in environment, redact output` comments. That merges the child's stderr into stdout and relays everything through the chunked Python redactor in `redact_stream`. The exact blocking mechanism is **not confirmed**. Only ~96 bytes reach the wrapper's stderr when it is read, too little to fill a pipe, so check what else in the `aidevops` CLI → `secret-helper.sh` chain writes to or waits on stderr.

Merging stderr into stdout is also wrong for MCP stdio servers in principle: diagnostic lines get injected into the JSON-RPC stream.

## Expected

`aidevops secret NAME -- <cmd>` should be usable as a transparent stdio launcher for MCP servers. Responses must not depend on whether the parent reads stderr, and stdout must carry only the child's stdout.

## Suggested approach (verify before implementing)

- Add an explicit stdio-passthrough mode for launchers, for example `aidevops secret NAME --exec -- <cmd>` or `--mcp`. It injects env and `exec`s the command with stdout/stderr left separate and unfiltered. Tool-output redaction is already covered by the registered redaction digests the OpenCode plugin applies (`register_redaction_digests`). Document it for `mcp.*.command` entries and use it in any aidevops-generated MCP configs.
- Separately, find why the default redacting relay stalls when its stderr is unread, and make it not depend on the parent draining stderr.

Files: `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh` (run paths, `redact_stream`), the `aidevops` CLI dispatcher for `secret`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-secret-helper.sh`.

Verification: a fixture stdio server that answers two concurrent requests with ~200 KB payloads, launched through the wrapper with the parent's stderr pipe left unread, must deliver both responses. Existing redaction tests must still pass for the default (non-passthrough) mode.
<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->
<!-- aidevops:sig -->

**Task ID:** `t18782` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-10-29
**Tags:** `auto-dispatch` `bug`

## Outcome

OpenCode V2: wire DB activity heartbeat and adapt V2 event shape for idle-gated archive

## Done when

- [ ] V2 `session.status` busy/idle events (`{type, data:{sessionID, status:{type}}}`) update `busy_sessions` and list the session ID in the heartbeat file.
- [ ] V1 heartbeat behaviour is unchanged (existing V1 cases still pass) and the V2 plugin still loads (`test-opencode-v2-adapter.mjs` passes).

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/db-activity-heartbeat.mjs` — read payload from `event.properties || event.data`; resolve session ID from `data.sessionID`; add V2 activity prefixes; map `session.execution.started` → busy and `session.execution.{succeeded,failed,interrupted}` → idle as a fallback to `session.status`.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs` — install the heartbeat in `setupAidevopsV2`, feed it from the existing `startEventLoop` handler (same pattern as `index.mjs:808`), and remove the heartbeat file in `disposeAidevopsV2`.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-db-activity-heartbeat.mjs` — add V2-shaped event cases next to the V1 cases.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- V1 behaviour must not change: V1 events keep the `properties` path.
- Fail closed: any unknown shape must leave busy state unchanged rather than mark idle.
- Do not change `sessionIDFrom()` globally; other V1 consumers rely on it.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/db-activity-heartbeat.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-db-activity-heartbeat.mjs`

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief


## Origin

- Issue: GH#35898 (interactive session, follow-up to GH#35517)

## What

Wire the GH#35517 OpenCode DB activity heartbeat into the OpenCode 2.x plugin (`v2.mjs`) and teach `db-activity-heartbeat.mjs` the V2 event shape, so the idle-gated archive (v3.39.60) can archive V2-held databases instead of deferring forever.

## Why

GH#35517 / PR #35519 added a per-process busy/idle heartbeat that `opencode-db-archive.sh` requires before touching a held `opencode.db`. The heartbeat is only wired through the V1 entry (`index.mjs:682`, `index.mjs:808`). The V2 entry (`v2-plugin/index.mjs` → `v2.mjs`) never installs it, so any DB held by an `opencode2` process has no heartbeat and the gate fails closed: archive never runs for 24/7 V2 hosts.

Wiring alone is insufficient. Verified against `@opencode/schema@2.2.0` (the pinned `testedVersion` in `.agents/configs/opencode-runtime-profiles.json`):

- V2 events are `{ type, data, created }`, not `{ type, properties }`. `sessionIDFrom()` in `session-turn-state.mjs` reads only `properties`, so every V2 session ID resolves to `""`.
- `session.status` exists (`session-status-event.js`): `data.status.type` is `idle | busy | retry`. `session.idle` exists but is marked deprecated.
- V2 work events are `session.step.*`, `session.tool.*`, `session.text.*`, `session.reasoning.*`, `session.shell.*`, `session.execution.{started,succeeded,failed,interrupted}`, `session.compaction.*`, `session.retry.scheduled`, `permission.asked`, `permission.replied`. None are in the V1 `ACTIVITY_EVENTS` set.

## Context & Decisions

- Follow-up to GH#35517 (PR #35519, released v3.39.60). Until this ships, V2-held DBs defer (safe, but never archived).
- Event names were verified from the published `@opencode/schema@2.2.0` package, not inferred from V1.

title: t18783: OpenCode 2.x migration-readiness checks (V2 parity tracker)
body:
## Task


Persistent tracker for OpenCode 2.x (V2) migration-readiness checks: aidevops features that work on V1 (`opencode`) but are missing, degraded or unverified on V2 (`opencode2`). Each item links its own child issue; this parent is never dispatched itself.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Persistent tracker for OpenCode 2.x (V2) migration-readiness checks: aidevops features that work on V1 (`opencode`) but are missing, degraded or unverified on V2 (`opencode2`). Each item links its own child issue; this parent is never dispatched itself.

## Why

Many V2 parity gaps surface only by accident during unrelated work (for example GH#35898, found while shipping the GH#35517 idle-gated archive). The recurring canary (GH#35179-style "Promote passing OpenCode v2 compatibility candidate") proves that V2 loads, not that every framework feature works. Without one checklist, gaps get lost before `.agents/configs/opencode-runtime-profiles.json` switches `"default"` from `v1` to `v2`.

## How (Approach)

Add one checklist line per gap, with evidence and the child issue. File each fix as a separate worker-ready child issue (`Parent: #<this>`), and tick the line when that child merges.

### Checklist

- [ ] **DB activity heartbeat (GH#35898, PR #35901).** The V2 plugin never installed the GH#35517 heartbeat, so V2-held `opencode.db` files were never archived. The V1 module also misread V2 `{type, data}` events. Fixed in PR #35901 and runtime-verified through `setupAidevopsV2`.
- [ ] **Heartbeat PID match on a live `opencode2` host.** The archive gate matches heartbeat files by DB holder PID (`.agents/scripts/opencode-db-idle-gate-lib.sh:130`). `v2.mjs:523` says plugins run in-process, but this has not been confirmed on a real `opencode2` binary. Check: `lsof` holder PID equals the `pid` field in `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/state/opencode-activity/*.json`. The gate fails closed (defers) if they differ.
- [ ] **DB archive/maintenance path and schema on V2.** `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh:51-54` assumes the V1 data dir `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/opencode`. V2's storage path and schema compatibility are unverified (`@opencode/schema` 2.2.0 ships `session-legacy.js`). Exact paths are unknown until checked on an `opencode2` install.
- [ ] **Compaction cache-prefix divergence (GH#33471).** Existing blocked investigation.
- [ ] **`textCompletionHook: false`** (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs:115`). No V2 equivalent is wired. Needs an inventory of the V1 features that depend on it.
- [ ] **`compactionAutocontinue: false`** (`v2.mjs:116`). V1 post-compaction auto-continue has no V2 equivalent yet.
- [ ] **`tuiToast: false`** (`v2.mjs:117`). V1 toasts (greeting/advisories, update warnings) have no V2 surface yet.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-idle-gate-lib.sh`
- `.agents/configs/opencode-runtime-profiles.json`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every checklist item is either ticked against a merged child PR or recorded as an explicit accepted V2 limitation with rationale.
- [ ] Regression guard: `.agents/configs/opencode-runtime-profiles.json` `"default"` does not switch to `v2` while any unticked item affects interactive sessions or DB maintenance.

## Context & Decisions

- This is a parent tracker (`parent-task`): it blocks dispatch of itself only; children are dispatched normally.
- Capability flags are the authoritative in-code gap list; keep this checklist in sync when a flag flips.

title: docs(aws): aws login access, root-identity warning, Agent Toolkit decision, SES bypass proof
body:
## Goal

Fill the gaps left by #35879 / PR #35882 with what a live SES fix using `aws login` showed on 2026-10-29. Details: https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/35879#issuecomment-6486695882 and https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/35879#issuecomment-6486883715 (both posted after the PR merged, so not included in it).

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/services/hosting/aws.md`
- EDIT: `.agents/services/email/ses.md`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh`

`secret-helper.sh` changes only if the root warning goes into `secret verify aws`; otherwise state the readiness check in `aws.md`.

## Changes

1. `aws.md` "Access options": add **`aws login`** (AWS CLI ≥ 2.32, browser console session; 12 h credentials refreshed for up to 90 days; `--remote` for SSH hosts) as the simplest interactive option next to IAM Identity Center. Flow: the agent runs `aws configure set region <region> --profile aidevops-<account>`, the human runs `aws login --profile aidevops-<account>`, then the agent runs `aws sts get-caller-identity --profile ...`. On macOS, install with `brew install awscli` rather than AWS's piped installer.
2. Root warning: if `get-caller-identity` returns an ARN ending in `:root`, say so and recommend signing in as an IAM user, role or Identity Center user; until then, limit the work to the authorised scope. Observed in practice: the console session was root.
3. AWS Agent Toolkit (`aws configure agent-toolkit`, `aws/agent-toolkit-for-aws`): record the decision. It writes an `aws-mcp` entry straight into every runtime's MCP config (it conflicts with `generate-runtime-config-mcp.sh` and the `aidevops_mcp` registry) and appends AWS rules to project `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`. Do not run the wizard; treat `aws-mcp` (with `env.AWS_MCP_PROXY_PROFILES`) as a possible on-demand registry entry, to evaluate separately.
4. `ses.md` "Suppression and silent drops": add the tested way to prove the bypass. Put a plus alias of the internal inbox on the suppression list (`put-suppressed-destination --reason BOUNCE`), send through the configuration set, confirm a CloudWatch `AWS/SES` `Delivery` datapoint for dimension `ses-configuration-set=<name>` (needs an event destination; data appears 1–2 minutes after sending), then delete the test entry. Note that WordPress FluentSMTP's SES mailer sends raw MIME, so a `wp_mail` filter adding `X-SES-CONFIGURATION-SET` works, and that its log does not show custom headers.
5. `ses.md`: recommend a periodic `ses-helper.sh suppressed <account> --filter <own-domain>` for each verified domain. Doing this by hand found a client's own support inbox that had been suppressed since 2024.

## Verification

- `markdownlint` (or the repo's markdown lint) on the changed docs; ShellCheck if `secret-helper.sh` changes.
- `aws.md` stays within the progressive-disclosure size limits; no account IDs, client domains or private repo names in the docs.

title: test-migrate-orphaned-supervisor.sh mutates the real user crontab and leaks fixtures when interrupted
body:
## What

`tests/test-migrate-orphaned-supervisor.sh` writes the **real user crontab**. Isolate it so the test never touches host cron state.

## Evidence

On a maintainer macOS host, `crontab -l` contains only the test's fixture lines:

```
# aidevops: test-keep-this
*/5 * * * * echo keep-this # aidevops: test-keep
```

Lines 197-229 save `crontab -l`, install fixture entries with `crontab -`, run the migration, then restore. Exporting `HOME="$TEST_HOME"` (line 48) does not isolate `crontab`, which writes the system per-user spool. There is no `trap` around the save/restore. An interrupted, timed-out or killed run therefore leaves the fixture in place. On the next run, those leaked lines are saved as the "original" and restored again, so the leak persists.

## How

- Isolate cron: put a stub `crontab` executable first on `PATH`, backed by a file under `$TEST_HOME`. Alternatively, inject a crontab command override if the migration code accepts one. Never call the real `crontab` from tests.
- If any real-crontab path must stay, wrap it in `trap ... EXIT INT TERM` restoration and refuse to run unless an explicit opt-in env var is set.
- Check the other tests that call `crontab` for the same pattern: `rg -n "crontab" .agents/scripts/tests tests`.

### Files Scope

- tests/test-migrate-orphaned-supervisor.sh

## Verification

Run the test and confirm that `crontab -l` before and after is byte-identical, including when the test is killed mid-run (`timeout 2 bash tests/test-migrate-orphaned-supervisor.sh`).

Affected hosts can remove the leaked lines with `crontab -e`, deleting the two `test-keep` lines.

title: Docker cleanup as you go: sessions don't label test stacks, and teardown leaves anonymous volumes
body:
## What

Make aidevops sessions label and clean up the Docker resources they create as they go. The rule and the machinery from GH#34285 exist, but nothing makes sessions use them, and teardown leaves anonymous volumes behind.

## Why

Observed on the maintainer's Mac on 2026-10-29, after months of aidevops sessions and workers building and testing projects:

- `docker-resource-helper.sh report`: **0 labelled of 57 containers**, 0 of 8 custom networks, 0 of 1,948 volumes. Every test stack was made by an aidevops session, but none carried the `sh.aidevops.*` owner labels, so worktree teardown and the pulse reaper had nothing to act on.
- 35 containers stopped for 12-14 days, all named after issues or PRs (`<project>-ghNNN-web`, `-db`, `-crawler`, `-minio`).
- 1,893 unused anonymous volumes holding **345 GB**, plus 16 orphaned WordPress test sites (32 containers, 32 volumes, 16 networks), 20.5 GB of unused images and 31.7 GB of old build cache. All were removed by hand in an interactive session.
- The Docker tooling in the public WordPress plugin starter (`wpallstars/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding`: `scripts/test-site.sh`, `scripts/plugin-check.sh`, `scripts/update-test.sh`, `scripts/lib/docker-wordpress.sh`) was written and maintained by aidevops sessions without the owner labels. That repo's fix is wpallstars/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding#570; the cause is in the framework.

Causes in the framework:

1. **The rule isn't where sessions look.** "Every container, network and volume a session starts for testing ... carries the six `sh.aidevops.*` owner labels" is only in `tools/containers/disposable-resources.md`. Nothing routes a session there when it runs `docker run`, `docker compose up`, `docker network create` or `docker volume create`, or when it writes a script that does.
2. **Teardown leaves anonymous volumes.** `docker-resource-helper.sh` removes containers with `docker rm -f` without `-v` (`.agents/scripts/docker-resource-helper.sh:493`). Docker keeps the anonymous volumes those containers created (images with a `VOLUME` that isn't mounted from a named volume), and anonymous volumes don't inherit container labels, so the reaper never sees them. This probably accounts for some of the 1,893 volumes, though their source wasn't proven.
3. **Nobody is told about the pile-up.** `report` runs only when asked, and the pulse reap step is report-only by default (`AIDEVOPS_DOCKER_REAP=0`) and logs nothing about unlabelled growth.

## How

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/docker-resource-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh`

title: t18785: fix(badges): sync retains one worktree per failed retry when pre-push readiness blocks
body:
## Task


`badges-sync-helper.sh --apply` (routine r921) leaves one retained worktree per failed attempt when a repo's pre-push gate is blocked by `JS_TOOL_READINESS`, and the routine's failure backoff (15 min doubling to 6 h) turns that into a pile of identical worktrees.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`badges-sync-helper.sh --apply` (routine r921) leaves one retained worktree per failed attempt when a repo's pre-push gate is blocked by `JS_TOOL_READINESS`, and the routine's failure backoff (15 min doubling to 6 h) turns that into a pile of identical worktrees.

## Why

Observed 27–29 Oct on a managed JS/TS repo whose pre-push hook runs ESLint and `tsc`:

- r921 ran 8 times in ~3 days (`pulse.log`: `routine r921 is due ... last_run_epoch` unchanged; `script exited with code 1`). This is the intended retry path in `pulse-routines.sh` `_routine_retry_blocked`, since `last_run` advances only on success.
- Every attempt created a new `chore/badges-sync-<timestamp>-<pid>-<rand>` worktree. Worktree setup logged `dependency-provision-rejected reason=incomplete-installed-inventory` and `JS_TOOL_READINESS=blocked:snapshot-incomplete-installed-inventory (eslint tsc)`; the commit succeeded but the push was blocked by the gate, so nothing reached GitHub.
- `_apply_repo` retains failed worktrees by design ("Failures retain the worktree and branch for recovery"), but the next attempt never looks for them, so 8 copies of the same commit were retained. Guarded `worktree-helper.sh remove` then refuses all of them (unpushed commits), so they need manual cleanup.
- The open-PR dedup in `_apply_repo` only sees pushed PRs, so it cannot catch this.

## How

In `.agents/scripts/badges-sync-helper.sh`:

1. Before creating a new branch in `_apply_repo`, look for a retained local `"${_prefix}-*"` branch/worktree for the same repo. Reuse it (retry the push) or skip with `SKIPPED retained recovery worktree: <path>` instead of creating another.
2. Classify a push blocked by tool readiness as its own outcome (e.g. `BLOCKED-READINESS` with the `JS_TOOL_READINESS_HINT` text) so the routine output says why, rather than a generic `FAILED`.
3. Optional, worker's judgement: a readiness block isn't fixed by retrying sooner. Consider returning the routine tempfail code (`_ROUTINE_TEMPFAIL_EXIT` in `pulse-routines.sh`), or not counting it as a failure that triggers fast retries.

Do not bypass the repo's pre-push gate (`--no-verify`) or auto-download dependencies without approval; both are deliberate policy.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/badges-sync-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-badges-sync-worktree.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- Extending the existing fixture in `test-badges-sync-worktree.sh` (it already simulates retained-worktree failures): with a push rejected by a hook, two consecutive `--apply` runs leave at most one `chore/badges-sync-*` worktree, and the second run reports the retained one.
- Existing `test-badges-sync-worktree.sh` cases still pass; ShellCheck clean.

title: WordPress fleet: core minor-release updates, and wp core update --minor falsely reports latest when WP HTTP is filtered
body:
## What

Add a reusable way to apply WordPress core **minor** releases across a fleet of SSH-reachable installs. Document the trap where WP-CLI falsely reports core as up to date.

## Why (observed 2026-10-29, shared hosting, WP-CLI 2.12.0)

- A core RCE (4.7.0–7.1.3, fixed 7.1.4) was still unpatched on 15 of 18 installs on one shared-hosting account. Eight had `WP_AUTO_UPDATE_CORE=false`, set by a vendor stack opt-in that "excludes core … from WordPress auto-updates" and leaves no owner. The rest were waiting for the twice-daily update check.
- On installs whose `pre_http_request` is filtered (a restore-rehearsal isolation mu-plugin, `WP_HTTP_BLOCK_EXTERNAL`, and the like), `wp core update --minor` prints `Success: WordPress is at the latest minor release.` while still on the vulnerable version. `wp core check-update --force-check` likewise prints `Success: WordPress is at the latest version.` Mu-plugins still load under `--skip-plugins`. Nothing shows a failure.
- The operator had to write a one-off adapter. The framework has `wp-fleet-helper.sh` for self-hosted **plugin** rollouts, but no core path.

## How

1. Docs: `.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-cli-reference.md` "WordPress Core" (around line 216). Add a short warning about the false "latest" result under filtered WordPress HTTP. Fallback: query `https://api.wordpress.org/core/version-check/1.7/?version=<cur>&locale=<loc>` from the shell, take the newest offer on the same X.Y branch, download `https://downloads.wordpress.org/release/[<locale>/]wordpress-<v>.zip`, verify it against `<url>.sha1`, then run `wp core update <zip> --version=<v> --force`. Then run `core update-db` (`--network` on multisite) and `core verify-checksums`. Cross-link from `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md` near the existing `proc_open`/`mysqldump` notes (around line 310).
2. Capability: extend `.agents/scripts/wp-fleet-helper.sh` (pattern: its existing `plan`/`backup`/`deploy`/`verify`/`report` run-dir flow) with a core-minor mode, or add a sibling helper. Requirements:
   - stay on the same branch only; report majors, never apply them
   - back up the database outside the web root first (`mysqldump` with a 0600 defaults file, because `wp db export` needs `proc_open`)
   - use sha1-verified locale packages
   - verify with checksums plus a home/login HTTP probe (treat 401/403 as alive for Basic-Auth staging)
   - give a per-site hold list
   - never roll back automatically: rolling back reinstates the vulnerable version
   - print a dry-run summary line suitable for a `run:` routine
3. Reference implementation (operator-private, not in the repo): a ~200-line single-owner routine adapter in `custom/scripts/`. It pipes a remote bash script over `ssh <alias> bash -s` and has been verified against live API offers (7.1.3 → 7.1.4 for en_GB/en_US; 7.0.2 → 7.0.8 with major reported only).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-cli-reference.md`
- `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md`
- `.agents/scripts/wp-fleet-helper.sh`

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/wp-fleet-helper.sh` reports zero violations.
- The existing `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-wp-fleet-helper.sh` still passes.
- Dry run against a fixture or staging install on X.Y.(n-1) reports the same-branch target and reports a newer major without applying it.
- A site whose WordPress HTTP is blocked is updated from the verified zip, and `wp core verify-checksums` passes afterwards.

title: jq 1.8 binding precedence silently disables blocked-checkpoint attention on Homebrew runners
body:
## What

Make the framework's jq programs give identical results under jq 1.7.x (Ubuntu CI, macOS `/usr/bin/jq`, apt installs) and jq 1.8.x (Homebrew), fix the one production predicate jq 1.8 broke, and add a deterministic gate so binding-precedence ambiguity cannot return.

## Why

**Causal status**: confirmed.

1. #32162 (2026-09-21): managed-tool convergence moved runners from `/usr/bin/jq` 1.7.1 to `/opt/homebrew/bin/jq` 1.8.2. No compatibility check ran against the framework's jq programs.
2. jq 1.8.0 NEWS, "Language changes": "Fix precedence of binding syntax against unary and binary operators … This is a breaking change" (jqlang/jq#3053, #3326). `A and Term as $x | B` was `A and (Term as $x | B)` in 1.7. In 1.8 it is `(A and Term) as $x | B`. The same applies to `or`, comparisons, arithmetic, `//`, assignment operators, unary minus and `try`.
3. Probe: `jq -nc 'true and ("x") as $l | $l | type'` gives `"boolean"` on 1.8.2 and `true` on 1.7.1.
4. Production predicate: `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh:637`, `blocked_by_runner` in `_pcc_blocked_release_evidence`. Under 1.8, `$line` is bound to the boolean conjunction. `field("reason")` then raises `boolean (true) cannot be matched, as it is not a string`. The function fails whenever a release exists, so `_pcc_blocked_attention` reports `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION_SKIPPED: … has no current blocked release`.
5. Impact: GH#33132 (merged 2026-09-30, after the jq upgrade) never worked on this runner. Worker drafts released as `blocked` get no approval-ready attention record and stall silently. The current `pulse.log` starts 2026-10-25 and has 328 occurrences of this error. 307 of them are immediately followed by an attention skip, covering 39 distinct draft PRs across 5 managed repos (including #35757 here).
6. Detection gap: `test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` fails at `main` on the runner with exactly this error. It then aborts under `set -e` at line 529 and hides all later cases. With jq 1.7.1 it passes (106/106). CI does not run this suite, and CI's jq is 1.7.1.

Audit of other jq 1.8 breaking changes in tracked non-test files (the rest of the change list):

- No `last(f)` generator, no `limit/2` and no `--indent 0` uses.
- All 11 `ltrimstr`/`rtrimstr` sites receive strings (guarded by `startswith`, `scan`, `split`, a `type == "string"` check, or API string fields).
- Binding precedence: a prototype detector checked about 1,290 binding sites in tracked `.sh/.jq/.yml/.py` files. Exactly one is ambiguous: the predicate above.

## Reproducer

1. Run `jq -nc 'true and ("x") as $l | $l | type'` under each version. jq 1.7.1 prints `true`; jq 1.8.2 prints `"boolean"`.
2. On a runner whose `PATH` resolves jq 1.8.x, run `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` at `main`. It fails with `jq: error (at <stdin>:N): boolean (true) cannot be matched, as it is not a string` and aborts. With `/usr/bin/jq` 1.7.1 first in `PATH`, the same suite passes 106/106.
3. On an affected runner, `rg -N -A1 'cannot be matched, as it is not a string' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` shows each error followed by `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION_SKIPPED: PR #N … has no current blocked release`.

## How

1. Parenthesize the binding in `blocked_by_runner` so both jq versions parse it as 1.7 did.
2. Add a deterministic detector for `Term as <pattern>` whose Term is the operand of `and`/`or`/comparison/arithmetic/`//`/assignment/unary minus/`try`. Wire it into `linters-local.sh` (changed and full modes) with a zero baseline, following the existing `lint-*.sh` validator pattern.
3. Add a short jq 1.7/1.8 compatibility rule to `reference/shell-style-guide.md`: wrap any binding that follows an operator.

## Acceptance

- `test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` passes fully under both jq 1.7.1 and jq 1.8.2.
- The detector reports zero sites on the repository and flags each operator class in a fixture.
- `linters-local.sh --changed` runs the detector on changed jq-bearing files.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/lint-jq-binding-precedence.py`
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local-validators.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-lint-jq-binding-precedence.sh`
- `.agents/reference/shell-style-guide.md`

Follow-up decision (not in this scope): whether CI should also run jq-dependent suites under jq 1.8.x, so CI and Homebrew runners exercise the same semantics.

title: fix(issue-sync): detect expired SYNC_PAT, fall back for read-only hygiene, and warn before expiry
body:
## What

Make an expired or revoked `SYNC_PAT` visible and survivable in `issue-sync-reusable.yml`, and warn operators before the 90-day token expires.

Today an expired fine-grained `SYNC_PAT` makes every SYNC_PAT-backed `actions/checkout` fail with an unclear error:

```text
fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': terminal prompts disabled
The process '/usr/bin/git' failed with exit code 128   (retried 3x)
```

The `secrets.SYNC_PAT || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` fallback covers only an **empty** secret, not an invalid one. The "Check SYNC_PAT visibility (t2166)" step still reports `SYNC_PAT present`, so its notice points the wrong way.

## Why (observed evidence, private managed repo, name withheld)

- Repo secret `SYNC_PAT` was last updated `2026-07-29T18:07:51Z`. The framework creation URL uses `expiration=90` (`.agents/reference/sync-pat-platforms.md:69`), so expiry was due about `2026-10-27T18:07Z`.
- Last successful SYNC_PAT checkout: `2026-10-27T18:04Z` (sync-on-pr-merge, `Checkout repo before closing-hygiene validation` = success).
- First failure: `2026-10-27T18:39Z` (sync-on-issue `Checkout`). Since then, every PR-merge hygiene run with a linked issue has failed at `Checkout repo before closing-hygiene validation`, about 70 runs in 36 hours. Every t-prefixed issue→TODO sync has also failed at `Checkout`. Runs without a SYNC_PAT checkout still pass.
- Effect: post-merge closing hygiene (`status:done` normalisation, parent-task nudges, TODO.md proof-log) and issue→TODO projection were skipped. The only signal was red runs, found during a manual blocked-issue sweep.
- Expiry advisory is already listed as an unimplemented Phase 2 item at `.agents/reference/sync-pat-platforms.md:229-230`.

## How

1. **Validate the token, not just its presence.** In the four `Check SYNC_PAT visibility (t2166)` steps (`.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml` around lines 222-230, 451-460, 740-750, 834-842), pass `SYNC_PAT` via `env:` and probe it without printing it, e.g. `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H "Authorization: Bearer ${SYNC_PAT}" "https://api.github.com/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"`. Map `200` → valid, `401` → expired/revoked, `403`/`404` → missing repository access. On failure emit `::error title=SYNC_PAT invalid::<class> — rotate per reference/sync-pat-platforms.md` and set a step output such as `sync_pat_valid=false`. Give the step an `id:`.
2. **Fall back when invalid.** Change the SYNC_PAT checkout `token:` expressions (lines ~242, ~469, ~757, ~947) to use `SYNC_PAT` only when the probe passed, otherwise `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Read-only closing hygiene and labels use `GH_TOKEN: secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` already, so they keep working. TODO.md publication then follows the existing GH006/protected-branch PR path documented at lines ~1333-1337. Keep the `::error::` annotation so the run stays visibly degraded. Choose and document whether the job should finish red or green-with-annotation.
3. **Warn locally before expiry.** In `.agents/scripts/security-posture-helper-repo.sh` (`_check_sync_pat_need` at line ~1295, `_emit_sync_pat_advisory` at line ~1163), when `SYNC_PAT` is configured, write an advisory to `~/.aidevops/advisories/sync-pat-<SLUG_SAFE>.advisory` in either case: the secret's `updated_at` (from `gh secret list`) is 76+ days old (90 minus 14), or the latest issue-sync run failed at a SYNC_PAT checkout step. Secret age is a heuristic, because tokens can use other expiry periods, so word the advisory as "may expire". Extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-sync-pat-detection.sh` only where the existing harness already covers these functions.
4. **Document rotation.** Add a "Rotation / expired token" section to `.agents/reference/sync-pat-platforms.md` covering: the exact symptom string above; that regenerating keeps the token's permissions and repository list but revokes the old value everywhere; setting the secret with `gh secret set SYNC_PAT --repo <SLUG>` (interactive prompt); and rerunning the failed jobs with `gh run rerun <id> --failed`. Cross-reference the reusable-PAT guidance in t18777.

## Reproducer

1. In a scratch repository that uses the issue-sync reusable workflow, set `SYNC_PAT` to an expired or revoked fine-grained token. Leave the secret non-empty.
2. Merge a PR whose body contains `Resolves #N`.
3. Observe `sync / Sync Issue Hygiene on PR Merge`. `Check SYNC_PAT visibility (t2166)` prints `SYNC_PAT present`. `Checkout repo before closing-hygiene validation` then fails 3x with `fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': terminal prompts disabled`, and every later hygiene step is skipped.
4. Open or edit a `tNNN:`-titled issue. `sync / Sync GitHub Issue → TODO.md` fails at `Checkout` with the same error.

The observed evidence above is a live instance in a managed repository, confirmed on 2026-10-29.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-forge-event-workflow.sh` — necessary workflow-contract assertion integration (GH#35924)

- EDIT: `.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/security-posture-helper-repo.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-sync-pat-detection.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/sync-pat-platforms.md`

Touch the test file only where the existing harness already covers the changed functions.

## Verification

- `actionlint .github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml` and ShellCheck on changed scripts: zero findings.
- In a scratch repo or fork with a deliberately invalid `SYNC_PAT`, run a PR merge carrying `Resolves #N`. Confirm the probe step shows a single `SYNC_PAT invalid` error with no token value, the checkout falls back to `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and `Apply closing hygiene to linked issues` runs.
- Using a valid token, confirm the behaviour is unchanged: the probe passes and checkout uses `SYNC_PAT`.
- `security-posture-helper.sh` writes the advisory for an aged secret and does not write one for a fresh secret.

## Constraints

- Never print, export or log the token value. Use `env:` plus masked probes only.
- Do not weaken branch protection or add broader PAT scopes.

title: Trusted retry never releases first-observation permission_required (and policy-timeout) status:blocked holds
body:
## What

A trusted `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry` directive never releases a **first-observation** `status:blocked` hold whose class is `permission_required`. The issue stays blocked and undispatched for good, even though the recovery text tells the maintainer to "post the explicit retry directive".

This is the same defect family as GH#35745 (`unknown`, fixed by PR #35746) and GH#35095 (`target_code_blocker`, fixed by PR #35097), for the classes those fixes did not cover.

Also fix the misclassification that produced the live holds: workers classify a **runner-local host lock** (a serialization lock held on one runner, awaiting that host operator's reconciliation) as `permission_required` instead of `runner_capability_unmet`.

## Why (observed evidence, private managed repo, name withheld)

- Five open issues in one managed repository have each held `status:blocked` since 2026-10-27T02:23–02:26Z (three issues) and 2026-10-28T05:44–05:45Z (two issues). In every case one runner's worker ended `BLOCKED` with `Terminal blocker: reason=permission_required owner=permission-maintainer`, followed by `Projected state: status:blocked`.
- The worker dossiers show the cause was a host-local guarded sign-in lock on that one runner. It refused before authentication. No permission request (`perm-…`) and no `needs-maintainer-permissions` label exists on any of them. Other runners do not have that lock.
- On the three older issues, an OWNER/MEMBER posted standalone `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry` directives at 2026-10-27T03:08Z, 2026-10-27T07:23Z, 2026-10-28T03:12Z and 2026-10-29T03:18Z. None was followed by a label change, a dispatch or a re-arm receipt. A downstream queue retries three times, then marks the item unavailable, so the stranded hold permanently removes work from the queue.
- Installed framework v3.39.84; `origin/main` `0166e8cb81` has the same code.

## Root cause (code path)

1. `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh:549` `_hrff_blocked_exit_holds` projects `status:blocked` on the first observation for every class except `runner_capability_unmet` without missing secret names.
2. `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh:304` `_tbr_seed_reason` queues a first observation only when `terminal_blocker_rearms_on_revision` accepts its class. `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh:33` `_TBC_REVISION_REARM_REASONS` omits `permission_required`, `push_policy_timeout` and `network_policy_timeout`. Those first observations are therefore never queued on any runner, so `_tbr_release_circuit_hold` (`terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh:439`), the only path that turns a trusted retry into `status:available`, never runs for them.
3. `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh:1070` refuses every `status:blocked` candidate, so the issue is never dispatched again.
4. Misclassification: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh:1096-1098` tells workers that a rejected runner-local credential is `runner_capability_unmet`, but says nothing about a host-local lock or serialization guard held on this runner. Workers fall through to `permission_required` (`:1099-1106`).

## How

1. Give `permission_required` a release path driven only by a trusted retry. Its task revision is already constant (`terminal_blocker_task_revision`, `terminal-blocker-circuit.sh:362-366`), so a brief edit or an unrelated merge must still never release it. Either add it to the seeded classes, or add a separate retry-only set used by `_tbr_seed_reason` and `terminal_blocker_observation_hold_active` (`terminal-blocker-circuit.sh:562`). Choose whichever keeps "revision re-arm" semantics truthful. On release, the original permission guard must still verify the exact context at work time: retry is scheduling consent only.
2. Apply the same invariant to `push_policy_timeout` and `network_policy_timeout`. Every class that `_hrff_blocked_exit_holds` projects as `status:blocked` must have a trusted-retry release path. Alternatively, project these transient same-runner classes as `status:available`, as `runner_capability_unmet` already is. Their recovery text says "retry … on the same runner after host contention clears", so a global hold contradicts it.
3. In `headless-runtime-lib.sh` near `:1096-1098`, add one sentence: a host-local lock or serialization guard that this runner holds pending its operator's reconciliation is `runner_capability_unmet`, not `permission_required`, because another runner may not hold it.
4. Follow the PR #35746 pattern for tests: extend the existing `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` harness only.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** source `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`, then call `terminal_blocker_rearms_on_revision "$reason"` for each class (this is the gate `_tbr_seed_reason` uses to decide whether a first observation is queued for release):

```bash
source ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh
for reason in permission_required push_policy_timeout network_policy_timeout unknown target_code_blocker; do
  rc=0; terminal_blocker_rearms_on_revision "$reason" || rc=$?
  printf '%s rearms_on_revision_rc=%s\n' "$reason" "$rc"
done
```

**Actual output** (v3.39.84, 2026-10-29):

```text
permission_required rearms_on_revision_rc=1
push_policy_timeout rearms_on_revision_rc=1
network_policy_timeout rearms_on_revision_rc=1
unknown rearms_on_revision_rc=0
target_code_blocker rearms_on_revision_rc=0
```

**Expected:** every class that `_hrff_blocked_exit_holds` projects as `status:blocked` must have a trusted-retry release path. Today `rc=1` means the class is never seeded, so it has none.

Lifecycle:

1. A worker exits with `BLOCKED:` and a standalone `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=permission_required` on a first observation. The release comment shows `Projected state: status:blocked` and the label becomes `status:blocked`.
2. An OWNER/MEMBER posts a standalone `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry` comment.
3. Run `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh` seed/pending on any runner. The issue is never queued, because `_tbr_seed_reason` returns 1 for `permission_required`.
4. Pulse cycles skip the issue via `_dispatch_preclaim_brief_scope_verdict` (`status_blocked`). It remains blocked indefinitely.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`

## Acceptance

- A first-observation `permission_required` hold followed by a later standalone OWNER/MEMBER `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry` is queued, released to `status:available` exactly once, and gets a re-arm receipt.
- The same hold is **not** released by a brief edit, a dependency change, an unrelated default-branch merge, a COLLABORATOR or quoted retry, or a retry that predates the observation.
- `push_policy_timeout` and `network_policy_timeout` first observations either project `status:available` or follow the same trusted-retry release path. No class that projects `status:blocked` is left without a release path.
- The worker prompt classifies a runner-local host lock as `runner_capability_unmet`.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` passes, with new cases for the acceptance rows above.
- ShellCheck on the changed scripts reports zero findings.

## Constraints

- Do not let a retry grant access: the permission guard and permission-request flow stay authoritative.
- Keep GH#35540 intact: missing or foreign-collaborator evidence must never project availability.

<!-- aidevops:sig -->
