title: perf(claude-code): detect and mitigate hidden agent_summary token overhead
body:
## Goal

Detect and safely mitigate Claude Code's hidden `agent_summary` requests in aidevops-managed Claude workflows, without disabling useful agents or changing unrelated runtimes.

Requested by an aidevops user after reviewing this MIT-licensed external report:
https://gist.github.com/flamerix-ai/c3905705cc4205e5de3011fa2e74efce

## Evidence and limits

- The report describes periodic requests that summarize a background agent's full transcript into a 3–5 word UI status. It reports 16.4% of estimated spend and 19.7% of API requests in its own workload, falling to zero for this query source with its experimental Bun preload. These are third-party measurements, not savings reproduced for aidevops or a guarantee for subscription limits.
- Upstream feature request remains OPEN at filing: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/86879 . It requests a supported disable setting and contains additional workload measurements.
- Related OPEN upstream accounting issue: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/104358 . These background requests can be absent from transcript-based cost accounting; a missing transcript row does not prove zero usage.
- The external preload wraps timer callbacks and matches source strings. Its author tested Linux native Bun builds, with macOS/Windows untested, and explicitly notes fail-open behavior after updates. Do not download or execute this untrusted script as part of automatic triage, or adopt a global `BUN_OPTIONS` monkeypatch by default.
- Existing `claude -p` routes may already avoid this in some versions and configurations. Do not assume every headless or OpenCode session is affected. The report also demonstrates explicitly enabled headless cases in newer releases. Establish actual exposure before changing launch behavior.

## aidevops investigation / duplicate check

Checked current upstream `main` and the matching local checkout at `a218a38fc277b439f449ac26a2f1d0c4a114d79c` on 2026-10-29 UTC. Working tree was clean.

- Repository-wide tracked-file searches found no `agent_summary`, `AgentSummary`, `AGENT_PROGRESS_SUMMARIES`, `no-agent-summary`, `flamerix`, `BUN_OPTIONS`, `DISABLE_NON_ESSENTIAL_MODEL_CALLS`, `DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC`, `FORK_SUBAGENT`, or `ENABLE_NARRATION` implementation/planning references.
- GitHub code search returned zero matches for `agent_summary` and `AGENT_PROGRESS_SUMMARIES`.
- Searched open and closed issues/PRs using the gist identifier, `flamerix`, upstream issue number `86879`, `BUN_OPTIONS`, and summary/spinner/token-waste title variants. No matching mitigation or planned work was identified. Broad summary searches produced unrelated results; they are not evidence of an existing fix. Recheck before implementation because the repository is active.
- `.agents/tools/ai-assistants/claude-code.md:58–62` recommends avoiding nested subagents, but does not address this internal timer.
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:1134–1135` documents OpenCode as the default and `claude -p` for the Claude runtime; `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/claude-proxy-context.mjs:340–346` builds the CLI proxy invocation starting with `-p`.

## Bounded implementation scope

1. Add a version/runtime-aware exposure diagnostic and concise Claude guidance. Check the installed CLI version and actual available settings/exports before asserting that any flag disables summaries. Distinguish interactive background agents, ordinary `-p`, explicit SDK opt-in, and OpenCode direct-provider calls. Report unknown or not-measured honestly.
2. Prefer a supported upstream configuration if one becomes available and verify its effect. If none exists, document that limitation and a reviewed opt-in mitigation path rather than silently injecting a preload. Any runtime interception requires a separate compatibility/security review and explicit operator opt-in, preserving existing Bun options and isolating changes to intended Claude processes.
3. Document aggregate-only verification using `claude_code.api_request` / `query_source=agent_summary` where available, with a before/after control and version/platform evidence. Do not claim full cost coverage from transcript parsing. Never enable raw request-body capture or retain prompts, credentials, or customer data.
4. Preserve ordinary timers, useful agent/fork/background behavior, existing user settings, non-Claude runtimes, and rollback. Do not restart an operator's active daemon/session automatically. Document that an update can invalidate an unofficial workaround and that successful preload loading alone does not prove suppression.

## Files / reference patterns

Known starting points, to inspect rather than change all indiscriminately:

- `.agents/scripts/update-claude-settings.py` and `.agents/scripts/generate-claude-agents.sh`: existing Claude setup/settings integration; preserve user configuration.
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh`, `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-commands.sh`, `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-invoke.sh`: managed runtime selection and launch boundaries.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/claude-proxy-context.mjs`: existing Claude CLI argv construction pattern, if diagnostic coverage requires it.
- `.agents/tools/ai-assistants/claude-code.md` and `.agents/reference/observability.md`: document applicability, safe verification, accounting gaps, and rollback.
- New diagnostic/test filenames are intentionally not prescribed; discover and reuse the nearest existing patterns. Do not add new test infrastructure solely for this issue.

## Acceptance / verification

- [ ] A user can determine whether their installed runtime is potentially affected, unaffected by the relevant path, or not yet verified, without a paid model call just to run the diagnostic.
- [ ] Current supported controls are checked; nonexistent env vars or SDK `false` values are not presented as working opt-outs without evidence.
- [ ] Where a mitigation is implemented, controlled runtime evidence shows fewer/zero `agent_summary` requests while useful agents still finish; report measured scope, not a universal percentage. Live paid/subscription-consuming experiments require operator consent.
- [ ] Unsupported versions/platforms and signature drift have explicit diagnostics; no silent claim of successful mitigation based only on a preload marker.
- [ ] Existing relevant checks and focused regression coverage pass for any launch/settings behavior changed. No global timer patch, disabled background functionality, raw-body telemetry, or unrelated runtime changes are introduced by default.
- [ ] Documentation explains opt-in/rollback and the upstream issue to follow. If no safe supported mitigation exists, deliver honest diagnostic/guidance first and capture any independently reviewed runtime-hook proposal separately.

This issue authorizes bounded diagnostic/guidance implementation and supported safe configuration, not automatic deployment of the third-party preload. It does not authorize changing the application repository from which the investigation was requested.

title: fix(pulse): merged worker partials stay status:in-review when For #N is mid-line, under Remaining, or paired with a tracker
body:
## Problem

The partial-continuation reconciler (GH#34312, periodic sweep GH#34432) returns a merged worker partial's target issue to `status:available` + `auto-dispatch` only when `_extract_pr_work_issue <pr> <repo> explicit` resolves exactly that issue. After GH#34338 (t18660), explicit mode only accepts a standalone `For #N` / `Ref #N` line outside secondary sections such as `## Remaining`, `## Follow-up`, `## Related`, `## Next steps`.

Workers write partial PR bodies freely, and many valid partials do not use that exact shape. Those target issues stay `status:in-review` with the finished runner still assigned, there is no open PR, and nothing will ever release them. Dependants stay blocked silently.

## Evidence (one managed private repo, 2026-10-29)

I triaged 24 open `status:in-review` issues. Five were merged `origin:worker` partials that passed every other `_pm_restore_partial_continuation` guard: `_pmpc_issue_scope`=leaf, `_pmpc_release_owner_from_comments` released, `_pmpc_owned_assignees` ok, no other open PR, no closing reference. Their PRs had been merged 8 to 14 days earlier. In all five the PR title was `t<issue>: ...` and the body contained `For #<issue>`, but the explicit resolver returned nothing:

| Shape in PR body | Count | Resolver result |
|---|---|---|
| `For #N` on its own line, but under `## Remaining` | 2 | none (secondary section skipped) |
| `For #N` mid-line (`People phase ... (data only ...). For #N`) | 2 | none (line must start with For/Ref) |
| `For #N. For #<tracker>.` on one line | 1 | rc=1 ambiguous |

Three other in-review issues were correctly not restored: their newest merged cross-referencing PR targeted or closed a different issue.

I restored four of the five interactively by calling the deployed `_pmpc_*` guards and `_pmpc_project_available`, so the framework marker comment was posted. One was deliberately left in review because its remaining routes need operator authority.

## Proposed fix

File: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`, `_pm_restore_partial_continuation` (target resolution near the `_extract_pr_work_issue ... explicit` call and the `expected_target` comparison).

When explicit resolution is empty, ambiguous, or different, accept a **corroborated** fallback target only when all of these hold:

1. The PR title starts with `t<N>` or `GH#<N>` (the same title pattern `_extract_pr_work_issue` repair mode already reads).
2. The body contains a `For`/`Ref` `#<N>` reference to that same N anywhere outside code fences, blockquotes and HTML comments. Secondary sections and mid-line positions are allowed here because the title independently names the target.
3. All existing guards still apply unchanged: worker origin label, no closing reference in any form, merge confirmed, leaf/parent scope, finished-run owner, owned assignees only, no other open PR, and the marker idempotency check.
4. For periodic reconciliation, N must also equal `expected_target`.

This keeps GH#34338's protection: a mid-line or secondary reference alone still never associates. Only agreement between the title and the body does.

Optional prevention (separate PR if non-trivial): have the worker partial-PR guidance or `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` emit a leading standalone `For #N` line for non-closing worker PRs. The composition path is not yet identified; the worker should locate it.

## Verification

- Extend the existing `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`. Keep the current "ambiguous/no explicit reference: no write" case for PRs without title agreement. Add these cases:
  - `For #N` under `## Remaining` with title `tN` → write.
  - Mid-line `For #N` with title `tN` → write.
  - `For #N. For #M.` with title `tN` → write for N only.
  - Title `tN` with body `For #M` → no write.
  - Title `tN` with a closing ref → no write.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`

<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: Capability-release checkpoint attention never fires: jq iterates comment pages instead of comments
body:
## What

Make `_pcc_blocked_attention` post the runner-capability variant for `runner_capability_unmet` releases, as #35806 intended. Today every runner posts the brief-owner variant. That variant asks a human to edit the issue body and publish an approval line for a problem that is not in the brief.

## Why

**Causal status**: confirmed by reproducer; misrouted outcome observed in production.

1. `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh:805` (added by #35806 for GH#35788) tests the release with `jq -e … 'any(.[]; .id == $id and …)' <<<"$comments"`.
2. `$comments` comes from `_pcc_issue_comments`, which runs `gh api … --paginate --slurp`. That returns an array of pages, so `.[]` yields page arrays and `.id` raises `Cannot index array with string "id"`. jq exits 5, the `if` treats that as false, and the brief-owner body is posted. Every other evidence query in this helper iterates `flatten[]` and is documented as accepting "paginated or flat" comments.
3. Detection gap: `test_capability_checkpoint_attention` in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` stubs `_pcc_issue_comments` with a flat array, a shape the production fetch never returns. `test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` uses paginated fixtures and prints this jq error on every blocked-attention case, but no assertion there covers the capability variant, so it passes.
4. Observed: #35858 received the brief-owner variant (comment 6485037960, 2026-10-29T01:08Z, posted by a COLLABORATOR runner) for capability release 6484759751. The poster's aidevops version is not recorded, so this alone does not distinguish a pre-v3.39.81 runner from this defect. Earlier examples predate #35806: #35592 (3 records) and #35600 (3 records) on 2026-10-25.
5. Sequencing hazard with #35920 (PR #35930): jq 1.8 runners currently fail in `_pcc_blocked_release_evidence` before reaching this branch. Once #35920 lands they start posting blocked attention on the drafts that were silently stalled, and every capability release among them would get the brief-owner variant. This fix must land no later than #35920.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** the production query from `_pcc_blocked_attention`, fed one capability release in the shape `_pcc_issue_comments` returns (an array of pages):

```bash
printf '%s' '[[{"id":10,"body":"Terminal blocker: reason=runner_capability_unmet owner=runner-recovery"}]]' |
  jq -e --argjson id 10 --arg line 'Terminal blocker: reason=runner_capability_unmet ' \
  'any(.[]; .id == $id and ((.body // "") | split("\n") | any(startswith($line))))'
```

**Actual output:**

```text
jq: error (at <stdin>:0): Cannot index array with string ("id")
```

jq exits 5. The `if` treats that as false, so the brief-owner variant is posted.

**Expected output:** `true`. The same input prints `true` with `flatten[]` in place of `.[]`.

## How

1. `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`, `_pcc_blocked_attention`: iterate `flatten[]`, matching the rest of the helper.
2. `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`, `test_capability_checkpoint_attention`: make the `_pcc_issue_comments` stub return the production shape (an array of pages). With that fixture, unmodified `main` fails the test.

## Acceptance

- `test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` passes with the paginated fixture and fails on unmodified `main`.
- `test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` passes under jq 1.7.1 and jq 1.8.2 with no `Cannot index array` errors on stderr.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`

title: dispatch-stage-instrument: report ignores its window, never trims, and cannot finish on real logs (strands #35605)
body:
## What

`dispatch-stage-instrument.sh report [window_s]` must finish in seconds on real logs and report only the requested window. The stage log must stay bounded, and an interrupted report must not leave a copy of the log behind.

## Why (observed evidence, maintainer runner, 2026-10-29)

- `~/.aidevops/logs/dispatch-stages.tsv` is 200 MB, 1,888,848 lines, covering 2026-04-29 to 2026-10-29. `_ds_trim_log` exists, but no production path calls it; only the manual `trim` subcommand does. `gh_trim_log` runs every pulse cycle from `pulse-wrapper-cycle-gates.sh`; the stage log has no equivalent.
- `report 86400` timed out at 60 s. `report 604800` was killed at a 300 s operation budget with no output.
- `_ds_report` copies the log line by line through a Bash `while read` loop into `mktemp "${DS_LOG}.report.XXXXXX"`. `dispatch-stage-aggregate.awk` then keeps every sample and insertion-sorts each stage (O(n²)). The awk ignores `cutoff` ("currently unused"), so the documented "last 24h" report is all-time data.
- Killed reports have no cleanup path. Six orphaned `dispatch-stages.tsv.report.*` copies, about 748 MB in total, remain in `~/.aidevops/logs/`; two are from today's timed-out runs.
- One `awk` pass over the same 200 MB file takes 4.2 s.
- Impact: the #35605 brief makes `report 86400` its precondition. The command cannot finish on the host that has the data, and on other runners it counts all-time records. #35605 has been `status:blocked` (`external_trigger_pending`) since 2026-10-25, although this runner holds 60 `precreate.helper_add` records from the last 24 h (278 in 7 days).
- `stats-health-dashboard-data.sh` `_dashboard_latest_match` also reads the whole file line by line in Bash on every dashboard run. A bounded log fixes that cost too.

## Reproducer

1. On a runner whose `dispatch-stages.tsv` has months of records, run `time ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dispatch-stage-instrument.sh report 86400`. It runs for minutes, and a killed run leaves `dispatch-stages.tsv.report.*` behind.
2. With a small synthetic log that has one record dated 30 days ago and one dated now, `report 3600` counts both rows (`n=2`), because the window is ignored.
3. `rg -n "_ds_trim_log" .agents/scripts` shows only the definition and the manual `trim` subcommand. Nothing bounds the log.

## How

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/dispatch-stage-instrument.sh`
  - `_ds_report`: in one awk pass, filter to the window (ISO-8601 UTC string comparison) and skip `start` rows. Then `LC_ALL=C sort` by stage and elapsed time. No temp copy of the log.
  - `_ds_trim_log`: keep the `tail` line cap and write to a `${DS_LOG}.trim.*` temp file. Remove stale `${DS_LOG}.report.*` / `${DS_LOG}.trim.*` files older than 60 minutes.
  - Default `AIDEVOPS_DISPATCH_STAGES_LOG_MAX_LINES` to 200000 (about 16 days at the observed ~12.5k lines/day), so 7-day reports keep their data.
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/dispatch-stage-aggregate.awk`: compute percentiles from the pre-sorted stream in O(n) and print stage rows in sorted order.
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle-gates.sh`: call `_ds_trim_log` next to `gh_trim_log` at cycle finish.
- EDIT `.agents/reference/dispatch-timing.md`: document the window, the automatic trim and the new default.

## Verification

- `shellcheck` on the changed scripts.
- On a copy of the 1.9M-line log, `time dispatch-stage-instrument.sh report 86400` finishes in seconds. Its `precreate.helper_add` n matches an independent awk count for the same window.
- `trim` on a copy reduces the file to the line cap, removes stale temp files, and leaves recording working.
- Existing tests that source the instrument still pass: `test-prelaunch-publication-reserve.sh`, `test-stats-worker-zero-diagnostics.sh`, `test-pulse-current-state-helper.sh`.

title: t18787: Feedback routes close worker PRs while the worker dispatch lease is still live
body:
## Task


Feedback routes (review and CI) close a worker PR without checking whether the linked issue still has a live headless worker lease. If that worker pushes during the close, the route sees head drift, reopens the PR, applies `AUTOMATION_HOLD_PROVENANCE` plus `hold-for-review` to both the issue and the PR, and nothing owns them afterwards.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Feedback routes (review and CI) close a worker PR without checking whether the linked issue still has a live headless worker lease. If that worker pushes during the close, the route sees head drift, reopens the PR, applies `AUTOMATION_HOLD_PROVENANCE` plus `hold-for-review` to both the issue and the PR, and nothing owns them afterwards.

## Why (evidence)

- #35824 / PR #35835 (2026-10-28): worker attempt `attempt:eb8097e5…` held a `DISPATCH_LEASE phase=ready` lease from 14:04 until its terminal lease at 15:04:36 UTC. At 14:58 the review route closed the PR expecting head `d75bd23a`, but the live worker had already pushed `108d31ab`. The route logged `review route head changed during close`, reopened the PR and applied `hold-for-review`. It has been stuck since then: the issue shows `status:available` + `hold-for-review` and the PR is blocked.
- Labels are not a liveness signal. The worker moved the issue to `status:available` at 14:57 while its lease was still live.
- `_feedback_route_owner_allows` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback-finalizer.sh`, around line 38) fences interactive claims only. The comment above it already requires re-reading ownership at each destructive boundary, but a live headless worker lease is not checked.
- #35884 (GH#35867) stopped bot-only change requests from starting this route. Trusted human change requests and the CI route still close through the same `_feedback_route_close_and_finish` path.

## How

1. In `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback-finalizer.sh`, add `_feedback_route_worker_lease_allows <issue> <repo>`. It runs `dispatch-claim-helper.sh check <issue> <repo>` (same directory as the finalizer) and allows the route only on exit 1 (no active claim or lease). Exit 0 (active claim, prelaunch or ready lease) and any other exit (unreadable) defer.
2. In `_feedback_route_close_and_finish`, call it right after `_feedback_route_owner_allows` and before `_feedback_route_gh_write pr close`. On failure, return `$PULSE_FEEDBACK_ROUTE_DEFERRED_RC`. The route then re-evaluates on a later cycle, after the worker's terminal lease or lease expiry.
3. Reference pattern: `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` `check-claim`, which invokes `"$CLAIM_HELPER" check` and treats exit 0 as an active claim.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback-finalizer.sh`

## Verification

- Existing suites still pass: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-ci-repair-routing.sh`, `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-fix-worker-dispatch.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-integration-recovery.sh`.
- `shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback-finalizer.sh` reports zero violations.
- Reasoning check against the #35835 timeline: at 14:58 `dispatch-claim-helper.sh check 35824 marcusquinn/aidevops` would have returned 0 (ready lease, unexpired), so the route defers instead of closing.

</details>

title: aidevops update npm-installs Claude Code over a Homebrew claude-code cask (EEXIST, permanent false update)
body:
## Problem

`aidevops update` → "Maintaining Key Tools" always updates Claude Code CLI with
`npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest`, even when the `claude` binary is
owned by the Homebrew `claude-code` cask. npm correctly refuses to overwrite the
cask's symlink, so the maintenance step fails on every run:

```
npm error code EEXIST
npm error path /opt/homebrew/bin/claude
npm error File exists: /opt/homebrew/bin/claude
npm error Remove the existing file and try again, or run npm
npm error with --force to overwrite files recklessly.
Tool maintenance failed: 1 action(s) did not complete or verify.
```

Observed state (macOS arm64, Homebrew prefix `/opt/homebrew`, aidevops v3.39.84):

- `/opt/homebrew/bin/claude -> /opt/homebrew/Caskroom/claude-code/2.1.308/claude`
- `brew update && brew upgrade --cask claude-code` → "latest version is already installed" (cask stable channel 2.1.308)
- npm registry `latest` = 2.1.312, so the checker reports `2.1.308 → 2.1.312 (UPDATE AVAILABLE)` indefinitely

The version comparison and the upgrade route both assume npm ownership, so a
Homebrew-cask user gets a permanent false "update available" plus a failing
npm install. The only workaround is uninstalling the cask and switching to npm.

Same class of bug as the OpenCode fixes in #24107 and #34181, but for Claude Code,
and for a Homebrew **cask** rather than a formula.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/tool-version-check.sh:200` — the hard-coded
  `"npm|Claude Code CLI|claude|--version|@anthropic-ai/claude-code|npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest"` spec.
- `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh` — add a Claude Code owner probe alongside
  `aidevops_opencode_owner_payload` / `aidevops_opencode_install_owner` (~lines 280-349),
  or generalise that probe to take a package/cask name.

## Reference pattern

Follow the OpenCode handling in `tool-version-check.sh:72-110` and
`shared-constants.sh:aidevops_opencode_upgrade_command`:

1. Resolve the `claude` binary and its symlink target.
2. If the target is under `$(brew --prefix)/Caskroom/claude-code` (or
   `claude-code@latest`), treat the owner as `brew` (cask): compare against
   `brew info --cask --json=v2 <cask>` `.version`, and upgrade with
   `brew upgrade --cask <cask>`.
3. Otherwise keep the existing npm path. Consider also skipping the native installer
   case (`~/.local/bin/claude`, self-updating) rather than npm-installing over it.

Note the cask check differs from the formula check: use `brew list --cask --versions`
and the Caskroom path, not `brew --prefix <formula>`.

## Verification

- With the `claude-code` cask installed: `tool-version-check.sh --category brew`
  lists Claude Code against the cask version; no npm install is attempted;
  `aidevops update` tool maintenance exits clean when the cask is current.
- With an npm global install: behaviour unchanged (npm version compare + npm install).
- ShellCheck clean on both scripts.

body:
**Task ID:** `t18788` | **Status:** open
**Assignee:** @marcusquinn | **Started:** 2026-10-29
**Tags:** `bug` `interactive`

## Outcome

Pulse-merge regression suites drift unseen: repair harnesses and run them in Framework Validation

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->
<!-- SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 Marcus Quinn -->


## What

Pulse-merge regression suites drift silently because CI runs only 3 of the 49 `test-pulse-merge-*.sh` suites. Repair the drifted harnesses and make Framework Validation run every pulse-merge suite whenever pulse-merge sources or their tests change, so a change that breaks a suite cannot merge unseen.

## Why (evidence)

- `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml` Framework Validation (a required check) runs only `test-pulse-merge-approve-collaborator-guard.sh`, `-ruleset-fallback.sh` and `-phantom-pending-checks.sh`.
- On `origin/main` `d47f778316` (2026-10-29), seven suites fail or abort. Each failure is harness drift from a merged production change, not a reported behaviour regression:
  - `test-pulse-merge-ci-repair-routing.sh` aborts after 13 of 79 cases (`_PULSE_MERGE_DIR: unbound variable`) and `test-pulse-merge-review-thread-remediation.sh` fails 14 of 27 (`_review_feedback_active_change_requests: command not found`). Cause: GH#35867 / PR #35884 review-gate dependencies. The ci-repair-routing harness is repaired in PR #35941 (t18787); this task covers the rest.
  - `test-pulse-merge-stuck-auto.sh` fails 8 of 8 (every case returns 2): the fixture lacks `.head.ref` / `.labels` for the protected-release identity read added by GH#35798 / PR #35861 in `_set_native_auto_merge_or_skip`. The t3192 stuck native auto-merge fallback ("PRs that never merge") is therefore unguarded.
  - `test-pulse-merge-rest-readiness.sh` aborts (`_PMP_CHECK_FAILURE: unbound variable`).
  - `test-pulse-merge-pr-json-fields.sh` fails 1 of 6 (merge-ready list failure fallback).
  - `test-pulse-merge-first-nonblocking.sh` fails its static ordering check: `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` now calls `_preflight_early_dispatch` through `_pulse_run_budget_priority_stage`, so the line-anchored grep no longer matches.
  - `test-pulse-merge-superseded-duplicates.sh` exits 1 without a FAIL line: GH#30610 made `_psh_find_merged_closer_for_closed_issue` call `_psh_gh_read`, which the harness never extracted; production's `2>/dev/null` hid the missing-function error.
  - In `test-pulse-merge-review-thread-remediation.sh`, the external-contributor case still expected the close-and-redispatch route that GH#35867 removed on purpose (`#aidevops:trust-boundary`: external-contributor PRs are held, never routed).
- Merge and routing defects then reach production and surface as stranded issues, comment loops and unmerged PRs (for example #35824 / PR #35835).

## How

1. Repair each drifted harness to match current production contracts. Never weaken an assertion to fit a behaviour change: if a failure turns out to be a production regression, fix production or report it with evidence.
2. Add a Framework Validation step in `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml` that runs every `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-*.sh` and `*.py` suite (a glob, so new suites are covered automatically; `*-cases.sh` / `*-mocks.sh` are sourced fixtures). It runs whenever Framework Validation runs: the suites also read `.agents/configs/`, so narrower path scoping would reopen the gap. Suites run in parallel (`nproc`) with a private `HOME`/`TMPDIR` each and a per-suite timeout; failures print the suite log in a group and fail the job. Reference pattern: the existing "Approve Collaborator Author Guard" step.

### Files Scope

- `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-review-thread-remediation.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-stuck-auto.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-rest-readiness.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-pr-json-fields.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-first-nonblocking.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-superseded-duplicates.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every `test-pulse-merge-*` suite exits 0 on the branch, on macOS locally and on the CI Ubuntu runner.
- Framework Validation runs the full pulse-merge suite set and fails when any suite fails.
- No production behaviour changes unless a confirmed regression is fixed and named in the PR.

title: t18789: Pulse blocker_recovery trigger drops partial pending counts, so terminal-blocker recovery never wakes the AI owner
body:
## Task


Fix the Pulse `blocker_recovery` supervisor trigger. It drops the partial count from `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh pending --count` whenever the helper exits 2, so terminal-blocker recovery never wakes the AI owner by itself.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Fix the Pulse `blocker_recovery` supervisor trigger. It drops the partial count from `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh pending --count` whenever the helper exits 2, so terminal-blocker recovery never wakes the AI owner by itself.

## Why (evidence)

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` `_pulse_blocker_recovery_due` runs `pending=$(bash "$helper" pending --count 2>/dev/null) || pending=0`. Any non-zero exit replaces the printed count with 0.
- The helper's documented contract is different. `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh` says: "Incomplete observations return 2 and a diagnostic on stderr; stdout remains JSONL (or a partial count)". `tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` `test_bounded_recovery_intake` asserts `rc -eq 2` with the count on stdout.
- On a fleet runner, exit 2 happens on every call. `tbr_seed` writes `last_seed_epoch` only after one bounded call has scanned every pulse repo. That scan is a policy load, two Search API calls and comment reads per repo, all inside the 8s `BLOCKER_RECOVERY_STAGE_SECONDS` cap. This runner has 67 pulse repos, so the scan never finishes. The 134 search calls alone exceed the 30/min Search limit.
- Live runner state, 2026-10-29:
  - `last_seed_epoch` is `1792523886` (2026-10-20T20:26Z), but `seed_repo_cursor` and `pending_cursor` were rewritten at 13:47Z. `pending` keeps running and keeps returning 2.
  - `last_blocker_recovery_check_epoch` shows the 3h check still runs (latest 10:16Z).
  - The queue holds 25 entries, several with decisions older than the 24h TTL.
  - Yet `pulse.log` (from 2026-10-25) and `pulse-wrapper.log` contain zero `terminal-blocker recovery entr` trigger lines.
  - Only unrelated `backlog stalled` runs reach the recovery directive, so circuit-held issues wait for a coincidental stall.

## How

- In `_pulse_blocker_recovery_due`, capture the helper exit code separately. Accept the numeric stdout count for exit 0 (complete) and exit 2 (incomplete but partial). Treat any other exit, or non-numeric output, as 0.
- Keep the interval stamp, the `_pulse_llm_failure_cooldown_active` gate and the trigger-mode write unchanged.
- Log the partial case, so an incomplete scan that still found work can be attributed later.
- Do not change helper semantics. `tbr_seed` deliberately keeps a timed-out scan incomplete. Durable cross-call sweep completion is a separate design question.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- A helper that prints `3` and exits 2 makes `_pulse_blocker_recovery_due` write trigger mode `blocker_recovery` and return 0.
- A helper that prints `0` and exits 2, prints nothing, or exits 1 returns 1 without writing a trigger mode.
- The interval and failure-cooldown behaviour are unchanged.

## Verification

- Run `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`.
- Run a bounded harness that sources the function with stub helpers covering the exit 0, exit 2 (count 0 and >0) and exit 1 cases.
- Run the existing `tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` and the pulse dispatch-engine suites that source this file.

title: cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh: approval issue body keeps literal <this-issue-number> placeholder in the maintainer approve command
body:
## Problem

`cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh request <repo> <pr>` creates release-approval issues whose body tells the maintainer to run:

```
sudo aidevops approve issue <this-issue-number> <owner/repo>
```

The literal `<this-issue-number>` placeholder stays in the published issue (observed on a managed Cloudron app's v0.2.8 approval issue). The maintainer has to work out and type the number, and the copy-paste command is wrong as published. The `request` stdout also prints only the issue URL, so agents relay a link rather than the ready command.

## Cause

`.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh` `release_request()` (around line 137) renders the whole body with `printf`, including `Maintainer command: \`sudo aidevops approve issue <this-issue-number> %s\``, before `gh_create_issue` returns the number. Nothing fills in the number afterwards.

## Fix

1. After `gh_create_issue` returns `$url`, extract the number (`${url##*/}`, validate it is numeric) and rewrite the body so the command contains the real number. Do this immediately, before the URL is printed or any approval can be signed: approval signatures bind the body digest, so the edit must happen first. Use the existing safe issue-edit wrapper with `--body-file`, not raw `gh issue edit`. If the body is rendered in a function, reuse it with the number filled in rather than doing a string replace on the live body.
2. Print the ready command on stdout after the URL, e.g. a `APPROVAL_COMMAND=sudo aidevops approve issue N owner/repo` line, so callers and agents can show it verbatim in chat.
3. Check the related agent guidance (Cloudron release workflow / `workflows/release.md` Cloudron approval section): when an agent requests approval, the completion message should give the exact command in chat with the real issue number and repo, not only a link.
4. `post-merge-review-scanner.sh:612` and `auto-decomposer-scanner.sh:486` use `Resolves #<this-issue-number>` in generated issue bodies. Fill those in the same way if they are meant to be copied verbatim.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh` is clean.
- Run `request` against a test PR, or exercise the body render with the number. The created issue body contains `sudo aidevops approve issue <N> <owner/repo>` with the real `N`, and stdout includes the `APPROVAL_COMMAND=` line.
- `approval-helper.sh verify issue <N> <repo>` and `cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh process --apply` still verify a signature made after the body edit (digest bound to the final body).
- `rg -n 'this-issue-number' .agents/scripts/` shows no remaining user-facing placeholders, or only intentionally documented ones.
### Files Scope
- `.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-release-approval.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/post-merge-review-scanner.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/auto-decomposer-scanner.sh`

title: t18790: Task-ID Collision Guard CI turns its full-history clone shallow, so claimed task IDs older than 100 claims fail as unclaimed
body:
## Task


Stop the Task-ID Collision Guard CI job from rejecting task IDs that were properly claimed. The workflow re-fetches `main`, `develop` and `task-id-counter` with `--depth=100` after a full-history checkout. That turns the clone shallow and hides every `chore: claim` commit older than the last 100 counter commits, so the guard reports real, claimed IDs as unclaimed.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Stop the Task-ID Collision Guard CI job from rejecting task IDs that were properly claimed. The workflow re-fetches `main`, `develop` and `task-id-counter` with `--depth=100` after a full-history checkout. That turns the clone shallow and hides every `chore: claim` commit older than the last 100 counter commits, so the guard reports real, claimed IDs as unclaimed.

## Why (evidence)

- PR #35946, run 40891580553: `t18514 — ≤ counter 18790, but no 'chore: claim t18514' commit on this branch, in repo history, or linked issue title`. The claim commit `f02a3fd9d9 chore: claim t18514` exists on `origin/task-id-counter`, 274 commits behind its tip. The local commit-msg hook, which has full history, accepted the same commit.
- PR for GH#33881, runs 37644437253 (PR) and 37645805307 (push to main): t18403, t18405 and t18407 were rejected the same way. Their range claim `6a7b535014` exists, about 208 claims before the counter value at the time (18611).
- `.github/workflows/task-id-collision-check.yml` checks out with `fetch-depth: 0` ("Full history needed"), then runs `git fetch origin main --depth=100`, `git fetch origin develop --depth=100` and `git fetch origin '+refs/heads/task-id-counter:...' --depth=100`. A depth-limited fetch into a complete clone writes `.git/shallow`. History walks then stop at the boundary for every ref that passes through it. Local reproduction: a full clone showed 7 commits on a counter branch with the old claim visible; after `git fetch --depth=3` of that branch it reported `shallow=true`, 3 commits, and the claim was gone.
- The guard's cross-reference rule (`_repo_has_claim`, added for #20291) depends on `git log --all`. In CI it can see only the last ~100 claims.
- The `--depth=100` lines came in with the original guard (main/develop) and with t18225 (the counter branch, 2026-08-10). Every PR or main push that mentions an older claimed task fails this check.
- Impact: the check is not branch-required, but the Pulse pre-merge snapshot treats an unclassified non-required terminal failure as a merge blocker (`pulse-merge-required-checks.sh`, "unclassified non-required check ... merge blocked (GH#27137)"). Red checks on PRs that cite earlier tasks also invite repair churn and manual merges.

## How

1. `.github/workflows/task-id-collision-check.yml`: remove `--depth=100` from the three fetches, and add a comment saying why depth must never be limited here. Checkout `fetch-depth: 0` already fetched full history for every branch, so these fetches only refresh refs.
2. `.agents/hooks/task-id-collision-guard.sh` `_check_tid`: a task ID that is at or below the counter, with no visible claim commit and no linked-issue proof, still blocks in a full-history repository. When `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` is `true`, the missing claim cannot be proven, so warn with an actionable message and do not block for that ID. Other IDs in the same message are still checked. This prevents a recurrence from any future shallow checkout. IDs above the counter keep their current behaviour.

## Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.github/workflows/task-id-collision-check.yml` — "Fetch comparison and task counter branches" step.
- EDIT: `.agents/hooks/task-id-collision-guard.sh` — `_check_tid` at-or-below-counter branch, plus a small shallow-history helper.

## Files Scope

- .github/workflows/task-id-collision-check.yml
- .agents/hooks/task-id-collision-guard.sh

## Acceptance Criteria

- The CI guard passes on a PR whose commit body cites an old, properly claimed task ID such as t18514.
- A task ID at or below the counter with no claim anywhere in full history still fails.
- A shallow clone produces a `[task-id-guard][WARN]` for a missing claim instead of a block.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/hooks/task-id-collision-guard.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-task-id-collision-guard.sh`
- The fix PR's own Task-ID Collision Guard run passes with a commit body that cites t18514.
- An ad-hoc local reproduction of full and shallow clones shows: full history plus an old claim passes; full history plus a never-claimed ID blocks; shallow history plus a hidden claim warns and passes.

title: t18791: Interactive claim refresh fails when the stamp worktree branch has an open PR for a different issue
body:
## Task


`interactive-start-helper.sh --issue N` aborts with `ERROR: initial interactive claim failed` when the issue's claim stamp points at a worktree whose branch already has an open PR for a different issue. The claim refresh treats that unrelated PR as the issue's own PR, finds no `status:in-review` on the issue, and fails closed. Make PR normalization skip PRs that do not close the claimed issue.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`interactive-start-helper.sh --issue N` aborts with `ERROR: initial interactive claim failed` when the issue's claim stamp points at a worktree whose branch already has an open PR for a different issue. The claim refresh treats that unrelated PR as the issue's own PR, finds no `status:in-review` on the issue, and fails closed. Make PR normalization skip PRs that do not close the claimed issue.

## Why (evidence)

- 2026-10-29: `claim-task-id.sh` created #35949 from the linked worktree of GH#35945. Its auto-claim (`claim-task-id-issue.sh` `_interactive_session_auto_claim`, `"$helper" claim "$issue_num" "$slug" --worktree "$repo_path" ... || true`) wrote the #35949 stamp with that worktree. Its open PR, #35946, closes #35945.
- `interactive-start-helper.sh --issue 35949 ...` then failed. A `bash -x` trace of `interactive-session-helper.sh claim 35949 marcusquinn/aidevops --implementing --defer-comment` shows ownership class `own`. `_isc_refresh_existing_claim` falls back to the stamp's worktree. `_isc_normalize_owned_pr` lists the branch's open PRs (`[#35946]`), finds no `status:in-review` on #35949, and returns 1, so the claim exits 1. The stamp had already been rewritten, so failing closed protected nothing and only blocked the start.
- The workaround was the helper's own later steps: `pre-edit-check.sh --loop-mode --issue 35949`, `claim --worktree <new>`, then `full-loop-helper.sh start`. With the fresh worktree the claim succeeded because its branch had no PR.
- This is a sibling of #31500 (closed), which added the zero-PR early return. The same function still fails closed on any non-empty PR list, including PRs for other issues. The same path also blocks parent-task PRs that use `For #N` and have no closing reference.

## How

`.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh` `_isc_normalize_owned_pr`: once `prs` is fetched, keep only PRs whose `closingIssuesReferences` include `$issue`. If none remain, return 0, because there is no owned PR to normalize. Leave the rest unchanged and run it on the filtered set: `status:in-review` required, exactly one PR, same repository, closing references exactly `[$issue]`, unchanged metadata re-read, then the label edit. PRs that do not reference the issue are never edited.

## Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh` — `_isc_normalize_owned_pr`.

## Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh

## Acceptance Criteria

- A claim refresh whose stamp or supplied worktree branch has only PRs for other issues exits 0 and edits no PR.
- Takeover normalization of a PR that closes exactly the claimed issue still relabels it `origin:interactive`.
- A PR that closes the claimed issue still fails closed when the issue lacks `status:in-review`, the PR is cross-repository, or the PR closes additional issues.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-integration-recovery.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-interactive-session-claim.sh`
- Ad-hoc: source the helper with stubbed `gh`/metadata. An unrelated-PR fixture returns 0 with no `pr edit`; a matching-PR fixture performs one `pr edit`.

title: t18792: fix(pulse): let capable runners continue capability-released worker drafts
body:
## Task


A worker draft checkpoint released with `runner_capability_unmet` must be continued by a runner that has the missing capability. Two defects in the exact-head continuation path stop this. As a result, finished drafts sit indefinitely while Pulse re-evaluates them every cycle.

1. **Cross-runner stall count.** `_pcc_stall_release_evidence` counts every trusted capability release since the draft head toward the per-head retry bound (`stalls >= 2` → attention, no further continuation). The count ignores which runner posted the release. Releases from runners that lack the tool therefore use up the retry budget of runners that have it. GH#34758 classifies a capability release as runner-local, and GH#35788's fleet circuit already requires two *different* runners. The stall bound is the only place that ignores runner locality.
2. **`origin:interactive` treated as a hold despite `auto-dispatch`.** `_pr_checkpoint_issue_metadata_is_eligible` marks `origin:interactive` as `protected` unless the newest release is `worker_draft_checkpoint`. A released (unassigned, `status:available`) issue that carries `auto-dispatch` was explicitly delegated. Ordinary dispatch (`_dispatch_has_interactive_hold`, `pulse-dispatch-core.sh`) never holds such an issue, so the continuation path is stricter than the dispatch it continues.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

A worker draft checkpoint released with `runner_capability_unmet` must be continued by a runner that has the missing capability. Two defects in the exact-head continuation path stop this. As a result, finished drafts sit indefinitely while Pulse re-evaluates them every cycle.

1. **Cross-runner stall count.** `_pcc_stall_release_evidence` counts every trusted capability release since the draft head toward the per-head retry bound (`stalls >= 2` → attention, no further continuation). The count ignores which runner posted the release. Releases from runners that lack the tool therefore use up the retry budget of runners that have it. GH#34758 classifies a capability release as runner-local, and GH#35788's fleet circuit already requires two *different* runners. The stall bound is the only place that ignores runner locality.
2. **`origin:interactive` treated as a hold despite `auto-dispatch`.** `_pr_checkpoint_issue_metadata_is_eligible` marks `origin:interactive` as `protected` unless the newest release is `worker_draft_checkpoint`. A released (unassigned, `status:available`) issue that carries `auto-dispatch` was explicitly delegated. Ordinary dispatch (`_dispatch_has_interactive_hold`, `pulse-dispatch-core.sh`) never holds such an issue, so the continuation path is stricter than the dispatch it continues.

## Why (evidence)

- #35592 → draft PR #35598 (head `7d006ea`, required checks green, `MERGEABLE`, worker `MERGE_SUMMARY` posted 2026-10-25T01:39Z). Three `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked` releases, all from the same runner, each with `Terminal blocker: reason=runner_capability_unmet`. The brief requires `php -l` and a LocalWP differential test. `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION ... stalls=2` was posted at 02:59Z. Since then every Pulse cycle on a runner that has PHP 8.5, wp-cli and LocalWP logs `WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT` → `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION_EXISTS` → `routed stall-released worker draft PR #35598 (GH#33654)` → `DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=dedup_active_claim`. Each pass costs 12–296 s, and no worker launches.
- #35600 → draft PR #35603 (head `b9513c3`, no failing checks, `MERGEABLE`): the same pattern, with capability releases from two runners that lack the tool and none from the capable runner.
- Both issues are `origin:interactive` + `auto-dispatch`, so fixing (1) alone still ends in `PR_CHECKPOINT_TARGET_REJECTED: reason=issue_metadata_ineligible`.
- History: this path has had 10 targeted fixes (GH#33132, GH#33654, GH#34008, GH#34758, GH#35174, GH#35363, GH#35622, GH#35683, GH#35715, GH#35788). Neither predicate was made runner- or delegation-aware.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`:
  - `_pcc_stall_release_evidence`: accept an optional authenticated-login argument. Count a capability release toward `stalls` only when that login posted it. Count non-capability stall releases for every runner, as now. The newest-ownership-event requirement and the attention dedup key are unchanged. When no login is supplied, keep the old behaviour so other callers do not change.
  - `_pcc_dispatch_stalled`: pass `$login`.
- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh` `_pr_checkpoint_issue_metadata_is_eligible`: do not treat `origin:interactive` as protected when `allow_released` is true, the issue carries `auto-dispatch` and the issue has no assignees. This mirrors `_dispatch_has_interactive_hold`. Every other protected label still blocks (`hold-for-review`, `no-auto-dispatch`, `needs-maintainer-review`, `blocked`, …). Assigned and non-released paths are unchanged.

## Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` — `_pcc_stall_release_evidence`, `_pcc_dispatch_stalled`.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh` — `_pr_checkpoint_issue_metadata_is_eligible`.

## Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh

## Acceptance Criteria

- Capability releases posted only by other runners leave `stalls=0` for the authenticated runner, and `dispatch-stalled` reaches `_pcc_dispatch`.
- A capability release from the authenticated runner still counts. Two such releases still post or deduplicate `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION` without dispatching.
- Non-capability stall releases (`no_activity`, `stale_assignment_reset`, `worker_ownership_lost`, …) still count for every runner. Existing stall-bound tests pass unchanged.
- A released `origin:interactive` + `auto-dispatch` issue with no assignees is eligible for the released continuation path. Without `auto-dispatch`, with assignees, or with any other protected label it remains ineligible.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh`
- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-revision.py` and `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-private-member.py`

</details>

title: gh_create_issue: derived status:available label blocks issue creation on external repos without label permission
body:
## Observed

`gh-write-helper.sh issue create --repo <external-owner>/<repo> ...` fails on an external (non-managed) public repo where the session user is a contributor without label permission:

```
gh_create_issue: could not verify or provision canonical status:* labels on <repo> (label-create permission or API failure); creation fails if derived status:available is absent — create the standard status labels or pass an existing status:* label
could not add label: 'status:available' not found
[aidevops][gh-write-helper][ERROR] GitHub write failed (exit 1).
```

No issue is created. The same wrapper created issues on that repo earlier the same day (v3.39.80, no labels applied), so this regressed with the GH#34003 derived-status-label path.

## Cause

`shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh` `_gh_ci_prepare_status_label` always appends `--label status:available` when no `status:*` label is passed. `_gh_ci_ensure_derived_status_label` is best-effort and only warns when provisioning fails, but `gh issue create` then rejects the whole request because the label doesn't exist. The caller can't pass an existing `status:*` label either, because the external repo has none.

## Expected

On repos where labels can't be provisioned (external contributions, no triage permission), the wrapper drops lifecycle labels it derived itself and creates the issue with the body and signature only. The workflow rules for external non-maintainer repos already say no claim/dispatch/label routines.

## Suggested fix

In `gh_create_issue`, if `_gh_ci_ensure_derived_status_label` can't verify that `status:available` exists on the target repo, clear `_GH_CI_STATUS_LABEL_ARGS` before building `_issue_cmd` and `_rest_args`. Apply the same check to the injected origin label. Caller-supplied labels stay unchanged and still fail loudly.

## Verification

Create an issue through `gh-write-helper.sh issue create` on a repo where the user has read access only: it succeeds with no labels and with the signature footer. On a managed repo, `status:available` is still applied.

Workaround used: `gh-signature-helper.sh footer` appended to the body file, then plain `gh issue create --body-file`.

title: Playwriter Task-child handoff still races a ~37s relay window and fails closed on stale auto-reattached tabs
body:
## Description

The Playwriter selected-tab handoff still fails when `@playwriter` runs as a Task child. GH#35516 asked for a handoff that does not "require the user to race a brief subagent's start/disconnect window". It was closed by PR #35608, which changed docs only (handoff order plus a pin test). The race is still there, and a second failure mode now shows up on top of it.

## Observed (2026-10-29, OpenCode 1.19.5, aidevops 3.39.84, playwriter 0.9.0)

The parent delegated a read-only inspection to `subagent_type: playwriter`. Child session timeline from the session export:

1. `aidevops_mcp connect playwriter`: success.
2. `playwriter_execute`: `context.pages().length` returned `1`, and that page did not match the target origin.
3. The child classified this as "unmatched non-blank approved tab" (preflight step 5) and failed closed.
4. It ran `mcp-diagnose.sh playwriter`: `extension-connected`.
5. `aidevops_mcp disconnect playwriter`. The relay stopped.

The whole child run took about **37 seconds**. It never waited for a user click.

The relay log (`~/.playwriter/relay-server.log`) shows where the one page came from:

- `Successfully re-attached tab: <id>` with `attachOrder: 74`. On reconnect, the extension automatically re-attached a tab the user had authorized in an **earlier, unrelated session** (a private webmail tab on another local app).
- The extension's `currentTabId` (the user's focused tab, which was the intended target) differed from the re-attached tab id.

From the operator's side:

- Before delegation, clicking the icon shows "Daemon not running yet" / "Waiting for MCP WS server..." because no relay exists yet.
- During delegation, the relay lives for about 37 s. The child cannot talk to the user, and the stale tab makes the preflight fail closed almost at once.
- After delegation the relay is gone again, so the next click goes back to "Daemon not running".

**Result:** with the Task path, the user has no reliable way to hand over the intended tab.

## Root causes

1. **Relay lifetime equals child task lifetime.** `aidevops_mcp connect/disconnect` and the guardian tie the relay to a child turn that runs unattended, has no user I/O, and is short.
2. **The preflight has no bounded wait for a new attachment.** `tools/browser/playwriter.md` "Authenticated Relay and Tab Preflight" steps 3 and 5 treat "pages present, none matching" as terminal. "Keep polling" is documented only for the zero-page case.
3. **A stale auto-re-attached tab is not a distinct state.** The extension's re-attachment of previously authorized tabs is misclassified as the user's current approval. It is also a privacy hazard: a private tab from another session becomes visible to the new session.
4. **Parent-supplied URLs act as an exact-prefix allow-list.** A user's fresh click on the intended tab (consent) gets no consideration if its URL differs (for example `www.`, a dev server, or a path variant).

## Expected Behavior

- A Task-delegated `@playwriter` child waits a bounded window (suggested 120 s) for a **new** attachment that matches the approved origin, polling `context.pages()` without inspecting non-matching pages beyond URL classification.
- Tabs that were auto-re-attached at connect time (present at the first poll, from an earlier attach order) are classified as `stale-reattached` and are never treated as the target. The report says so explicitly and tells the user how to detach them (click the icon on that tab, or remove it from the `playwriter` tab group).
- The parent can tell the user, before the Task call, "click the Playwriter icon on <tab> once the relay starts". That instruction must then work inside the wait window.
- Optional, needs a security review: a parent-session-scoped relay with an idle TTL, so a click before or between delegations does not hit "Daemon not running". Keep the token, loopback and guardian guarantees.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/tools/browser/playwriter.md`: preflight steps 3 to 5 (bounded attachment wait, `stale-reattached` class, parent handoff instruction), plus the Troubleshooting entry for stale re-attach.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/agent-mcp-tools.mjs` and/or `mcp-registry.mjs`: where the Playwriter connect/disconnect lifecycle is scoped, if a session-scoped relay or idle TTL is adopted.
- `.agents/scripts/playwriter-relay-guardian.mjs`, `.agents/scripts/playwriter-authenticated-relay.mjs`: relay lifetime, only for the TTL option.
- `.agents/scripts/mcp-diagnose.sh`: optionally report the re-attached-at-connect tab count, plus whether the attached tab equals the extension's `currentTabId`, without printing URLs.
- Reference pattern: the existing `relay-up-no-extension` / `extension-connected` verdict classification in `mcp-diagnose.sh`, and the GH#35516 handoff-order section.

## Verification

1. Authorize an unrelated tab in one session, end the session, then start a new one and delegate a Task `@playwriter` child targeting a different, open tab.
2. The child reports `stale-reattached` for the old tab without reading its content. It waits; the user clicks the intended tab within the window; the child attaches, matches and completes.
3. No click within the window gives a classified timeout, not "unmatched non-blank".
4. Existing tests: `scripts/tests/test-playwriter-authenticated-relay.mjs`, `plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-playwriter-selection-guard.mjs`, `scripts/tests/test-playwriter-pin.sh`.

Ref #35516

title: macOS: worktree-helper.sh remove always fails (producer:evidence-unavailable): restore proof requires managed-lifetime enrollment that Darwin never creates
body:
## Summary

On macOS, `worktree-helper.sh remove` can't remove any clean worktree. Capture succeeds, but the git-only restoration proof always fails because the verification copy is never enrolled in `worktree_managed_lifetimes` on Darwin. The user sees only `producer:evidence-unavailable`, followed by `Cleanup stopped: the source remains protected and its recoverable archive was retained.`

Each attempt also leaves a registered, detached verification worktree under `~/.aidevops/recovery/archives/.producer-transactions/<id>/.restore-*/worktree`, with journal `canonical_restore.state: "restoring"`. A retry on the same source then stops with `restore-proof:unsealed-copy-retained; inspect owned scratch`. This machine has 38 such slots.

- Introduced by `39418e667` (GH#35305, "Verify archive recovery before source retirement"), first released in v3.39.56. Still present in v3.39.84 and current `main`.
- Environment: macOS 26.6.2, aidevops v3.39.84, OpenCode v1.19.5, Python 3.14.

## Reproduction

1. `worktree-helper.sh add chore/x --base origin/main` (a fresh, clean worktree).
2. `worktree-helper.sh remove <that path>` → `producer:evidence-unavailable`.

To see the hidden exception, call `worktree_recovery_producer.main()` for `capture` and then `verify`, without the `__main__` handler. `capture` succeeds in 8.8s. `verify` fails:

```text
worktree_recovery_producer.py:296 check -> RestorationProof(...)
worktree_archive_restore.py:183 __init__ -> command("restore", ..., "--registered-verification-copy")
worktree_recovery_migrate.py:43 archive_command -> CalledProcessError (worktree-archive-helper.sh restore, exit 1)
```

The verification worktree itself is created and owner-registered: owner row `(pid, "archive-verification:.restore-qc4x4jp6", "HEAD")`. However, `.creation.json` is never written. Replaying `creation_receipt`'s checks read-only against that slot gives:

```text
worktree-managed-lifetime.py:101 load -> NotEnrolled: worktree is not enrolled
```

## Root cause

- `.agents/scripts/worktree_lifetime_owner.py:283-292` `register()`: when `sys.platform == "darwin"` (or `AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_MANAGER=legacy-guards`), a newly created worktree is written to `worktree_creation_backends` as `backend: legacy-guards` and returns early. It is never enrolled in `worktree_managed_lifetimes`. The comment there calls this deliberate ("not a synthetic managed completion receipt").
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_restore.py:32-54` `creation_receipt()` calls `managed.load(connection, str(target))`, which requires that enrollment. The same assumption appears in `RestorationProof.__init__` (lines 207-222) and `cleanup()` (lines 263-271).

So on macOS the restore proof can never pass, and every guarded removal of a git-only worktree is refused.

## Secondary: the failure is not diagnosable

`NotEnrolled` is a `ValueError` subclass, but it is raised in a child process. The parent sees `CalledProcessError` with the child's stderr captured. `failure_reason()` (`worktree_recovery_producer.py:39-59`) only recognizes a final line starting with `ValueError: `, so `archive_managed_lifetime.NotEnrolled: …` collapses into the generic `producer:evidence-unavailable`. The removal-audit path also discards the child's stderr. A bounded, credential-free reason (for example `restore-proof:verification-copy-not-enrolled`) would have made this a one-line diagnosis.

## Suggested direction (maintainer's call: this is the restoration-proof trust model)

- Either let the restoration proof accept the Darwin/legacy-guards creation identity (`worktree_creation_backends` record plus owner row) for `archive-verification:*` copies,
- or have `register()` enroll `archive-verification:*` copies on Darwin under a dedicated manager the proof recognizes.

Either way, the macOS case needs coverage. The existing lifecycle tests (`.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py`, `tests/worktree_archive_canonical_cases.py`) appear to exercise only the Linux/managed path. CI runners are Linux, which would explain why this wasn't caught.

title: wp-plugin-new: aidevops init's .gitignore lines make a new plugin's core-files check fail against the starter
body:
## Observed

`wp-plugin-new-helper.sh create` runs `aidevops init code-quality` in the new plugin's identity worktree. Init appends an "aidevops runtime artifacts" block to `.gitignore` (`.agents/tmp/`, `.agents/memory/`, `.agents/commands`, `.windsurf/`, `.env*`, key files, `credentials.json`, `.aidevops.json`) and removes `.aidevops.json` from the index.

`.gitignore` is a WP Plugin Starter core file (`scripts/core-files.txt`) with no `{css}-own` block, so the plugin's first `scripts/preflight-release.sh` immediately warns:

`differs .gitignore changed here: no starter version has it; take the change to the starter first, or move plugin-only lines into ump-own blocks`

and `scripts/sync-core.sh` would later revert the lines (or refuse without `--discard-local`). Seen creating a private plugin from starter v1.0.46 on 2026-10-29. Older plugins from the same starter still track `.aidevops.json` and lack the block, so plugins now differ depending on creation date.

## Expected

A freshly created plugin passes preflight's core-files check, and init's ignore lines survive Starter sync.

## Fix options (pick one)

1. Add the aidevops runtime-artifact lines to the starter's `.gitignore` (wpallstars/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding), so every plugin gets them through sync-core; or
2. Give the starter's `.gitignore` an empty `# {css}-own:start` / `# {css}-own:end` block and have init write inside it when the repo has one.

## Files

- `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/wp-plugin-new-helper.sh` (create → init order)
- aidevops init's `.gitignore` writer (the "Added .agents/ runtime artifact ignores to .gitignore" step)
- Starter `.gitignore`, `scripts/core-files.txt`, `scripts/sync-core.sh` (own-block merge)

## Verification

Create a throwaway plugin with `wp-plugin-new-helper.sh create --local` (or dry run plus init in a scratch clone), then `scripts/preflight-release.sh --from <starter>`: the Core files section reports no `.gitignore` difference.

title: session-continuation-guard misses alternating tool-call loops
body:
## Problem

The session continuation guard doesn't detect a model that alternates between two
(or a few) tool calls. In an OpenCode headless run (`opencode run --agent SEO-GLM`,
local `studio-glm-5.3-flash`, 2026-10-29), the agent alternated between shell commands
about 360 times over 1,181 s and never produced output. The guard never fired.

## Reproducer

Deterministic, no model needed. Create the guard with `createSessionContinuationGuard`
(default threshold) and call `afterTool` for one session scope, alternating two failing
calls: `bash {command:"A"}`, `bash {command:"B"}`, and so on, 20 times. Expected: a
recovery correction after a few cycles. Actual: `replan` is never true, because each
call's fingerprint differs from the stored previous one, so `count` stays at 1. Swap
in a succeeding call between the failures and the state is deleted every time.

## Cause

`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-continuation-guard.mjs`, `afterTool`
(lines ~151-161):

- Only the last failure fingerprint is stored per scope:
  `previous?.fingerprint === fingerprint ? count + 1 : count = 1`. An A, B, A, B
  sequence resets the count to 1 on every call, so `threshold` is never reached.
- Any successful call runs `state.failures.delete(call.scope)`. A loop that mixes
  succeeding reads with failing commands is never counted.
- Failures are the only signal. A loop of individually successful but non-progressing
  calls isn't detected at all.

## Proposed fix

- Keep a bounded window per scope (for example, the last 20 fingerprints) instead of a
  single previous fingerprint. Trigger when a cycle of period 1-4 repeats at least
  `threshold` times, or when one fingerprint makes up most of the window, whether the
  calls succeed or fail.
- Don't clear the window on success. Clear it on evidence of progress, such as a
  successful edit or write, or a TodoWrite state change (`recordEdits` and the
  TodoWrite branch already see these).
- Keep the existing correction text and recovery checkpoint, and name the repeating
  cycle (the tool names only, with bounded text).

## Files

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-continuation-guard.mjs`: `afterTool`,
  failure state shape.
- Existing tests for this plugin: path not confirmed; locate them with
  `git ls-files '.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/*test*'`.

## Verification

- A test that feeds `afterTool` an A/B/A/B sequence of failures fires the guard by
  repetition N, where N is threshold multiplied by the period.
- Mixed success/failure alternation fires.
- Distinct progressing calls (for example, different file reads followed by an edit)
  don't fire.
- The existing identical-failure test still passes.

title: Pulse: scheduled routines deferred for 60+ minutes when REST-core quota is exhausted
body:
## Problem

Scheduled routines are classified as `deferrable` in the Pulse budget-priority gate, so when the REST-core quota is exhausted a due calendar slot is silently pushed until the quota window resets — and, if Pulse exhausts the next window too, further. On 2026-10-29 a 17:00 Europe/London routine slot (`cron(0 7,12,17 * * *)`) did not start until 18:19 UTC (~79 minutes late).

## Evidence (local logs, 2026-10-29)

- `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`: 82 lines of `budget-priority: deferred deferrable stage 'evaluate_routines' (... rest=emergency:0/5000@<reset-seconds> ...)`, across consecutive quota windows (e.g. reset in 58s, then 20s, later 154s/99s/57s/6s) — REST-core reached 0/5000 in more than one hour.
- GraphQL budget was healthy throughout (`graphql=normal:~4400-4500/5000`), so only REST-core blocked routines.
- `~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls-by-stage.json` (24h window): ~228k total calls; REST by consumer: `pulse` 92,099, `unknown` 32,900. Top REST callers: `gh_api_rest` 74,992, `_rest_issue_list` 11,237, `_rest_pr_list` 6,561, `_rest_pr_view` 5,902, `gh_issue_list` 4,449, `full-loop-helper.sh` 3,207. That is close to the full 120k/day REST-core allowance (5000/h).
- Once quota recovered the routine dispatched and completed normally (`handle_run_result ... result_label=success`, 18:35 UTC), so the routine itself is healthy.

## Root cause (hypothesis to verify)

1. `.agents/scripts/pulse-budget-priority.sh` `_pulse_stage_priority_class()` puts `evaluate_routines` in the `deferrable` class with cache priming, scanners, etc. A user-scheduled calendar slot is time-sensitive and the *evaluation* itself is cheap (state file + cron match, REST cost happens inside the routine worker).
2. Pulse background stages spend REST-core to zero each hour, leaving nothing for scheduled work.

## Proposed fix

- Evaluate due routines regardless of REST class (treat as `progress` or a new `scheduled` class): the cron match / state read needs no API; only gate the *dispatch* on a small reserved REST floor (e.g. per-routine reserve), not on the global deferrable policy.
- Reserve REST headroom for scheduled routines so background deferrable stages cannot drain the window to 0 (e.g. raise `hard_floor` for deferrable stages when a routine slot is due within the window).
- Log a single `routine_slot_late` line with slot time and delay when a routine starts > N minutes after its slot, so lateness is observable.
- Separately investigate the largest REST consumer (`gh_api_rest` 75k/24h from `pulse`) for cacheable or GraphQL-movable calls.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-budget-priority.sh` — `_pulse_stage_priority_class()` (line ~186) and `_pulse_rest_core_budget_defers_priority()`.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — `_pulse_run_routines_while_busy()` (~1087) and in-cycle `evaluate_routines_locked` call (~1820).
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh` — per-work-unit REST hard-floor checks.

## Verification

- Existing tests: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh`, `test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh`.
- With REST-core simulated at `emergency:0/5000`, a due routine is still evaluated and either dispatched within one tick or logged as explicitly deferred with slot lateness; deferrable scanners remain deferred.
- ShellCheck clean on changed scripts.

title: Full-loop PR reconcile on an existing PR replaces its curated Summary and runtime-verified Testing with the template
body:
## What

`full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr`, rerun on a branch whose PR already exists ("Continuing existing issue-linked PR #N at the final creation boundary" / "Reconciled and verified recovered PR #N metadata"), rewrites the PR body from the template when `--summary` and `--testing` are not passed. The curated Summary becomes "Implementation for issue #N." and Runtime Testing becomes "self-assessed — no additional evidence supplied", even though the PR was created with `--summary`, `--testing`, `--risk-level medium` and `--testing-level runtime-verified`.

## Observed (aidevops v3.39.68 runtime bundle, OpenCode)

1. A PR was created with `commit-and-pr --issue N --summary "..." --testing "..." --risk-level medium --testing-level runtime-verified`. The body was correct.
2. Another release took the version, so the branch was rebased and its version bumped.
3. `commit-and-pr --issue N --message "..." --title "..."` (no `--summary`/`--testing`) force-pushed the branch with a lease, which was correct. It then replaced the body: Summary "Implementation for issue #N.", Verification "self-assessed".
4. Rerunning with `--summary` and `--testing` restored the body.

The risk is silent loss of runtime-verified evidence, which feeds review and merge gates (the testing level falls to self-assessed).

## Expected

When continuing an existing PR, keep the current body's Summary, Runtime Testing (risk level and testing level) and Decisions sections unless the caller passes replacements. Refresh only derived sections such as Files Changed.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-commit-and-pr-partial-success.sh`

The PR-body reconcile path may live in a sourced sub-library (search for "Reconciled and verified recovered PR"). The paths are not verified here.

## Verification

- Create a PR with `--summary`/`--testing`/`--testing-level runtime-verified`, then rerun `commit-and-pr --issue N --message M`. The body keeps the Summary and the runtime-verified evidence; Files Changed reflects the new diff.
- Passing `--summary` on a rerun still replaces the Summary.

title: t18794: Dispatch: minimize finished-attempt lifecycle comments to cut thread noise while keeping the audit trail
body:
## Task


When a dispatch attempt reaches its terminal lease (`DISPATCH_LEASE phase=terminal`), the runner that wrote the attempt minimizes that attempt's superseded lifecycle comments with GraphQL `minimizeComment` (classifier `OUTDATED`). That covers `DISPATCH_CLAIM`, `DISPATCH_LEASE phase=prelaunch|ready|terminal` and `Dispatching worker`. Minimized comments stay in the thread (expandable) and in REST/GraphQL reads, so lease, dedup and checkpoint parsers and audits keep working. The attempt's `CLAIM_RELEASED` / terminal-blocker evidence and the latest live attempt stay visible.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

When a dispatch attempt reaches its terminal lease (`DISPATCH_LEASE phase=terminal`), the runner that wrote the attempt minimizes that attempt's superseded lifecycle comments with GraphQL `minimizeComment` (classifier `OUTDATED`). Minimized comments stay in the thread (expandable) and in REST/GraphQL reads, so lease, dedup and checkpoint parsers and audits keep working. The attempt's `CLAIM_RELEASED` / terminal-blocker evidence and the latest live attempt stay visible.

- Each attempt posts 5–6 comments. Example, #35918 on 2026-10-29: 04:28:29 `DISPATCH_CLAIM`, 04:28:46 lease `prelaunch`, 04:29:36 lease `ready`, 04:43:35 `CLAIM_RELEASED`, 04:43:45 lease `terminal`. A second runner repeated the pattern at 05:03–05:21 and added `Dispatching worker`.
- #35689 reached 140 comments and #35751 reached 125, which buries the human-relevant evidence.

title: Support verified tagless deployments when finalizing cleanup receipts
body:
## Observed problem

A maintained application uses reviewed PRs into its integration branch and a normal push-triggered rolling deployment, without version tags or GitHub Releases. The PR merged through `full-loop-helper.sh merge`, its exact source checks and review-bot gate passed, the canonical checkout was synchronized through the audited helper, and the deployment workflow completed successfully. Runtime health reported the deployed source SHA; ancestry proved it contained the merge.

Despite this verified delivery, `full-loop-helper.sh finalize-receipt <PR> <REPO>` exited 1 with `Finalization blocked: terminal release evidence is missing`. The merged worktree remains safely retained. No receipt was hand-edited, no tag or GitHub Release was fabricated, and `record-no-release` was not used to misrepresent an explicitly authorized deployment.

Observed with aidevops v3.39.84. Repository names, local paths, run IDs and deployment details are intentionally omitted from this public report.

## Implementation scope

- Inspect `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-state-lifecycle-commands.sh`: `cmd_finalize_receipt` calls `_full_loop_terminal_release_status`; the recognized terminal states require an existing release receipt. Published/included-release recording requires a version tag and versioned release evidence.
- Reference `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md`: maintained applications may use their normal deployment path and should not need an unrelated versioned publication solely to finalize cleanup.
- Add or document an existing supported path for recording verified tagless application deployment evidence and finalizing the matching cleanup receipt. Do not weaken existing versioned-release, exact-head, ancestry, trust, or live-owner cleanup guards.
- If a supported adapter already exists, document its exact invocation and wire it into the maintained-application lifecycle instead of adding a competing mechanism. Paths to existing focused tests are not yet known; discover and reuse them.

## Acceptance and verification

1. A merged PR with a successful explicitly identified deployment workflow, immutable deployed source identity, and verified merge inclusion can finalize through a supported tagless-deployment evidence path.
2. Missing, failed, pending, stale, unrelated or untrusted deployment evidence must not become a successful terminal receipt. A merely healthy endpoint or arbitrary local JSON file is insufficient.
3. Finalization must not create a tag/GitHub Release, falsely record publication as not requested, delete a live-owned worktree, or require an extra application environment.
4. Existing versioned-release and cleanup-ownership regression checks remain green. Run ShellCheck for changed helpers and the narrow existing lifecycle/receipt tests, adding focused coverage for this observed gap within that existing tooling.

This is a framework bookkeeping follow-up, not a request to redeploy or mutate any application or its data.
